`X` be of type (S) (*formal-schemes-of-type-S*), with morphisms adic. Huber's Proposition 1.9.1:
there are an adic space `d(X)` and a morphism of topologically ringed spaces `λ = λ_X: d(X) → X`
such that (a) `d(X)` is analytic: for the ideal sheaf `I ⊆ O_X` of sections vanishing at every
point, `λ⁻¹(I)·O_{d(X)} = O_{d(X)}`; (b) `O_X → λ_* O_{d(X)}` factors through `λ_* O⁺_{d(X)}` and
`λ: (d(X), O⁺_{d(X)}) → (X, O_X)` is a morphism of locally ringed spaces; (c) `(d(X), λ)` is
universal among adic spaces with a morphism to `X` satisfying (a) and (b). Hence `d` is a functor
from type-(S) formal schemes with adic morphisms to analytic adic spaces, and `λ` is natural. Affine
formulas: for `X = Spf A` with `A` noetherian, `d(X) = t(X)_a` with the restriction of `π_X`
(*noetherian-formal-scheme-as-adic-space*; case (a) of the construction uses Huber94 §4); in case
(b), with `B` the integral closure of (the image of) `A` in `A(1/s)`, `d(X) = Spa(A(1/s), B)` and
`λ(x) = {a ∈ A : |a(x)| < 1}` — `d(Spf A)` is an adic space because `A(1/s)` is a strongly
noetherian Tate ring (AdicSpaces layer 4). For `X` locally tfp over `O_K` (in particular
admissible), `d(Spf A) = Spa(A[1/ϖ], B)`; when `K` is discretely valued (so `X` is locally
noetherian and `t(X)` is defined) `d(X)` is the open locus `{|ϖ| ≠ 0}` of `t(X)` over `Spa(O_K,
O_K)` (Hübner §8, after Def. 8.5, p. 38), while for non-discrete `K` no adic space `t(X)` is
available and only the affine formula is used; `d(X) = d(X^{tf})`, so `ϖ`-torsion is invisible. Open
formal subschemes `U ⊆ X` give open subspaces `d(U) = λ⁻¹(U)`, and for every affine `U` whose ring satisfies
(S)(a) or (S)(b), `d(U)` is spectral (Huber96 §1.9, (1.9.3)). In `FormalScheme`, define `genericFibre` as `d(X)`,
an analytic adic space, for `X` of type (S). Prove `genericFibre.lift` (a morphism of topologically
ringed spaces `g: Z → X` from an adic space satisfying (a) and (b) factors uniquely as `λ_X ∘ g̃`
with `g̃: Z → d(X)`), `genericFibre.lift_unique` (two morphisms `Z → d(X)` with the same composite
to `X` are equal), `genericFibre.map` (an adic morphism `f: X → Y` of type-(S) formal schemes
induces `d(f): d(X) → d(Y)` with `λ_Y ∘ d(f) = f ∘ λ_X`; `d(id) = id` and `d(g ∘ f) = d(g) ∘ d(f)`),
`genericFibre_spf_of_typeSb` (an isomorphism: if `sA` is an ideal of definition and `A(1/s)` is
Hausdorff and strongly noetherian, `d(Spf A) ≅ Spa(A(1/s), integralClosure A A(1/s))`),
`genericFibre_spf_of_isNoetherian` (for `A` noetherian adic with principal defining ideal
`sA`, the same normalized localization formula), and
`genericFibre_spf_of_isNoetherian_analyticLocus` (for any noetherian adic `A`, the generic fibre
is the analytic open subspace `spaAnalytic` of `(A, A)`, hence `t(Spf A)_a`; no principal
defining ideal is required), `genericFibre_ofIsOpenImmersion` (for an open formal subscheme `U ⊆ X`, `d(U) → d(X)`
is an open immersion with image `λ⁻¹(U)`), `genericFibre_torsionFreeQuotient` (for `X`
locally tfp over `O_K`, there is an admissible quotient `X^{tf} → X` whose maps on affine
sections are surjective with kernel the `ϖ`-power torsion, and `d(X^{tf}) → d(X)` is an
isomorphism), `genericFibre_isAnalytic` (an
instance: every point of `d(X)` is analytic), `genericFibre_spectralSpace` (an instance: for `U`
affine whose coordinate ring satisfies (S)(a) or (S)(b), `d(U)` is a spectral space
and `λ` is a spectral map (Huber96 §1.9, (1.9.3))),
`genericFibre_quasiCompact` (if `X` is quasi-compact and locally tfp over `O_K` then `d(X)` is
quasi-compact; if `X` is also quasi-separated, then so is `d(X)`; a finite affine cover and
Huber96 (1.9.3), p. 98, give these implications) and `genericFibre_spf_microbial` (for a microbial valuation ring
`A`, complete for its valuation topology, with fraction field `L`,
`d(Spf A) = Spa(L, A)` and `λ` is a homeomorphism onto `Spf A`: both are the chain of primes of `A`
containing the height-one prime, `λ(v_q) = q` (Huber96 §1.9, Ex. 1.9.2(i))) (Huber96 §1.9, Prop.
1.9.1, pp. 96–97, existence and universal property of the generic fibre functor; Huber96 §1.9, proof
of 1.9.1, p. 97: the plus ring in case (b) is the integral closure of `A`, not `A` itself; Hübner
§8, after Def. 8.5, p. 38; Hübner §8, Ex. 8.7, p. 39, the fibre `{|p| ≠ 0}` of `t(Spf ℤ_p[[T]])`
over `Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p)` is the non-quasi-compact open disc). *Needs:* *formal-schemes-of-type-S*;
*noetherian-formal-scheme-as-adic-space*; *admissible-formal-scheme*; *adic-morphism*,
*noetherian-type-stably-sheafy* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R0); AdicSpaces layer 4; Tau Ceti
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spa`, `TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spaAnalytic`,
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spa_integralClosure`, `TauCeti.Huber.Pair`; Mathlib `integralClosure`.

The affine localization statements quantify over Part II’s `AdicSpace.Affinoid`: a
topological ring isomorphism identifies its ring with `A[1/s]`, and its plus ring is
exactly `integralClosure A A[1/s]`. The image of `sⁿA` is a neighbourhood basis at zero,
including when `A` has torsion. The type-(S)(b) comparison explicitly requires
`T2Space A[1/s]`: the pinned `Huber.IsStronglyNoetherian` tests completed restricted
series rings and does not by itself assert separatedness of `A[1/s]`. The noetherian
case derives separatedness from the noetherian adic source (Huber96, proof of
Proposition 1.9.1, p. 97). In the microbial statement, `Valuation.IsMicrobial`, the
valuation-ball basis, and equality of the plus ring with the valuation ring specify
the field presentation. Membership outside `Spf.basicOpen a` expresses the centre
formula `|a| < 1`.

**Checks.**

- `genericFibre_test_formalAffineLine` (computation) — `d(Spf O_K⟨T⟩)` is the adic space `Spa(K⟨T⟩,
  O_K⟨T⟩)`, the closed unit disc, whose underlying set is `closedPolydisc 1 K`.
- `genericFibre_test_powerSeries_dvr` (computation) — for `K` discretely valued with uniformiser
  `ϖ`, `d(Spf O_K[[T]]) = t(Spf O_K[[T]])_a = R(T/ϖ) ∪ R(ϖ/T)` is quasi-compact and contains the
  point `|ϖ| = 0, |T| ≠ 0`; its open subspace `{|ϖ| ≠ 0}` over `Spa(K, O_K)` is the union of the
  rational subsets `{|Tⁿ| ≤ |ϖ|}`, `n ≥ 1`, i.e. the open unit disc, and is not quasi-compact.
- `genericFibre_test_torsion` (degenerate) — `d(Spf O_K/ϖ) = ∅` and `d(Spf O_K⟨T⟩/(ϖT)) ≅ d(Spf O_K)
  = Spa(K, O_K)`, a one-point space mapping to the closed point of `Spf O_K`: `ϖ`-torsion does not
  contribute.
- `genericFibre_test_plusRing` (non-example) — for `char K ≠ 2` (so that `X² − ϖ² = (X − ϖ)(X +
  ϖ)` with coprime factors over `K`; the residue characteristic may be `2`) and `A = O_K[X]/(X² − ϖ²) =
  O_K⟨X⟩/(X² − ϖ²)`, `A[1/ϖ] ≅ K × K` and the image `{(a + bϖ, a − bϖ)}` of `A` is not integrally
  closed (`X/ϖ ↦ (1, −1)` is integral but not in `A`, since `bϖ = 1` has no solution in `O_K`);
  the plus ring of `d(Spf A)` is the integral closure `O_K × O_K` (`(1, 0)` and `(0, 1)` are
  idempotent, hence integral), while `spa` of `A` and of its integral closure agree
  (`spa_integralClosure`).
- `genericFibre_test_noetherian` (compatibility) — for `A = ℤ_p⟨T⟩` (both (a) and (b) apply) the two
  affine formulas agree: `Spa(ℤ_p⟨T⟩, ℤ_p⟨T⟩)_a = Spa(ℚ_p⟨T⟩, ℤ_p⟨T⟩)`.

`FormalScheme.IsAdicMorphism` tests the intrinsic affine ring maps, including
nonnoetherian bases. `AnalyticSpecialisation.postcomp` composes the specialization
with an adic formal morphism, and `genericFibre.map` is its unique universal lift.
The lift commutes with specialization (`specialisation_naturality`).

**Checks for formal morphisms and their generic fibres.**

- `IsAdicMorphism_identity`: identities are adic.
- `IsAdicMorphism_open`: formal open immersions are adic.
- `IsAdicMorphism_discrete`: every morphism between discrete schemes is adic.
- `AnalyticSpecialisation.postcomp_identity` and `genericFibre.map_identity`: the identity acts identically.
- `AnalyticSpecialisation.postcomp_composition` and `genericFibre.map_composition`: composition is preserved.
- `AnalyticSpecialisation.postcomp_points` and `genericFibre.map_points`: the point maps commute with specialization.

  The postcomposed specialization itself sends `x` to `f(σ(x))`.
- `AnalyticSpecialisation.postcomp_empty`: postcomposition from an empty adic space has empty range.
- `AnalyticSpecialisation.postcomp_sheaf`: the underlying ring-presheafed morphism is exactly the categorical composite.


The carrier `FormalScheme.AnalyticSpecialisation Z X` retains the continuous map and
its map of ring sheaves. On formal affine opens this map is continuous for the intrinsic
adic topology. Its image has valuation at most one; a section has valuation less than one
precisely when its germ at the centre is a nonunit. At every source point some
topologically nilpotent formal section has nonzero value. Thus it records the integral
locality and analytic conditions of Huber96, Proposition 1.9.1, without asserting that
the map into the full analytic structure sheaf is local. `GenericFibreData` represents
these maps, and `genericFibreData`, `genericFibre`, `specialisation` and
`genericFibre.lift` are its chosen data, space, point map and unique lift.

**Checks for the generic-fibre carrier.**

- `AnalyticSpecialisation.precomp_identity`: precomposition by the identity preserves the map.
- `AnalyticSpecialisation.precomp_composition`: two precompositions agree with precomposition by their composite.
- `AnalyticSpecialisation.precomp_points`: the point map is ordinary composition.
- `genericFibre.lift_identity`: the specialization map lifts to the identity.
- `genericFibre.lift_composition`: lifting a precomposition composes the lift.
- `genericFibre.lift_unique`: equality of the integral ring-sheaf maps determines the lift.
- `genericFibre_empty`, `genericFibreData_empty`, `specialisation_empty`, `GenericFibreData_empty`:
  an empty formal scheme has empty generic fibre.
- `genericFibre_discrete`, `genericFibreData_discrete`, `specialisation_discrete`, `GenericFibreData_discrete`:
  a discrete adic ring has empty analytic generic fibre.
- `genericFibre_rankOne`, `genericFibreData_rankOne`, `specialisation_rankOne`, `GenericFibreData_rankOne`:
  for a complete rank-one valuation base, the generic fibre is nonempty and specialization
  is bijective on points.

**For formal `O_K`-schemes locally of tf presentation, `d(X)` is the adic space of Raynaud's rigid
generic fibre.** (*raynaud-generic-fibre*) Let `K` be complete with nontrivial rank-one valuation
(`O_K` may be non-noetherian) and `X` a formal `O_K`-scheme locally of tf presentation over `Spf
O_K` (including the case where `X` is admissible); `r` and its properties are those of *rigid-adic-comparison-functor*
(AdicSpacesPartII layer R1). Prove: (i) for `X = Spf A` the integral closure `B` of the image of `A` in `A_K = A ⊗_{O_K} K` equals the power-bounded subring `A_K°`, so `d(Spf A) = Spa(A_K, A_K°) = r(Sp A_K)`,
where `r` is Huber's rigid–adic comparison functor (Huber94 §4, Lem. 4.4, p. 543: the plus ring of a
Tate ring of topologically finite type over `K` is `A°`); (ii) Raynaud's generic fibre `X_rig` (BL I
§4, p. 306: glue `Sp(A_K)` over formal affine opens `Spf A`, basic opens `Spf A⟨f⁻¹⟩` going to
Laurent domains `Sp A_K⟨f⁻¹⟩ = {|f| ≥ 1}`; Conrad-AWS §3.3, Exercise 3.3.8, p. 32, the construction
of `X ↦ X_rig` by gluing affinoids along Laurent domains) is a quasi-separated rigid `K`-space, and
there is an isomorphism of adic spaces `d(X) ≅ r(X_rig)`, functorial in `X` and compatible with open
formal subschemes (`U ↦ λ⁻¹(U)`); (iii) in particular `d(X)` is locally of finite type over `Spa(K,
O_K)`, and `d(X)` is quasi-compact (resp. quasi-separated) when `X` is quasi-compact (resp. always)
(Huber96 §1.9, Ex. 1.9.2.ii, pp. 97–98, the comparison with Raynaud's functor `s` for rank-one
valuation rings; Huber94 §4, Rem. 4.6(ii), p. 544, the discretely valued case `r_K ∘ s ≅ t_a ∘ u`).
For instance `d(Spf O_K⟨T⟩) = r(Sp K⟨T⟩)` is the closed unit disc, and `d` of the `ϖ`-adic
completion of `P¹_{O_K}` is `r` of the rigid projective line glued from two closed unit discs along
`{|T| = 1}` (Conrad-AWS §3.3, Ex. 3.3.9); for `K` discretely valued with uniformiser `ϖ`, `X =
Spf(O_K⟨T⟩/(T² − ϖ)) = Spf O_L` with `L = K(√ϖ)` (Eisenstein), `d(X) = Spa(L, O_L)` is one point and
`X_rig = Sp L`. *Needs:* *generic-fibre-functor-d*; *admissible-formal-scheme*;
*topologically-finitely-presented-algebra*; *rigid-adic-comparison-functor*,
*tft-plus-ring-power-bounded*, *rigid-analytic-space*, *rigid-adic-quasi-separated-equivalence*
(AdicSpacesPartII layer R1); Tau Ceti `TauCeti.Huber.powerBoundedSubring`,
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spa_integralClosure`.

The affine statement is `FormalScheme.genericFibre_spf_tfp`. For a tfp `O`-algebra
`A` with continuous structural map and its `ϖ`-adic topology, it asserts that
`genericFibre (ofSpf A)` is isomorphic to the adic spectrum of the generic affinoid of `A`.
Here the generic affinoid of `A` (the generic-fibre clause of
*topologically-finitely-presented-algebra*) has precisely the ring
`Localization.Away (algebraMap O A ϖ)`, the generic-fibre topology, and the
plus ring `powerBoundedSubring`; completeness and sheafiness are part of the
construction. The ring calculation, that this plus ring is the integral closure of the image of
`A`, remains a separate statement.
Neither the construction nor the isomorphism requires flatness or a reduced ring
(Huber96, proof of 1.9.1 and Example 1.9.2(ii), pp. 97–98).

`FormalScheme.LocallyTFPFormal O ϖ` is the full subcategory of formal schemes
over `Spf O` satisfying `IsLocallyTFP`, with no quasi-compactness or admissibility
condition. `FormalScheme.genericFibre_raynaud` constructs a functor from this
category to Part II's `RigidSpace K`, together with isomorphisms from `d(X)` to
the underlying spaces of Part II's `rigidToAdic K` applied to its values. Its
hypotheses identify `O` topologically with `K°`, with `K` complete, nontrivially
normed and nonarchimedean and `ϖ` giving the complete rank-one base topology.
The isomorphisms commute with all formal morphisms and with the structural
maps to `Spa(K,K°)`; the base isomorphism sends each `O`-section to its specified
image in `K`. On affine objects the rigid value is `Sp(A[1/ϖ])`, with the
localization topology and the same scalar map. Open immersions become rigid
open immersions, and formal affine opens correspond under `rigidToAdic.rho`
to their specialization preimages. These conditions specify the gluing and
its comparison on the imported rigid carriers (Conrad-AWS, Exercise 3.3.8,
p. 32; Huber96, Example 1.9.2(ii), pp. 97–98).

**Checks.**

- (generic affinoid, plus ring) — its plus ring is
  exactly Tau Ceti's power-bounded subring, including nilpotents.
- (generic affinoid, torsion) — if a power of
  `ϖ` kills `1` in `A`, its generic-fibre ring is zero; this includes `A = O/ϖ`.
- (generic affinoid, base) — for `A = O`, its
  generic-fibre ring is `FractionRing O` as an `O`-algebra.
- `LocallyTFPFormal_base` — the identity of `Spf O` is an object.
- `LocallyTFPFormal_empty` — the empty formal scheme is an object.
- `LocallyTFPFormal_torsion` — a nonzero tfp algebra killed by `ϖ`, with its
  `ϖ`-adic topology, defines an object of this category but is not admissible.

**The generic fibre commutes with fibre products and with completed extension of the base field.**
(*generic-fibre-fibre-products*) Let `X`, `Y`, `Z` be locally tfp over `O_K`. Prove: (a) for
morphisms `X → Z ← Y` of formal `O_K`-schemes locally of tf presentation, the natural map `d(X ×_Z Y) → d(X) ×_{d(Z)} d(Y)` is an isomorphism of adic spaces, where the right side is the fibre product
of *fibre-products-existence* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R0) (it exists because `d(X) → d(Z)` is locally of finite
type); since `d` kills `ϖ`-torsion, the same holds for the fibre product in the admissible category;
(b) for a complete nonarchimedean extension `K'/K` — any complete extension of rank-one valued
fields — `d(X ⊗̂_{O_K} O_{K'}) ≅ d(X) ×_{Spa(K,O_K)} Spa(K', O_{K'})`, functorially in `X` (BL I §4,
Cor. 4.6, p. 310, the rigid generic fibre commutes with fibre products; Conrad-MR §3.1, Thm
3.1.5(a), p. 16, the same for Berthelot-type generic fibres on `FS_C`). For instance `d(Spf O_K⟨S⟩ ×_{Spf O_K} Spf O_K⟨T⟩) = d(Spf O_K⟨S,T⟩)` is the closed unit bidisc, the fibre product of two
closed unit discs over `Spa(K, O_K)`; and for `P`, `P'` locally topologically finitely presented formal `O_K`-schemes, `d(P × P') = d(P) × d(P')`, written `(P × P')_K = P_K × P'_K` in the rigid-cohomology literature.
Clause (a) is `FormalScheme.genericFibre_isPullback`. For clause (b),
`FormalScheme.genericFibre_baseExtension` uses complete nontrivially valued rank-one fields
`K`, `K'`, topological identifications `O ≃ O_K`, `O' ≃ O_{K'}`, and a continuous
Huber-pair homomorphism `φ : (K, O_K) → (K', O_{K'})`. Its restriction `φO : O → O'`
must agree with those identifications; a pseudouniformiser `ϖ` and its image give the
adic topologies. No algebraicity, finite degree or discrete valuation is assumed.
Put `b = Spf(φO)`. For a locally tfp structural map `s : X → Spf O`, the formal
pullback `W = X ×_{Spf O} Spf O'` is the completed extension: on affine charts its
ring is `A ⊗̂_O O'`, as identified by `Spf.tensorPullbackIso`. The theorem supplies
local tfp over `O'`, type (S) for `W`, and adicness of its two projections. It states
`IsPullback (d(pr₁)) (d(pr₂) ≫ β') (d(s) ≫ β) (Affinoid.map φ)`.
Here `β`, `β'` identify the two valuation-ring generic fibres with their field
spectra and satisfy `d(b) ≫ β = β' ≫ Affinoid.map φ`;
`FormalScheme.genericFibre_baseExtension_baseIso` supplies such compatible
identifications and adicness of `b` (Huber96 Prop. 1.9.1 and Ex. 1.9.2(i), pp. 96–97).
`FormalScheme.genericFibre_baseExtension_naturality` states both projection equations
for the canonical map `W_X → W_Y` induced by any adic `O`-morphism `X → Y`, giving
functoriality in `X`. The base-extension assertion follows from the affine generic-fibre
construction and gluing in Conrad-AWS Ex. 3.3.8, p. 32, using completed scalar extension
on affinoids, and the adic comparison in Huber96 Ex. 1.9.2(ii), pp. 97–98.

Checks:

- `genericFibre_baseExtension_identity`: for the identity extension the first
  projection induces an isomorphism on generic fibres.
- `genericFibre_baseExtension_empty`: the completed extension of the empty formal
  scheme has empty generic fibre.
- `genericFibre_baseExtension_base`: for `X = Spf O`, the second projection identifies
  the generic fibre of the completed extension with `d(Spf O')`.

*Needs:* *generic-fibre-functor-d*; *raynaud-generic-fibre*; *admissible-formal-scheme*;
*completed-tensor-product*, *affinoid-fibre-product*, *fibre-products-existence* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R0).

### R2.4 specialisation, tubes and rig-points

**The specialisation map `λ_X = sp: d(X) → X`.** (*specialisation-map*) For `X` of type (S) the
specialisation map is the continuous map `λ_X: d(X) → X` underlying Huber's Proposition 1.9.1
(*generic-fibre-functor-d*). For `X = Spf A` and `x ∈ d(X)`, `λ(x) = {a ∈ A : |a(x)| < 1}`, an open
prime of `A`; equivalently `λ(x)` is the image of the closed point of `Spec κ(x)⁺` under the map
`Spec κ(x)⁺ → Spec A` induced by `A → κ(x)⁺` (`|A(x)| ≤ 1`), i.e. the centre on `Spec A` of the
valuation ring `(x, k(x)⁺)` in the sense of *adic-valuation-rings-and-centres* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R0), which
owns the notion of centre. Properties, (i)
and (ii) for `X` of type (S) and (iii)–(v) for `X` admissible over `O_K`: (i) `λ` is continuous: for
`s ∈ A`, `λ⁻¹(D(s)) = {|s| = 1} = {|s| ≥ 1}` is open and `λ⁻¹(V(s)) = {|s| < 1}` is closed; (ii) `λ`
is natural: `λ_Y ∘ d(f) = f ∘ λ_X`; (iii) for `X` admissible over `O_K`, `λ` maps each classical
point (residue field finite over `K`) to a closed point of `X_s`, and every closed point of `X_s` is
the image of a classical point (BL I §3, 3.4, 3.5), `λ` of the classical point attached to a
rig-point being its special point; the restriction `sp: X_rig → X` to classical points is
Berthelot's specialisation map of rigid geometry, which is anticontinuous: preimages of closed
subsets are admissible opens (the tubes of *tube*); (iv) `λ` is compatible with admissible blow-ups
`φ: X' → X`, i.e. `φ ∘ λ_{X'} = λ_X ∘ d(φ)` with `d(φ)` an isomorphism
(*generic-fibre-inverts-admissible-blow-ups*); (v) for `X` quasi-compact admissible, the maps
`λ_{X'}` over all admissible blow-ups `X' → X` induce a homeomorphism `d(X) → lim_{X'} |X'|` and an
isomorphism `(d(X), O⁺) ≅ lim (X', O_{X'})` (the Zariski–Riemann description; Hübner Thm 8.9, and Conrad-AWS §4.1, p. 35). Care: in the adic space,
`λ⁻¹` of a closed set is closed, not open; the rigid "anticontinuity" concerns classical points and
corresponds to the interior (*tube*). In `FormalScheme`, define `specialisation` (`λ_X: d(X) → X`,
the continuous map of Proposition 1.9.1) and `rigidSpecialisation` (on classical points, `λ` agrees
with Berthelot's `sp: X_rig → X` under *raynaud-generic-fibre* and AdicSpacesPartII layer R1's identification of
classical points). Prove `specialisation_spf_apply` (a simp theorem: for `X = Spf A`, `λ(x) = {a ∈ A :
v_x(a) < 1}`), `specialisation_eq_center` (`λ(x)` is the image of the closed point of `Spec κ(x)⁺`
under `Spec κ(x)⁺ → Spec A`),
`specialisation_preimage_basicOpen` (`λ⁻¹(D(s)) = {x : |s(x)| ≥ 1} = rationalSubset {1} s`, open;
`λ⁻¹(V(s)) = {|s| < 1}`, closed), `specialisation_naturality` (`λ_Y ∘ d(f) = f ∘ λ_X` for every adic
morphism `f: X → Y` of type-(S) formal schemes), `specialisation_classical_isClosed` (for `X`
admissible and `x` classical, `λ(x)` is a closed point of `X_s`),
`exists_classical_specialisation_eq` (for `X` admissible, every closed point of `X_s` equals `λ(x)`
for some classical `x`), `specialisation_blowUp` (for an admissible blow-up `φ: X' → X`, `φ ∘ λ_{X'} = λ_X ∘ d(φ)`), `specialisationLimitHomeomorph` (for `X` quasi-compact admissible, `d(X) → lim_{X'} |X'|` over admissible blow-ups is a homeomorphism) and `RigPoint.specialPoint_eq_specialisation`
(for `X` admissible and a rig-point `u: Spf B → X` with classical point `x ∈ d(X)` under
`RigPoint.equivClassicalPoints` of *rig-point*, `λ(x)` is the special point of `u`; this is stated
here rather than in *rig-point* because it refers to `λ`) (Huber94 §4, proof of Prop. 4.1, point
(1), p. 539, the pointwise definition and continuity of the specialisation map; Hübner §8, p. 37,
the specialisation is the centre map; Conrad-AWS §3.3, Ex. 3.3.13, p. 34, rigid-analytic
anticontinuity on classical points; Conrad-AWS §4.1, p. 35, the Zariski–Riemann description over all
formal models). *Needs:* *generic-fibre-functor-d*; *raynaud-generic-fibre*; *rig-point*;
*admissible-formal-scheme*; *rigid-adic-comparison-functor*, *rigid-analytic-space* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R1); Tau
Ceti `TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset`.

Continuity is carried by the `TopCat` morphism `specialisation`. The affine targets `specialisation_spf_apply`, `specialisation_eq_center` and
`specialisation_preimage_basicOpen` use `Spf.prime` and the pullback valuation
`genericFibre.spfValuation`; their point is the actual `specialisation (ofSpf A) x`
(Huber96 Prop. 1.9.1, pp. 96–97). The algebraic statement
`specialisation_spf_apply_affine` constructs the prime for any ring map `φ : A → B`
with `φ(A) ⊆ B⁺` and `v ∈ Spa(B, B⁺)`; `specialisation_preimage_basicOpen_affine`
identifies the locus `1 ≤ |s|` in `Spa(B, B⁺)` with `R(1/s)`. These two statements
concern valuations on rings; the three formal-scheme statements above identify the
actual specialisation map. The two classical-point theorems use
`genericFibre.classicalPoints O K β s hs`: finiteness of the residue-field map induced by
`d(s)` and a fixed base identification `β : d(Spf O) ≅ Spa(K,K°)`.
Here `O` is a complete rank-one valuation ring, `s` is adic, and `X` is admissible;
no discreteness or quasi-compactness is required (Conrad-AWS Ex. 3.3.13, p. 34;
[FK] II, Cor. 8.2.13, p. 555, and Cor. 8.2.18, p. 558, applied on affine
neighbourhoods to the tube of a closed point). Closed points are expressed by closed singletons on `X`,
whose topological space is also that of the special fibre.

`RigPoint` records a sheaf ideal, its special point, and the existence of an admissible
closed immersion from `Spf B` for a finite flat `O_K`-algebra `B` that is a
one-dimensional local domain. The algebra structure induces the composite map to
`Spf O_K`. Isomorphic
presentations therefore give the same rig-point. The closed immersion is expressed
by its closed embedding and surjective stalk maps, with an adic formal morphism,
including over nonnoetherian valuation rings. `RigPoint.equivClassicalPoints` is fixed
by `RigPoint.equivClassicalPoints_kernel`: on every open containing the specialisation,
a section belongs to the rig-point ideal exactly when its analytic value is zero.
`RigPoint.specialPoint_eq_specialisation` then identifies the distinguished closed
point with `λ(x)` ([FK] II, Prop. 8.2.6, pp. 552–553, Prop. 8.2.10 and Cor. 8.2.11, p. 554,
the finite local domain obtained by schematic closure; Conrad-AWS Ex. 3.3.13, p. 34).

`specialisation_blowUp` includes both the commuting square and invertibility of the
actual generic-fibre morphism, for a finitely generated open centre on an admissible
formal scheme (Conrad-AWS Ex. 3.3.11 and Exer. 3.3.12, pp. 33–34).
`specialisationLimitHomeomorph` states existence of a homeomorphism for quasi-compact
admissible `X` to the compatible families of centres on all admissible blow-ups.
The target has the subspace topology of the product; compatibility is with every
formal morphism over `X`. Its projection at each blow-up sends a lifted analytic point
to its specialisation, fixing the homeomorphism rather than just its isomorphism class
(Conrad-AWS §4.1, p. 35).

`rigidSpecialisation` is the restriction of `specialisation` to this classical subset,
identified with rigid points through Part II's `rigidToAdic.classicalPointsEquiv`.
It therefore uses the same centre formula (Conrad-AWS Ex. 3.3.13, p. 34).

**Checks for the point carriers.**

- `rigidSpecialisation_base`: every classical point over `Spf O` maps to its unique formal point.
- `rigidSpecialisation_empty`: its image for an empty formal scheme is empty.
- `rigidSpecialisation_rigPoint`: it sends the classical point of a rig-point to its special point.
- `genericFibre.classicalPoints_base`: every point over `Spf O` is classical.
- `genericFibre.classicalPoints_empty`: the empty formal scheme has no classical points.
- `genericFibre.classicalPoints_rankTwo`: a point with valuation-ring dimension two is not classical.
- `RigPoint_base`: the identity of `Spf O` gives the zero ideal rig-point.
- `RigPoint_empty`: an empty formal scheme has no rig-points.
- `RigPoint_ideal`: the ideal determines the rig-point, including its special point.
- `RigPoint.equivClassicalPoints_base`: over `Spf O` the correspondence covers the unique analytic point.
- `RigPoint.equivClassicalPoints_empty`: its image on an empty formal scheme is empty.
- `RigPoint.equivClassicalPoints_affine`: a formal affine coefficient belongs to the rig-point ideal
  exactly when its value at the corresponding classical point is zero.

**Checks.**

- `specialisation_test_closedDisc` (computation) — for `X = Spf O_K⟨T⟩`, `λ` sends the Gauss point
  to the generic point of `A¹_k` (`|f| < 1` at the Gauss point iff all coefficients of `f` lie in
  `m_K`), the classical point `T = c` (`c ∈ O_K`) to the closed point `T = c̄`, and the rank-two
  point `η_{1⁻}` (the Gauss point specialised towards `0`: `|T(η_{1⁻})| < 1` but `|T(η_{1⁻})|^m > |ϖ|` for every `m`) to the closed point `0`: `λ` is not injective on the disc, since a rank-two point
  and a classical point share an image. On the closure of the Gauss point, `λ` instead
  identifies the points with `A¹_k` (Wedhorn Ex. 7.57(5), p. 72).
  The Check uses topological nilpotence of a restricted series for the coefficient
  condition, and tests `T − d` at `T = c` by whether `c − d` is a nonunit of `O_K`.
- `specialisation_test_Spf_OK` (degenerate) — for `X = Spf O_K`, `d(X) = Spa(K, O_K)` is one point
  and `λ` maps it to the unique point of `Spf O_K`.
- `specialisation_test_preimage_closed` (non-example) — in the closed unit disc, `λ⁻¹({0}) = {|T| < 1}` is closed and not open: it contains the rank-two point `η_{1⁻}` (the specialisation of the
  Gauss point towards `0`) but contains no neighbourhood of that point.
- `specialisation_test_blowUp` (compatibility) — for the admissible blow-up `X'` of `(T, ϖ)` on `Spf O_K⟨T⟩`, `λ_X(η_{|ϖ|})` is the closed point `0` of `A¹_k`, while `λ_{X'}(η_{|ϖ|})` is the generic
  point of the exceptional component, and `φ ∘ λ_{X'} = λ_X`.
- `specialisation_test_surjective_closed` (characterisation) — for `X` admissible, the set of `λ(x)`
  with `x` classical is exactly the set of closed points of `X_s`.

**Tubes `]T[` of locally closed subsets of the special fibre, adic and rigid.** (*tube*) Let `X` be an
formal scheme of type (S) with specialisation `λ: d(X) → X` (*specialisation-map*).
The open–closed construction defines `FormalScheme.tube X T hT : Opens (genericFibre X).obj`
for every locally closed `T`. The affine rational-domain formula requires a principal ideal of
definition `(s)`, using `s` in place of `ϖ`; no principal generator is asserted for type (S)(a).
The classical-point and admissible-blow-up comparisons below assume admissibility over `O_K`. For `T ⊆ X` locally closed (`X`
and `X_s` have the same space): (i) if `T = U` is open, `]U[ := λ⁻¹(U) = d(X|_U)`, an open subspace;
(ii) if `T = Z` is closed and `X = Spf A` with `Z = V(f_1, …, f_r) ⊆ Spec A/ϖ` (`f_i ∈ A`), then
`]Z[ := ⋃_{m≥1} {x ∈ d(X) : |f_i(x)|^m ≤ |ϖ| for all i}`; this is independent of the chosen `f_i`
and of `ϖ`, equals the interior of the closed set `λ⁻¹(Z)`, and glues over affine covers; (iii) for
`T = U ∩ Z`, `]T[ := λ⁻¹(U) ∩ ]Z[`. Each `]T[` is open in `d(X)`. Rigid comparison: the classical
points of `]T[` are exactly the classical points `x` with `sp(x) ∈ T`, i.e. Berthelot's tube
`sp⁻¹(T)`, which is an admissible open of `X_rig`, and `r(sp⁻¹(T)) = ]T[` under
*rigid-adic-comparison-functor* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R1). For closed `Z` and rational `q > 0`, the closed tube of radius `|ϖ|^q` attached to the chosen equations `f_i` is `[Z]_q := {x : |f_i(x)| ≤ |ϖ|^q for all i}`; unlike `]Z[`, this depends on those equations, in the convention of
*fractional-valuation-bound* — radii `|ϖ|^q` with `q ∈ ℚ_{>0}` use that convention, never an element
`ϖ^q` of `K`; it is quasi-compact and `]Z[ = ⋃_{q>0} [Z]_q`. The set `λ⁻¹(Z)` itself is closed, and
in general strictly larger than `]Z[` by non-classical boundary points; Huber's pseudo-adic spaces
`d(X, L)` use `λ⁻¹(L)`, not the interior. In `FormalScheme`, define `tube` (`]T[ ⊆ d(X)` for `T ⊆ X`
locally closed) and `closedTube` (with the equations `f_i` as explicit data, `[Z]_q = {|f_i| ≤ |ϖ|^q for all i}` for `q ∈ ℚ_{>0}`, fractional
convention, a quasi-compact open with `]Z[ = ⋃_q [Z]_q`). Prove `tube_of_isOpen` (a simp lemma: for
`U` open, `]U[ = λ⁻¹(U)`, the image of `d(X|_U)`), `tube_spf_of_isClosed` (for `X = Spf A` and `Z =
V(ϖ, f_1, …, f_r)`: `]Z[ = ⋃_m {|f_i|^m ≤ |ϖ| for all i}`, independent of the `f_i` and of `ϖ`),
`tube_eq_interior_preimage` (for `Z` closed: `]Z[ = interior(λ⁻¹(Z))`), `isOpen_tube` (`]T[` is open
in `d(X)`), `tube_inter` (`]T ∩ T'[ = ]T[ ∩ ]T'[` and `]U ∩ Z[ = λ⁻¹(U) ∩ ]Z[`), `tube_preimage`
(for `f: Y → X` adic between admissible formal schemes: `d(f)⁻¹(]T[) = ]f⁻¹(T)[`),
`tube_classicalPoints` (the classical points of `]T[` are the classical `x` with `λ(x) ∈ T`; under
`r` they form Berthelot's admissible open `sp⁻¹(T)`) and `tube_blowUp` (for an admissible blow-up
`φ: X' → X`, `d(φ)` maps `]φ⁻¹(T)[` isomorphically onto `]T[`) (GK02 §2.3, p. 18, tubes of
immersions into the closed fibre are admissible opens of the rigid generic fibre; Conrad-AWS §3.3,
Ex. 3.3.13, p. 34, tubes as preimages under `sp` in rigid geometry; Conrad-MR Appendix A.1, before
the proof of Lem. A.1.4, p. 38, the tubes of a closed point and of its open complement do not form
an admissible covering). *Needs:* *specialisation-map*; *generic-fibre-functor-d*;
*admissible-formal-scheme*; *fractional-valuation-bound*; *rigid-adic-comparison-functor*,
*rigid-analytic-space* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R1); *affinoid-maximum-modulus* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R0); Tau Ceti
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset`.

The open–closed presentation is independent of all choices:
`tube_open_inter_closed X U Z hU hZ` identifies `tube X (U ∩ Z)` with
`λ⁻¹(U) ∩ tube X Z` whenever `U` is open and `Z` closed. Together with `tube_inter`,
this also identifies restrictions to formal affine opens. These identities and
`tube_of_isOpen`, `tube_eq_interior_preimage`, and `isOpen_tube` hold for every type-(S)
formal scheme (Huber96 §1.9, Prop. 1.9.1 and (1.9.3), pp. 96–98, followed by the
open–closed construction). The affine `tube_spf_of_isClosed` takes `IsAdic (Ideal.span {s})`
and finitely many equations whose common vanishing set is `Z`; this makes independence of
the equations and of `s` an equality with the same intrinsic left side.
`genericFibre.spfValuation A x` pulls the stalk valuation back through specialisation and
`Spf.globalSectionsIso A`, so the inequalities evaluate actual formal coefficients.
`closedTube_isCompact` asserts compactness for a type-(S) affine `Spf A`, a principal
ideal of definition `(s)`, finitely many equations, and `q > 0`.
`tube_eq_iUnion_closedTube` identifies their union with the tube of their common zero set.
The exponent convention is `|f|^q.den ≤ |s|^q.num.toNat`, with no fractional ring power
(Huber96 Prop. 1.9.1, affine construction, p. 97; rational domains and Conrad-AWS
Ex. 3.3.13, p. 34).

`tube_preimage` assumes that both formal schemes are admissible over the same complete
rank-one valuation ring and that the morphism is adic. `tube_blowUp` states both that the
actual generic-fibre map is an isomorphism and that it pulls back the target tube to the
source tube. Thus its restriction identifies these open adic subspaces, including their
sheaves (Conrad-AWS Ex. 3.3.11 and Exer. 3.3.12, pp. 33–34).
`tube_classicalPoints` uses finiteness of the stalk residue field along the structural
`K`-map obtained from `genericFibre.map` and a fixed identification
`d(Spf O_K) ≅ Spa(K,O_K)`. For an admissible `X`, `tube_rigid` additionally
states that an identification of its generic fibre with `rigidToAdic R` over `K` carries
the tube to `rigidToAdic.rho U`, where the classical point set of the admissible open `U`
is exactly `sp⁻¹(T)`. Neither comparison requires quasi-compactness
(Conrad-AWS Ex. 3.3.13, p. 34; Huber96 Ex. 1.9.2(ii), pp. 97–98).
`tube_eq_empty_iff` says that a closed subset of an admissible formal scheme has empty
tube exactly when it is empty, by the lifting of closed points on affine special fibres.

**Checks.**

- `genericFibre.spfValuation_zero` — zero has value zero at every generic-fibre point.
- `genericFibre.spfValuation_unit` — a unit of the formal affine ring has value one.
- `genericFibre.spfValuation_definitionIdeal` — a generator `s` of an ideal of definition
  has value strictly between zero and one, so it is neither a unit nor zero at such a point.
- `closedTube_zero` — the zero equation gives the whole generic fibre for every `q > 0`.
- `closedTube_unit` — the unit equation gives the empty open for every `q > 0`.
- `closedTube_half` — the exponent `1/2` gives `|f|² ≤ |s|`; its open is contained in
  the open for exponent `1/3`.
- `tube_test_origin_disc` (computation) — for `X = Spf O_K⟨T⟩` and `Z = {0} ⊆ A¹_k`, `tube X Z = ⋃_{m ≥ 1} {x : |T(x)|^m ≤ |ϖ|}`, the open unit disc.
- `tube_test_preimage_not_open` (non-example) — for `X = Spf O_K⟨T⟩` and `Z = {0}`, the point
  `η_{1⁻}` lies in `λ⁻¹(Z)` but not in `tube X Z`; so defining the adic tube as `λ⁻¹(Z)` gives a
  closed, non-open set. The witness has valuation-ring dimension two and
  `|T|^m > |ϖ|` for every positive `m`, as in Wedhorn Ex. 7.57(5), p. 72.
- `tube_test_classical` (compatibility) — the classical points of `tube X {0}` for `X = Spf O_K⟨T⟩`
  are the Galois orbits of `c ∈ K̄` with `|c| < 1`, i.e. Berthelot's `sp⁻¹(0)`.
  The Check proves the stronger membership criterion at every rank-one point;
  classical points have rank one (Wedhorn Ex. 7.57(1) and 7.58, pp. 71–72).
- `tube_test_open_complement` (characterisation) — for `X = Spf O_K⟨T⟩`: `tube X (A¹_k ∖ {0}) = {|T| = 1}`, and `tube X {0} ∪ tube X (A¹_k ∖ {0}) ≠ d(X)`: the union misses the point `η_{1⁻}`,
  matching the non-admissible rigid covering `{|t| = 1} ⊔ {|t| < 1}` of `{|t| ≤ 1}` (Conrad-MR
  Appendix A.1, before the proof of Lem. A.1.4).
- `tube_test_whole` (degenerate) — `tube X X_s = d(X)` and `tube X ∅ = ∅`; for admissible `X`,
  `tube X Z = ∅` for closed `Z` only when `Z = ∅`, every closed point of `Z` being `λ` of a
  classical point (*rig-point*).
- `tube_test_torsion_empty` (non-example) — for the non-admissible `X = Spf(O_K⟨T⟩/(ϖT))`

  point `Z = {T = 1} ⊆ X_s = A¹_k`: `λ⁻¹(Z) = ∅`, so `]Z[ = ∅` although `Z ≠ ∅`; the interior
  formula and the openness of `]Z[` survive, the surjectivity of `λ` onto closed points does not.
  `tube_test_torsion_empty_geometric` states the singleton generic fibre, the nonempty zero
  locus of `T − 1`, its empty preimage, and its empty tube on these formal-scheme carriers.
- `tube_test_closedTube_radius` (convention) — for `X = Spf O_K⟨T⟩`, `Z = {0}` and `q = 1/2`:

  point `T = c` with `|c| = |ϖ|^{1/3}` (available in `ℂ_p`) does not (`|ϖ|^{2/3} > |ϖ|`), and

**Rig-points of admissible formal schemes.** (*rig-point*) Let `X` be an admissible formal
`O_K`-scheme over a complete rank-one `O_K`. A rig-point of `X` is a morphism `u: T → X` of
admissible formal `O_K`-schemes that is a closed immersion, with `T = Spf B` affine and `B` a local
integral domain of dimension `1`; its residue field is `Frac(B)`. (Bosch–Lütkebohmert allow locally
closed immersions; over a complete rank-one valuation ring locally closed rig-points are closed.)
Properties: (BL I 3.2) `B` is finite over `O_K` and the integral closure of `B` in `Frac(B)` is the
valuation ring `O_{K'}` of the finite extension `K' = Frac(B)` of `K`; (BL I 3.3) for an admissible
blow-up `X' → X` the induced map on rig-points is bijective and preserves residue fields; (BL I 3.4)
for `X = Spf A` the rig-points correspond bijectively to primes `p ⊂ A` with `ϖ ∉ p` and `dim A/p =
1`, and to closed points of `Spec A[1/ϖ]`, i.e. to maximal ideals of the `K`-affinoid algebra `A_K`;
(BL I 3.5) every closed point of `X_s` is the special point of some rig-point — in the rank-one case
the existence applies [BGR 7.1.5/4], the lifting of closed points of the reduction to points of `Sp
A`, to the integral closure of `A` in `A ⊗ K`. Consequently rig-points of
`X` correspond bijectively to the classical points of `d(X)` (residue field finite over `K`); the
compatibility with the specialisation map `λ` (the special point of `u` is `λ` of the corresponding
classical point) is `RigPoint.specialPoint_eq_specialisation` of *specialisation-map*, which depends
on this target. Conrad's Lemma A.1.5: for `Y` flat and locally tfp over `Spf O_K`, every point `y:
Sp(K') → Y_rig` is `y_rig` for a unique closed immersion `Spf B → Y` with `B` a finite flat
`O_K`-domain, and every closed point of `Y_s` underlies such a map. In `FormalScheme`, define
`RigPoint` (isomorphism classes over `X` of closed immersions `Spf B → X` of admissible
formal `O_K`-schemes, where `B` is a finite flat `O_K`-algebra and a local domain of
dimension `1`), `RigPoint.residueField` (`Frac(B)`, a finite extension of `K`) and
`RigPoint.specialPoint` (the closed point of `X_s` underlying `u`). Prove
`RigPoint.integralClosure_eq_valuationRing` (the integral closure of `B` in `Frac(B)` is the
valuation ring of `Frac(B)`, and `B` is finite over `O_K`), `RigPoint.map` (a morphism `Y → X`
induces `rig-pts(Y) → rig-pts(X)`; residue fields may shrink), `RigPoint.equivOfBlowUp` (for an
admissible blow-up `X' → X`, `rig-pts(X') → rig-pts(X)` is a bijection preserving residue fields),
`RigPoint.equivMaxSpec` (for `X = Spf A`: rig-points ↔ primes `p` with `ϖ ∉ p` and `dim A/p = 1` ↔
maximal ideals of `A ⊗_{O_K} K`), `RigPoint.exists_of_isClosedPoint` (every closed point of `X_s` is
the special point of a rig-point) and `RigPoint.equivClassicalPoints` (rig-points of `X` ↔ classical
points of `d(X)`) (BL I §3, Def. 3.1(b), p. 303, the definition of rig-points; BL I §3, Lem. 3.3, p.
304, invariance under admissible blow-ups; BL I §3, Prop. 3.5, p. 305, every closed point of the
special fibre lifts; Conrad-MR Appendix A.1, Lem. A.1.5, p. 38, Conrad's formulation for flat
locally tfp formal schemes over non-discrete `R`). Rig-points of `Spf O_K⟨T⟩` correspond to Galois
orbits of `c ∈ K̄` with `|c| ≤ 1`; for `c ∈ O_K`, `u` is `Spf O_K → Spf O_K⟨T⟩`, `T ↦ c`. *Needs:*
*admissible-formal-scheme*; *topologically-finitely-presented-algebra*; *raynaud-generic-fibre*;
*admissible-blow-up*; *rigid-adic-comparison-functor* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R1); *affinoid-residue-fields-finite*
(AdicSpacesPartII layer R0); Mathlib `ValuationRing`, `integralClosure`.

The carrier `RigPoint O ϖ s` fixes the structural morphism `s : X → Spf O`.
Its sheaf kernel represents the isomorphism class of the closed immersion; the
presentation carries `Module.Finite O B`, `Module.Flat O B`, a domain structure,
and equality of the composite with `Spf` of the algebra map. The singleton support
defines `RigPoint.specialPoint`. The source is `Spf B`; normalization gives `O_L`
and need not give the same closed immersion. `RigPoint.integralClosure_eq_valuationRing`
identifies the residue field with `Frac(B)` as an `O`-algebra for every adic closed
presentation whose composite is admissible and whose kernel is the given ideal,
and asserts finiteness of `B` and the valuation-ring property of its normalization.
`RigPoint.integralClosure_eq_valuationRing_affine` states finiteness and the
valuation-ring property for an admissible one-dimensional local domain over the
complete rank-one base, without a chosen closed presentation into a formal scheme.
`RigPoint.residueField_finite` gives the finite map from `Frac(O)` for every rig-point
([FK] II, Prop. 8.2.5–8.2.6, pp. 550–553).

For an adic `f : Y → X` with both structural morphisms admissible,
`RigPoint.map_sections` specifies `RigPoint.map` by contraction of the ideal on every
open, and `RigPoint.map_specialPoint` sends the support by `f`. These are schematic
images, so the source algebra may change ([FK] II, Prop. 8.2.14, p. 555).
For an admissible blow-up with finitely generated open centre,
`RigPoint.equivOfBlowUp_apply` identifies the forward equivalence with this map;
`RigPoint.equivOfBlowUp_residueField` gives an `O`-algebra isomorphism of residue fields
(Conrad-AWS Ex. 3.3.11 and Exer. 3.3.12, pp. 33–34; [FK] II, Prop. 8.2.10, p. 554).
`RigPoint.exists_of_isClosedPoint` assumes admissibility and a closed singleton in
`X`, and produces a rig-point with that special point; it requires neither discreteness
of `O` nor quasi-compactness of `X`. This follows locally by finding a classical point
in the tube ([FK] II, Cor. 8.2.13, p. 555, and Cor. 8.2.18, p. 558).

For an admissible algebra `A` with its `ϖ`-adic topology and continuous structural
map, `RigPoint.equivMaxSpec` has the global carrier over `Spf A` as its source.
`RigPoint.equivMaxSpec_apply_asIdeal` says that contraction of the resulting maximal
ideal to `A`, then passage through `Spf.globalSectionsIso`, is the rig-point's ideal
of global sections. `RigPoint.equivMaxSpec_eq_affine` identifies it with
`RigPoint.equivMaxSpec_affine` on the corresponding prime, including its avoidance
of `ϖ` and one-dimensional quotient ([FK] II, Prop. 8.2.10 and Cor. 8.2.11, p. 554).

**Checks.**

- `rigPoint_test_disc` (computation) — for `c ∈ O_K`, the `O_K`-algebra map `O_K⟨T⟩ → O_K`, `T ↦ c`,
  defines a rig-point of `Spf O_K⟨T⟩` with residue field `K` whose special point is `T = c̄` and
  whose classical point is `T = c`.
- `rigPoint_test_notDim1` (non-example) — the closed immersion `Spec k → Spf O_K⟨T⟩` at `T = 0` is
  not a rig-point: `k` is a field (dimension `0`) and `Spec k` is not admissible (it is
  `ϖ`-torsion).
- `rigPoint_test_blowUp` (compatibility) — for the admissible blow-up `X'` of `(T, ϖ)` on `Spf
  O_K⟨T⟩`, the rig-point `T = 0` lifts uniquely to `X'`, into the chart `Spf O_K⟨T, U⟩/(T − ϖU)` at
  `U = 0`, with the same residue field `K`.
  The chart uses the equivalent ring `O_K⟨U⟩`: its open immersion has bijective
  stalk maps and pulls `T` back to `ϖU`; the lifted ideal is the kernel of evaluation at `U = 0`.
- `rigPoint_test_base` (degenerate) — the only rig-point of `Spf O_K` is the identity, with `B =
  O_K`, zero sheaf kernel and residue field `K` ([FK] II, Prop. 8.2.10 and Cor. 8.2.11, p. 554).

**Checks for the global interfaces.**

- `RigPoint.residueField_base`: the identity rig-point has field `Frac(O)` as an `O`-algebra.
- `RigPoint.residueField_affine`: on `Spf A` the field is the quotient by the corresponding
  maximal ideal of `A[1/ϖ]`.
- `RigPoint.residueField_blowUp`: the inverse blow-up correspondence preserves this `O`-field.
- `RigPoint.map_identity`: the identity preserves the sheaf ideal.
- `RigPoint.map_empty`: a map from an empty formal scheme has empty image on rig-points.
- `RigPoint.map_special`: the special point is sent by the underlying formal morphism.
- `RigPoint.equivMaxSpec_base`: every rig-point of `Spf O` maps to the zero maximal ideal of `K`.
- `RigPoint.equivMaxSpec_empty`: the zero algebra has neither rig-points nor maximal ideals
  after inverting `ϖ`.
- `RigPoint.equivMaxSpec_contract`: the inverse equivalence contracts the maximal ideal
  to the formal ideal of global sections.
- `RigPoint.equivOfBlowUp_unit`: the unit centre gives an isomorphism of formal schemes,
  and its point map agrees with the equivalence on special points.
- `RigPoint.equivOfBlowUp_empty`: blowing up the empty formal scheme yields no rig-points.
- `RigPoint.equivOfBlowUp_special`: projecting the special point of the unique lift recovers
  the original special point.

The affine correspondence is specified by `RigPoint.equivMaxSpec_affine_apply_asIdeal`:
its forward map extends ideals along localisation, and its inverse contracts ideals.

**Affine Checks.**

- `rigPoint_test_base_core` — the sole prime of `O_K` avoiding `ϖ` is `(0)`, which maps to
  `(0)` in the fraction field.
- `rigPoint_test_torsion_core` — `FormalScheme.RigPoint O ϖ s` is empty whenever
  the structural section `sectionsHom X O s ϖ` is zero. This applies to `Spf(O_K/ϖ)`;
  the accompanying prime calculation explains the affine obstruction.
- `rigPoint_test_contract_core` — the inverse sends a maximal ideal `Q` of `A[1/ϖ]` to
  `Q ∩ A`.

### R2.5 admissible blow-ups and Raynaud's theorem

**Admissible formal blow-ups and strict transforms.** (*admissible-blow-up*) Let `X` be an
admissible formal `O_K`-scheme and `𝒜 ⊆ O_X` a coherent open ideal (coherent, and locally `ϖ^N O_X ⊆
𝒜` for some `N`; a single `N` when `X` is quasi-compact); a non-open centre changes the generic
fibre. The admissible blow-up of `𝒜` is `X' := lim_m Proj(⊕_{n≥0} 𝒜ⁿ ⊗_{O_X} O_X/ϖ^{m+1})` with its
projection `φ: X' → X`. (a) Over a formal affine open `Spf A` with `𝒜 ↔ a = (f_0, …, f_r) ∋ ϖ^N`,
`φ⁻¹(Spf A)` is the `ϖ`-adic completion of the scheme-theoretic blow-up of `a` on `Spec A`, covered
by the charts `Spf A'_i` with `A'_i = A⟨ζ_j : j ≠ i⟩/(f_iζ_j − f_j)_{j≠i}` modulo its `ϖ`-power
torsion (which equals its `f_i`-power torsion: `f_i` divides `ϖ^N` on the chart, so `f_i`-power
torsion is `ϖ`-power torsion, and the quotient by the `f_i`-power torsion is the completed scheme
chart, `ϖ`-torsion-free because `X` is), `Spf A'_i` being the locus where `f_i` generates `𝒜O_{X'}`.
(b) `X'` is admissible and `𝒜O_{X'}` is invertible. (c) Universal property: every adic morphism `ψ: Z →
X` of formal `O_K`-schemes (`Z` not necessarily admissible) with `𝒜O_Z` invertible factors uniquely
through `φ`. Further: `φ` is an isomorphism over `X ∖ V(𝒜)`; formation commutes with flat base
change and, in the admissible category, with arbitrary base change (strict transform); `φ` is proper
and surjective on special fibres; blowing up `𝒜` and then `ℬO_{X'}` is blowing up `𝒜ℬ`; for `X`
quasi-compact and quasi-separated a composite of admissible blow-ups is an admissible blow-up (BL I §2, 2.5, which uses
RG §5.1, Lem. 5.1.4 and EGA I_new 6.9.9), blow-ups of finitely many quasi-compact opens extend to `X` and are
dominated by one admissible blow-up of `X` (BL I §2, 2.6, which uses EGA I_new 6.9.7), and any two
admissible blow-ups of `X` are dominated by a third, so admissible blow-ups of `X` form a cofiltered
system. The strict transform of a coherent `O_X`-module `ℳ` is `ℳ' = φ*ℳ/𝒩`, where `𝒩` is the
`𝒜O_{X'}`-power torsion of `φ*ℳ` (sections killed locally by a power of `𝒜O_{X'}`; the
scheme-theoretic "sections supported in `φ⁻¹(V(𝒜))`" of Raynaud–Gruson 5.1.1, `V(𝒜)` being read
scheme-theoretically since the underlying space of `X'` is its special fibre); `𝒩` lies in the
`ϖ`-power torsion, and if `ℳ'` has no `ϖ`-torsion, `𝒩` is the `ϖ`-power torsion of `φ*ℳ`, which is
coherent (BL I §1, Lem. 1.4(c)). The scheme-theoretic charts of the blow-up are Tau Ceti's
`affineBlowupι` and `iSup_opensRange_affineBlowupι`, and the chart algebra `A[ζ_j : j ≠ i]/(f_iζ_j
− f_j)` modulo `f_i`-power torsion of (a) is the chart of *submodule-blow-up* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R0) at `C = B
= A` for the ideal `a`; this target forms the `ϖ`-adic completion of that chart and removes
`ϖ`-torsion. Strict transforms along blow-ups and modifications of schemes are
SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 4 (§4.11; §4.12, `modification_domination`); the strict
transform here is taken on `ϖ`-adic formal schemes, with the `𝒜O_{X'}`-power torsion in place of
the sections supported on the exceptional locus. In `FormalScheme`, define `admissibleBlowUp` (`X' = Bl_𝒜 X` for a coherent open
ideal `𝒜`), `admissibleBlowUp.π` (`φ: Bl_𝒜 X → X`), `admissibleBlowUp.chart` (over `Spf A` with `𝒜 =
(f_0, …, f_r)`: the open `Spf(A⟨ζ⟩/(f_iζ_j − f_j)/ϖ-power torsion)` where `f_i` generates, with
`ϖ`-power torsion = `f_i`-power torsion), `strictTransform` (for a coherent `ℳ`: `ℳ' = φ*ℳ / (𝒜O_{X'}-power torsion of φ*ℳ)`; when `ℳ'` has no `ϖ`-torsion this is `φ*ℳ` modulo its `ϖ`-power
torsion, a coherent `O_{X'}`-module) and `strictTransformBaseChange` (for `f: X → T` locally of tf
presentation, a coherent `O_X`-module `ℳ` and the admissible blow-up `φ: T' → T` of a coherent open
ideal `𝒜`: `ℳ' = ℳ_{X'}/(sections of ℳ_{X'} supported over V(𝒜), i.e. killed by a power of 𝒜O_{X'})`
on `X' = X ×_T T'` (RG §5.1, Déf. 5.1.1(ii)); this torsion lies in the `ϖ`-power torsion, and for `ℳ
= O_X` it defines the strict transform of `X`, a closed formal subscheme of `X ×_T T'`). Prove
`admissibleBlowUp.isAdmissible` (an instance: `Bl_𝒜 X` is admissible),
`admissibleBlowUp.isInvertible` (`𝒜O_{Bl_𝒜 X}` is an invertible ideal sheaf),
`admissibleBlowUp.lift` (`ψ: Z → X` with `𝒜O_Z` invertible lifts to `Z → Bl_𝒜 X`),
`admissibleBlowUp.lift_comp_π` (`π ∘ lift ψ = ψ`; the lift is unique),
`admissibleBlowUp.isIso_of_disjoint` (`φ` is an isomorphism over `X ∖ V(𝒜)`),
`admissibleBlowUp.baseChange` (for `Y → X` in the admissible category, the strict transform of `Y`
is `Bl_{𝒜O_Y} Y` (BL I §2, Rem. 2.3)), `admissibleBlowUp.isProper_surjective_specialFibre` (`φ` is
proper, and surjective on special fibres), `admissibleBlowUp.mul` (`Bl_{ℬO_{X'}}(Bl_𝒜 X) ≅ Bl_{𝒜ℬ} X` over `X`), `admissibleBlowUp.comp` (for `X` quasi-compact and quasi-separated, a composite of admissible blow-ups is
an admissible blow-up), `admissibleBlowUp.extend` (for `X` quasi-compact and quasi-separated and admissible blow-ups of
finitely many quasi-compact opens `U_i`, there is one admissible blow-up of `X` restricting to blow-ups dominating
each), `admissibleBlowUp.dominate` (any two admissible blow-ups of `X` are dominated by the blow-up
of the product ideal), `strictTransformBaseChange_comp` (for admissible blow-ups `T'' → T' → T`
obtained by completing scheme blow-ups with centres outside a schematically dense open
`U ⊆ Spec A` on an affine chart `T = Spf A`, the iterated strict transform agrees with the
strict transform of the composite: compute sections vanishing over the preimage of `U`
on the scheme charts before completion (RG §5.3, Rem. 5.3.2). Here `U` is an open of
`Spec A`, not of `Spf A`; the ideal of definition `(ϖ)` has empty complement in `Spf A`; a general open centre can have a nonempty complement)) and `admissibleBlowUp.comp_of_disjoint` (for `X` quasi-compact and quasi-separated, an open `U ⊆ X` and
admissible blow-ups `X' → X` with centre disjoint from `U` and `X'' → X'` with centre disjoint from
the preimage of `U`, the composite is an admissible blow-up with centre disjoint from `U` (RG §5.1,
Lem. 5.1.4, "`U`-admissible")) (BL I §2, p. 298, the definition of the admissible formal blow-up; BL
I §2, Prop. 2.1(c), p. 299, the universal property; BL I §2, Lem. 2.2, p. 299, the chart
description; BL I §2, Rem. 2.4(c), p. 301, properness and surjectivity on special fibres; Conrad-AWS
§3.3, Ex. 3.3.11, p. 33, the chart construction by the `f_i`-torsion quotients and `ϖ`-adic
completion; RG Première partie, §5.1, Déf. 5.1.1(ii), p. 35, the strict transform of a module; RG
Première partie, §5.1, Lem. 5.1.4, p. 36, composition of `U`-admissible blow-ups; RG Première
partie, §5.3, Rem. 5.3.2, p. 38, strict transforms as quotients by sections vanishing over `U`).
*Needs:* *admissible-formal-scheme*; *tfp-algebra-coherent*; *flat-tft-is-tfp*;
*saturated-submodule-finitely-generated*; *tfp-locality*; *colimit-of-thickenings*,
*formal-scheme-gluing*, *morphisms-as-compatible-systems-finite-ideal-type* (layer F0);
*submodule-blow-up* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R0); Tau Ceti `affineBlowupι`, `iSup_opensRange_affineBlowupι`; Mathlib
`reesAlgebra`, `AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper`.

The carrier is `AdmissibleBlowup O ϖ s J`: the construction and projection
called `admissibleBlowUp` and `admissibleBlowUp.π` above are its representing object
and `projection`. The API uses the namespace `AdmissibleBlowup`.
`AdmissibleBlowup.isAdmissible` and `AdmissibleBlowup.isInvertible` expose its
admissible source and invertible extended centre. Except for these carrier properties,
geometric results assume `IsAdmissible ϖ s` and `IsAdmissibleCentre O ϖ s J`.
`AdmissibleBlowup.lift` accepts an adic `f : Z → X` with invertible extended centre,
including non-admissible `Z`; `AdmissibleBlowup.lift_comp_π` specifies the factorization
and uniqueness ([FK] II, Prop. 1.1.4, pp. 435–436).

`AdmissibleBlowup.chart` supplies an affine open cover for a finite generating family
on `Spf A`, where `A` is an admissible `O`-algebra with its `ϖ`-adic topology.
Each chart's coefficient homomorphism has kernel equal both to the `ϖ`-saturation
and to the chosen generator's saturation of the relation ideal. A redundant variable
`Z_i` is set to one, so the presentation has the same meaning for a singleton family.
`AdmissibleBlowup.scheme` identifies the whole blow-up with `idealCompletion` of
Part II's `submoduleBlowup` and fixes the identification on coefficients
([FK] II, §1.1(b), pp. 433–435; Conrad-AWS Ex. 3.3.11, p. 33).

`AdmissibleBlowup.isIso_of_disjoint` takes an actual pullback over `X|U` and assumes
`J` extends to the unit ideal there. `AdmissibleBlowup.baseChange` identifies the
blow-up of the extended centre on an admissible `Y → X` with a closed formal
subspace of the given fibre product: its ideal is exactly the sections locally
annihilated by powers of the centre. It also identifies this space, over `Y`, with
`admissiblePullback`; when `f` is flat on stalks, the closed inclusion is an
isomorphism onto the ordinary formal fibre product.
`AdmissibleBlowup.isProper_surjective_specialFibre`
states surjectivity on formal points and properness of every reduction for any
compatible finite ideals of definition with source ideal equal to the extended target
ideal. This expresses adic properness without a noetherian assumption; formal points
and special-fibre points have the same underlying space ([FK] II, Prop. 1.1.4(1),
p. 435, Prop. 1.1.8, p. 437, and Prop. 1.2.9, p. 442; BL I, Rem. 2.4(c), p. 301).

`IdealSheafData.mul` is the sheaf ideal generated by products of local sections.
`AdmissibleBlowup.mul` gives an isomorphism over `X` for the two successive centres
`J` and the extension of `L`. `AdmissibleBlowup.dominate` supplies maps from the
product-centre blow-up to both given blow-ups, commuting with the projections.
For quasi-compact, quasi-separated `X`, `AdmissibleBlowup.comp` also supplies an
integer `n > 0` and an admissible ideal `K` downstairs whose extension is
`L · (J O_{X'})^n`; the composite is the blow-up of `J · K`.
`AdmissibleBlowup.comp_of_disjoint` retains a specified open on which both centres
are unit ideals. `AdmissibleBlowup.extend` gives one global blow-up dominating a
finite family on quasi-compact opens of such an `X`, including the empty family
([FK] II, Props. 1.1.8–1.1.10, pp. 437–439, and Prop. 1.3.1, p. 443;
RG I, Lem. 5.1.4, p. 36; [FK] II, Exercise 1.1, p. 444, for the product formula).

`strictTransform` and `strictTransformBaseChange` return `IdealTorsionQuotient`
data, including the quotient map and its local kernel, on the blow-up and on a
specified formal fibre product respectively. For a finitely presented input on an
admissible base, `strictTransform_coherent` gives finite presentation when the
quotient is `ϖ`-torsion-free on every open. `strictTransformBaseChange_coherent`
gives the relative version when the formal fibre product is locally topologically
finitely presented over `O`. `strictTransformBaseChange_comp` compares
the iterated and composite quotients of a finitely presented module on a locally
topologically finitely presented source, using a pair of Cartesian squares over an
admissible base and three admissible centres. Its composite blow-up is identified over the original base, and positive powers of the extended
composite centre and the product of the successive centres are required to contain
one another. These conditions express equality of their radicals and fix the common
scheme-theoretic open used for the strict transforms. In particular they apply to
the centre supplied by `AdmissibleBlowup.comp`; arbitrary choices of a centre
presenting the same morphism are not interchangeable for module strict transforms
([FK] II, Def. 1.2.1 and Props. 1.2.7, 1.2.11, pp. 440–443;
RG I, Rem. 5.3.2, p. 38).

**Checks for the operations.**

- `IdealSheafData.mul_unit`: multiplication by the unit ideal fixes the ideal.
- `IdealSheafData.mul_zero`: multiplication by zero gives zero.
- `IdealSheafData.mul_square`: multiplying an ideal by itself agrees with its second power.
- `AdmissibleBlowup.lift_projection`: lifting the blow-up projection gives the identity.
- `AdmissibleBlowup.lift_unit`: the unit-centre lift factors through an isomorphism.
- `AdmissibleBlowup.lift_empty`: every map from the empty formal scheme is the unique lift.
- `strictTransform_unit`: the quotient map for a unit centre is invertible.
- `strictTransform_zero`: the zero module has zero strict transform.
- `strictTransform_annihilated`: a module annihilated by a power of the centre has zero transform.
- `strictTransformBaseChange_unit`: a unit centre removes no sections after base change.
- `strictTransformBaseChange_zero`: base change and strict transform preserve the zero module.
- `strictTransformBaseChange_annihilated`: a module killed by a power of the extended centre
  has zero relative strict transform.

**Checks.**

- `admissibleBlowUp_test_disc_origin` (computation) — for `X = Spf O_K⟨T⟩` and `𝒜 = (T, ϖ)`: `X'` is
  covered by `Spf O_K⟨U⟩` (`T = ϖU`) and `Spf O_K⟨T,V⟩/(TV − ϖ)`, and `X'_s` is the union of `P¹_k`
  (exceptional) and `A¹_k` (strict transform of `X_s`) meeting in one point.
- `admissibleBlowUp_test_unit` (degenerate) — for `𝒜 = O_X` or `𝒜 = ϖ^n O_X` (an invertible open
  ideal), `φ: X' → X` is an isomorphism; for `𝒜 = ϖ^n O_X` with `n > 0` the locus `X ∖ V(𝒜)` of
  `isIso_of_disjoint` is empty, so that statement is vacuous there and the isomorphism comes from
  invertibility.
- `admissibleBlowUp_test_zeroIdeal` (non-example) — on nonempty admissible `X` the zero ideal is coherent but
  not open (`ϖ^N ∉ 0`), so it is not an admissible centre; the scheme blow-up of `0`, `Proj` of
  `⊕_n 0^n = O_X` concentrated in degree `0`, is empty, and `d(∅) = ∅ ≠ d(X)`: openness of the
  centre is what makes *generic-fibre-inverts-admissible-blow-ups* possible. On `X = ∅`, `0 = O_X`
  is open and the blow-up is `∅`.
- `admissibleBlowUp_test_torsion_zeroIdeal` (negative control) — `A = O_K/(ϖ)` is nonzero
  and topologically finitely presented, but `ϖ = 0` in `A` and its topology is discrete.
  Thus its zero ideal is open. Admissibility is essential in the preceding check.
- `admissibleBlowUp_test_torsion_notSurjective` (non-example) — for the non-admissible `X =
  Spf(O_K⟨T⟩/(ϖT))`, completion of the scheme blow-up of `(ϖ)` gives `Spf O_K → X`.
  This computation uses the scheme blow-up, outside the admissible-domain definition above (the
  blow-up of a principal ideal is the quotient by its power torsion), not surjective on special
  fibres (`A¹_k` receives only the origin): the surjectivity in `isProper_surjective_specialFibre`
  uses that `X` is admissible, through *rig-point* lifting the closed points of `X_s`.
- `admissibleBlowUp_test_nonOpenCentre` (non-example) — blowing up the non-open ideal `(S, T)` of
  `Spf O_K⟨S,T⟩` (the formal completion of the scheme blow-up of the origin) changes the generic
  fibre: it produces the blow-up of the origin in the closed bidisc, which is not isomorphic to the
  bidisc; so the openness condition in the definition is necessary for
  *generic-fibre-inverts-admissible-blow-ups*.
- `admissibleBlowUp_test_universal` (characterisation) — for `𝒜 = (T, ϖ)` on `Spf O_K⟨T⟩` and `ψ:
  Spf O_K → Spf O_K⟨T⟩`, `T ↦ ϖ²`, the ideal `ψ*𝒜 = (ϖ)` is invertible and `ψ` lifts uniquely to
  `X'`, into the chart `U = T/ϖ` with `U ↦ ϖ`.
- `admissibleBlowUp_test_scheme` (compatibility) — for `X = Spf A` and `a = (ϖ, f)`, `φ⁻¹(X)` is the
  `ϖ`-adic completion of the `Proj` of the Rees algebra `reesAlgebra a` over `Spec A`, modulo
  `ϖ`-torsion.
- `strictTransform_test_annulus` (computation) — for `X = Spf O_K⟨ζ, ξ⟩/(ζξ − ϖ) → T = Spf O_K⟨ζ⟩`
  and `𝒜 = (ζ, ϖ)`: on the chart `ζ = ϖu` of `T'` the pull-back of `O_X` is `O_K⟨u, ξ⟩/(ϖ(uξ − 1))`,
  and its strict transform is `O_K⟨u, ξ⟩/(uξ − 1) ≅ O_K⟨u, u⁻¹⟩`.

**The generic fibre of an admissible blow-up is an isomorphism.**
(*generic-fibre-inverts-admissible-blow-ups*) Let `X` be an admissible formal `O_K`-scheme, `𝒜` a
coherent open ideal (`ϖ^N ∈ 𝒜`) and `φ: X' → X` its admissible blow-up (*admissible-blow-up*). Prove
that `d(φ): d(X') → d(X)` is an isomorphism of adic spaces (equivalently `φ_rig` is an isomorphism
of rigid spaces): over `Spf A` with `𝒜 = (f_0, …, f_r)`, the `f_i` generate the unit ideal of `A_K`,
the chart `Spf A'_i` has generic fibre the rational subset `R(f_0, …, f_r / f_i)` of `Spa(A_K,
A_K°)` (the locus where `|f_i|` is maximal), and these rational subsets cover `Spa(A_K, A_K°)` (BL I
§4, proof of Thm 4.1(a), p. 307, the charts of the blow-up give the rational covering; Conrad-AWS
§3.3, Ex. 3.3.11, p. 33, the statement for affine admissible formal schemes). For `𝒜 = (T, ϖ)` on
`Spf O_K⟨T⟩` the charts have generic fibres `{|T| ≤ |ϖ|}` and `{|ϖ| ≤ |T| ≤ 1}`, which cover the
closed unit disc (Conrad-AWS §3.3, Exercise 3.3.12). *Needs:* *admissible-blow-up*;
*generic-fibre-functor-d*; *raynaud-generic-fibre*; Tau Ceti
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spa_eq_biUnion_rationalSubset_of_span_eq_top`,
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spaLocalizationHomeomorph`, `TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset`.

**Adjoining power-bounded functions to an admissible algebra is an admissible blow-up.**
(*bounded-functions-blow-up*) Let `A` be an admissible `O_K`-algebra and `f_1, …, f_n ∈ A_K = A ⊗_{O_K} K` power-bounded in the affinoid algebra `A_K`, i.e. `|f_i|_sup ≤ 1`, `f_i ∈ A_K°`. Prove
that `B = A[f_1, …, f_n] ⊆ A_K` is an admissible `O_K`-algebra, finite over `A`, with `B_K = A_K`;
and that if `r ∈ ℕ` satisfies `ϖ^r f_i ∈ A` for all `i`, then `Spf B → Spf A` is the admissible
blow-up of the coherent open ideal `(ϖ^r, ϖ^r f_1, …, ϖ^r f_n)` (BL I §4, Lem. 4.5, p. 309). The
proof uses [BGR 6.3.4/1]: `A_K°` is integral over the image of `O_K⟨ξ⟩` for any presentation
(*affinoid-power-bounded-integral* (RigidAnalyticGeometry §2.3, presentation-ring integrality)). For residue characteristic `p ≠ 2` and `A =
O_K[X]/(X² − ϖ²)`: `f = X/ϖ ∈ A_K° ∖ A`, `B = A[f] = O_K(1, 1) + O_K(1, −1) = O_K × O_K` (as `2`
is a unit), and `Spf B → Spf A` is the admissible blow-up of `(ϖ, X)` (`r = 1`). Here `p ≠ 2` is
load-bearing for the identification of `B`, not for the blow-up: for `K = ℚ_2`, `ϖ = 2`, `A =
ℤ_2[X]/(X² − 4)` and `f = X/2 ↦ (1, −1)`, `B = A[f] = {(x, y) ∈ ℤ_2² : x ≡ y mod 2}` is a proper
subring of the integral closure `ℤ_2 × ℤ_2` (`(1, 0)` is integral over `B` and not in `B`), while
`Spf B → Spf A` is still the admissible blow-up of `(2, X)` and `B_K = A_K = ℚ_2 × ℚ_2`.

**Hypothesis check.** `boundedFunctions_test_residueChar2` computes that
`(1,0)` is absent from the `ℤ₂`-subalgebra generated by `(1,−1)`.
It tests the invertibility-of-two requirement in the split-product identification.
The geometric blow-up Checks below use `boundedFunctions_eq_blowupChart`.

More generally, `FormalScheme.boundedFunctions_eq_blowupChart` takes any finite family
`f_i ∈ A[1/ϖ]`, an integer `N ≥ 0`, and numerators `g_i ∈ A` with `g_i = ϖ^N f_i`.
Here `O_K` is a complete rank-one valuation ring, `A` is admissible with its `ϖ`-adic
topology, and the structural map is continuous. The coherent ideal sheaf `J` has affine
sections `(ϖ^N, g_1, …, g_n)`. The theorem asserts that this is an admissible centre and,
for every `AdmissibleBlowup` at `J`, identifies its distinguished affine open `U` where
`ϖ^N` generates the extended centre. This is the corresponding `AdmissibleBlowup.chart`,
with the redundant variable eliminated: its ring is
`A⟨Z_1,…,Z_n⟩/(ϖ^N Z_i − g_i : i)`, modulo `ϖ`-power torsion. The continuous quotient
map agrees with the blow-up projection on coefficients. Under the generic-fibre
isomorphism of the blow-up, `d(U)` is exactly `{|g_i| ≤ |ϖ|^N for all i}`, equivalently
`{|f_i| ≤ 1 for all i}`. Here `d(U)` is the preimage of `U` under specialisation;
`genericFibre_ofIsOpenImmersion` identifies it as an open adic subspace, including its
sheaf. If all `f_i` are power-bounded on `A[1/ϖ]`, the same theorem gives `U = ⊤` and a
coefficient-compatible topological ring isomorphism `A[f_1,…,f_n] ≃ Γ(U,O)`, where the
adjoin has its `ϖ`-adic topology. Thus its formal spectrum is the whole blow-up.
The ring is finite and admissible by the first clause of *bounded-functions-blow-up* (admissibility
of `A[f_1, …, f_n]` for power-bounded `f_i`)
(Fujiwara–Kato II, Proposition 1.1.3, pp. 434–435; Conrad-AWS §3.3, Example 3.3.11 and
Exercise 3.3.12, pp. 33–34; BL I §4, Lemma 4.5, p. 309 for the power-bounded case).

**Checks.**

- `boundedFunctions_eq_blowupChart_empty` — an empty family imposes no inequalities,
  for every `N`; its bounded locus is the entire generic fibre.
- `boundedFunctions_eq_blowupChart_integral` — with `N = 0`, every numerator in `A`
  has value at most one, so the distinguished chart has the whole generic fibre.
- `boundedFunctions_eq_blowupChart_inverse` — the single function `ϖ⁻¹`, with numerator
  `1` and `N = 1`, gives the empty locus since `1 > |ϖ|`; the distinguished chart of
  this unit-centre blow-up is empty, even though the blow-up itself is the identity.

*Needs:* *admissible-blow-up*; *topologically-finitely-presented-algebra*; *raynaud-generic-fibre*;
*affinoid-power-bounded-integral* (RigidAnalyticGeometry §2.3, presentation-ring integrality); Tau Ceti `TauCeti.Huber.powerBoundedSubring`; Mathlib
`integralClosure`.

**Quasi-compact opens of the generic fibre come from open formal subschemes of an admissible
blow-up.** (*quasi-compact-opens-from-blow-ups*) Let `X` be a quasi-compact admissible formal
`O_K`-scheme and `(U_i)_{i∈I}` a finite family of quasi-compact open subsets of the adic space
