§4, Lem. 4.4, p. 308; Conrad-AWS §3.3, p. 34, the same statement in Conrad's summary). For instance
`U = {|T| ≥ |ϖ|} ⊆ d(Spf O_K⟨T⟩)` is `d` of the chart `Spf O_K⟨T,V⟩/(TV − ϖ)` of the blow-up of `(T, ϖ)`; by contrast the open unit disc `⋃_{m≥1}{|T|^m ≤ |ϖ|}` is not quasi-compact and is `d` of no open formal
subscheme of any admissible blow-up. *Needs:* *admissible-blow-up*;
*generic-fibre-inverts-admissible-blow-ups*; *rig-point*; *specialisation-map*; Tau Ceti
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset`, `TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset_inter`.

**Every affinoid has an admissible formal model.** (*affinoid-admissible-model*) Let `B = K⟨ξ_1, …,
ξ_n⟩/b` be a `K`-affinoid algebra, a quotient of a Tate algebra `K⟨ξ⟩` with `K` complete of rank
one. Prove that `A := O_K⟨ξ⟩/(b ∩ O_K⟨ξ⟩)` is an admissible `O_K`-algebra with `A_K = B`, that the
map `A → B` is injective, and that `d(Spf A) = Spa(B, B°)`; in particular every affinoid adic space
`Spa(B, B°)` of finite type over `Spa(K, O_K)` is the generic fibre of an affine admissible formal
scheme (BL I §4, after Thm 4.1, p. 306, the affinoid case of the existence of formal models;
Conrad-AWS §3.3, Exercise 3.3.3, p. 31). For `B = K⟨ξ⟩/(ξ² − c)` with `c ∈ K`, `|c| ≤ 1`, the model
is `A = O_K⟨ξ⟩/(ξ² − c)`: the ideal `(ξ² − c)O_K⟨ξ⟩` is saturated because `O_K⟨ξ⟩/(ξ² − c) =
O_K[ξ]/(ξ² − c)` is free of rank `2` over `O_K`. For `|c| > 1` the ideal `b` is generated by the
unit `1 − c⁻¹ξ²` of `K⟨ξ⟩`, which is also a unit of `O_K⟨ξ⟩`, so `B = 0`, `b ∩ O_K⟨ξ⟩ = O_K⟨ξ⟩` and
`A = 0`: the empty affinoid has the empty formal model, and `A → B` is injective. *Needs:*
*saturated-submodule-finitely-generated*; *topologically-finitely-presented-algebra*;
*raynaud-generic-fibre*.

**Raynaud's theorem: quasi-compact admissible formal schemes localised at admissible blow-ups are
quasi-compact quasi-separated rigid spaces.** (*raynaud-theorem*) Let `K` be complete with
nontrivial rank-one valuation (not necessarily discrete; `O_K` may be non-noetherian). Prove that
the functor `X ↦ X_rig` from quasi-compact admissible formal `O_K`-schemes to rigid `K`-spaces sends
admissible blow-ups to isomorphisms and induces an equivalence between (1) the category of
quasi-compact admissible formal `O_K`-schemes (quasi-separated automatically, their underlying
spaces being noetherian) localised by admissible blow-ups and (2) the category
of quasi-compact quasi-separated rigid `K`-spaces (BL I §4, Thm 4.1, p. 306, Raynaud's theorem as
stated by Bosch–Lütkebohmert; Conrad-AWS §3.3, p. 34, the same statement with no discreteness
assumption). Composing with *raynaud-generic-fibre* and Huber's equivalence `r` between
quasi-separated rigid `K`-spaces and quasi-separated adic spaces locally of finite type over `Spa(K,
O_K)` (*rigid-adic-comparison-functor* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R1)), `X ↦ d(X)` induces an equivalence between (1)
and the category of quasi-compact quasi-separated adic spaces locally of finite type over `Spa(K,
O_K)` (Hübner §8, Thm 8.8, p. 39, the adic formulation; Hübner §8, before Thm 8.8, p. 39, the role
of admissible blow-ups). Concretely: (a) admissible blow-ups become isomorphisms; (b) morphisms `φ,
ψ: Y → X` with `φ_rig = ψ_rig` are equal — this uses that `Y` has no `ϖ`-torsion: `S ↦ 0` and `S
↦ T` from `Spf(O_K⟨T⟩/(ϖT))` to `Spf O_K⟨S⟩` differ, but both have generic fibre the point `S = 0`
of the closed disc, since `T ↦ 0` in `K`; (c) for quasi-compact `X`, `Y` and any morphism `g: Y_rig
→ X_rig` there are an admissible blow-up `Y' → Y` and a morphism `φ: Y' → X` inducing `g`; (d) if
`g` is an isomorphism, `φ` can be chosen to be an admissible blow-up of `X` as well; (e) every
quasi-compact quasi-separated rigid `K`-space (resp. adic space as above) has a quasi-compact
admissible formal model. Morphisms in the localised category are `Hom(X, Y) = colim` over admissible
blow-ups `X' → X` of `Hom(X', Y)` (calculus of fractions, BL I §5). Quasi-compactness of formal
models and quasi-compactness plus quasi-separatedness of rigid spaces are necessary: `X ↦ X_rig`
produces only quasi-separated spaces, and the open unit disc, which is quasi-separated but not
quasi-compact, has no quasi-compact admissible formal model. For instance the closed annulus `{|ϖ| ≤
|T| ≤ 1}` (qcqs) has the formal model `Spf O_K⟨T, V⟩/(TV − ϖ)`; the closed disc has models `Spf
O_K⟨T⟩` and its blow-up at `(T, ϖ)`, which become isomorphic in the localised category; the rigid
projective line has formal models `P̂¹_{O_K}` and all its admissible blow-ups, and morphisms between
rigid projective lines of degree `d` are realised on suitable blow-ups. *Needs:*
*generic-fibre-inverts-admissible-blow-ups*; *rig-point*; *quasi-compact-opens-from-blow-ups*;
*bounded-functions-blow-up*; *affinoid-admissible-model*; *admissible-blow-up*;
*raynaud-generic-fibre*; *rigid-adic-comparison-functor*, *rigid-analytic-space*,
*rigid-adic-quasi-separated-equivalence* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R1).

`FormalScheme.AdmissibleFormal O ϖ` is the full subcategory of
`Over (ofSpf O)` satisfying `IsAdmissible ϖ X.hom ∧ CompactSpace X.left`.
The standing assumptions are that `O` is a valuation domain with its complete
rank-one `ϖ`-adic topology (`Huber.IsCompleteRankOneBase O ϖ`). Its objects
are of type (S), by `IsTypeS.of_isLocallyTFP`. For a complete nontrivially
normed nonarchimedean field `K`, `genericFibre_baseIso_exists` supplies an
isomorphism `β : genericFibre (ofSpf O) ≅ (fieldAffinoid K).spa` whenever a
ring isomorphism `O ≃+* K°` is a homeomorphism. Fix such a base identification;
`rigFunctor O ϖ K β` uses `genericFibre.map` on both the structural maps and
the morphisms. Choosing `β` specifies the scalar identification. The construction
and conclusions hold for every such choice (Conrad-AWS §3.3, Ex. 3.3.8, p. 32;
Huber96 §1.9, Prop. 1.9.1 and Ex. 1.9.2(i), pp. 96–97).

`admissibleBlowupClass O ϖ` consists of the arrows isomorphic over their targets
to `AdmissibleBlowup` projections at `IsAdmissibleCentre` ideals. The unit ideal
is allowed. `rigFunctor_inverts` sends this class to isomorphisms
(Conrad-AWS §3.3, Ex. 3.3.11–3.3.12, pp. 33–34).
`rigFunctor_qcqs` gives compactness and quasi-separatedness of every image
(Ex. 3.3.10, p. 33). `raynaud_isLocalization` states Mathlib's `IsLocalization`
for the corestriction of `rigFunctor` to the qcqs full subcategory of the imported
`AdicSpace.AdicOver K`. The corestriction is essential: the ambient category
also contains non-quasi-compact spaces. `rigFunctor_essImage` identifies the
essential image in that ambient category by compactness, quasi-separatedness,
and local finite type of the structural morphism; the last condition is already
part of `AdicOver K` (Conrad-AWS §3.3, p. 34; BL I, Thm 4.1).

`rigFunctor_map_injective_of_torsionFree` states injectivity on each Hom set
of admissible models; the source's torsion-free condition comes from its
`IsAdmissible` proof (Conrad-AWS Ex. 3.3.10, p. 33). The existing
`raynaud_test_torsion_notFaithful` checks why the condition matters.
`rigFunctor_hom_roof` realizes every generic morphism after blowing up the
source; `rigFunctor_iso_roof` gives a common admissible blow-up for an isomorphism.
`rigFunctor_roof_eq_iff` says that two roofs represent the same generic morphism
exactly when their numerators agree on a common admissible refinement over the
source. Together these give the stated colimit description of Hom sets
(Conrad-AWS §3.3, p. 34; BL I §5).

**Checks.**

- `AdmissibleFormal_base`: the identity of `Spf O` is an object.
- `AdmissibleFormal_empty`: an empty formal scheme over the base is an object.
- `AdmissibleFormal_specialFibre`: a nonempty source on which `ϖ` vanishes cannot be an object.
- `admissibleBlowupClass_identity`: identity arrows belong to the class, using the unit centre.
- `admissibleBlowupClass_empty`: a map from an empty model to a nonempty model does not belong to the class.
- `admissibleBlowupClass_invertible`: blowing up an invertible ideal gives an isomorphism, which belongs to the class.
- `rigFunctor_base`: the base model maps to the identity object over `Spa(K,K°)`.
- `rigFunctor_empty`: the empty model has empty generic fibre.
- `rigFunctor_noncompact`: a non-quasi-compact object, in particular the open unit disc, lies outside the essential image.
- `rigFunctor_closedDisc`: the structural model `Spf O⟨T⟩` maps to Part II's closed unit disc, as an object over `Spa(K,K°)` (Conrad-AWS Ex. 3.3.9, p. 32).
- `rigFunctor_discBlowup`: the ideal with global sections `(T,ϖ)` on that model is an admissible centre, its blow-up is quasi-compact and admissible, and its projection maps to an isomorphism (Ex. 3.3.11–3.3.12, pp. 33–34).

### R2.6 separatedness, flattening, quasi-finite models and finiteness criteria

The formal blow-up carrier `FormalScheme.AdmissibleBlowup O ϖ s J` represents maps
from admissible formal schemes over `Spf O` on which `J` becomes invertible. Its
projection is adic and its source admissible. `IdealSheafData.IsInvertible` means
locally principal with a regular generator. `IsAdmissibleCentre` means locally
finitely generated and containing a power of the structural `ϖ`.
`nonempty_admissibleBlowup` supplies the representing object; the generic-fibre
map is an isomorphism by `AdmissibleBlowup.genericFibre_isIso` (BL I, §§2 and 4).
`exists_formalOpen_of_genericOpen` realizes each quasi-compact generic open as
the inverse image under specialization of an open on a blow-up (BL I, 4.4).

**Checks for the centre and blow-up.**

- `IdealSheafData.IsInvertible_unit`: the unit ideal is invertible.
- `IdealSheafData.IsInvertible_zero`: the zero ideal on a nonempty formal scheme is not invertible.
- `IdealSheafData.IsInvertible_product`: every power of an invertible ideal is invertible.
- `IsAdmissibleCentre_unit`: the unit ideal is an admissible centre.
- `IsAdmissibleCentre_zero`: the zero ideal on a nonempty admissible model is not a centre.
- `IsAdmissibleCentre_power`: positive powers remain admissible centres.
- `AdmissibleBlowup_unit`: on an admissible source, blowing up the unit ideal is an isomorphism.
- `AdmissibleBlowup_specialFibre`: on a nonempty source killed by the pseudouniformizer, an admissible blow-up cannot have an invertible projection.
- `AdmissibleBlowup_invertible`: an already invertible centre has an isomorphic blow-up.
- `AdmissibleBlowup_power`: positive powers of the centre give uniquely isomorphic blow-ups over the base.

`FormalScheme.TorsionQuotient` is the quotient of a module sheaf by its locally
`ϖ`-power-torsion sections. The epimorphism and its kernel on every open specify
the quotient; the exponent may vary locally. This locality is needed on opens
that are not quasi-compact. The construction is the torsion quotient used for
strict transforms in BL II, §4.

**Checks for the torsion quotient.**

- `TorsionQuotient_zero`: the quotient of zero is zero.
- `TorsionQuotient_admissible`: the structure sheaf of an admissible model is unchanged.
- `TorsionQuotient_killed`: a module all of whose sections are power torsion has zero quotient.

`FormalScheme.IdealTorsionQuotient J M` specifies the quotient of `M` by sections
locally killed by a power of `J`. Its epimorphism and sectionwise kernel equation determine
the quotient. Applying it to the pulled-back centre and coefficient module gives the
strict transform in `exists_flattening`, `exists_flattening_lowerDimension`,
`exists_flattening_smooth` and `exists_flattening_largerOpen`.

**Checks for centre torsion.**

- `IdealTorsionQuotient_unit`: the unit ideal kills no nonzero section, so the quotient map is invertible.
- `IdealTorsionQuotient_zero`: the zero ideal makes the quotient zero.
- `IdealTorsionQuotient_annihilated`: if a fixed power of the ideal annihilates the module, its quotient is zero.

**A morphism of admissible formal schemes is separated iff its generic fibre is.**

a complete rank-one `O_K`. Prove that `f` is separated if and only if `f_rig: X_rig → Y_rig` is
separated (BL I §4, Prop. 4.7, p. 310; Conrad-MR Appendix A.1, proof of Thm A.1.2, p. 38, its use in
Conrad's fibral finiteness criterion), equivalently, by Huber's comparison of separatedness for
rigid and adic morphisms (*proper-separated-comparisons* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R1)), iff `d(f): d(X) → d(Y)` is
separated in the sense of *separated-morphism* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R0). For instance the formal affine line with doubled origin (glue two copies of `Spf O_K⟨T⟩` along
the formal open `Spf O_K⟨T, T⁻¹⟩`) is not separated, and its generic fibre (two closed discs glued
along the annulus `{|T| = 1}`) is not separated either. *Needs:* *generic-fibre-fibre-products*;
*rig-point*; *saturated-submodule-finitely-generated*; *raynaud-generic-fibre*; *separated-morphism*
(AdicSpacesPartII layer R0); *proper-separated-comparisons*, *rigid-analytic-space* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R1).

**Separatedness, properness and partial properness of a formal model versus its generic fibre (Huber
1996 Remark 1.3.18).** (*formal-rigid-properness-comparison*) Let `K` be complete of rank one,
discreteness not assumed, and `f: X → Y` a morphism of formal schemes that are flat and locally of
finite type over `Spf O_K` (admissible formal `O_K`-schemes), with generic fibre `d(f) ≅ r_K(f_rig)`
(*raynaud-generic-fibre*). Clause (i), `d(f)` separated iff `f` separated, is
*formal-model-separatedness* (with AdicSpacesPartII layer R1's comparison of rigid and adic separatedness) and is
not restated. Prove: (ii) `d(f)` is proper in the sense of *universally-closed-and-proper-morphism* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R0) iff `f` is
proper; (iii) `d(f)` is partially proper in the sense of *partially-proper-morphism* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R0) iff
`f|_Z: Z → Y_s` is proper for every irreducible closed subset `Z` of the special fibre `X_s` (with
its reduced structure) (Huber96 §1.3, Rem. 1.3.18, p. 59: `A` complete of rank 1, `X`, `Y` flat and
locally of finite type over `A`, statements (i)–(iii) quoted from [Hu4, 3.11, 3.13]; Huber96 §1.3,
Rem. 1.3.19, pp. 59–60, Huber's use of 1.3.18(iii), the formal partial-properness criterion, in the
rigid–adic comparison; Conrad-MR §3.1, proof of Thm 3.1.6, p. 18, properness of the generic fibre of
a proper formal model without discreteness). Huber states the remark quoting [Hu4, 3.11, 3.13].
Clause (ii) is the adic statement, and its forward direction supplies clause (d) of

for Kiehl's properness is a different statement: without discreteness it is Temkin's comparison
through Berkovich spaces [Te, Cor. 4.4 and 4.5, p. 18 of the
[author version](https://math.huji.ac.il/~temkin/papers/Local_Properties_I.pdf)], and in the
discretely valued case it is Lütkebohmert [L1]. This target does not assert Kiehl-properness, and
*proper-relatively-compact-covers* takes it as a hypothesis for general `K`. For instance
`P̂¹_{O_K} → Spf O_K` is proper and `P^{1,ad}_K → Spa(K, O_K)` is proper;
`Spf O_K⟨T⟩ → Spf O_K` is not proper (special fibre `A¹_k`) and the closed unit disc is not proper
over `Spa(K, O_K)` (it is not partially proper); Mumford's formal model of `G_m` for the Tate curve
(an infinite chain of `P¹_k`'s in the special fibre, each component proper) has partially proper

*raynaud-generic-fibre*; *specialisation-map*; *admissible-formal-scheme*;
*proper-separated-comparisons*, *rigid-analytic-space* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R1);
*universally-closed-and-proper-morphism*, *partially-proper-morphism*,
*separated-proper-partially-proper* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R0); Mathlib `AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper`.

**The fibres of a formal model bound the fibres of its generic fibre (Conrad-MR Theorem A.2.1).**
(*formal-model-fibre-comparison*) Let `K` be complete of rank one, discreteness not assumed, and
`m_K` the maximal ideal of `O_K`. For an `O_K`-algebra `A` topologically of finite presentation
(*topologically-finitely-presented-algebra*), write `A_K = A[1/ϖ] = A ⊗_{O_K} K` for the ring of its
generic affinoid (*raynaud-generic-fibre*) and `A_k = A/m_K A`, a finitely generated `k`-algebra,
for its special fibre. Prove: (i) `dim A_K ≤ dim A_k` for Krull dimensions, without flatness;
(ii) if `A` is `O_K`-flat then `dim A_K = dim A_k`; (iii) if `A` is `O_K`-flat, `A_k` is reduced
and `Spec A_k` has pure dimension `d`, then `A_K` is reduced and `Spec A_K` has pure dimension
`d`. For (i), lift a Noether normalisation `k[x_1, …, x_n] → A_k` to `O_K⟨t_1, …, t_n⟩ → A`; this
lift is finite because its reduction is finite and `A` is `ϖ`-adically complete and separated. For
(ii), Noether normalisation for affinoid algebras applied to a presentation of `A` gives a finite
injective map `O_K⟨t_1, …, t_e⟩ → A` with `e = dim A_K`; flatness makes `A → A_K` injective. For
(iii), every nonzero element of `A_K` has a `K^×`-multiple in `A ∖ m_K A`, because ideals of Tate
algebras are closed and the residue norm is attained. This makes `A`, hence `A_K`, reduced.
Flatness makes every minimal prime `p` of `A` meet `O_K` only in `0`, and (ii) applied to the
quotients `A/p`, together with the same lemma, gives the pure dimension (Conrad-MR Appendix A.2,
Thm A.2.1, p. 39, statement; proof of Thm A.2.1, pp. 39–41, the finiteness criterion, equation
(A.2.2) and the pure-dimension argument; Lem. A.2.2, pp. 40–41).

Let `f : X → Y` be a morphism of formal `O_K`-schemes locally of tf presentation, and
`f_0 : X_0 → Y_0` its reduction modulo `ϖ`. Let `K'/K` be a complete extension of rank-one valued
fields with residue field `k'`, not necessarily finite over `K`, and `y : Spa(K', O_{K'}) → d(Y)`
a morphism over `Spa(K, O_K)`. Prove: (iv) `y = d(ỹ)` for a unique morphism
`ỹ : Spf O_{K'} → Y` over `Spf O_K`. The fibre `X_ỹ = X ×_Y Spf O_{K'}` is locally of tf
presentation over `O_{K'}`, and `O_{K'}`-flat when `f` is flat. Its generic fibre is
`d(X_ỹ) ≅ d(X) ×_{d(Y)} Spa(K', O_{K'})` over `Spa(K', O_{K'})`. Its special fibre is
`f_0⁻¹(s) ⊗_{κ(s)} k'`, where `s ∈ Y_0` is the image of `ỹ`, the specialisation of `y`.
(v) The analytic fibre `d(X) ×_{d(Y)} Spa(K', O_{K'})` is covered by the charts
`d(Spf A_i) = Spa(A_{i,K'}, A_{i,K'}°)` for the formal affine opens `Spf A_i` of `X_ỹ`. If every
fibre of `f_0` has dimension `≤ d`, then `dim A_{i,K'} ≤ d` for every `i`. If `f` is flat and
every fibre of `f_0` is geometrically reduced of pure dimension `d`, then every `A_{i,K'}` is
reduced and `Spec A_{i,K'}` has pure dimension `d`. For (iv), `Spa(K', O_{K'})` is a single point,
so `y` lands in some `d(Spf B) = Spa(B_K, B_K°)`. There `y` is a continuous map of pairs
`(B_K, B_K°) → (K', O_{K'})` (Huber94 §2, Prop. 2.1(i), p. 522), and its restriction to `B`
defines `ỹ`; uniqueness holds because `O_{K'}` is `ϖ`-torsion free. The generic fibre of `X_ỹ` is
*generic-fibre-fibre-products* (b) followed by (a) over `O_{K'}`. Clause (v) is (i) and (iii) over
`O_{K'}` applied to the `A_i`. Here `Spec A_{i,k'}` is an open subscheme of
`f_0⁻¹(s) ⊗_{κ(s)} k'`, and the local dimension of a scheme of finite type over a field, hence its
pure dimension, does not change under field extension (Stacks Tag 00P4). Conrad proves the same
comparison at points with `K'/K` finite through *rig-point* (Conrad-MR Appendix A.1, Lem. A.1.5,
p. 38; proof of Thm A.2.1, p. 39). Since (v) allows every complete `K'`, it also covers the field
extensions needed for geometric reducedness. *Needs:* *topologically-finitely-presented-algebra*;
*raynaud-generic-fibre*; *generic-fibre-fibre-products*; *generic-fibre-functor-d*;
*specialisation-map*; *rig-point*; Tau Ceti `TauCeti.IsPureDimensional`; Mathlib `ringKrullDim`,
`IsReduced`, `Module.Flat`.

The affine clauses (i)–(iii) are `IsTopologicallyFinitePresentation.ringKrullDim_genericFibre_le`,

`FormalScheme.genericFibre_fibreDimension` and `FormalScheme.genericFibre_fibreReducedPure` for (v).

- `formalModelFibre_zero` (degenerate) — for `A = 0` both fibres are zero rings of dimension `⊥`
  with empty spectra, pure of every dimension. A nonzero `A` has `A_k ≠ 0`: `m_K A = A` would
  give `A = ϖA`, hence `A = 0` by `ϖ`-adic separatedness. A nonzero flat `A` also has `A_K ≠ 0`,
  so (ii) never compares `⊥` with a natural number.
- `formalModelFibre_annulus` (computation) — `A = O_K⟨S, T⟩/(ST − ϖ)` is flat. Its special fibre
  `k[S, T]/(ST)`, two crossing lines, is reduced of pure dimension `1`, and `A_K`, the ring of the
  annulus `{|ϖ| ≤ |S| ≤ 1}`, is a domain of dimension `1`, as (ii) and (iii) predict.
- `formalModelFibre_gaussPoint` (point beyond rig-points) — for `Y = Spf O_K⟨T⟩` let `y` be the
  Gauss point, with `K'` the completion of `K(T)` for the Gauss norm and `k' = k(T)`. Then `ỹ` is
  the inclusion `O_K⟨T⟩ → O_{K'}` and `s` is the generic point of `A¹_k`. For `f = id_Y` the fibre
  is `Spa(K', O_{K'})` with special fibre `Spec k(T)`. Here `K'/K` is not finite, so *rig-point*
  does not supply this lift.

**Flattening by admissible blow-up (Bosch–Lütkebohmert II Theorem 5.2).** (*flattening-by-blow-up*)
For a morphism `f: X → Y` of quasi-compact admissible formal `O_K`-schemes with `f_rig` flat
(resp. flat in dimension `≥ n`), there is an admissible blow-up `Y' → Y` of the target such that
the strict transform `X'` of `X` — the closed formal subscheme of `X ×_Y Y'` cut out by the
sections supported over the centre, not the total transform — is flat (resp. flat in dimension
`≥ n`) over `Y'`: this is the case `T = Y`, `ℳ = O_X` of *module-flattening-by-blow-up* (BL II §5,
Thm 5.2, p. 426, deduced there from Thm 4.1; Conrad-MR Appendix A.1, proof of Thm A.1.2, p. 38, its
use in the fibral finiteness criterion), and is a corollary, not a separate statement. For `X = ∅`
the statement is empty; with `Y = Spf O_K⟨ζ⟩` and `X = Spf O_K⟨ζ, ξ⟩/(ζξ − ϖ)`, `f_rig` is the
open immersion of the annulus `{|ϖ| ≤ |ζ| ≤ 1}` into the disc, `f` is not flat (`ζ` is a
zero-divisor on `k[ζ, ξ]/(ζξ)`), and after blowing up `(ζ, ϖ)` on `Y` the strict transform maps
isomorphically onto the chart `{ζ generates}` of `Y'`. *Needs:* *module-flattening-by-blow-up*;
*admissible-blow-up*.

**Quasi-finite and bounded-fibre-dimension formal models (Bosch–Lütkebohmert II Corollary 5.3).**
(*quasi-finite-formal-model*) Let `f: X → Y` be a morphism of quasi-compact admissible formal
`O_K`-schemes (`K` complete of rank one; the classical rigid case), dimensions of rigid fibres being
taken at rig-points (*rig-flat-in-dimension*). Prove: (a) if all fibres of `f_rig` have dimension `≤
n` (`dim(X/Y)_rig ≤ n`), there is an admissible blow-up `Y' → Y` such that the induced `f': X' → Y'`
(`X'` the strict transform) has relative dimension `≤ n`: every fibre of `f'_0: X'_0 → Y'_0` has
dimension `≤ n` (BL II §5, proof of Cor. 5.3(a), p. 426); (b) if `f_rig` is quasi-finite, there is
an admissible blow-up `Y' → Y` with `f': X' → Y'` quasi-finite (`f'_0` locally quasi-finite, Mathlib
`AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyQuasiFinite`) (BL II §5, Cor. 5.3(b), p. 426; Conrad-MR Appendix A.1,
proof of Thm A.1.2, p. 38, its use in Conrad's criterion). For instance, with `Y = Spf O_K⟨ζ⟩` and
`X = Spf O_K⟨ζ, ξ⟩/(ζξ − ϖ)`, `f_rig` is quasi-finite (an open immersion) while `f` has the
one-dimensional fibre `A¹_k` over `ζ = 0`; after blowing up `(ζ, ϖ)` the strict transform is
quasi-finite (an open immersion). *Needs:* *flattening-by-blow-up*; *admissible-blow-up*;
*rig-flat-in-dimension*; *flat-in-dimension*; *rig-point*; Mathlib
`AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyQuasiFinite`, `AlgebraicGeometry.locallyQuasiFinite_iff_isFinite_fiber`.

`FormalScheme.locallyQuasiFinite_reduction_iff` identifies locally quasi-finite
reduction with finite set-theoretic fibres for a locally finite-type,
quasi-compact reduction. Quasi-compactness is necessary: an infinite disjoint
union of copies of a field point is étale over that point and has infinite fibre
(Mathlib `AlgebraicGeometry.locallyQuasiFinite_iff_finite_preimage_singleton`).
The Check `LocallyQuasiFinite_infiniteFibre` instantiates this with the actual
countable coproduct of `Spec K`: its map to `Spec K` is locally quasi-finite,
is not quasi-compact, and has an infinite fibre.

**The finite part over a henselian local base.** (*henselian-quasi-finite-finite-part*)
Let `A` be a henselian local ring and `f : X → Spec A` separated and locally quasi-finite,
with finite closed fibre. Construct an open-and-closed decomposition `X = X_fin ⊔ X_miss`
with `X_fin → Spec A` finite and `X_miss` having empty closed fibre. The finite part is the
union of the finitely many open-and-closed neighbourhoods `Spec O_{X,x}` of the points
in that fibre; its closed fibre equals that of `X` (EGA IV₄ 18.5.11(c), pp. 130–131;
Conrad-MR Appendix A.1, proof of Lemma A.1.4, p. 38).
*Needs:* Mathlib `HenselianLocalRing`, `AlgebraicGeometry.IsSeparated`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyQuasiFinite`, `AlgebraicGeometry.IsFinite`, open-and-closed restrictions.

Checks:

- For a finite `A`-scheme, take `X_fin = X` and `X_miss = ∅`.
- Over `A = k⟦t⟧`, `Spec A ⊔ Spec A[1/t]` has finite part `Spec A` and missing part `Spec A[1/t]`.
- An infinite disjoint union of `Spec A` is separated and locally quasi-finite but has infinite
  closed fibre; no finite part can contain that fibre. This excludes dropping fibre finiteness.

**Finiteness of scheme morphisms descends along fpqc covers.** (*scheme-finite-fpqc-descent*)
For a scheme morphism `f : X → Y` and a faithfully flat quasi-compact cover `g : Y' → Y`,
prove that `f` is finite if and only if its base change to `Y'` is finite. Descend
both affineness and finiteness of the coordinate algebra; ring-level descent alone
requires the source to be affine and cannot supply the first step
(EGA IV₂ 2.7.1(xiii), (xv), pp. 29–30).
*Needs:* ModularCurves §0E, effective faithfully flat descent of affine schemes;
Mathlib `RingHom.Finite.codescendsAlong_faithfullyFlat`, scheme fibre products,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Flat`, `AlgebraicGeometry.QuasiCompact`, `AlgebraicGeometry.IsFinite`.

Checks:

- For `g = id_Y`, the descended finite map is the original map.
- An empty source remains empty and finite after every base change.
- Over a field `k`, `A¹_k → Spec k` remains nonfinite after any faithfully flat field
  extension: the polynomial algebra has infinite dimension.

**Conrad's scheme lemma: a flat, locally finitely presented, separated morphism with finite fibres
of locally constant rank is finite.** (*fibral-finiteness-scheme-lemma*) Let `f: X → Y` be a flat
morphism of schemes that is locally of finite presentation. Prove (Conrad's Lemma A.1.4) that `f` is
finite if and only if it is separated with finite fibres and its fibre rank `y ↦ dim_{κ(y)} Γ(X_y, O)` is locally constant on `Y`; no quasi-compactness and no noetherian hypothesis is needed
(Conrad-MR Appendix A.1, Lem. A.1.4, p. 38; Conrad-MR Appendix A.1, proof of Lem. A.1.4, p. 38, the
finite-part decomposition). Apply *henselian-quasi-finite-finite-part* after base change
from a local base to its henselization and descend by *scheme-finite-fpqc-descent*.
The finite part is flat and locally finitely presented, hence finite free of rank `d` over
the local base. Its rank at the closed point is the full fibre rank. When this rank is
constant on the base, it exhausts every fibre, so the complementary part is empty.
Spread the resulting finite free neighbourhood from each local base as in Conrad's proof. The "only if" direction is in Mathlib, where a finite morphism is locally quasi-finite
(`AlgebraicGeometry.IsFinite` implies `LocallyQuasiFinite`) and a finite flat morphism of finite
presentation has locally constant rank (`Scheme.Hom.isLocallyConstant_finrank`); the "if" direction
is the content of this target, since Mathlib's `IsFinite.of_locallyQuasiFinite` needs an
`IsLocallyArtinian` base and `IsFinite.of_isProper_of_locallyQuasiFinite` needs properness. For
instance, over `Y = Spec k[t]`, `X = Spec k[t] ⊔ Spec k[t, t⁻¹] → Y` is flat,
separated, of finite presentation with finite fibres, but its fibre rank is `2` over `t ≠ 0` and `1`
over `t = 0` (not locally constant) and it is not finite, as the lemma predicts; for `X = ∅` the
map is a closed immersion, hence finite, with empty fibres of rank `0`, as the criterion says; and
the fibre rank over `y` is finite because a finite fibre of a morphism locally of finite type over
`κ(y)` is a finite `κ(y)`-scheme. *Needs:* Mathlib
`AlgebraicGeometry.Flat`, `AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFinitePresentation`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.IsSeparated`, `AlgebraicGeometry.IsFinite`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isLocallyConstant_finrank`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.IsFinite.of_isProper_of_locallyQuasiFinite`, `HenselianLocalRing`;
*henselian-quasi-finite-finite-part*; *scheme-finite-fpqc-descent*.

`RigidSpace.fibreRank` sums the dimensions of the local fibre algebras over
the residue field of the base point, so it records multiplicities as well as points.
**Checks:** `fibreRank_identity` gives one; `fibreRank_empty` gives zero on an
empty fibre; `fibreRank_doubleLength` gives two for a single point with a
length-two local fibre algebra.


**Conrad's fibral finiteness criterion for flat rigid (adic) morphisms.**
(*fibral-finiteness-criterion*) Let `K` be an arbitrary complete nonarchimedean field, not
necessarily discretely valued, with formal models over `Spf R` for `R = O_K` possibly
non-noetherian. Prove (Conrad's Theorem A.1.2) that a flat map `f: X → Y` of rigid spaces over `K`
is finite if and only if it is quasi-compact and separated with finite fibres and locally constant
fibre rank on `Y`; the hypotheses are: `f` flat; quasi-compact; separated (quasi-separated is
insufficient, cf. Conrad's Remark A.1.3); finite fibres; fibre rank locally constant on `Y`
(Conrad-MR Appendix A.1, Thm A.1.2, p. 37, the exact statement and hypotheses; Conrad-MR Appendix
A.1, Rem. A.1.3, p. 37, why noetherian formal geometry in the sense of layer F0 cannot supply this
criterion; Conrad-MR Appendix A.1, proof of Thm A.1.2, p. 38, whose Bosch–Lütkebohmert imports are
*formal-model-separatedness*, *flattening-by-blow-up*, *quasi-finite-formal-model* and *rig-point*).
Through *rigid-adic-comparison-functor* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R1) the same holds for flat morphisms of
quasi-separated adic spaces locally of finite type over `Spa(K, O_K)`, with fibres and ranks taken
at classical points. Quasi-compactness is necessary: `{|t| = 1} ⊔ {|t| < 1} → {|t| ≤ 1}` is a
bijective local isomorphism, flat with fibres of rank `1`, not finite. A finite flat rigid map has
locally constant fibre rank, and conversely under the stated hypotheses; over a discretely valued
`K` the statement is Abbes–Mokrane [AM], Lemme A.1, with "separated" in place of "quasi-separated"; Conrad
applies it to show that the multiplication maps defining canonical subgroups over the Hasse loci are
finite (Conrad-MR, proof of Thm 4.1.3). *Needs:* *fibral-finiteness-scheme-lemma*;
*formal-model-separatedness*; *quasi-finite-formal-model*; *flattening-by-blow-up*; *rig-point*;
*raynaud-theorem*; *finite-morphism*, *separated-morphism* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R0);
*rigid-adic-comparison-functor*, *rigid-analytic-space*, *rigid-adic-quasi-separated-equivalence*
(AdicSpacesPartII layer R1).

**Topological invariance of affinoidness and finiteness (Conrad A.1.1).**
(*topological-invariance-of-affinoid*) Let `K` be a complete nonarchimedean field, with no
discreteness assumed, and `X` a rigid space over `K`. Prove that `X` is affinoid iff `X_red` is
affinoid; hence a morphism `f: Y → Z` of rigid spaces is finite iff `Y_red → Z_red` is finite
(Conrad-MR Appendix A.1, Thm A.1.1, p. 36). Through *rigid-adic-comparison-functor* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R1) —
affinoids correspond to affinoids, Huber96 1.1.11 — the same holds for quasi-separated adic spaces
locally of finite type over `Spa(K, O_K)`. No Serre-type cohomological criterion is available: over
every nonarchimedean `K` there is a quasi-compact separated surface with vanishing higher coherent
cohomology that is not affinoid [Liu] (Conrad-MR Appendix A.1, after Thm A.1.1, p. 36). The proof
imports [BGR 6.1.1/4, 7.3.5/3, 9.5.3/5], which are cited, not re-derived. For instance
`Sp(K⟨T⟩[ε]/(ε²))` is affinoid and its reduction is the closed disc; a finite morphism can be
recognised on reduced spaces, and Conrad uses this with Theorem A.1.2 in the canonical subgroup
construction. *Needs:* *rigid-analytic-space*, *rigid-adic-comparison-functor*,
*rigid-adic-quasi-separated-equivalence*, *gerritzen-grauert* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R1); *finite-morphism*,
*closed-adic-subspaces-and-embeddings* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R0).

### R2.7 the proof of flattening

This subsection proves the flattening theorem of Bosch–Lütkebohmert II by breaking it into the
lemmas of their §§1–4: lifting generators, bases and smooth morphisms from the reduction modulo `ϖ`;
the étale-local structure theorem of Raynaud–Gruson and its formal counterpart (finite over smooth
with geometrically irreducible fibres); ideals of coefficients and contents along smooth morphisms
with geometrically irreducible fibres; dévissages of coherent modules and the flatness criteria they
give; rig-flatness, flatness in dimension `≥ n` and Fitting ideals; and the induction that lowers
the dimension of the non-flat locus by one admissible blow-up at a time. Throughout, `K` is complete
for a nontrivial rank-one valuation, `O_K` is its valuation ring and `ϖ` a pseudouniformiser; formal
schemes are formal `O_K`-schemes locally of topologically finite presentation
(*admissible-formal-scheme*), `X_λ = X ⊗ O_K/ϖ^{λ+1}`, `X_0` has the underlying space of `X`, and
for `t ∈ T_0` the fibre `X ⊗ k(t)` is `X_0 ×_{T_0} Spec k(t)`. The classical rigid case (base `Spf
O_K`) is the one proved; Bosch–Lütkebohmert's noetherian base case uses parallel arguments that are
not decomposed here. Smooth and étale formal morphisms, elementary étale neighbourhoods and the
étale-site invariance used throughout are *smooth-formal-scheme* and *formal-etale-site-invariance*
of R2.9.

**Generators modulo `ϖ` generate topologically.** (*topological-generation-mod-definition-ideal*) Let
`f : X → Y` be an affine morphism of formal `O_K`-schemes locally of tf presentation, `ℳ` a coherent
`O_X`-module and `E ⊆ Γ(X, ℳ)` a family of sections, possibly infinite. Prove that if the images of
`E` generate `f_*(ℳ/ϖℳ)` as an `O_{Y_0}`-module, then `E` generates `f_*ℳ` topologically over `O_Y`:
over every formal affine open `Spf A ⊆ Y`, with `f⁻¹(Spf A) = Spf B` and `ℳ` corresponding to the
finite `B`-module `M`, every `m ∈ M` is a `ϖ`-adically convergent sum `Σ_{e∈E} a_e e` with `a_e ∈ A`
and `a_e → 0` (for each `λ` only finitely many `a_e` lie outside `ϖ^λ A`); equivalently the
`A`-linear map `Â^{(E)} → M` from the `ϖ`-adic completion of the free `A`-module on `E` is
surjective (BL II §1, Lem. 1.3(a) and its proof, p. 405: Nakayama on the powers of the ideal of
definition, reduction to the affine case and the approximation argument of BL I 1.5). Generation is
required modulo `ϖ`, the ideal of definition, not modulo `m_K`, and the conclusion is topological
generation, not generation: for `Y = Spf O_K`, `X = Spf O_K⟨ζ⟩`, `ℳ = O_X` and `E = {ζ^i : i ≥ 0}`,
`E` generates `(O_K/ϖ)[ζ]` modulo `ϖ` and every `g ∈ O_K⟨ζ⟩` is `Σ c_i ζ^i` with `c_i → 0`, while
`Σ_i ϖ^i ζ^i ∈ O_K⟨ζ⟩` is not a finite `O_K`-linear combination of the `ζ^i`. The affine core —
a map into a `ϖ`-adically complete module that is surjective modulo `ϖ` is surjective after
completing the source — is Mathlib's `AdicCompletion.map_surjective_of_mkQ_comp_surjective`; this
target adds the sheaf form on `Y` and the convergent-sum description over `Spf A`. *Needs:*
*admissible-formal-scheme*; *topologically-finitely-presented-algebra*;
*saturated-submodule-finitely-generated*; *flat-tft-is-tfp*; Mathlib `IsAdicComplete`,
`AdicCompletion.map_surjective_of_mkQ_comp_surjective`.

**A basis modulo `ϖ` of a flat module lifts to a topological basis.** (*topological-basis-lifting*) In
the situation of *topological-generation-mod-definition-ideal* (`f : X → Y` affine, `ℳ` coherent on
`X`, `E ⊆ Γ(X, ℳ)`), assume that the images of `E` form a basis of `f_*(ℳ/ϖℳ)` over `O_{Y_0}` — a
basis, not only a generating family — and that `ℳ` is flat over `O_Y` (`ℳ_x` flat over `O_{Y,f(x)}`
for all `x`; over `Spf B → Spf A`: `M` flat over `A`). Prove that `E` is a topological basis of
`f_*ℳ` over `O_Y`: over `Spf A` the map `φ : Â^{(E)} → M` is bijective, so every `m ∈ M` has a
unique expansion `m = Σ_{e∈E} a_e e` with `a_e → 0` (BL II §1, Lem. 1.3(b) and its proof, p. 405:
the kernel lies in every power of the ideal of definition and the completed free module is
separated). For `X = Spf O_K⟨ζ⟩` over `Y = Spf O_K`, `{ζ^i : i ≥ 0}` is a topological basis of
`O_K⟨ζ⟩`, restricted power series having unique coefficients. Flatness is needed: for `Y = X = Spf
O_K`, `ℳ = O_K/ϖ` and `E = {1}`, `E` is a basis modulo `ϖ` but `φ : O_K → O_K/ϖ` is not injective.
*Needs:* *topological-generation-mod-definition-ideal*; *tfp-locality*; Mathlib `Module.Flat`,
`IsAdicComplete`.

The affine carrier `TopologicalBasis I E M` is a linear equivalence between `M` and the
`I`-adic completion of the free module `E →₀ A`. Its `vector` and `coord` maps send standard
unit vectors to basis vectors and recover coefficients. For complete `A`, `coord_vector`
gives the Kronecker coefficients and `coord_decay` gives finite support outside each `I^n`;
`ext` gives uniqueness. For finitely generated `I`, `existsUnique_of_decay` gives existence
for every decaying coefficient family. `ofModBasis` and `ofModBasis_vector` lift the specified
vectors, with flatness and completeness as hypotheses (BL II Lem. 1.3(b), p. 405).

**Checks for the completed basis, vectors and coordinates.**

- `topologicalBasis_test_empty` — an empty basis exists exactly for the zero module.
- `topologicalBasis_test_rankOne` — the complete base ring has basis `{1}` and its coordinate
  map is the identity.
- `topologicalBasis_test_twoTerm` — the coordinates of `a e₀ + c e₁` are `(a,c)`, in that order.
- `topologicalBasis_test_infinite` — over `ℤ_p`, the coefficients `p^i` determine an element
  outside the algebraic span of a countably infinite topological basis.
- `topologicalBasis_test_torsion` — `ℤ_p/p` has no rank-one topological basis over `ℤ_p`.

The constructor itself has three computed Checks: `liftedBasis_test_rankOne` lifts the
residue basis `1` and recovers the identity coordinate map; `liftedBasis_test_twoTerm` lifts
the standard two vectors and sends `(a,c)` to coordinates `(a,c)`; `liftedBasis_test_empty`
lifts the empty basis of the zero module and its representation is zero.

`TopologicalBasis.coefficientIdeal b N` is the ideal generated by all coordinates of all
members of the submodule `N`. It does not assert finite generation. Its Checks are:

- `coefficientIdeal_test_zero` — the zero submodule has coefficient ideal zero.
- `coefficientIdeal_test_vector` — the submodule generated by `a e_i` has ideal `(a)`.
- `coefficientIdeal_test_twoTerm` — the submodule generated by `a e₀ + c e₁` has ideal `(a,c)`.
- `coefficientIdeal_test_unit` — the whole module has unit coefficient ideal when the basis
  is nonempty; this hypothesis excludes the zero module with its empty basis.

`TopologicalBasis.coefficientIdeal_span_isPrincipal` states the additional valuation-base
conclusion: for a complete rank-one base `O_K` and a topological basis over `O_K`, the
coefficients of one element generate a principal ideal. Zero gives the zero ideal; for a
nonzero element, decay and the rank-one topology give a coefficient of largest absolute
value (BL II Prop. 2.3(b), p. 408).

**Smooth morphisms of the reduction lift to smooth formal morphisms.**
(*smooth-lifting-from-level-zero*) Let `(T, t)` be a pointed formal `O_K`-scheme locally of tf
presentation (`t ∈ T_0`) and `h_0 : (Y_0, y) → (T_0, t)` a pointed morphism of schemes that is
smooth of relative dimension `r` at `y`. Prove that after replacing `Y_0` by an open neighbourhood
of `y` there are a formal `O_K`-scheme `Y` locally of tf presentation with `Y ⊗ O_K/ϖ = Y_0` and a
smooth pointed formal morphism `h : (Y, y) → (T, t)` of relative dimension `r`
(*smooth-formal-scheme*) reducing to `h_0`. Concretely, over an affine open `Spf A ∋ t` with `Y_0 = V(f̄_{r+1}, …, f̄_n) ⊆ A^n_{A_0}` and an `(n − r)`-minor `Δ̄` of the Jacobian matrix `(∂f̄_i/∂ξ_j)`
invertible on `Y_0`, one may take `Y = V(f_{r+1}, …, f_n) ⊆ D^n_T = Spf A⟨ξ_1, …, ξ_n⟩` for
arbitrary lifts `f_i ∈ A⟨ξ⟩` of the `f̄_i`, restricted to the open where the lift `Δ` of `Δ̄` is a
unit (BL II §1, Lem. 1.4(a) and its proof, p. 405: the proof lifts a Jacobian presentation of the
reduction). The lift is not unique; only its existence after shrinking is claimed. The affine
one-level lifting is Mathlib's `Algebra.FormallySmooth.exists_mkₐ_comp_eq_of_isAdicComplete`, and
the scheme-level lifting of a smooth scheme across a single thickening, with formal smoothness of
morphisms of schemes, is SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 4 (§4.6,
§4.1); this target lifts along all the levels `O_K/ϖ^{m+1}` at once, over an
`O_K` that need not be noetherian. For `T = Spf O_K`
and `Y_0 = V(ξ_2 − ξ_1²) ⊆ A²_{O_K/ϖ}`, `Y = Spf O_K⟨ξ_1, ξ_2⟩/(ξ_2 − ξ_1²) ≅ Spf O_K⟨ξ_1⟩` is
smooth of relative dimension `1`; in the étale case `r = 0` a standard étale `Y_0 = Spec (A_0[ξ]/(p̄))_{ḡ}` lifts to the étale formal scheme `Y = Spf (A⟨ξ⟩/(p))⟨g⁻¹⟩`. *Needs:*
*smooth-formal-scheme*; *admissible-formal-scheme*; *topologically-finitely-presented-algebra*;
Mathlib `AlgebraicGeometry.Smooth.exists_isStandardSmooth`, `Algebra.IsStandardSmooth`.

**Lifting factorisations through smooth and étale morphisms.** (*smooth-lifting-of-diagrams*) Let `f
: (X, x) → (T, t)` be a pointed morphism of formal `O_K`-schemes locally of tf presentation and
suppose the reduction factors as `f_0 = h_0 ∘ g_0` with `g_0 : (X_0, x) → (Y_0, y)` and `h_0 : (Y_0,
y) → (T_0, t)` smooth. Prove that after shrinking `X`, `Y_0` and `T` to open neighbourhoods of `x`,
`y` and `t` there are a smooth formal morphism `h : (Y, y) → (T, t)` lifting `h_0` and a formal
morphism `g : (X, x) → (Y, y)` with `h ∘ g = f` and `g ⊗ O_K/ϖ = g_0`; and that if `h_0` is étale
(not necessarily affine), the lift `(Y, h)` exists without shrinking and is unique up to unique
isomorphism, and `g` is unique (BL II §1, Lem. 1.4(b) and its proof, p. 405: part (a) and
infinitesimal lifting). Shrinking is needed in the smooth case only. In the étale case with `h_0 =
id` the lift is `Y = T`, `h = id` and `g = f`, uniquely; in the smooth case lifts are not unique:
for `Y_0 = A¹_{T_0} → T_0` and `g_0` given by a section `s̄ ∈ Γ(X_0, O)`, lifts `g` correspond to
lifts `s ∈ Γ(X, O_X)` of `s̄`, and `s + ϖc` is another lift. In the affine étale case the
existence of `g` is Mathlib's `Algebra.FormallySmooth.exists_mkₐ_comp_eq_of_isAdicComplete` and its
uniqueness is `Algebra.FormallyUnramified.ext_of_iInf`; the target is the pointed, shrinking, all-levels
form over a possibly non-noetherian `O_K`. *Needs:*
*smooth-lifting-from-level-zero*; *smooth-formal-scheme*; *formal-etale-site-invariance*;
*flat-tft-is-tfp*; Mathlib `Algebra.FormallySmooth.exists_mkₐ_comp_eq_of_isAdicComplete`,
`Algebra.FormallyUnramified.ext_of_iInf`, `Algebra.FormallyUnramified.ext`,
`Algebra.IsStandardSmooth`, `IsAdicComplete`.

The target statements are `FormalScheme.exists_lift_through_smooth` and
`FormalScheme.exists_unique_lift_through_etale`. For a complete rank-one valuation
base `O` with pseudouniformizer `ϖ`, they take formal `O`-schemes locally of
topological finite presentation, `f : T → Y`, and `h : X → Y`. Smoothness is local
on `X`, allowing the relative dimension to vary between components. For any finite
type ideal of definition `J` on `T`, put `T₀ = T/J` with its canonical map `ι`.
Given `g₀ : T₀ → X` with `h ∘ g₀ = f ∘ ι` and `t ∈ T`, the smooth target supplies
an open `U` containing `t` and `g : U → X` satisfying `h ∘ g = f|U` and reducing
to `g₀|U₀`. The pullback square in the conclusion identifies `U₀` with the
restriction of `T₀` to `U`. For étale `h`, the second theorem gives a unique lift
on all of `T`; neither affineness nor separatedness is assumed.
The principal choice `J = ϖO_T` gives the reduction used above. These statements
follow by complete infinitesimal lifting on affine neighbourhoods and gluing;
the all-level smooth and étale criteria are [FK] I, Prop. 5.3.18, pp. 346–347,
and Prop. 5.3.11, pp. 344–345.

`FormalScheme.exists_smooth_factorisation` also constructs the smooth formal
model of `h₀`, together with the lifted factorisation near the specified source
point. It uses a finite type ideal of definition `J` on the base, its extension
on the source, and the given commuting reduction diagram. Its conclusion
restricts the source and `Y₀` to neighbourhoods of the specified points and
identifies the reduction of the resulting model by a pullback square over the
base quotient. The base itself can stay fixed. This is the formal consequence
of lifting a standard smooth presentation (`exists_smooth_lift_algebraic`) and
[FK] I, Def. 5.3.16 and Prop. 5.3.18, pp. 346–347.
`FormalScheme.exists_etale_factorisation` gives the corresponding global model
and unique factorising map, and a unique isomorphism to any other étale model
respecting both its base map and its specified reduction. It combines
`FormalScheme.etale_reduction_equivalence` with the global lifting theorem
and [FK] I, Prop. 5.3.11, pp. 344–345.

Checks:

- `exists_unique_lift_through_etale_identity`: when `h = id`, the unique lift is
  exactly `f`, including its prescribed reduction.
- `exists_unique_lift_through_etale_empty`: the global étale assertion includes
  the empty source, although the pointed smooth assertion has no point to choose.
- `exists_lift_through_smooth_distinct_sections`: the two maps `ℤ_p[z] → ℤ_p`
  sending `z` to `0` and to `p` are distinct and have the same reduction modulo
  `p`. Their continuous extensions to the formal affine line give the distinct
  smooth sections described above.

**Generisation maps of stalks of formal schemes are flat.** (*formal-stalk-generization-flat*) Let
`X` be a formal `O_K`-scheme locally of tf presentation and `x, y ∈ X_0` with `x` a specialisation
of `y`; stalks are the colimits of `Γ(U, O_X)` over open neighbourhoods, without completion. Prove
that the canonical map of stalks `O_{X,x} → O_{X,y}` is flat (BL I §1, Cor. 1.8(b) and its proof, p.
297: via the flatness of `A → A⟨f⁻¹⟩`). For `X = Spf O_K⟨ζ⟩`, `x` the point `ζ = 0` of `X_0` and `y`
the generic point of `X_0`, `O_{X,x} → O_{X,y}` is a colimit of the flat maps `O_K⟨ζ⟩⟨g⁻¹⟩ →
O_K⟨ζ⟩⟨(gh)⁻¹⟩`. *Needs:* *admissible-formal-scheme*; *tfp-locality*; Mathlib `Module.Flat`,
`Module.Flat.iff_rTensor_injective`.

The formal-stalk target is `FormalScheme.flat_stalkSpecializes`: for a complete rank-one
base, a locally tfp formal `O_K`-scheme, and `y ⤳ x`, the actual presheaf generisation map
`O_{X,x} → O_{X,y}` supplies the scalar action for flatness. The Check
`stalkGenerization_test_identity` takes `x = y` and obtains flatness of the identity map.

**Connected elementary étale neighbourhoods at points with geometrically irreducible closure are
geometrically irreducible.** (*rg-etale-neighbourhood-irreducible*) Let `k` be a field, `Z` a
`k`-scheme of finite type that is geometrically normal, `z ∈ Z` a point whose closure is
geometrically irreducible, and `(T, t) → (Z, z)` a connected elementary étale neighbourhood (`T → Z`
étale, `t` over `z` with `k(t) = k(z)`, `T` connected). Prove that `T` is geometrically irreducible
over `k` (RG Première partie, §1.1, Lemme 1.1.2, p. 4; its proof, pp. 4–5). For `Z = A¹_k`, `z` its
generic point and `T = A¹_k ∖ {0}`, `T` is geometrically irreducible. The residue condition is
needed: for `k = ℝ`, `Z = Spec ℝ` and `T = Spec ℂ` (connected, étale, `k(t) ≠ k(z)`), `T ⊗_ℝ ℂ = Spec(ℂ × ℂ)` is not irreducible. Normality is needed: for the nodal cubic `Z = Spec k[a, b]/(b² − a²(a + 1))` and `z` the node, the henselisation `O^h_{Z,z}` has two minimal primes (the two
branches), so some connected affine elementary étale neighbourhood `(T, t)` of `z` has two
irreducible components through `t` and is not irreducible, although the closure of `z` is the
point `z`. Here the nodal example assumes `char k ≠ 2`.

**Checks.**

- `geometricallyIrreducible_test_nodal_cubic` (non-example) — when `2 ≠ 0`, a connected
  reducible elementary étale neighbourhood has its marked point `t` over the node
  `(a, b)`: `u.base t = ⟨(X 0, X 1)⟩` in the quotient ring. The two tangent
  directions `b = a` and `b = −a` are distinct.
- `geometricallyIrreducible_test_char_two` (negative control) — over `𝔽₂`,
  `X² − 1 = (X − 1)²`; the two tangent directions coincide, so this equation does not
  give the asserted node in characteristic two.

*Needs:* Mathlib `AlgebraicGeometry.Etale`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.IsFinite`, `AlgebraicGeometry.Flat`.

**After an elementary étale base change, a smooth morphism has geometrically integral fibres near a
geometrically integral fibre.** (*rg-geometrically-integral-fibres-etale-locally*) Let `(S, s)` be a
pointed scheme and `T → S` a smooth morphism such that `T ⊗ k(s)` is geometrically integral of
dimension `n`; only the fibre over `s` is assumed geometrically integral. Prove that there are an
elementary étale neighbourhood `(S', s') → (S, s)` and an open subscheme `U' ⊆ T' = T ×_S S'`
containing `T ⊗ k(s')` such that all fibres of `U' → S'` are geometrically integral of dimension `n`
(RG Première partie, §1.1, Lemme 1.1.3 and its proof, p. 5, whose first step cites EGA IV 17.16.3).
The fibre predicates are Mathlib's `AlgebraicGeometry.GeometricallyIntegral` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.GeometricallyIrreducible`; the lemma itself, like Raynaud–Gruson 1.1.1 and 1.1.2,
is not in Mathlib, and the nearest scheme-level statement — openness of the geometrically integral
fibre locus of a flat proper morphism — is SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 0
(§0.8), which does not give the étale neighbourhood. If all fibres of `T → S`
are geometrically integral (for instance `T = A^n_S`) one can take `S' = S`
and `U' = T`. Shrinking is needed: over `S = Spec k[u]`, `T = A¹_S ⊔ A¹_{D(u)}` is smooth with
geometrically integral fibre over `s = (u)` but two-component fibres over `u ≠ 0`; `U' = A¹_S` works
and `U' ≠ T`. *Needs:* *rg-etale-neighbourhood-irreducible*; Mathlib `AlgebraicGeometry.Smooth`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Etale`, `AlgebraicGeometry.GeometricallyIntegral`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.GeometricallyIrreducible`, `HenselianLocalRing`, `AlgebraicGeometry.IsFinite`.

**Étale-local structure of a morphism locally of finite type: finite over smooth with geometrically
integral fibres.** (*rg-zariski-local-structure*) Let `f : (X, x) → (S, s)` be a pointed morphism of
schemes with `X` locally of finite type over `S` (no noetherian hypothesis), and `n = dim_x(X ⊗
k(s))`. Prove that there is a commutative diagram of pointed schemes `(Y, y) → (T, t) → (S', s')`
over `(X, x) → (S, s)` such that (a) `Y`, `T` and `S'` are affine and `(Y, y) → (X, x)`, `(S', s') →
(S, s)` are elementary étale neighbourhoods (étale, with trivial residue field extension at the
marked points); (b) `T → S'` is smooth with geometrically integral fibres of dimension `n`; (c) `Y →
T` is finite and `y` is the only point of `Y` above `t` (RG Première partie, §1.1, Théorème 1.1.1,
p. 3; condition (b), p. 3; proof of 1.1.1, step 2, p. 4, the use of Zariski's Main Theorem over the
henselisation). For `X = S`, `n = 0` and one can take `Y = T = S'` an affine open neighbourhood of
`s`; for `X = A^n_S`, `T` is `X` restricted to an affine open neighbourhood and `Y = T`; for `X =
Spec k[a, b]/(b² − a³)` over `S = Spec k` at the cusp, `n = 1`, `T = A¹_k` with coordinate `a`, and
`Y → T` is finite of degree `2` with a single point over `a = 0`. *Needs:*
*rg-etale-neighbourhood-irreducible*; *rg-geometrically-integral-fibres-etale-locally*; Mathlib
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_etale_isCompl_of_quasiFiniteAt`, `AlgebraicGeometry.Smooth`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Etale`, `AlgebraicGeometry.IsFinite`.

**Local structure of formal morphisms: finite over smooth with geometrically irreducible fibres.**
(*formal-zariski-local-structure*) Let `f : (X, x) → (T, t)` be a pointed morphism of formal
`O_K`-schemes locally of tf presentation (`x ∈ X_0`, `t = f(x)`), with no flatness assumption, and
`d = dim_x(X ⊗ k(t))`, the dimension of the fibre of the reduction at `x`. Prove that there is a
commutative diagram `(X, x) ←u (X', x') →g (Z', z') →h (T', t') →v (T, t)` of pointed formal
`O_K`-schemes with `f ∘ u = v ∘ h ∘ g` such that (a) `T'`, `Z'`, `X'` are affine and `u`, `v` are
elementary étale neighbourhoods (étale, with trivial residue field extensions at `x'` and `t'`); (b)
`h` is smooth with geometrically irreducible fibres of dimension `d`; (c) `g` is finite and `x'` is
the only point of `X'_0` above `z'` (BL II §1, Thm 1.5 and the paragraph before it, p. 406: Lemma
1.4 applied to Raynaud–Gruson 1.1.1; conditions (b) and (c), p. 406). If `f` is smooth at `x` with
geometrically irreducible fibre of dimension `d`, take `X' = Z'` and `g = id` locally. For `f : X =
Spf O_K⟨ζ, ξ⟩/(ζξ − ϖ) → T = Spf O_K⟨ζ⟩` at `x = (ζ, ξ)`, `d = 1` (the fibre over `ζ = 0` is the
`ξ`-line), and one may take `Z' = D¹_T = Spf O_K⟨ζ, ξ⟩`, `g` the closed immersion and `h` the
projection, without étale localisation. *Needs:* *rg-zariski-local-structure*;
*smooth-lifting-from-level-zero*; *smooth-lifting-of-diagrams*; *formal-etale-site-invariance*;
*smooth-formal-scheme*; *admissible-formal-scheme*; *topological-generation-mod-definition-ideal*;
Mathlib `AlgebraicGeometry.IsFinite`.

**A smooth algebra with geometrically integral fibres is a projective module.**
(*rg-smooth-geometrically-integral-projective*) Let `A` be a commutative ring, not assumed
noetherian, and `B` a smooth `A`-algebra (Mathlib `Algebra.Smooth`: finitely presented and formally
smooth) all of whose fibres `B ⊗_A k(p)`, `p ∈ Spec A`, are geometrically integral (empty fibres
excluded). Prove that `B` is a projective `A`-module (Mathlib `Module.Projective`) (RG Première
partie, §3.3, Prop. 3.3.1 and its proof, p. 19, the noetherian reduction; BL II §1, after Thm 1.5,
p. 406, Bosch–Lütkebohmert's use of the proposition). `B = A[t_1, …, t_n]` is free on the monomials
and `B = A[t, t⁻¹]` is free on the `t^k`, `k ∈ ℤ`. The fibre hypothesis is needed: `B = k[u, u⁻¹]`
over `A = k[u]` is smooth with empty fibre over `u = 0`, and is not a projective `k[u]`-module (a
projective module over a principal ideal domain is free, and `k[u, u⁻¹]` is `u`-divisible). *Needs:*
Mathlib `Algebra.Smooth`, `Module.Projective`, `Algebra.Smooth.exists_finiteType`, `Module.Flat`.

**Smooth formal morphisms with geometrically irreducible fibres admit local topological bases.**
(*smooth-geometrically-irreducible-topological-basis*) Let `h : Z = Spf B → T = Spf A` be an affine
smooth surjective morphism of formal `O_K`-schemes locally of tf presentation whose fibres `Z ⊗
k(t)`, `t ∈ T_0`, are geometrically irreducible of one dimension `m`. Prove that every point of
`T_0` has an affine open neighbourhood `Spf A⟨a⁻¹⟩` over which `B⟨a⁻¹⟩ = B ⊗̂_A A⟨a⁻¹⟩` has a
topological basis `(e_i)_{i∈I}` over `A⟨a⁻¹⟩` in the sense of *topological-basis-lifting*; the basis
exists locally on `T` and may be infinite (BL II §1, Prop. 1.8(b), p. 406; its proof, p. 407: the
finitely generated case and the reduction to a connected noetherian base). This is the case `ℳ =
O_Z` of Bosch–Lütkebohmert II Proposition 1.8(b) used by the flattening proof: smooth surjective
morphisms with geometrically irreducible fibres are flat and pure (their Examples 1.7(c)); the
notion of purity is not needed here. For `B = A⟨ζ_1, …, ζ_m⟩` the monomials `ζ^ν` form a topological
basis; for `B = A⟨ζ, ζ⁻¹⟩` the `ζ^k`, `k ∈ ℤ`, do; for `m = 0` the fibres `Spec k(t)` force `Z_0 →
T_0` to be an isomorphism locally, with basis `{1}`. *Needs:*
*rg-smooth-geometrically-integral-projective*; *topological-basis-lifting*; *smooth-formal-scheme*;
*admissible-formal-scheme*; Mathlib `Module.Projective`, `Module.free_of_flat_of_isLocalRing`,
`Algebra.Smooth.exists_finiteType`, `Module.Flat`.

**Affine Checks for `IsSmoothGeomIrredAffine`.** The predicate itself is defined for any
ring map `A → B`, element `ϖ`, and dimension `n`: smoothness on all positive-power reductions,
and geometric irreducibility and dimension on the first reduction. Its formal applications
retain the complete rank-one base hypotheses.

- `smoothGeomIrred_test_identity` — `A = B = k`, `ϖ = 0`, `n = 0` satisfies it.
- `smoothGeomIrred_test_line` — `k → k[T]`, `ϖ = 0`, `n = 1` satisfies it.
- `smoothGeomIrred_test_split` — `k → k × k`, `ϖ = 0`, `n = 0` is smooth but fails it.

**Ideals of coefficients.** (*ideal-of-coefficients*) Let `h : Z → T` be a morphism of formal
`O_K`-schemes locally of tf presentation and `𝒥 ⊆ O_Z` a coherent ideal, with closed formal
subscheme `V(𝒥)` (locally `Spf(B/b)`, `b` finitely generated). A coherent ideal `𝒞 ⊆ O_T` is an
ideal of coefficients of `𝒥` if (i) the projection `Z ×_T V(𝒞) → Z` factors through `V(𝒥)`, and (ii)
for every morphism `T' → T` of formal `O_K`-schemes locally of tf presentation such that `Z ×_T T' →
Z` factors through `V(𝒥)`, the morphism `T' → T` factors through `V(𝒞)`. Equivalently: `𝒥 ⊆ 𝒞O_Z`,
`𝒞` is the smallest coherent ideal of `O_T` with this property, and this remains true after every
base change `T' → T`. Existence is not part of the definition (it is
*ideal-of-coefficients-existence* and *rig-ideal-of-coefficients-existence*); an ideal of
coefficients is not the ideal of the scheme-theoretic image and is not determined by the zero locus:
`(a², ϖ)` and `(a, ϖ)` have the same zero locus. In `FormalScheme`, define `IsIdealOfCoefficients`
as conditions (i) and (ii) for `h : Z → T` and coherent `𝒥 ⊆ O_Z`, `𝒞 ⊆ O_T`; prove
`IsIdealOfCoefficients.unique` (two ideals of coefficients of `𝒥` are equal),
`IsIdealOfCoefficients.le_map` (`𝒥 ⊆ 𝒞O_Z`, and `𝒞 ⊆ 𝒞'` for every coherent `𝒞' ⊆ O_T` with `𝒥O_{Z'} ⊆ 𝒞'O_{Z'}` after every base change), `IsIdealOfCoefficients.baseChange` (for `T' → T`, `𝒞O_{T'}` is
an ideal of coefficients of `𝒥O_{Z ×_T T'}`), `IsIdealOfCoefficients.restrict` (restriction to an
open `U ⊆ T` and to `h⁻¹(U)` preserves ideals of coefficients), `IsIdealOfCoefficients.glue` (ideals
of coefficients existing on the members of an open cover of `T` glue to one on `T`, by uniqueness),
`IsIdealOfCoefficients.mem_zeroLocus_iff` (under the affine topological-basis hypothesis of `isIdealOfCoefficients_of_topologicalBasis`, for `t ∈ T_0`: `t ∈ V(𝒞)` iff `𝒥O_{Z ⊗ k(t)} = 0`, equivalently the fibre map
`Z ⊗ k(t) → Z` factors through the closed formal subscheme `V(𝒥)`; for a
rig-point `t` of `T`: `t` factors through `V(𝒞)` iff `𝒥O_{Z_t} = 0` on the rigid fibre.
Thus the underlying set `V(𝒞) ∩ T_0` parametrises scheme-theoretic fibre containment;
containment of the underlying point sets is equivalent under the additional
hypothesis that the fibre is reduced.
The forward implications hold for every ideal of coefficients by (i)) and
`IsIdealOfCoefficients.isOpen` (if `𝒥` is open, `ϖ^N O_Z ⊆ 𝒥`, and `h` is faithfully flat, then `𝒞`
is open — Remark 2.2, which Bosch–Lütkebohmert state without the flatness hypothesis; some
hypothesis on `h` is needed, because `0` is an ideal of coefficients of the zero ideal for every
`h`, and the zero ideal of `O_Z` is open as soon as `ϖ^N O_Z = 0`: for `Z = Spf(A/ϖ) → T = Spf A`
with `A = O_K⟨a⟩`, `𝒥 = 0` is open and `𝒞 = 0` is not; `h` is surjective on points there, so
surjectivity does not suffice, while for faithfully flat `h` the map `O_T/𝒞 → h_*O_Z/𝒞O_Z` is
injective and `ϖ^N ∈ 𝒞`). Prove the affine formula
`isIdealOfCoefficients_of_topologicalBasis`: if `Z = Spf B → T = Spf A` and `B` has a topological
basis `(e_i)_{i∈I}` over `A` (*topological-basis-lifting*), and `b = (f_1, …, f_r)` with
`f_j = Σ_i a_{ij} e_i`, then the ideal `a = (a_{ij})` is contained in every ideal `c ⊆ A` with `b ⊆
Bc`, and is the ideal of coefficients of `b` whenever it is finitely generated. Define `content` as
`c(f) ⊆ A`, the ideal of coefficients of `fB` for `f ∈ B`, when it exists, and prove
`content_polynomial`: for `f = Σ a_i ξ^i ∈ A[ξ] ⊆ A⟨ξ⟩`, `c(f) = (a_0, …, a_n)` (the coordinate calculation above),
which is Mathlib's `Polynomial.contentIdeal f` for the polynomial `f`; the object of this target,
the ideal of coefficients of a coherent ideal of restricted power series along a formal morphism
with base change and rig-points, is not the polynomial content ideal. The same definitions apply on
generic fibres, to ideals of `B_K = B ⊗_{O_K} K` and `A_K` (coherent
ideals of `O_{Z_rig}`, `O_{T_rig}`), with rig-points in place of points (BL II §2, Def. 2.1, p. 407;
after Def. 2.1, p. 407, uniqueness, base change and the set-theoretic description; Rem. 2.2, p. 407,
openness). *Needs:* *admissible-formal-scheme*; *tfp-algebra-coherent*; *topological-basis-lifting*;
*flat-tft-is-tfp*; *rig-point*; *raynaud-generic-fibre*; *formal-fibre-product* (layer F0); Mathlib
`Polynomial.contentIdeal`.

**Checks.**

- `idealOfCoefficients_test_polynomial_core` (computation) — over `A = O_K` and `B = O_K⟨ξ⟩`, the content
  of `f = ϖ² + ϖξ + ϖ³ξ²` is `(ϖ)`.
- `idealOfCoefficients_test_unit_core` (degenerate) — for `h` surjective, the ideal of coefficients of `𝒥
  = O_Z` is `O_T`; for `h` faithfully flat and `𝒥 = 𝒜O_Z` with `𝒜 ⊆ O_T` coherent, it is `𝒜`.
- `idealOfCoefficients_test_baseChange` (compatibility) — for `Z = Spf O_K⟨a, ζ⟩ → T = Spf O_K⟨a⟩`
  and `𝒥 = (aζ, ϖ)`: `𝒞 = (a, ϖ)`; after the base change `a ↦ 0` to `T' = Spf O_K`, `𝒥' = (ϖ)` and
  `𝒞' = (ϖ) = 𝒞O_{T'}`.
- `idealOfCoefficients_test_notZeroLocus_core` (non-example) — for `A = O_K⟨a⟩`, `B = A⟨ζ⟩` and `𝒥 =
  (a²ζ, ϖ)`, `(a², ϖ)` is the ideal of coefficients and `(a, ϖ)` is not, although both have the same
  zero locus: the set of base points satisfying scheme-theoretic fibre containment
  does not determine the coefficient ideal.
- `idealOfCoefficients_test_dualNumbers` (negative control) — for `A = ℤ_p`,
  `B = A[ε]/(ε²)` and `𝒥 = (ε)`, the topological basis `(1, ε)` gives `𝒞 = A`,
  since the ε-coordinate is `1`; hence `V(𝒞) = ∅`. Every point of the special fibre
  belongs to the point-set zero locus of ε, but ε remains nonzero in
  `B ⊗_A 𝔽_p = 𝔽_p[ε]/(ε²)`. Thus `𝒥O_{Z_t} ≠ 0` and that fibre does not
  factor through `V(𝒥)`. No reduced-fibre hypothesis holds in this example.
- `idealOfCoefficients_test_isOpen_needsFlat_core` (non-example) — for `Z = Spf(A/ϖ) → T = Spf A`,
  `A = O_K⟨a⟩` (a closed immersion, surjective on points, not flat) and `𝒥 = 0`: `𝒥` is open
  (`ϖO_Z = 0`), its ideal of coefficients is `𝒞 = 0`, which is not open; Remark 2.2 needs the
  faithful flatness of `h`, and for `Z = ∅` the same `𝒞 = 0` occurs.

The affine Check `idealOfCoefficients_test_baseChange` uses
`IsIdealOfCoefficients_completed`: the evaluation maps preserve constants, send `a` to
zero and preserve `ζ`. They send the two displayed ideals to `(ϖ)` and retain the
completed-base-change coefficient property (BL II Definition 2.1, p. 407).

**Checks for `content_algebraic`.** The infimum is defined for any commutative algebra;
attainment is asserted only under additional hypotheses, such as freeness.

- `content_test_zero_one` — in `A[T]`, `c(0) = 0` and `c(1) = A`.
- `content_test_twoTerm` — `c(4 + 6T) = (2)` over `ℤ`, agreeing with `Polynomial.contentIdeal`.
- `content_test_nonfaithful` — for `ℤ → ℚ`, every nonzero ideal extends to the unit ideal,
  so `c(1) = ⋂_{n≥1}(n) = 0`, although `1 ∉ 0·ℚ`.

**Existence of ideals of coefficients for open ideals along smooth morphisms with geometrically
irreducible fibres.** (*ideal-of-coefficients-existence*) Let `h : Z → T` be a quasi-compact
morphism of formal `O_K`-schemes locally of tf presentation that is, locally on `T`, affine, smooth
and surjective with geometrically irreducible fibres of constant dimension. Prove (a) that every
open coherent ideal `𝒥 ⊆ O_Z` (`ϖ^N O_Z ⊆ 𝒥`) has an ideal of coefficients in `O_T`
(*ideal-of-coefficients*), and that it is open; in the affine case `Z = Spf B → T = Spf A` with a
topological basis `(e_i)` of `B` over `A` and `𝒥 ↔ b = (f_1, …, f_r)`, it is the ideal `a = (a_{ij})` of coordinates `f_j = Σ_i a_{ij} e_i`, which is finitely generated. Prove (b) that if `T =
Spf R` with `R` a complete valuation ring of height one (`R = O_L`, `L/K` finite), every finitely
generated ideal `b ⊆ B`, open or not, has an ideal of coefficients, generated by the coordinate of
largest absolute value of each generator; in particular every content `c(f)` is principal.
Part (a) is BL II §2, Prop. 2.3(b), p. 407, with proof on p. 408. Part (b) is the following
coordinate argument, not a separate valuation-ring clause of that proposition: choose a
topological basis over the local ring `R`; the coefficients of each generator tend to zero,
so a nonzero family has a coefficient of maximal absolute value. All other coefficients are
divisible by it. Thus the coordinate ideal is principal and closed, and the basis argument
of BL II, proof of Prop. 2.3(a), p. 408, gives its universal property. The algebraic
core `content_isPrincipal_algebraic` uses an ordinary free basis, hence finite expansions;
the completed-basis assertion in (b) is a separate formal target. Bosch–Lütkebohmert state (a) more generally for affine pure flat morphisms and for flat
morphisms with geometrically irreducible fibres without embedded components; only the smooth case is
used. For `Z = Spf O_K⟨a, ζ⟩ → T = Spf O_K⟨a⟩` and `𝒥 = (aζ + ϖ, ϖ²)` the coordinates are `ϖ, a,
ϖ²`, so `𝒞 = (a, ϖ)`; over `R = O_K`, `c(ϖ + ϖ²ζ + ζ²) = O_K` and `c(ϖ³ζ + ϖ²) = (ϖ²)`. *Needs:*
*ideal-of-coefficients*; *smooth-geometrically-irreducible-topological-basis*;
*topological-basis-lifting*; *flat-tft-is-tfp*; *admissible-formal-scheme*.

**Ideals of coefficients on generic fibres, and openness when the rigid ideal of coefficients is the
unit ideal.** (*rig-ideal-of-coefficients-existence*) Let `h : Z = Spf B → T = Spf A` be an affine
smooth surjective morphism of admissible formal `O_K`-schemes (`A`, `B` without `ϖ`-torsion) with
geometrically irreducible fibres of constant dimension, and assume `B` has a topological basis
`(e_i)` over `A` (true locally on `T`, *smooth-geometrically-irreducible-topological-basis*). Prove
(i) that every ideal `b_K ⊆ B_K = B ⊗_{O_K} K` has an ideal of coefficients `a_K ⊆ A_K` in the rigid
sense of *ideal-of-coefficients*: with `b = b_K ∩ B`, finitely generated, and `a = (a_{ij})` the
coordinate ideal of generators of `b`, `a_K = aA_K` is finitely generated and is the smallest ideal
of `A_K` with `b_K ⊆ a_K B_K`, compatibly with base change along rig-points (`a` itself need not be
finitely generated); and (ii) that if `b ⊆ B` is finitely generated, not necessarily open, and `A_K`
is the ideal of coefficients of `bB_K`, then `b` has an ideal of coefficients, and it is open (BL II
§2, proof of Prop. 2.3(b), p. 408, parts (i) and (ii)). For `A = O_K⟨a⟩`, `B = A⟨ζ⟩` and `b = (aζ −
1)`, the coordinates `−1, a` generate `A`, so `b` has the open ideal of coefficients `A`; for `b =
(aζ)` the rigid ideal of coefficients is `aA_K ≠ A_K` and the ideal of coefficients `(a)` of `b` is
not open, so the hypothesis of (ii) is needed. *Needs:* *ideal-of-coefficients-existence*;
*ideal-of-coefficients*; *saturated-submodule-finitely-generated*; *flat-tft-is-tfp*;
*raynaud-generic-fibre*.

`FormalScheme.exists_rigIdealOfCoefficients` states (i) for the same complete rank-one
base, admissible algebras, smooth geometrically irreducible reductions of constant
dimension, and topological basis. It contracts an arbitrary `b_K` to `J ⊆ B` and
concludes that `J` and `a_K = (b.coefficientIdeal (J.restrictScalars A))A_K` are
finitely generated, that `b_K ⊆ a_K B_K`, and that `a_K ⊆ a'` whenever
`b_K ⊆ a' B_K`. The generic rings are localizations at the structural image of `ϖ`.
For each closed rig-point presented by a surjection `A → A'` with `A'` an
admissible domain of dimension one, put `C = A' ⊗̂_A B`. The theorem also states,
for every ideal `c' ⊆ A'_K`, that `J C_K ⊆ c' C_K` iff `a A'_K ⊆ c'`.
Thus the extended coefficient ideal has the same least-ideal property on the
completed rigid fibre. No finite-generation hypothesis on `a ⊆ A` is imposed
(BL II §2, Def. 2.1, p. 407, and Prop. 2.3(b), proof p. 408).
`FormalScheme.coefficientIdeal_open_of_generic_unit` states (ii): for finitely
generated `J`, unit generic coefficient ideal implies finite generation and
openness of its integral coordinate ideal, which satisfies
`IsIdealOfCoefficients_completed` (BL II Prop. 2.3(b), proof p. 408).

**Checks for generic coefficient ideals.**

- `exists_rigIdealOfCoefficients_zero` — when `B → B_K` is injective, the zero
  generic ideal contracts to zero and has zero coefficient ideal.
- `exists_rigIdealOfCoefficients_unit` — a nonempty topological basis gives the
  unit coefficient ideal for the unit generic ideal.
- `exists_rigIdealOfCoefficients_identity` — for the one-element basis `1` of
  `A` over itself, contracting any ideal of `A_K` and extending its coordinate
  ideal recovers that ideal exactly, including nonradical ideals.

The affine completed predicate `IsIdealOfCoefficients_completed O_K ϖ J c` requires `J`
and `c` finitely generated and tests the coefficient condition after every tfp base change
`A → A'` and every finitely generated ideal `c' ⊆ A'`. Its tensor product is completed for
`ϖ`; the maps from `B` and `A'` are the canonical maps into that completion.
`isIdealOfCoefficients_of_topologicalBasis_completed` identifies it with
`b.coefficientIdeal (J.restrictScalars A)` when that ideal is finitely generated.
`coefficientIdeal_fg_of_open` supplies finite generation for an open finitely generated `J`.
Both retain the complete rank-one base, tfp hypotheses on `A` and `B`, and a topological
basis of `B` over `A` (BL II Prop. 2.3(b), proof pp. 407–408). For coherent ideals on formal schemes the same condition uses sheaf pullback, with
restriction and gluing as specified above.

**Checks for completed coefficient ideals.**

- `completedCoefficients_test_zero` — zero is a coefficient ideal of the zero ideal,
  including an empty source.
- `completedCoefficients_test_identity` — under the identity formal morphism, every
  finitely generated ideal is its own coefficient ideal.
- `completedCoefficients_test_thickening` — under the identity of `Spf O_K`, the ideal
  `(ϖ²)` has coefficient ideal `(ϖ²)`, not `(ϖ)`, although the two ideals have the same radical.

**A function vanishing on no fibre is a non-zero-divisor at every level.**
(*nonvanishing-on-fibres-nonzerodivisor-levels*) Let `h : Z = Spf B → T = Spf A` be a smooth
surjective morphism of formal schemes locally of tf presentation over a complete valuation ring `R`
of height one (`R = O_K`, or `R = O_L` for a finite extension `L/K`, as needed after base change to
rig-points) whose fibres `Z ⊗ k(t)`, `t ∈ T_0`, are geometrically irreducible of one dimension `m`,
and let `f ∈ B` be an element that does not vanish identically on any fibre of `Z_0 → T_0`; no
torsion hypothesis is made on `A`. Prove that for every `λ ∈ ℕ` the image of `f` in `B_λ = B/ϖ^{λ+1}B` is a non-zero-divisor (BL II §2, Lem. 2.5(a) and its proof, p. 409: the reduction to the
case with a section). For `B = A⟨ζ⟩` and `f = ζ`, `ζ` vanishes on no fibre and is a non-zero-divisor
on every `A_λ[ζ]`. Vanishing on a whole fibre can make `f` a zero-divisor: for `A = O_K⟨a, b⟩/(ab)`
(admissible), `B = A⟨ζ⟩` and `f = a`, `f` vanishes on the fibres over `{a = 0}` and `a·b = 0` in
every `B_λ`. *Needs:* *smooth-formal-scheme*; *admissible-formal-scheme*; Mathlib
`Algebra.Smooth.exists_finiteType`, `Algebra.Smooth.flat`, `associatedPrimes`, `IsSMulRegular`.

**A function vanishing on no fibre is a non-zero-divisor.**
(*nonvanishing-on-fibres-nonzerodivisor*) In the situation of
*nonvanishing-on-fibres-nonzerodivisor-levels* (a smooth surjective morphism `h : Z = Spf B → T =
Spf A` of formal schemes locally of tf presentation over a complete valuation ring `R` of height
one, with geometrically irreducible fibres of one dimension `m`, and `f ∈ B` vanishing identically
on no fibre of `Z_0 → T_0`), prove that `f` is a non-zero-divisor on `B` (BL II §2, proof of Lem.
2.5(b), p. 409). The passage from the levels to `B` uses only that `B` is `ϖ`-adically separated
(automatic for `B` of tf presentation, and the hypothesis of the stated form
`isSMulRegular_of_ne_zero_on_fibres_affine`): if `fg = 0` then `g ∈ ϖ^{λ+1}B` for every `λ`.
`isSMulRegular_test_of_levels` is a hypothesis check for this separatedness step:
regularity on every positive-power quotient implies regularity in a separated ring.
For `B = A⟨ζ⟩`, `ζ − a` is a non-zero-divisor for every `a ∈ A`; the fibre condition is needed,
as the non-example of *nonvanishing-on-fibres-nonzerodivisor-levels* shows.
*Needs:* *nonvanishing-on-fibres-nonzerodivisor-levels*; *topologically-finitely-presented-algebra*;
*flat-tft-is-tfp*; Mathlib `IsSMulRegular`.

**Hartogs-type extension across subsets of the special fibre of smaller relative dimension.**
(*smooth-geometrically-irreducible-extension*) Let `h : Z = Spf B → T = Spf A` be a smooth
surjective morphism of formal schemes locally of tf presentation over a complete valuation ring `R`
of height one (`R = O_K`, or `R = O_L` for `L/K` finite, as needed after base change to rig-points)
whose fibres `Z ⊗ k(t)`, `t ∈ T_0`, are geometrically irreducible of one dimension `m`; assume `A`
has no `ϖ`-torsion, and let `Y_0 ⊆ Z_0` be a closed subscheme with `dim(Y_0/T_0) < m` (every fibre
of `Y_0 → T_0` has dimension `< m`). Prove that the restriction map `Γ(Spec B, O) → Γ(Spec B ∖ Y_0,
O)` is bijective, `Spec B` being the ordinary spectrum and `Y_0 ⊆ V(ϖ) ⊆ Spec B` (BL II §2, proof of
Lem. 2.5(c), p. 409: injectivity, and the reduction of surjectivity to a statement modulo `ϖ`). For
`Z = Spf O_K⟨ζ⟩ → T = Spf O_K` and `Y_0` the point `ζ = 0` of the special fibre (dimension `0 < 1`),
functions on `Spec O_K⟨ζ⟩ ∖ Y_0` extend. The dimension hypothesis is needed: for `Y_0 = V(ϖ)`
(dimension `1 = m`), `Γ(Spec O_K⟨ζ⟩ ∖ V(ϖ), O) = K⟨ζ⟩ ≠ O_K⟨ζ⟩`. The algebraic Hartogs lemma for
coherent sheaves on locally noetherian schemes, with the depth-`≥ 2` hypothesis, is
SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 0 (§0.6); this target is the non-noetherian form
over a rank-one valuation ring, with the relative fibre dimension of `Y_0` in place of depth.
*Needs:*
*nonvanishing-on-fibres-nonzerodivisor-levels*; *smooth-formal-scheme*; *admissible-formal-scheme*;
*topologically-finitely-presented-algebra*.

`isSMulRegular_of_ne_zero_on_fibres_levels` states the all-level affine conclusion:
for `IsSmoothGeomIrredAffine ϖ n` and `f` nonzero on every fibre over a prime containing `ϖ`,
its image in `B/ϖ^{λ+1}B` is regular for every `λ ≥ 0`. Separatedness is needed only for the
subsequent conclusion in `B`. The Check `nonzerodivisorLevels_test_parameter` takes
`B = ℤ_p`, `f = p`: modulo `p` it is zero and is not regular, so the fibre condition
cannot be omitted (BL II Lem. 2.5(a), p. 409).

**Contents are homogeneous.** (*content-ideal-smul*) Let `h : Z = Spf B → T = Spf R` be a smooth
surjective morphism of formal schemes locally of tf presentation over a complete valuation ring `R`
of height one, with base `T = Spf R` itself, whose fibres are geometrically irreducible of one
dimension `m`, so that contents exist by *ideal-of-coefficients-existence* (b). Prove that for `f ∈
B` and `a ∈ R`, `c(af) = a·c(f)` (BL II §2, Lem. 2.6, p. 409, its hypotheses; proof of Lem. 2.6(a),
p. 410). Bosch–Lütkebohmert also allow `A` noetherian; the flattening proof uses the valuation-ring
case, at rig-points. For `B = O_K⟨ζ⟩` and `f = 1 + ζ`, `c(f) = O_K` and `c(ϖf) = (ϖ)`; for `a =
0`, `c(0) = 0 = (0)·c(f)`. The form `content_smul_algebraic` is more general: for `B` free
over any commutative ring `R` and the content taken as the ideal generated by the coordinates,
`c(af) = (a)·c(f)` holds with no hypothesis on `R`. For polynomials the product inequalities used in
the next two targets are Mathlib's `Polynomial.contentIdeal_mul_le_mul_contentIdeal`,
`Polynomial.mul_contentIdeal_le_radical_contentIdeal_mul` and
`Polynomial.contentIdeal_mul_eq_top_of_contentIdeal_eq_top`; here the content is taken on restricted
power series along a smooth formal morphism and is principal by *ideal-of-coefficients-existence* (b),
which is what makes the product formula an equality. *Needs:*
*ideal-of-coefficients-existence*; *ideal-of-coefficients*;
*smooth-geometrically-irreducible-topological-basis*.

**Multiplying by a function vanishing on no fibre does not change contents.**
(*content-ideal-nonvanishing-factor*) In the setting of *content-ideal-smul* (smooth surjective `Z =
Spf B → Spf R` with geometrically irreducible fibres, `R` a complete valuation ring of height one),
let `f ∈ B` vanish identically on no fibre of `Z_0 → T_0`. Prove that `c(fg) = c(g)` for every `g ∈
B` (BL II §2, proof of Lem. 2.6(b), p. 410: the easy inclusion, and the converse via Lemma 2.5). For
`B = O_K⟨ζ⟩`, `f = ζ` and `g = ϖ + ϖ²ζ`, `c(fg) = c(ϖζ + ϖ²ζ²) = (ϖ) = c(g)`. *Needs:*
*ideal-of-coefficients*; *nonvanishing-on-fibres-nonzerodivisor*; *ideal-of-coefficients-existence*.

**Contents are multiplicative when one factor has principal content.** (*content-ideal-product*) In
the setting of *content-ideal-smul* (smooth surjective `Z = Spf B → T = Spf R` with geometrically
irreducible fibres, `R` a complete valuation ring of height one, where every content is principal by
*ideal-of-coefficients-existence* (b)), prove that for `f_1, f_2 ∈ B`, `c(f_1 f_2) = c(f_1)·c(f_2)`;
the hypothesis used is that `c(f_1)` is principal (BL II §2, proof of Lem. 2.6(c), p. 410: the key
step and conclusion). This is Gauss's lemma for restricted power series: in `O_K⟨ζ⟩`, `c(f)` is
generated by a coefficient of maximal absolute value, and `c(fg) = c(f)c(g)` says `|fg| = |f||g|`
for the Gauss norm; for instance `c(ϖζ·(1 + ζ)) = (ϖ) = c(ϖζ)c(1 + ζ)`. *Needs:*
*content-ideal-smul*; *content-ideal-nonvanishing-factor*; *ideal-of-coefficients*;
*ideal-of-coefficients-existence*; Mathlib `Polynomial.contentIdeal_mul_le_mul_contentIdeal`,
`Polynomial.mul_contentIdeal_le_radical_contentIdeal_mul`,
`Polynomial.contentIdeal_mul_eq_top_of_contentIdeal_eq_top`.

**Fibres over the generic fibre of the base are integral.**
(*smooth-geometrically-irreducible-generic-fibres-integral*) Let `h : Z = Spf B → T = Spf A` be a
smooth surjective morphism of admissible formal `O_K`-schemes whose fibres `Z ⊗ k(t)`, `t ∈ T_0`,
are geometrically irreducible of constant dimension `m`. Prove that for every prime `p ⊆ A` with `ϖ
∉ p` (a point of `Spec A_K`), `pB` is a prime ideal of `B` lying over `p`; it is the generic point
of the fibre of `Spec B → Spec A` over `p`, and that fibre is irreducible and reduced. Over primes
containing `ϖ` the fibres are those of `Z_0 → T_0`, geometrically irreducible by hypothesis and
reduced because `h` is smooth, hence geometrically integral, so all
fibres of `Spec B → Spec A` are irreducible and reduced (BL II §2, Prop. 2.4(a), p. 408; its proof,
p. 410: the classical rigid case is proved on rig-points, with the choice of the rig-point). For `A
= O_K⟨a⟩`, `B = A⟨ζ⟩` and `p = (a − ϖ)`, `pB` is prime with `B/pB ≅ O_K⟨ζ⟩`. The hypotheses cannot
be dropped: for `B = A⟨ζ⟩/(ζ² − a)` (finite flat over `A = O_K⟨a⟩`, residue characteristic `≠ 2`;
not smooth along `a = 0` and with geometrically reducible fibres over `a ≠ 0` in `T_0`) and `p = (a
− ϖ²)`, `B/pB = O_K⟨ζ⟩/((ζ − ϖ)(ζ + ϖ))` is not a domain. *Needs:*
*rig-ideal-of-coefficients-existence*; *content-ideal-product*; *ideal-of-coefficients*;
*affinoid-jacobson* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R0); *rig-point*; *flat-tft-is-tfp*; *smooth-formal-scheme*;
*admissible-formal-scheme*; *raynaud-generic-fibre*.

**Associated primes of B are generic points of fibres over the generic fibre.**
