### R2.8 formal completions of schemes and the good-reduction locus

This subsection compares the generic fibre of the formal completion of a scheme with the
analytification of its generic fibre: Huber's morphism `σ` and the comparison `φ` of his Proposition
1.9.6, its specialisation to models over `O_K` (the image of `φ` is the locus of good reduction, and
`φ` is an isomorphism for proper models), and the converse for flat quasi-projective models.

**Formal completion of a scheme, the morphism `σ: d(X̂) → X` and the comparison `φ: d(X̂) → X ×_Y d(Ŷ)`.** (*formal-completion-and-algebraic-comparison*) (1.9.4) For a scheme `X` and its formal
completion `X̂` along a closed subscheme defined by an ideal of finite type — the formal scheme of
the thickening system `(X_n)` of *colimit-of-thickenings* (layer F0), which for locally noetherian
`X` is *formal-completion* (layer F0) and on the scheme side is SchemeAndStackFoundations
Layer 4 (§4.8); no noetherian hypothesis on `X` is made here — assumed of type (S),
prove that there is a natural
morphism of locally ringed spaces `σ_X : d(X̂) → X`, the unique one such that for every open `U ⊆
X`, with `e = (X̂ → X) ∘ λ`, one has `e⁻¹(U) ⊆ σ⁻¹(U)` and `e* = σ*` on `O_X(U)`. (1.9.5) Let `f : X
→ Y` be locally of finite type between schemes, `Y' ⊆ Y` closed and defined by a quasi-coherent
ideal of finite type, `X' = X ×_Y Y'`, and `X̂`, `Ŷ` the completions along `X'` and `Y'`. Prove that
if `Ŷ` is of type (S) then so is `X̂`, that `f̂` is adic, and that the square formed by `σ_X`,
`σ_Y`, `d(f̂)` and `f` induces a `d(Ŷ)`-morphism `φ : d(X̂) → X ×_Y d(Ŷ)` into the fibre product of
a scheme locally of finite type with an adic space (*scheme-fibre-product-analytification*, AdicSpacesPartII layer
R1). Prove Proposition 1.9.6: (i) `φ` is a local isomorphism; (ii) if `f` is separated, `φ` is
injective; (iii) if `f` is universally specializing (e.g. universally closed, e.g. proper), `φ` is
surjective; hence if `f` is separated and universally specializing, `φ` is an isomorphism (Huber96
§1.9.4–1.9.5 and Prop. 1.9.6, p. 98, the construction and its geometric properties; Huber94
§4, Rem. 4.6(iv), p. 544, the noetherian version with `t` in place of `d`, stated without proof).
The hypotheses are: `X̂` (resp. `Ŷ`) of type (S); the ideal defining `Y'` of finite type; `f`
locally of finite type; (ii) requires `f` separated and (iii) requires `f` universally specializing.
`σ` and the fibre product `X ×_Y d(Ŷ)` come from Huber 1994 Huber94 Rem. 4.6(iv), [Hu4, 3.10.7] and
Huber94 Prop. 3.8; The completions `X̂`, `Ŷ` and the morphism `f̂` are formed by
*colimit-of-thickenings* and *morphisms-as-compatible-systems-finite-ideal-type* (layer F0), since
`Y` is allowed to be `Spec O_K` with `O_K` non-noetherian. For `X = A¹_{O_K} → Y = Spec O_K` (not
proper), `φ` identifies `d(X̂)` with the closed unit disc inside the adic affine line over `Spa(K,
O_K)`: a local isomorphism which is injective but not surjective; for `X` proper over `Y`, `d(X̂) ≅
X ×_Y d(Ŷ)`. *Needs:* *generic-fibre-functor-d*; *formal-schemes-of-type-S*; *specialisation-map*;
*scheme-fibre-product-analytification* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R1); *colimit-of-thickenings*,
*morphisms-as-compatible-systems-finite-ideal-type* (layer F0), and *formal-completion* (layer F0)
when `X` is locally noetherian; Mathlib `AlgebraicGeometry.IsSeparated`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.UniversallyClosed.eq_valuativeCriterion`, `AlgebraicGeometry.ValuativeCriterion`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.IsSeparated.valuativeCriterion`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.ValuativeCriterion.Existence.eq`.

The general targets use `FormalScheme.idealCompletion X I hI`, with `I` a
quasi-coherent ideal locally of finite type; `Y'` is `I.subscheme` and its inverse
image is defined by Mathlib's `I.comap f`. No noetherian or valuation-base
hypothesis is imposed. `idealCompletion.comap_finiteType` supplies finite
generation on `X`. `idealCompletion.map`, `idealCompletion.map_toScheme` and
`idealCompletion.map_isAdic` specify the induced morphism and its completion
square; `idealCompletion.isTypeS_comap` supplies type (S) on the source from
local finite type of `f` and type (S) on the target completion (Huber96 1.9.5,
p. 98).

`formalCompletionSigma` and `formalCompletionSigma_characterization` give `σ` and
its uniqueness by the inverse-image inclusion and equality of restricted
section maps above; `formalCompletionSigma_naturality` gives its square with
`d(f̂)` (Huber96 1.9.4–1.9.5, p. 98). The target of
`formalCompletionComparison` is the space of Part II's imported `SchemePullback`.
`formalCompletionComparison_exists` gives existence of that fibre product, and
`formalCompletionComparison_projections` fixes both projections of `φ`.
`formalCompletionComparison.isOpenImmersion_local` gives an open neighbourhood
of each source point on which `φ` is an open immersion;
`formalCompletionComparison.injective_of_isSeparated` requires separatedness;
`formalCompletionComparison.surjective_of_universallySpecializing` requires
`(AlgebraicGeometry.topologically @SpecializingMap).universally f`.
`formalCompletionComparison.isIso_of_isSeparated_of_universallySpecializing`
combines these two hypotheses, and
`formalCompletionComparison.isIso_of_isProper` is the proper case
(Huber96 Proposition 1.9.6, p. 98). The valuation-base statement
`idealCompletion_goodReduction` identifies the image of this comparison with
the integral locus.

**Checks for the constructions.**

- `idealCompletion.map_identity`: completion sends the identity to the identity,
  with the canonical equality of pulled-back ideals.
- `idealCompletion.map_emptyCentre`: a unit pulled-back ideal gives a completion
  morphism with empty image.
- `idealCompletion.map_nilpotent`: a nilpotent centre gives back the scheme, and
  the completion morphism agrees with `f` through the completion maps.
- `formalCompletionSigma_emptyCentre`: the unit ideal gives an empty generic
  fibre and an empty image for `σ`.
- `formalCompletionSigma_nilpotent`: even though completion at a nilpotent ideal
  gives the original scheme with discrete topology, its analytic generic fibre
  and `σ`'s image are empty.
- `formalCompletionSigma_specialization`: `σ(z)` specializes to the image of `λ(z)`
  under the completion map; the order of these two points is fixed.
- `formalCompletionComparison_identity`: the comparison for the identity is an
  isomorphism and its base projection is the identity.
- `formalCompletionComparison_proper`: every proper `f` gives an isomorphism.
- `formalCompletionComparison_emptyCentre`: a unit pulled-back ideal gives
  `IsEmpty (genericFibre (idealCompletion …)).obj`; `φ` is surjective exactly when
  the mixed fibre product is empty. This is also `formalCompletion_test_emptyCentre`.
- `formalCompletionComparison_affineLine`: over `ℤ_p`, `φ` is an open immersion
  with image `|T| ≤ 1` and is not surjective, as in `formalCompletion_test_affineLine`.
- `formalCompletionComparison_doubledPoint`: over a complete nontrivially valued
  rank-one field `K`, glue two copies of `Spec O_K[T]` along `D(ϖ) ∪ D(T)`,
  using the scheme pushout, where `ϖ` is nonzero and topologically nilpotent.
  The resulting nonseparated morphism has noninjective `φ` with image `{|T| ≤ 1}`,
  as in `formalCompletion_test_doubledPoint`. The check constructs the
  folding map `r : X → A¹_{O_K}`, fixes its restriction to each chart as the
  identity, and states the image equality using the stalk valuation of the
  coordinate pulled back along `P.snd ≫ r`. This includes `O_K = ℤ_p`, `ϖ = p`.

**Checks.**

- `formalCompletion_test_affineLine` (computation) — `X = A¹_{O_K} → Y = Spec O_K`, `Y' = V(ϖ)`:
  `φ` is the open immersion of the closed unit disc `{|T| ≤ 1}` into `A^{1,ad}_K`, injective and
  not surjective; the type-1 point `T = ϖ⁻¹` is not in the image.
- `formalCompletion_test_emptyCentre` (degenerate) — if `X' = X ×_Y Y' = ∅` (for `Y = Spec O_K`:
  `ϖ` invertible on `X`, e.g. `X = Spec K`), the completion along the empty closed subset is the
  empty formal scheme, `d(X̂) = ∅`, and `φ : ∅ → X ×_Y d(Ŷ)` is a local isomorphism and injective;
  it is surjective iff `X ×_Y d(Ŷ) = ∅`, and for `X = Spec K → Spec O_K` (not universally
  specializing) the target `Spa(K, O_K)` is nonempty, so (iii) fails as it must.
- `formalCompletion_test_doubledPoint` (non-example) — `X` the affine line over `O_K` with the
  origin `x₀` of the special fibre doubled (not separated; `X_K = A¹_K` is separated):
  the two formal charts meet along `D(T)`, whose generic fibre is `{|T| = 1}`.
  Thus `d(X̂)` is the closed unit disc with the closed, non-open set
  `λ⁻¹(x₀) = {|T| < 1}` doubled. This set contains `η_{1⁻}`, for which
  `|T|^m > |ϖ|` for every positive integer `m`; it is strictly larger than the
  open residue disc `⋃_{m≥1}{|T|^m ≤ |ϖ|}` of `tube_test_preimage_not_open`.
  The comparison `φ` is a surjective local isomorphism onto `{|T| ≤ 1}` and is
  not injective, so (ii) needs `f` separated. The check states
  `¬ Function.Injective φ.hom.base` and `Set.range φ.hom.base = {|T| ≤ 1}`
  on the imported `AdicSpace.SchemePullback` carrier. The gluing description
  follows from Huber96 (1.9.1), p. 97, and (1.9.3)–(1.9.6), p. 98; the
  rank-two valuation is described in Wedhorn Example 7.57(5), p. 72.

**The generic fibre of the completion of an `O_K`-scheme is the integral (good-reduction) locus of the
analytified generic fibre.** (*good-reduction-locus*) Let `K` be complete of nontrivial rank one,
discreteness not assumed, `X` a separated `O_K`-scheme locally of finite type, `X_K` its generic
fibre and `X_K^ad = X ×_{Spec O_K} Spa(K, O_K)` its adic analytification, Huber's fibre product of
*analytification-functor* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R1). Let `X̂` be the `ϖ`-adic completion of `X`, a formal
`O_K`-scheme locally of tf type, of type (S). Prove that the comparison map `φ_X : d(X̂) → X_K^ad`
of *formal-completion-and-algebraic-comparison* (with `Y = Spec O_K`, `Y' = V(ϖ)`) is an open
embedding, whose image is the integral locus `X_K^{ad,int} := {x ∈ X_K^ad : the morphism Spec κ(x) → X extends to Spec κ(x)⁺ → X}`, `κ(x)` the completed residue field and `κ(x)⁺` its valuation ring;
that under `φ_X` the specialisation `λ(x) ∈ X_s` of `x ∈ d(X̂)` is the image of the closed point of
that extension; that if `X` is proper over `O_K`, `φ_X` is an isomorphism `d(X̂) ≅ X_K^ad`; and that
a classical point of `X_K^ad` (residue field `K'` finite over `K`) lies in the integral locus iff it
extends to an `O_{K'}`-point of `X` (Huber96 §1.9, Prop. 1.9.6, p. 98, specialised to `Y = Spec
O_K`; Conrad-AWS §3.3, Ex. 3.3.9, pp. 32–33, the rigid-analytic form over any complete rank-one `R`;
Huber94 §4, Rem. 4.6(iv)(a), p. 544, the description of the image of `φ` by specialisations to
trivially valued points in the noetherian case). The converse 'image `= X_K^ad` implies proper'
needs flatness and is *good-reduction-locus-properness-converse*. For `X = A¹_{O_K}` the image is
the closed unit disc `{|T| ≤ 1} ⊂ A^{1,ad}_K`, not all of it; for `X = G_{m,O_K} = Spec O_K[T, T⁻¹]`
the image is `{|T| = 1}`; for `X = P¹_{O_K}`, `φ` is an isomorphism `d(P̂¹) ≅ P^{1,ad}_K`, and more
generally for `P = P̂ⁿ`, `P_K ≅ P^{n,ad}_K`, the form the rigid-cohomology roadmap uses; for a
smooth proper curve `X` over `O_K` (`K` finite over `ℚ_p`), `d(X̂) = X_K^ad` and `λ` is the
specialisation to `X_k`, the form used for Coleman integration. *Needs:* *formal-completion-and-algebraic-comparison*;
*formal-schemes-of-type-S*; *generic-fibre-functor-d*; *specialisation-map*;
*colimit-of-thickenings* (layer F0); *analytification-functor* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R1);
*rigid-analytification-comparison* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R1); Mathlib `AlgebraicGeometry.IsSeparated`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper`, `AlgebraicGeometry.UniversallyClosed.eq_valuativeCriterion`.

`FormalScheme.idealThickeningSystem` forms the powers of any locally finitely
generated ideal; `idealCompletion` is their formal colimit. Its map
`idealCompletion.toScheme` is characterized by `idealCompletion.toScheme_ι`.
This construction supplies the completion carrier over nondiscrete valuation rings.
`idealCompletion_goodReduction` states the open image and properness assertion;
its affine boundedness condition expresses extension to the valuation ring.

**Checks for ideal completion.**


- `idealThickeningSystem_square` — level one is exactly Mathlib's closed subscheme defined by the square of the ideal sheaf.

- `idealThickeningSystem_nilpotent`, `idealCompletion_nilpotent`,
  `idealCompletion.toScheme_nilpotent` — a nilpotent ideal has eventually constant
  thickenings and completion is the original scheme; the statement explicitly identifies each sufficiently high term of `idealThickeningSystem` with that scheme.
- `idealThickeningSystem_unit`, `idealCompletion_unit`,
  `idealCompletion.toScheme_unit` — the unit ideal gives empty thickenings and empty completion.
- `idealThickeningSystem_noetherian`, `idealCompletion_noetherian`,
  `idealCompletion.toScheme_noetherian` — for a noetherian scheme and the ideal of a
  closed subset, this is the earlier completion, including its map to the scheme, and the terms of `idealThickeningSystem` equal those of `schemeThickeningSystem`.

`AlgebraicGeometry.IsQuasiProjective b`, for `b : X → Spec R`, means that for some
finite `n` there is a quasi-compact scheme immersion `i : X → Pⁿ_R` with
`i ≫ projectiveSpace.toSpec R n = b`. The projective space and structural map are
imported from Part II and use Mathlib's homogeneous-polynomial `Proj`.
`AlgebraicGeometry.IsQuasiProjective.finiteType_and_isSeparated` states that every
such morphism is of finite type and separated: these properties hold for projective
space over `R` and are preserved by a quasi-compact immersion (Part II,
`AdicSpace.projectiveSpace.locallyOfFiniteType`; Mathlib,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Proj.isSeparated` and the quasi-compactness instance in
`Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/ProjectiveSpectrum/Proper.lean`, §§IsSeparated and
QuasiCompact; the finite-type immersion instance in
`Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Morphisms/Immersion.lean`).

**Checks for `IsQuasiProjective`.**

- `IsQuasiProjective_identity` — `Spec R → Spec R` embeds into `P⁰_R`.
- `IsQuasiProjective_empty` — every empty scheme over `Spec R` is quasi-projective.
- `IsQuasiProjective_affineLine` — `A¹_R → Spec R` is quasi-projective but not proper
  for every nonzero commutative ring `R`; quasi-projectivity does not imply properness.
- `IsQuasiProjective_notSeparated` — a morphism that is not separated cannot admit
  the required immersion (for example, the affine line with doubled origin over a field).

**If the completion's generic fibre is all of the analytified generic fibre, a flat quasi-projective
model is proper.** (*good-reduction-locus-properness-converse*)
`FormalScheme.goodReductionLocus_eq_univ_iff_isProper` states that, over a complete
rank-one valuation ring `O_K` with nonzero nonunit pseudouniformizer `ϖ`, a flat
quasi-projective `O_K`-scheme `X` is proper if and only if its good-reduction locus
is all of `X_K^ad`. In particular this applies to integral `X`; irreducibility and
reducedness are not needed. Quasi-projectivity supplies finite type and separatedness,
and flatness supplies finite presentation. The set is exactly the affine
boundedness locus identified with `image φ_X` by `idealCompletion_goodReduction`:
the analytic point lies over an affine open of `X` and every section there has
valuation at most one. The generic fibre is specified by a scheme pullback along
`O_K → K = O_K[1/ϖ]`; its analytification uses Part II's `SchemePullback` over
`Spa(K, O_K)`, with the continuous coefficient map and the integral subring fixed.
Thus the equality of sets is equivalent to surjectivity of `φ_X : d(X̂) → X_K^ad`.
FK Ch. 0, §9.2(a), Cor. 9.2.3, p. 222 supplies finite presentation; Huber,
Prop. 1.9.6, p. 98 and Conrad-AWS §3.3, Ex. 3.3.9, pp. 32–33 supply the
properness implication. For the converse, the scheme-theoretic closure `X̄` of `X`
in projective space over `O_K` is flat because `X` is, so `X_K` is dense in `X̄`.
If `X` is not proper, the nonempty closed boundary `X̄ ∖ X` is proper over `O_K`,
hence meets the special fibre and contains a closed point `z` there. This point is the
specialisation of a classical point `Spec K'` of `X_K` (the classical points of the tube of `z` are
dense and `X̄_K ∖ X_K` is nowhere dense in it), and properness of `X̄` extends `Spec K' → X̄` to `Spec O_{K'} → X̄` centred at `z`.
The valuation ring is unique because `K` is complete; the closure of the classical point need
not itself be normal or equal to `Spec O_{K'}`. This gives a classical point of `X_K^ad` whose
integral extension lands outside `X`, so `φ_X` misses it. Quasi-projectivity is assumed because
for general separated `X` of finite type the compactification step needs Nagata's theorem over
`O_K`, which this roadmap does not own. Flatness cannot be dropped: `X = Spec O_K ⊔ A¹_{O_K/ϖ}`
is separated and of finite presentation, `φ_X` is an isomorphism (both sides are `Spa(K, O_K)`),
and `X` is not proper. For `X = P¹_{O_K}` minus a closed point `x` of the special fibre, `φ_X`
has image `λ⁻¹(P¹_k ∖ {x}) = P^{1,ad}_K ∖ λ⁻¹(x)` (`λ⁻¹(x)` is closed and strictly larger than
the open residue disc `]x[`), which is not all of `X_K^ad = P^{1,ad}_K`, and `X` is not proper —
consistent with the criterion. For `X = P¹_{O_K} ⊔ Spec K` (`Spec K = Spec O_K[1/ϖ]` open in
`P⁰_{O_K}`, so `X` is quasi-projective): flat, separated, of finite type,
with proper generic fibre `P¹_K ⊔ Spec K` and proper special fibre `P¹_k`, but not proper; `φ_X : d(X̂) = P^{1,ad}_K → P^{1,ad}_K ⊔ Spa(K, O_K)` misses the extra point, as the criterion predicts.
*Needs:* *good-reduction-locus*; *rig-point*; *tube*; *specialisation-map*;
*admissible-formal-scheme*; *analytification-constructible-closure* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R1);
*analytification-completed-local-rings* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R1); *analytification-functor* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R1); Mathlib
`AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper.eq_valuativeCriterion`, `AlgebraicGeometry.Flat`.

### R2.9 Conrad's `FS_C`, smooth formal schemes, étale sites, Frobenius lifts and residue discs

This subsection builds Conrad's Berthelot-type generic fibre on the category `FS_C` of locally
noetherian formal schemes over an adic noetherian ring `C`, for an arbitrary complete nonarchimedean
base field; defines smooth and étale morphisms of formal schemes locally of tf presentation with
their continuous differentials; identifies the étale site of a formal scheme with that of its
special fibre, proves étaleness of generic fibres of formal étale morphisms, and gives the Frobenius lifts on
opens étale over the formal torus and the residue discs of rational smooth points.

`FormalScheme.FSC` is the full category over `Spf C` with locally noetherian
source and locally finite type reduced structural map.
**Checks:** `FSC_base` contains the base; `FSC_discrete` contains discrete
locally noetherian schemes with the required reduced map; `FSC_powerSeries`
contains `Spf(C[[q]])` with the `q`-adic topology when `C` is discrete.
`ContinuousIntegralMap` records a continuous map of sites and a map from `𝒪_X` to
the direct image of the locally power-bounded sheaf `𝒪_Zᵇ`, over the coefficient
map, with continuity, topological nilpotence and integral centres as specified below.
**Checks:** `ContinuousIntegralMap_empty` has a unique map from the empty source;
`ContinuousIntegralMap_noCentre` has none from a nonempty source to the empty target;
`ContinuousIntegralMap_base` has at most one map to the coefficient base.
**Checks for precomposition:** `ContinuousIntegralMap.precomp_identity`,
`ContinuousIntegralMap.precomp_composition`, `ContinuousIntegralMap.precomp_points`.
`BerthelotData` represents these maps, and `rigOfFSC` is its functor to adic spaces
over the valued-field point, using the rigid–adic comparison.
**Checks:** `BerthelotData_empty` / `rigOfFSC_empty` give the empty space;
`BerthelotData_base` / `rigOfFSC_base` give the valued-field point;
`BerthelotData_unique` / `rigOfFSC_unique` identify two representing choices naturally.


**Conrad's Berthelot-type functor `(·)^rig` on `FS_C` for arbitrary complete `k`.**
(*berthelot-type-rig-functor-nonnoetherian-base*) Fix an adic noetherian ring `C` with a continuous
map `C → R` to the valuation ring `R` of a complete nonarchimedean field `k`, with no discreteness
assumption on `k` (examples: `C = R` if `k` is discretely valued; `C = R_0` a complete discrete
valuation ring with `R_0 → R` local; `C = ℤ` discrete). `FS_C` is the category of locally noetherian
formal schemes `X` over `Spf C` whose underlying reduced scheme is locally of finite type over
`C_red`; affine opens have algebras that are quotients of `C[[q_1, …, q_n]]{{T_1, …, T_m}}` with the
`(I, q)`-adic topology. For `X` in `FS_C` and a rigid space `Z` over `k`,
`Hom^cont_C(Z, X)`, realized by `ContinuousIntegralMap`, consists of the following
integral specialization data. There is a map `f` on rigid points whose inverse images
take formal opens to admissible opens and open coverings to admissible coverings,
and a map of sheaves of `C`-algebras `f♯ : 𝒪_X → f_*𝒪_Zᵇ`, where `𝒪_Zᵇ` is the
subsheaf of locally power-bounded sections of the ordinary analytic sheaf `𝒪_Z`.
On each formal affine `Spf A ⊆ X` and affinoid `V ⊆ f⁻¹(Spf A)`, the resulting map
`A → 𝒪_Z(V)` is continuous for the adic and affinoid topologies. The sheaf map
carries locally topologically nilpotent sections to locally topologically nilpotent
sections. For each rigid point `z`, evaluation gives a local homomorphism
`𝒪_{X,f(z)} → κ(z)°`: the inverse image of `κ(z)°°` is the maximal ideal of
`𝒪_{X,f(z)}`. Equivalently, on `Spf A`, `f(z) = {a ∈ A : |f♯(a)(z)| < 1}`.
This is the integral-centre condition of R2.4; evaluation factors through the
integral germ `(𝒪_Zᵇ)_z`. The analytic sheaf map is the composite with
`f_*𝒪_Zᵇ → f_*𝒪_Z`; locality is imposed on the evaluated integral map, with
no locality condition on `𝒪_{X,f(z)} → 𝒪_{Z,z}`. No ideal-of-definition element
is required to have nonzero analytic value.
Prove the representability assertion of Conrad-MR Theorem 3.1.5 for these
integral specialization data: `Hom^cont_C(·, X)` is represented by a
quasi-separated rigid space `X^rig`; `(·)^rig` takes open/closed immersions to open/closed
immersions and open covers to admissible covers, commutes with fibre products (a), with analytic
extension of `k` (b) and with change of `C` (c), preserves separatedness (d), and sends
topologically finite type maps to quasi-compact maps (e); and `Spf(C[[q]])^rig` is the open unit
disc `Δ = {|t| < 1}`. Through *rigid-adic-comparison-functor* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R1) this gives an adic space
`r(X^rig)` over `Spa(k, R)`. Objects of `FS_C` are locally noetherian, so the functor does not apply
to non-noetherian formal `O_K`-models when `k` is not discretely valued; those are handled by
*generic-fibre-functor-d* and *raynaud-generic-fibre*. In `FormalScheme`, define `FSC` (locally
noetherian formal schemes over `Spf C` with reduced scheme locally of finite type over `C_red`) and
`rigOfFSC` (`X ↦ X^rig`); prove `rigOfFSC.homEquiv` (`Hom_k(Z, X^rig) ≃ Hom^cont_C(Z, X)`, naturally
in the rigid space `Z`), `rigOfFSC_isOpenImmersion` (open, resp. closed, immersions go to open,
resp. closed, immersions and open covers to admissible covers), `rigOfFSC_pullback` (`(X ×_Y Z)^rig ≅ X^rig ×_{Y^rig} Z^rig`, 3.1.5(a)), `rigOfFSC_baseChangeField` (`k' ⊗̂_k X^rig_{/k} ≅ X^rig_{/k'}`
for an analytic extension `k'/k`, 3.1.5(b)), `rigOfFSC_changeCoefficients` (`X^rig ≅ (Spf C' ×_{Spf C} X)^rig` for `C → C'` compatible with the maps to `R`, 3.1.5(c)), `rigOfFSC_isSeparated` (`f`
separated implies `f^rig` separated, 3.1.5(d)), `rigOfFSC_quasiCompact` (`f` topologically of finite
type implies `f^rig` quasi-compact, 3.1.5(e)), `rigOfFSC_powerSeries` (`Spf(C[[q]])^rig ≅ Δ`) and
`rigOfFSC_eq_genericFibre` (for `k` discretely valued, `C = R` and `X` in `FS_R` locally
topologically of finite type over `Spf R`: `r(X^rig) ≅ d(X) = t(X)_a`, compatibly with
specialisation as a map of ring sheaves — Huber96 Example 1.9.2(ii), pp. 97–98).
The statement identifies `C` homeomorphically with the valuation DVR of `k`, identifies
the chart field and its plus ring with `(k, R)`, and requires the coefficient map to be this
inclusion. It assumes `IsTypeS X.obj.left` and `IsLocallyTFP ϖ X.obj.hom`; no flatness is required.
Type (S) alone does not give this comparison: for the `(ϖ,q)`-adic formal disc, `d(X)` also
contains points where `ϖ` vanishes. De Jong [deJ, 7.2.4] describes the relative Berthelot
functor on all of `FS_R`, rather than identifying all those images with the absolute `d(X)` (Conrad-MR
§3.1, Thm
3.1.5, p. 16, representability without discreteness of the valuation; Def. 3.1.1, p. 16, the exact
class of formal schemes; proof of Thm 3.1.5, p. 17, `Spf(C[[q]])^rig` is the open unit disc). When
`k` is discretely valued and `C = R` the functor recovers de Jong's [deJ, 7.2.4, 7.2.6]. *Needs:*
*locally-noetherian-formal-scheme* (layer F0); *formal-spectrum* (layer F0); *rigid-analytic-space*
(AdicSpacesPartII layer R1); *rigid-adic-comparison-functor* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R1); *raynaud-generic-fibre*;
*noetherian-formal-scheme-as-adic-space*; *raynaud-theorem*; *affinoid-power-bounded-iff-sup* (AdicSpacesPartII layer
R0); *specialisation-map* (R2.4); *adic-valuation-rings-and-centres* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R0).

For `rigOfFSC_powerSeries`, the topology on `C[[q]]` is explicitly `(I,q)`-adic,
where `I` defines the topology on `C`. The continuous coefficient map has image in `R`;
the isomorphism with `FormalScheme.openPolydisc k 1` preserves both field scalars and the
parameter `q`. This adic open disc is the interior of the strict coordinate bound in the
imported closed disc (Conrad-MR, proof of Theorem 3.1.5, p. 17; Conrad AWS,
Example 5.2.5, pp. 50–51, for the rigid open residue disc).

**Checks.**

- `rigOfFSC_test_powerSeries` (computation) — for `C = ℤ` (discrete) and any `k`, `Spf(ℤ[[q]])^rig`
  is the open unit disc `Δ = {|t| < 1}` over `k`, admissibly covered by the closed discs `{|t| ≤
  r}`. The check realizes the object in `FSC ℤ` and bounds each image point by
  `|t|^m ≤ |π|` for some positive `m`, with `0 < |π| < 1`.
- `rigOfFSC_test_nondiscrete` (non-example) — for `k = ℂ_p`, `Spf O_k⟨T⟩` is not an object of `FS_C`
  for any `C` (it is not locally noetherian); its generic fibre is given by Raynaud's functor
  instead. The example works for any complete rank-one valuation ring whose maximal ideal
  is not finitely generated and excludes equality with every `FSC C` source.
- `rigOfFSC_test_restricted` (compatibility) — for `k` discretely valued and `C = R`, `Spf
  R{{T}}^rig` is the closed unit disc, equal to Raynaud's generic fibre of `Spf R⟨T⟩`.
  The example supplies its `FSC R` object and type-(S) instance and preserves the full
  specialization map in the comparison with `genericFibre`.
- `rigOfFSC_test_point` (degenerate) — `Spf(C)^rig = Sp(k)`, the final object of rigid spaces over
  `k`. For `C = R = ℤ_p` and `k = ℚ_p`, construct the unique integral specialization
  `Sp(ℚ_p) → Spf(ℤ_p)` and prove that `rigOfFSC.homEquiv` sends the identity to it.
  Its integral evaluation is `ℤ_p → ℤ_p`, local with centre `(p)`; its analytic
  stalk map is `ℤ_p → ℚ_p`, which is not local, since `p` is a nonunit in the
  source and a unit in the target.

**Smooth and étale morphisms of formal schemes locally of tf presentation; continuous
differentials.** (*smooth-formal-scheme*) Let `f : X → Y` be a morphism of formal `O_K`-schemes
locally of tf presentation, `K` complete of rank one, or of noetherian formal schemes
(Bosch–Lütkebohmert's case II); PerfectoidSpaces layer P7 uses it with `O_K = W(κ)`, `κ` perfect.
`f` is smooth at `x ∈ X` of relative dimension `d` if there are an open neighbourhood `U` of `x` and
a `Y`-immersion `j : U → D^n_Y = Spf O_Y⟨ζ_1, …, ζ_n⟩` such that, locally at `j(x)`, the ideal of
`j(U)` is generated by `n − d` sections `g_{d+1}, …, g_n` whose differentials are linearly
independent in `Ω¹_{D^n_Y/Y} ⊗ κ(j(x))`; `f` is smooth if smooth at all points, and étale if smooth
of relative dimension `0` (Bosch–Lütkebohmert II Definition 1.1). Equivalently (II Lemma 1.2) `f` is
flat at `x` and `f_0 : X_0 → Y_0` is smooth at `x` of relative dimension `d`; equivalently every
reduction `f_m : X_m → Y_m` modulo `ϖ^{m+1}` is smooth at `x` of relative dimension `d` (Mathlib
`AlgebraicGeometry.Smooth` for schemes); equivalently `f` is formally smooth and locally
topologically of finite presentation, and then locally `f` factors as an étale morphism to `D^d_Y`.
Smoothness is a condition on all levels `X_m`, not on the generic fibre: `d(f)` smooth does not
imply `f` smooth. The module of continuous differentials `Ω¹_{X/Y} := lim_m Ω¹_{X_m/Y_m}` is
coherent; for `f` smooth of relative dimension `d` it is locally free of rank `d`, with basis `dT_1,
…, dT_d` on an étale chart `X → D^d_Y`. For `Spf B → Spf A` with `A`, `B` tfp over a discretely
valued `K`, this module and the module of *continuous-differentials* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R0) of `A → B` are both
the `ϖ`-adic completion of Mathlib's `KaehlerDifferential A B`, and the identification
`kaehler_eq_continuousDifferentials` is part of this target; for non-discrete `K` the formal module
is the one used. A formal scheme smooth over `Spf O_K` is admissible. In
`FormalScheme`, use `IsSmoothAt ϖ f x d fY` (smoothness on a neighbourhood of `x`,
equivalently a local Jacobian presentation in `D^n_Y`) and
`IsSmoothOfRelativeDimension ϖ fY f d` (smooth at every point with the fixed dimension `d`;
`IsSmooth` is the namespace for its consequences, and `IsEtale` is dimension `0`), `kaehler` (`Ω¹_{X/Y} = lim_m Ω¹_{X_m/Y_m}`, a coherent `O_X`-module with continuous
derivation `d`) and `IsElementaryEtaleNbhd` (an étale neighbourhood of `x ∈ X_0` is an étale pointed
morphism `(X', x') → (X, x)`; it is elementary if moreover `k(x') = k(x)`, Bosch–Lütkebohmert II
§1); prove `isSmoothAt_iff_flat_specialFibre` (`f` is smooth at `x` of relative dimension `d` iff
`f` is flat at `x` and `f_0` is smooth at `x` of relative dimension `d`),
`isSmooth_iff_forall_level` (`f` has the fixed relative dimension `d` iff every
`f_m : X_m → Y_m` has `AlgebraicGeometry.SmoothOfRelativeDimension d`, hence is smooth), `IsSmooth.exists_etale_affineSpace` (if `f` is smooth of relative
dimension `d` at `x`, there are an open `U ∋ x` and an étale `U → D^d_Y` over `Y`),
`IsSmooth.kaehler_locallyFree` (for `f` smooth of relative dimension `d`, `Ω¹_{X/Y}` is locally free
of rank `d`, free on the `dT_i` over an étale chart to `D^d_Y`), the instance
`IsSmooth.isAdmissible` (a formal scheme smooth over `Spf O_K` is admissible), `IsSmooth.comp`
(smooth morphisms are stable under composition and base change; étale ones likewise),
`IsSmooth.of_isEtale` (if `𝔛` is smooth of relative dimension `d` over `Spf O_K` and `𝔜 → 𝔛` is
étale, `𝔜` is smooth of relative dimension `d` and `Ω¹_{𝔜/O_K}` is the pullback of `Ω¹_{𝔛/O_K}`),
`IsSmooth.genericFibre` (if `f` is smooth of relative dimension `d` then `d(f)` is smooth of
relative dimension `d` in the sense of *smooth-morphism* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R0, `AdicSpace.Smooth`); if `f` is
étale then `d(f)` is étale (`AdicSpace.Etale`); `d(X)` and `d(Y)` are analytic and locally
noetherian, hence locally Huber-standard (`AdicSpace.IsLocallyHuberStandard`), which is where
Part II states these classes), `kaehler_eq_continuousDifferentials` (for `Spf B → Spf A` tfp over a discretely valued `K`,
`Ω¹_{Spf B/Spf A}` is the `ϖ`-adic completion of `KaehlerDifferential A B`, hence the module of
*continuous-differentials* of `A → B`) and `IsEtale.lift_unique` (for `f` étale, liftings along nilpotent thickenings of affine
formal schemes exist and are unique, by `Algebra.FormallyEtale.iff_comp_bijective` on each level)
(BL II §1, Def. 1.1, p. 404, smooth and étale formal morphisms; after Lem. 1.2, p. 404, elementary
étale neighbourhoods; Conrad-MR §3.1, proof of Thm 3.1.6, p. 17, the local structure and the rank of
`Ω¹`; TT §2.2, p. 12, smooth formal schemes over `W(κ)` and their adic generic fibres). *Needs:*
*admissible-formal-scheme*; *tfp-locality*; *formal-etale-site-invariance*; *smooth-morphism* (AdicSpacesPartII layer
R0); *locally-huber-standard* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R0); *differentials-unramified-smooth-etale* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R0); *continuous-differentials* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R0);
Mathlib `AlgebraicGeometry.Smooth`, `Algebra.Smooth`, `KaehlerDifferential`, `Algebra.Etale`.

**Checks.**

- `smoothFormal_test_affineSpace` (computation) — `Spf O_K⟨T_1, …, T_d⟩ → Spf O_K` is smooth of
  relative dimension `d` and `Ω¹` is free with basis `dT_1, …, dT_d`.
- `smoothFormal_test_torus` (computation) — the formal torus `Spf W(κ)⟨T_1^{±1}, …, T_d^{±1}⟩` is
  smooth of relative dimension `d` over `Spf W(κ)`, with `Ω¹` free on the `dT_i`.
- `smoothFormal_test_semistable` (non-example) — `Spf O_K⟨S, T⟩/(ST − ϖ) → Spf O_K` is flat with
  smooth generic fibre (an annulus) but is not smooth: its special fibre `k[S, T]/(ST)` is singular
  at the origin.
- `smoothFormal_test_levels` (compatibility) — for a smooth `O_K`-scheme `X`, the `ϖ`-adic
  completion `X̂` is smooth over `Spf O_K`, and each `X̂_m = X ⊗ O_K/ϖ^{m+1}` is smooth in the sense
  of Mathlib `AlgebraicGeometry.Smooth`.
- `smoothFormal_test_identity` (degenerate) — `id : Spf O_K → Spf O_K` is étale (smooth of relative
  dimension `0`) and `Ω¹ = 0`.

The formal-scheme statements use a complete rank-one valuation ring `O` with a
pseudouniformizer `ϖ`, and require both structural morphisms to be locally tfp.
In `isSmooth_iff_forall_level` and `isSmoothAt_iff_flat_specialFibre`, `P` and `Q`
are the existing `IdealPair` carriers. The target ideal is the ideal generated by
the structural section `ϖ` on every affine open, and the source ideal is its
extension along `f`. The point in the second theorem is transported through
`thickeningι`. Its flatness condition uses the actual stalk homomorphism; smoothness
of the zeroth reduction means smoothness on an open neighbourhood of that point.
Here level zero means reduction modulo `(ϖ)`. It agrees with the residue-field
special fibre when `ϖ` generates the maximal ideal; for a nondiscrete valuation
these are different schemes. The residue-field formulation follows by the
finite-presentation smooth-fibre criterion. Sources: Fujiwara–Kato I.4.8.2,
p. 329, and I.5.3.18, pp. 346–347.

`IsSmooth.exists_etale_affineSpace` gives a source neighbourhood, an affine target
neighbourhood `Spf A`, and an étale map to `Spf A⟨T₁,…,T_d⟩`. Its composite with
the projection and target inclusion equals the original formal morphism, and the
pulled-back coordinate derivatives form a basis of the complete differential
sheaf on the source neighbourhood. Over `Spf O` the local target is
`Spf O⟨T₁,…,T_d⟩`.
`IsSmooth.kaehler_locallyFree` gives local bases indexed by `Fin d`.
`IsSmooth.genericFibre` uses the existing adic generic-fibre map, requires its
adicness and locally noetherian generic fibres, and concludes smoothness with
Part II's intrinsic relative dimension equal to `d` everywhere; at `d = 0` it
also concludes étaleness. These are the formal étale chart construction in
Fujiwara–Kato I.5.3.15–18, pp. 346–347, followed by the analytic chart criterion
of Huber 1.6.7, 1.6.9 and Corollary 1.6.10, pp. 79–80.

`kaehler` and `kaehler.d` are fixed by `kaehler_affine`: on affine source and
target opens the sections are the adic completion of `KaehlerDifferential A B`,
and the universal derivative goes to the completed algebraic derivative.
`kaehler_d_naturality` states restriction compatibility and vanishing on pulled-back
base sections. `kaehler_isCoherent` gives finite presentation for the locally tfp
morphisms above. `kaehler_eq_continuousDifferentials` assumes additionally that
`O` is noetherian (the discretely valued case), complete Hausdorff affine rings
with the specified adic topologies, and continuous structural maps. It identifies
these formal sections with Part II's continuous module and identifies their
universal derivatives. Sources: Fujiwara–Kato I.5.1.3, p. 336, I.5.1.7–10,
pp. 338–339, I.5.2.1 and I.5.2.5, pp. 340–341; Huber (1.6.2), pp. 76–77.

**Checks for the complete differential sheaf and pointed neighbourhoods.**

- `kaehler_identity`, `kaehler.d_identity`: the identity has zero differential
  sheaf and zero derivative.
- `kaehler_etale`, `kaehler.d_etale`: an étale formal morphism has zero
  differential sheaf and zero derivative.
- `kaehler_affineSpace`, `kaehler.d_affineSpace`: the basis on the formal
  `d`-disc consists of the derivatives of its coordinates; at `d = 1` it is
  nonzero, and at `d = 0` the basis is empty. These are also the
  `smoothFormal_test_affineSpace` example.
- `IsElementaryEtaleNbhd_identity`: the identity at a point is elementary.
- `IsElementaryEtaleNbhd_open`: inclusion of an open neighbourhood is elementary
  at each of its points.
- `IsElementaryEtaleNbhd_residueExtension`: an étale pointed morphism whose
  induced residue-field map is not surjective is not elementary. The definition
  uses this induced map, rather than an unrelated abstract field isomorphism.

The torus Check uses `O⟨T₁,…,T_d,U₁,…,U_d⟩/(T_i U_i − 1)` over any such `O`,
including `W(κ)`, and identifies the basis with the `dT_i`.
The semistable Check uses the actual quotient by `ST − ϖ`, asserting flatness,
smoothness of its generic fibre, and failure of formal smoothness in every
fixed dimension. The levels Check uses `idealCompletion` for the ideal generated
by the structural `ϖ` on a smooth scheme of fixed relative dimension: it supplies
the formal structural map, its coefficient identity, and smooth scheme maps on
all power thickenings. The reduction maps commute with the original scheme
structural map (Fujiwara–Kato I.5.3.19, p. 347).

**The étale site of a formal scheme is the étale site of its special fibre.**
(*formal-etale-site-invariance*) Let `𝔛` be a formal `O_K`-scheme locally of tf presentation
(the same holds for adic noetherian formal schemes with an ideal of definition),
`𝔛_m = 𝔛 ⊗ O_K/ϖ^{m+1}`. Prove that the functor `𝔜 ↦ 𝔜_0` is an equivalence from the
category of formal schemes étale over `𝔛` (adic, locally tfp, each `𝔜_m → 𝔛_m` étale) to the
category of schemes étale over `𝔛_0`; composing with topological invariance for
`𝔛_{s,red} ⊆ 𝔛_0`, both are equivalent to schemes étale over `𝔛_{s,red}`. The equivalence
preserves fibre products, open immersions and jointly surjective families, so it is an
equivalence of small étale sites `𝔛_ét ≃ (𝔛_0)_ét ≃ (𝔛_{s,red})_ét`. Prove also that
`O_{𝔛_ét}(𝔜) := Γ(𝔜, O_𝔜)` is a sheaf on `𝔛_ét`.
Sources: Stacks Tag 039R, Étale Morphisms of Schemes, Thm 41.15.2, topological invariance
under thickenings; EGA IV 18.1.2; Stacks Tag 04DZ, Étale Cohomology, Thm 59.45.2, universal
homeomorphisms; Conrad-MR §3.1, proof of Thm 3.1.6, p. 17. The scheme-level equivalences
are supplied by SchemeAndStackFoundations §0.23a, using its §0.23 universal-homeomorphism
geometry. Their ring-level core is Mathlib's `Algebra.FormallyEtale.iff_comp_bijective` with
`Algebra.FormallyUnramified.ext`; this target adds the passage to the limit over the levels
`𝔛_m`.

For a formal étale morphism `𝔜 → 𝔛` with analytic locally noetherian generic fibres, prove
that `d(𝔜) → d(𝔛)` is étale by AdicSpacesPartII R0's
*differentials-unramified-smooth-etale*; the generic-fibre functor preserves fibre products
by R2.3 *generic-fibre-fibre-products* ([TT] §2.2, p. 12).
AdicEtaleGeometry A2.9a uses these facts to construct the continuous functor from the formal
étale site to the adic étale site and to prove preservation of coverings.

**Checks.**

- For `𝔛 = Spf ℤ_p⟨T⟩`, formal étale objects correspond to étale `𝔽_p[T]`-schemes;
  `Spf ℤ_p⟨T,(T^{p−1} − 1)⁻¹⟩` corresponds to `D(T^{p−1} − 1) ⊆ A¹_{𝔽_p}`.
- The formal finite étale cover `Spf W(𝔽_{p²}) → Spf ℤ_p` corresponds to
  `Spec 𝔽_{p²} → Spec 𝔽_p`.

*Needs:* *admissible-formal-scheme*; *generic-fibre-functor-d*;
*generic-fibre-fibre-products*; *specialisation-map*; AdicSpacesPartII R0
(*differentials-unramified-smooth-etale*, *etale-local-structure*);
*colimit-of-thickenings*, *adic-systems-equivalence-finite-ideal-type* (layer F0);
SchemeAndStackFoundations §§0.23–0.23a; Mathlib `AlgebraicGeometry.Etale`,
`Algebra.FormallyEtale.iff_comp_bijective`, `Algebra.FormallyUnramified.ext`, `Module.Flat`,
`ValuationRing`.

**Unique Frobenius lift on a formal scheme étale over the formal torus.**
(*frobenius-lift-etale-over-torus*) Let `κ` be a perfect field of characteristic `p`, `W = W(κ)`
with Witt-vector Frobenius `σ` (Mathlib `WittVector.frobenius`), and `𝕋^d = Spf W⟨T_1^{±1}, …, T_d^{±1}⟩` the formal torus. Let `𝔛 = Spf R` be affine with an étale morphism `𝔛 → 𝕋^d`, `T_i ↦ T_i ∈ R`, so that `R` is `p`-adically complete and étale levelwise over `W⟨T^{±1}⟩`. Prove that there is
a unique ring endomorphism `φ : R → R` such that `φ` is `σ`-semilinear (`φ(a·r) = σ(a)φ(r)` for `a ∈
W`), `φ(T_i) = T_i^p` for all `i`, and `φ(r) ≡ r^p mod pR` for all `r ∈ R`; more generally, that if
`A → R` is a formally étale map of `p`-adically complete rings (étale modulo every `p^m`) and `φ_A`
is a Frobenius lift on `A`, there is a unique Frobenius lift `φ_R` on `R` extending `φ_A`, so that
Frobenius lifts are compatible with étale maps over `𝕋^d`; uniqueness uses `p`-adic completeness and
formal unramifiedness. In general a smooth formal scheme over `W` admits no global Frobenius lift;
lifts exist on each open étale over a torus (TT §2.3, Rem. 2.20, p. 19: no global lift in general,
and existence and uniqueness on opens étale over the torus). On the torus itself `φ(Σ a_ν T^ν) = Σ σ(a_ν) T^{pν}`; on `𝔛 = Spf W⟨T^{±1}, (T − 1)⁻¹⟩` (open in the torus), `φ((T − 1)⁻¹) = (T^p − 1)⁻¹`,
which lies in `R` because `T^p − 1 ≡ (T − 1)^p mod p` is invertible. For `d = 0`, `R ≅ ∏ᵢ W(κ'ᵢ)`
for finitely many finite separable `κ'ᵢ/κ` (a single `W(κ')` when `Spf R` is connected, `R = 0`
allowed), and `φ` is the product of the Witt-vector Frobenii. Equal characteristic
is degenerate: if `pR = 0` the `p`-adic topology is discrete, the only Frobenius lift is the
absolute Frobenius `r ↦ r^p`, and `R` cannot be étale over `(W(κ)/p²)[T^{±1}]` unless `R = 0` (an
étale algebra over `(W(κ)/p²)[T^{±1}]` is flat over `W(κ)/p²`, and `p = 0` on a flat
`W(κ)/p²`-module forces the module to vanish); the general form with `A → R` of characteristic `p`
(étale levelwise, each level being `A → R` itself) is the statement that the absolute Frobenius
of `R` is the unique lift of that of `A`. The scheme-level absolute and relative Frobenius
are supplied by SchemeAndStackFoundations §0.29.

**Checks.**

- `frobeniusLift_test_charP_not_etale` (non-example) — a flat `ℤ/p²`-algebra killed by `p`
  is zero, including `p = 2`.
- `frobeniusLift_test_flat_product` (negative control) — let `A = ℤ/4 × 𝔽₂` and let
  `A → 𝔽₂` be the second projection. Its target is a nonzero flat summand, although
  `2 ≠ 0` and `2² = 0` in `A`. These two equations alone do not imply the preceding claim.

*Needs:*
*formal-etale-site-invariance*; *smooth-formal-scheme*; SchemeAndStackFoundations §0.29;
Mathlib `WittVector.frobenius`,
`Algebra.FormallyEtale.iff_comp_bijective`, `Algebra.FormallyUnramified.lift_unique`,
`IsAdicComplete`. Lean: `exists_unique_frobeniusLift_of_etale`, the general form for `A → R`
étale modulo every `p^{m+1}` between `p`-adically complete rings; the torus statement and the
Checks are specified in this README only.

On the formal-scheme carrier, `IsSmoothOfRelativeDimension ϖ fY f d` uses the
structural maps to `Spf O_K` and affine neighbourhoods of each source point. The ring map
is induced by `f`; every quotient by `ϖ^{m+1}` must be smooth of relative dimension `d`.
Both formal schemes are locally tfp over the base. `IsEtale` is the dimension-zero case.
`isSmoothOfRelativeDimension_spf_iff` identifies this neighbourhood definition with the
all-level affine criterion, with the given `ϖ`-adic topologies (BL II §1, pp. 405–406).

**Checks for formal smoothness and étaleness.**

- `formalSmooth_test_identity` — the identity of a locally tfp formal scheme is smooth
  of dimension zero and étale.
- `formalSmooth_test_empty` — a morphism from the empty formal scheme is smooth of every
  specified dimension and étale.
- `formalSmooth_test_torsion` — `Spf(O_K/ϖ) → Spf O_K` is not smooth in any dimension
  and is not étale. Its first reduction is the identity, but its second reduction is
  the nonflat map `O_K/ϖ² → O_K/ϖ`; testing only the first reduction without flatness fails.

**The residue disc of a rational smooth point is an open unit polydisc.** (*residue-disc*) Let `𝔛`
be a formal `O_K`-scheme, `K` complete of rank one, smooth of relative dimension `d`
(*smooth-formal-scheme*) at a closed point `x` of the special fibre with residue field `κ(x) = k` (a
`k`-rational point), and let `t_1, …, t_d ∈ Γ(U, O_𝔛)` on an open `U ∋ x` be local parameters at
`x`: their reductions lie in `m_{𝔛_s,x}` and form a regular system of parameters of `O_{𝔛_s,x}`. Let
`]x[ ⊆ d(𝔛)` be the tube of `{x}` (*tube*) and `D^d_{<1} = ⋃_{m≥1} {|T_i|^m ≤ |ϖ| ∀i} ⊆ Spa(K⟨T⟩, O_K⟨T⟩)` the open unit polydisc. `residueDisc_iso` states that the tube is isomorphic to this
polydisc, and `residueDisc_iso_coordinates` requires its pullback to send each coordinate to the
specified `t_i` and to preserve the structural `O_K`-map. `residueDisc_reparam` states that if `t'`
is another system of local parameters at `x`, then `t' = Φ(t)` for an
automorphism `Φ` of `D^d_{<1}` given by power series `Φ_i ∈ O_K[[T_1, …, T_d]]` with `Φ(0) ∈ m_K^d`
and invertible linear part modulo `m_K`. It includes convergence of each series to `t'_i` in
the section topology and the equation conjugating the tube automorphism to a polydisc
automorphism. `residueDisc_reparam_one` states that for `d = 1` and `t`, `t'` vanishing at a common
`K`-point of `]x[`, `t' = u·t·(1 + h)` with `u ∈ O_Kˣ` and `|h| < 1` at every adic point of the
disc. `residueDisc_unramified_split` states that for a closed point `x` with residue field
`k' ⊋ k` separable over `k`, `]x[` becomes, after base change
to a finite unramified extension of `K` whose residue field contains a normal closure of
`k'/k`, a disjoint union of `[k' : k]` open polydiscs. Using residue field `k'` itself suffices
when `k'/k` is Galois, but need not suffice otherwise. The hypotheses give the actual formal
base-change square, a finite étale coefficient extension, and splitting of every minimal
polynomial of `κ(x)` over the extended residue field; the conclusion gives the number of fibre
points, a disjoint open cover of their tube, and the polydisc isomorphisms.
`residueDisc_no_rationalPoint` excludes `K`-rational points when `k' ≠ k` by testing sections of
the tube's structural map to `Spa K`. No general inseparable splitting assertion is made. For the explicit example `k =
𝔽_p(t)`, `K = k((ϖ))`, `𝔛 = Spf O_K⟨T⟩` and `x` the closed point `T^p = t` of `A¹_k`,
`]x[ = ⋃_{m≥1} {|T^p − t|^m ≤ |ϖ|}` has no `K`-point and becomes the single open disc
`⋃_{m≥1} {|T − t^{1/p}|^m ≤ |ϖ|}` over `K(t^{1/p})`, as
`residueDisc_inseparable_root` states using `(T − b)^p = T^p − b^p`
(GK02 §2, Lem. 2.6,
p. 21, over a complete discretely valued field: the tube of the closed fibre of an étale chart
is a product with open unit polydiscs, with `r = 1` the smooth case; the nondiscrete rank-one
extension requires the corresponding completed étale-chart comparison, beyond this GK02 locator; Conrad-MR §3.1, proof of Thm 3.1.5, p. 17, the Berthelot generic
fibre of `Spf C[[q]]` is the open unit disc; Conrad-AWS §5.2, Ex. 5.2.5, p. 51, residue discs of the
closed unit disc are twisted open unit discs, ordinary over algebraically closed `k`). For `𝔛 = P̂¹_{O_K}` and `x = 0 ∈ P¹(k)`, `]x[ = D¹_{<1}` with `t = T`; for `x = ∞`,
`]∞[ = D¹_{<1}` in the coordinate `t = 1/T`. These are the increasing unions just defined;
the raw strict-inequality specialisation fibres include higher-rank boundary points. For `K` discretely valued and a smooth proper curve `X` over `O_K` with `x ∈ X_k(k)`, a
local parameter at a lift of `x` identifies `]x[` with the open unit disc, the form used for
Coleman integration. The case `d = 1` of an elliptic curve at its identity section is in Tau Ceti:
`WeierstrassCurve.kerReduction` with `formalPointAddEquivKerReduction` identifies the points of the
kernel of reduction with the formal group on the open unit disc; this target is the general smooth
point of any relative dimension, and no open polydisc exists in the library's `Spa/Polydisc`.
Non-example: for `K = ℚ_p` and `x ∈ P¹_{𝔽_p}` the closed point `T²
= 2` (`p` odd, `2` a non-square mod `p`), `]x[` has no `ℚ_p`-point and is not isomorphic to the open
unit disc over `ℚ_p`; over `ℚ_{p²}` it splits into two open unit discs. *Needs:*
*smooth-formal-scheme*; *tube*; *specialisation-map*; *formal-etale-site-invariance*;
*generic-fibre-fibre-products*; *berthelot-type-rig-functor-nonnoetherian-base*; Tau Ceti
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.closedPolydisc`, `WeierstrassCurve.kerReduction`,
`WeierstrassCurve.formalPointAddEquivKerReduction`.

`IsSmoothAt ϖ s x d (𝟙 (ofSpf O))` means that `s` has `IsSmoothOfRelativeDimension` `d` on some open
neighbourhood of `x`. For the coordinate theorems the parameter hypothesis is
`(t₁, …, t_d) + m_K O_{𝔛,x} = m_{𝔛,x}`. Smoothness of dimension `d` makes this precisely a
regular parameter system on the special fibre. The coefficient ring is an explicit complete
rank-one valuation ring `O` with fraction field `K`; its continuous embedding has image
`{a | ‖a‖ ≤ 1}`. Thus the statements include nondiscrete valuations and use `m_K`, not `(ϖ)`.

`tubeSpace` equips the already defined `tube` open with its restricted adic structure.
`openPolydisc K d` is the interior of the simultaneous strict coordinate bounds in Part II's
closed polydisc. `openPolydisc_eq_union` identifies this interior with the increasing union of
closed fractional-radius polydiscs for any pseudouniformiser; `openPolydisc.coeff` restricts the
Tate-algebra coefficient map. `tubeSection` pulls formal sections to the tube through specialization. These constructions
use Huber96 §1.9, Prop. 1.9.1 and Ex. 1.9.2(i–ii), pp. 96–98; the classical specialization and
residue-disc descriptions are Conrad-AWS Ex. 3.3.13, p. 34, and Ex. 5.2.5, pp. 50–51.
The power-series and splitting conclusions follow from the completed smooth chart and
henselian lifting, respectively; the cited Conrad examples describe the disc and its twists.

**Checks for the carriers and coordinates.**

- `tubeSpace_empty` — the empty centre gives the empty adic space.
- `tubeSpace_whole` — the whole centre gives the generic fibre.
- `tubeSpace_closed` — the inclusion has image the interior of the closed specialization fibre.
- `openPolydisc_zero` — dimension zero gives `Spa(K, O_K)`.
- `openPolydisc_origin` — the origin exists in every dimension.
- `openPolydisc_boundary` — no point of the one-dimensional open disc has coordinate value `1`.
- `openPolydisc.coeff_one` — the coefficient map preserves `1`.
- `openPolydisc.coeff_coordinate` — every coordinate remains a nonzero analytic function.
- `openPolydisc.coeff_injective` — restriction from the closed polydisc is injective.
- `IsSmoothAt_global` — global smoothness implies smoothness at every point.
- `IsSmoothAt_identity` — the formal base is smooth of dimension zero over itself.
- `IsSmoothAt_wrongDimension` — that same point is not smooth of relative dimension one.
- `tubeSection_zero` — specialization sends the zero section to zero.
- `tubeSection_one` — specialization preserves the unit section.
- `tubeSection_restrict` — restricting a section to a smaller neighbourhood gives the same tube section.
- `residueDisc_reparam_translation` — `T ↦ a + T`, with `a ∈ m_K`, has constant term `a` and unit linear determinant; the constant need not vanish.
- `residueDisc_reparam_contraction` — `T ↦ ϖT` has nonunit linear determinant and does not satisfy the automorphism criterion.

**Checks for residue-field splitting.**

- `residueDisc_test_inseparable` — for any complete rank-one base with residue field `𝔽_p(t)`
  and an integral lift `a` of `t`, the tube of `T^p − a = 0` in the formal affine line has no
  section over the generic fibre of the base. This includes `𝔽_p(t)[[ϖ]]`; the obstruction is
  that no residue coefficient has `p`-th power `t`.
- `residueDisc_test_nonnormal` — over a complete rank-one base with residue field `ℝ`, the
  tube of `T³ − 2 = 0` has two connected components, corresponding to the linear and irreducible
  quadratic residue factors. The cubic is separable and has a real root but does not split.
  Thus even extending residue coefficients to `ℝ` does not give three ordinary discs;
  the smaller field `ℚ(∛2)` cannot contain all three conjugates either.

### R2.10 fractional bounds, section domains and Hasse domains

This subsection defines the valuative loci `{|f| ≤ |g|^q}` and `{|f| ≥ |g|^q}` for rational
exponents `q` without adjoining a `q`-th root, the domains `{|s| ≥ |ϖ|^q}` cut out on the generic
fibre by a section of an invertible sheaf on a formal model together with their formal models (open
charts of an admissible blow-up), the Hasse domains `X(ε) = {|Ha| ≥ |p|^ε}` with their transition
maps, and Conrad's Hasse-invariant loci of a generalized elliptic curve; it closes with three
supporting results used across the layer: the adic flatness criterion behind Bosch–Lütkebohmert I
Lemma 1.6, the properties preserved by Conrad's generic-fibre functor, and coherent modules and
rings.

**Fractional valuation bounds `|f| ≤ |g|^q` and `|f| ≥ |g|^q` for `q ∈ ℚ_{≥0}`.**
(*fractional-valuation-bound*) Let `A` be a commutative ring, `f, g ∈ A` and `q ∈ ℚ_{≥0}`. For `v ∈ Spv A` write `q = a/b` with `a ∈ ℕ`, `b ∈ ℕ_{>0}`, and define `|f(v)| ≤ |g(v)|^q` to mean `v(f^b) ≤ v(g^a)` (the valuative relation `f^b ≤_v g^a`), and `|f(v)| ≥ |g(v)|^q` to mean `v(f^b) ≥ v(g^a)`;
strict versions likewise. This does not depend on the representative `(a, b)` of `q`, because `x ↦
x^n` is strictly increasing on a totally ordered value monoid. No element `g^q` of `A` (or of the
base field) is used: when `K = ℚ_p`, `|p|^{1/2}` is not the absolute value of any element of `K`,
yet `{|f| ≤ |p|^{1/2}}` is defined; the threshold `|g|^q` is realised by an element only after an
explicit extension. Second convention, compatible with the first: if `φ : A → B` is a ring map
and `B` contains `c` and a unit `u` with `u, u⁻¹ ∈ B⁺` and `c^b = φ(g)^a u` (e.g. `c = ϖ^{a/b} ∈ L = K(ϖ^{1/b})`, or `c = p^ε ∈ ℤ_p^cycl` of `p`-adic valuation `ε`), then for `v ∈ Spa(B, B⁺)` one has
`|φ(f)(v)| ≤ |φ(g)(v)|^q ⟺ v(φ(f)) ≤ v(c)`, since `v(u) = 1`. Degenerate values: for `q = 0` the
sets are `{v(f) ≤ 1}` and `{v(f) ≥ 1}` whatever `g` is; for `g = 0` and `q > 0`, `fracPowLE f 0 q =
{v(f) = 0}` and `fracPowGE f 0 q = Spv A`, consistently for every representative of `q` because
`0^n = 0`; for `g` a unit and `q > 0`, `fracPowGE f g q` contains no `v` with `v(f) = 0`; the
prime `p` plays no role in the definition (`p = 2` changes nothing, there being no signs). When
`A` is Huber and `g` is a unit (e.g. `g = ϖ` in a Tate ring), `fracPowLE f g q ∩
Spa(A, A⁺)` is the rational subset `R({f^b, g^a}/g^a)` and `fracPowGE f g q ∩ Spa(A, A⁺)` is
`R({g^a, f^b}/f^b)`. For `q = a/b` the set `fracPowLE f g q` differs from Tau Ceti's
`basicOpenFinset {f^b} (g^a)` only by the condition `v(g^a) ≠ 0`, which is automatic for a unit
`g`; Tau Ceti's `FarguesFontaine.IsRadiusLowerBound`/`IsRadiusUpperBound` on `Spv` of a Witt vector
ring are the case `f = [ϖ]`, `g = p`; this target is the general pair `(f, g)`, and those predicates
must be its specialisation. In `ValuationSpectrum`, define `fracPowLE f g q := {v ∈ Spv A : v(f^{q.den}) ≤ v(g^{q.num})}` and `fracPowGE f g q := {v ∈ Spv A : v(f^{q.den}) ≥ v(g^{q.num})}`;
prove `mem_fracPowLE_iff` (for every `a ∈ ℕ`, `b ∈ ℕ_{>0}` with `q = a/b`: `v ∈ fracPowLE f g q ↔
v(f^b) ≤ v(g^a)`); the simp lemma `fracPowLE f g n = {v : v(f) ≤ v(g^n)}` for `n ∈ ℕ`;
`fracPow_inter_spa` (if `g` is a unit: `fracPowLE f g q ∩ spa A⁺ = rationalSubset A⁺ {f^b, g^a}
(g^a)` and `fracPowGE f g q ∩ spa A⁺ = rationalSubset A⁺ {g^a, f^b} (f^b)`); monotonicity (on
`{v(g) ≤ 1}`: `q ≤ q'` implies `fracPowLE f g q' ⊆ fracPowLE f g q` and
`fracPowGE f g q ⊆ fracPowGE f g q'`); compatibility with pullback (for `φ : A → B`:
`(Spv φ)⁻¹(fracPowLE f g q) = fracPowLE (φ f) (φ g) q`); the explicit-extension form (if
`c^b = g^a u` with `u, u⁻¹ ∈ A⁺` and `q = a/b`, then for `v ∈ spa A⁺`:
`v ∈ fracPowLE f g q ↔ v(f) ≤ v(c)`); invariance under units (if `u, u⁻¹ ∈ A⁺`:
`fracPowGE (u f) g q ∩ spa A⁺ = fracPowGE f g q ∩ spa A⁺`, and likewise for LE); the power rule
(`fracPowLE (f^n) g (n q) = fracPowLE f g q` for `n > 0`); and the product rule
(`fracPowLE f g q ∩ fracPowLE f' g q' ⊆ fracPowLE (f f') g (q + q')`) (BHW §2.1, p. 7 of the author version, fractional thresholds with the explicit condition that `|p|^ε` lies in the value group;
Scholze15 §III.2, Def. III.2.12, p. 38, the explicit-extension convention with `p^ε ∈ ℤ_p^cycl`;
Conrad-MR §4.1, Thm 4.1.1(1), p. 26, thresholds in the divisible hull of the value group of `k`).
*Needs:* Tau Ceti `TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum`, `TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.comap`,
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spa`, `TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.basicOpenFinset`,
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset`, `TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.mem_rationalSubset_iff`,
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset_image_mul_right`,
`TauCeti.FarguesFontaine.IsRadiusLowerBound`; Mathlib `ValuativeRel`. Lean:
`ValuationSpectrum.fracPowLE`, `ValuationSpectrum.fracPowGE`, `ValuationSpectrum.mem_fracPowLE_iff`
and `ValuationSpectrum.fracPow_inter_spa`; the other lemmas and Checks are specified in this README only.

**Checks.**

- (computation, half disc) — in `Spa(ℚ_p⟨T⟩, ℤ_p⟨T⟩)`: `fracPowLE T p (1/2) = {v :
  v(T²) ≤ v(p)}`; the classical point `T = p` lies in it, the classical point `T = 1` does not, and
  it contains no `ℚ_p`-rational point with `|T| = p^{−1/2}`, while its points over `ℚ_p(√p)` include
  `T = √p`.
- (characterisation, representative) — `fracPowLE f g (2/4) = fracPowLE f g (1/2)`
  for all `f, g`: membership is `v(f⁴) ≤ v(g²)` iff `v(f²) ≤ v(g)`.
- (non-example, rounding) — rounding the exponent down (`|f| ≤ |g|^{⌊q⌋}`) is a
  different set: for `q = 1/2`, `f = T`, `g = p` it gives the whole unit disc `{|T| ≤ 1} ≠ {|T²| ≤
  |p|}`.
- (compatibility, root) — for `L = ℚ_p(√p)` with `c = √p` (`c² = p`): the preimage
  of `fracPowLE T p (1/2)` in `Spa(L⟨T⟩, O_L⟨T⟩)` equals `{v : v(T) ≤ v(c)}`.
- (degenerate, `q = 0`) — `fracPowLE f g 0 = {v : v(f) ≤ 1}` and `fracPowGE f g 0 = {v
  : v(f) ≥ 1}`.
- (degenerate, `g = 0`) — for `q > 0`: `fracPowLE f 0 q = {v : v(f) = 0}` (the
  support of `f`) and `fracPowGE f 0 q = Spv A`.
- (characterisation, direction of `GE`) — for `g` a unit and `q > 0`, every `v ∈ fracPowGE f g q` has `v(f) ≠ 0`; in `Spa(ℚ_p⟨T⟩, ℤ_p⟨T⟩)` the classical point `T = 1` lies in `fracPowGE T p (1/2)` and the classical point `T = p` does not (`|p| = p⁻¹ < p^{−1/2}`), which pins the
  direction of `GE`. Evaluation at `1` and `p` on the restricted-series carrier pulls back
  the `p`-adic valuative relation to these points.

**The domain `{|s| ≥ |ϖ|^q}` cut out by a section of an invertible sheaf on a formal model.**
(*section-valuation-domain*) Let `𝔛` be an admissible formal `O_K`-scheme, `ℒ` an invertible `O_𝔛`-module, `s ∈ Γ(𝔛, ℒ)` and `q ∈ ℚ_{≥0}`, interpreted by *fractional-valuation-bound*. Choose an open cover `𝔛 = ⋃ U_j`
by formal affines `U_j = Spf A_j` with generators `ℒ|_{U_j} = O e_j`, and write `s|_{U_j} = f_j e_j`. Define `𝔛_η(|s| ≥ |ϖ|^q) := ⋃_j (fracPowGE f_j ϖ q ∩ d(U_j)) ⊆ d(𝔛)`, and likewise `𝔛_η(|s| ≤
|ϖ|^q)` with `fracPowLE`. These sets do not depend on the cover or the generators: on `U_j ∩ U_k`
one has `e_k = u e_j` with `u ∈ O(U_j ∩ U_k)^×`, so `f_j = u f_k`, and `|u(x)| = 1` on `d(U_j ∩
U_k)` because `u, u⁻¹ ∈ O ⊆ O⁺`. They are open (finite unions of rational subsets when `𝔛` is
quasi-compact) and functorial under pull-back. Independence of lifts: if `s' ∈ Γ(𝔛, ℒ)` with `s − s'
∈ ϖ^c ℒ` for some `c ∈ ℚ` with `c > q` (`ϖ^c ℒ` meaning sections whose local coordinates satisfy
`|·| ≤ |ϖ|^c`), then `𝔛_η(|s| ≥ |ϖ|^q) = 𝔛_η(|s'| ≥ |ϖ|^q)`; hence a section `s̄` of `ℒ ⊗ O_K/ϖ^m`
(`m > q`) determines a well-defined domain `𝔛_η(|s̄| ≥ |ϖ|^q)` through arbitrary local lifts. The
domain depends on the integral structure `ℒ`, not only on the invertible sheaf `ℒ_η` on `d(𝔛)`. In
`FormalScheme`, define `sectionDomainGE` (`𝔛_η(|s| ≥ |ϖ|^q) ⊆ d(𝔛)`), `sectionDomainLE` (`𝔛_η(|s| ≤
|ϖ|^q)`) and `sectionDomainGE_ofMod` (for `s̄ ∈ Γ(𝔛, ℒ/ϖ^m ℒ)` and `q < m`, the domain defined
through arbitrary local lifts); prove the simp lemma `sectionDomainGE_of_trivialization` (on `U =
Spf A` with `ℒ|_U = O e` and `s = f e`: `sectionDomainGE ∩ d(U) = fracPowGE f ϖ q ∩ d(U) =
rationalSubset {ϖ^a, f^b} (f^b)`), `sectionDomainGE_indep_generator` (the local descriptions for two
generators `e`, `ue`, `u` a unit, agree), `isOpen_sectionDomainGE` (the domain is open;
quasi-compact if `𝔛` is), `sectionDomainGE_preimage` (for `g : 𝔜 → 𝔛`: `d(g)⁻¹(sectionDomainGE s q)
= sectionDomainGE (g*s) q`), `sectionDomainGE_congr` (if `s − s' ∈ ϖ^c ℒ` with `c > q` then
`sectionDomainGE s q = sectionDomainGE s' q`), `sectionDomainGE_mono` (`q ≤ q'` implies
`sectionDomainGE s q ⊆ sectionDomainGE s q'`), `sectionDomainGE_zero` (`sectionDomainGE s 0 = {|s| =
1} = λ⁻¹(𝔛_s ∖ V(s̄))`, the tube of the locus where `s̄` generates `ℒ/ϖ`), `sectionDomainGE_pow`
(for `n > 0`, `sectionDomainGE (s^{⊗n}) (n q) = sectionDomainGE s q` in `ℒ^{⊗n}`) and `sectionDomainGE_tensor`
(`sectionDomainGE s q ∩ sectionDomainGE t q' ⊆ sectionDomainGE (s ⊗ t) (q + q')` in `ℒ ⊗ ℳ`) (BHW
§2.1, p. 7 of the author version, the Hasse domain defined through arbitrary local lifts; Scholze15 §III.2, after Def.
III.2.12, p. 38, independence of the local lift; Conrad-MR §4.1, proof of Thm 4.1.1, p. 27,
independence of local coordinates for a valuation-bound locus). For `𝔛 = P̂¹_{O_K}`, `ℒ = O(1)` and
`s = T_0`, `𝔛_η(|s| ≥ |ϖ|^q)` is `P^{1,ad}_K` minus the closed valuation subset `{|z| < |ϖ|^q}` around `z =
T_0/T_1 = 0`; replacing `ℒ` by the lattice `ℒ' = ϖ⁻¹ℒ ⊇ ℒ` in the same `ℒ_η` (so `s ∈ Γ(ℒ) ⊆ Γ(ℒ')`
with coordinate `ϖf` for the generator `ϖ⁻¹e`) changes `𝔛_η(|s| ≥ |ϖ|^q)` into `𝔛_η(|s| ≥ |ϖ|^{q−1})` computed in `ℒ` (empty for `q < 1`): the domain depends on the formal model of the line
bundle. *Needs:* *fractional-valuation-bound*; *admissible-formal-scheme*;
*generic-fibre-functor-d*; *specialisation-map*; Tau Ceti
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset`,
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset_image_mul_right`.

The generic-fibre API assumes that `𝔛` has type (S), and that `O_K` is a
complete rank-one valuation ring with pseudouniformizer `ϖ`. The scalar
argument `a : Γ(𝔛, O)` is the image of `ϖ` under the structural map
`b : 𝔛 → Spf O_K`. `sectionDomainGE` and `sectionDomainLE` return
`Opens (genericFibre 𝔛).obj`. Their general scalar interface takes the interior of
the locus described by integral affine frames; for the admissible model and
pseudouniformizer above, `sectionDomainGE_of_trivialization` identifies that open
with the full local `fracPowGE` locus and also gives the `fracPowLE` identification.
Thus on these models the definitions glue the rational opens without changing
membership. This uses Huber96 §1.9, Prop. 1.9.1 and (1.9.3), pp. 96–98;
the rational-subset formulas are the two clauses of `fracPow_inter_spa`.
Invertibility is expressed by local isomorphisms with the structure module;
sections are morphisms from that module, using the existing `FormalScheme.Modules`.

`sectionDomainGE_indep_generator` is the integral-unit specialization of the unit-invariance
clause of *fractional-valuation-bound*. The separate `sectionDomainGE_congr_affine` supplies the
estimate for adding `ϖ^c t` with natural `c > q` and `t ∈ A⁺` on `Spa(A, A⁺)`.
`sectionDomainGE_congr` concerns sections of the invertible sheaf on the formal
model, with their difference locally bounded by `|ϖ|^c` for rational `c > q`; changing frames and
changing lifts are different operations. Under the same admissibility and
invertibility hypotheses, `isCompact_sectionDomainGE` adds quasi-compactness
when the formal scheme is quasi-compact. `sectionDomainGE_preimage` requires an
adic morphism between admissible models; any integral identification of its
pulled-back unit with the structure module gives the same domain. These assertions
follow by applying the affine formulas on the generic-fibre charts of Huber96
Prop. 1.9.1 and (1.9.3), pp. 96–98. The monotonicity, zero, power and tensor
identities above use those same charts and the ordered valuation laws; the
positive-power hypothesis excludes the zeroth-power counterexample below.

`sectionDomainGE_ofMod` uses the sheaf cokernel of a morphism `μ : ℒ → ℒ` and
local lifts of its section. In `sectionDomainGE_ofMod_eq`, `μ` acts on every
open by multiplication by `a^m`, and `q < m`; any global lift yields exactly
`sectionDomainGE`, and the same statement after restriction identifies local
lifts. Its definition requires no global lift. The strict estimate and gluing
are the general line-bundle form of Scholze15 Def. III.2.12, Lem. III.2.13 and
the following generic-fibre description, p. 38.

`SectionDomainModel.genericFibre_eq` identifies the image of the model's generic
fibre with `sectionDomainGE` and states that its projection is an open immersion.
It assumes an admissible model, an invertible `ℒ`, `c ≠ 0`, and
`c^(q.den) = ϖ^(q.num) · w` with `w ∈ O_Kˣ`; both formal schemes have type (S).
The unit factor has value one. The statement is the valuation-domain form of
`sectionDomainModel_genericFibre`, using the local equation in Scholze15
Lem. III.2.13, p. 38. For thresholds not realized in `O_K`, the existing model
of `(s^{⊗b}, ϖ^a)` and `sectionDomainGE_pow` give the same fractional domain.

**Checks for upper bounds and quotient sections.**

- `sectionDomainLE_zero` — the zero section lies below the unit threshold everywhere.
- `sectionDomainLE_unit` — the unit section at exponent zero gives the whole space.
- `sectionDomainLE_zeroThreshold` — a unit section cannot lie below the zero threshold at exponent `1/2`.
- `sectionDomainGE_ofMod_zero` — for `q < m`, the zero class modulo `ϖ^m` has empty lower domain.
- `sectionDomainGE_ofMod_generator` — the class of the unit section has the whole domain.
- `sectionDomainGE_ofMod_lifts` — adding `μ(t)` to a lift preserves its domain when `μ` is multiplication by `ϖ^m` and `q < m`.

**Checks.**

- `sectionDomain_test_projectiveLine` (computation) — for `𝔛 = P̂¹_{O_K}`, `ℒ = O(1)`, `s = T_0` and
  `q = 1`: `sectionDomainGE s 1 = {x : |T_0(x)| ≥ |ϖ| · max(|T_0(x)|, |T_1(x)|)}`, the complement of
  the closed valuation subset `{|T_0/T_1| < |ϖ|}` (which need not be open at higher-rank points).
  The check states the local homogeneous-coordinate formula for a pair of
  sections generating the line: in an integral frame their coordinates generate
  the unit ideal, so their maximum value is one. It applies to `T_0,T_1` on both
  standard formal charts of `P̂¹`.
- `sectionDomain_test_generatorIndependence` (characterisation) — on `𝔛 = Spf O_K⟨T, T⁻¹⟩` with `ℒ =
  O`, the generators `e` and `T·e` give the same domain for `s = T² e = T·(Te)`: `{|T²| ≥ |ϖ|^q} =
  {|T| ≥ |ϖ|^q}` because `|T| = 1` on `d(𝔛)`.
- `sectionDomain_test_liftIndependence` (characterisation) — on `Spf O_K⟨T⟩` with `ℒ = O` and `q =
  1/2`: `s = T` and `s' = T + ϖ` give the same domain `{|T²| ≥ |ϖ|}`; for `q = 1` they do not (the
  point `T = −ϖ` lies in the first but not the second). The check also
  evaluates these two sections after that constant specialization: at `q = 1`
  their domains are respectively the whole generic fibre and the empty open.
- `sectionDomain_test_integralStructure` (non-example) — replacing `ℒ` by the lattice `ϖ⁻¹ℒ ⊇ ℒ` in
  the same `ℒ_η` multiplies the local coordinates of `s` by `ϖ` and changes the domain from `{|s| ≥ |ϖ|^q}` to `{|s|_ℒ ≥ |ϖ|^{q−1}}`; a definition using only `ℒ_η` is ill-defined. The
  equality uses `q+1` on the rescaled side and `q` on the original side, and
  separately states emptiness for rescaled exponents below one.
- `sectionDomain_test_degenerate` (degenerate) — if `s̄` generates `ℒ/ϖℒ` everywhere then the domain
  is `d(𝔛)` for every `q ≥ 0`; if `s = 0` it is empty.

**Checks for powers and lift independence.**

- `sectionDomainGE_test_zeroPower` — the zeroth tensor power of the zero section is `1`:
  its threshold-zero domain is the whole space, whereas the original zero section's is empty.
  Thus the power identity requires `n > 0`.
- `sectionDomainGE_test_twoTerm` — `|1+p| = 1 ≥ |p|^{1/2}` and
  `|0+p| = |p| < |p|^{1/2}` at the `p`-adic valuation, including `p = 2`.
  Adding a term divisible by `p` preserves these two sides of the threshold.

`FormalScheme.SectionInverse` records a morphism from the pulled-back line bundle
to the pulled-back unit with composite multiplication by the threshold.
**Checks:** `SectionInverse_unit` has a unique solution for the unit section;
`SectionInverse_zeroThreshold` admits the zero solution; `SectionInverse_zeroSection`
has no solution for nonzero threshold on a nonempty admissible model.
`FormalScheme.SectionDomainModel` records the representing formal scheme and
`FormalScheme.sectionDomainModel` selects it.
**Checks:** `SectionDomainModel_unit` / `sectionDomainModel_unit` give the original
model for the unit section; `SectionDomainModel_zero` / `sectionDomainModel_zero`
give the empty model for the zero section and nonzero threshold;
`SectionDomainModel_associated` / `sectionDomainModel_associated` identify thresholds
differing by a unit.


**Checks for the selected model.** `sectionDomainModel_unitSection` makes its projection
an isomorphism for the unit section and any nonzero threshold;
`sectionDomainModel_zeroSection` makes its space empty for the zero section and nonzero
threshold; `sectionDomainModel_representing` gives a unique isomorphism over the original
formal scheme to any other model representing the same functor. These statements apply
to the selected `sectionDomainModel` itself, with the line-bundle and admissibility hypotheses.
At exponent `q = 0` the threshold is `c = 1`: the model is the open where the section
is invertible, and is the entire formal scheme when the section generates everywhere
(Scholze15, Lemma III.2.13, p. 38, the equation `u s = 1`).


**Formal model of a section domain: the open chart of the admissible blow-up of `(s, c)`.**
(*section-domain-formal-model*) Let `𝔛` be an admissible formal `O_K`-scheme, `ℒ` invertible, `s ∈
Γ(𝔛, ℒ)`, and `c ∈ O_K ∖ {0}` the threshold (e.g. `c = ϖ^a`, or `c = p^ε` when `K` contains such an
element; for a fractional `q = a/b` without such an element use `(s^{⊗b}, ϖ^a)` in `ℒ^{⊗b}`), so
that the ideal below contains `c O_𝔛` and is open. Let `𝒜 ⊆ O_𝔛` be the coherent open ideal locally
generated by `(f_j, c)` where `s = f_j e_j` (independent of generators), and let `𝔛(|s| ≥ |c|) ⊆
Bl_𝒜 𝔛` be the open formal subscheme where `s` generates `𝒜O`; the model is an open formal subscheme

Spf(R/R[ϖ^∞])`, where `R = A⟨u⟩/(fu − c)` and
