The affine section-model Checks compare the actual global section ring with the
displayed quotient and preserve the base coordinates. The torsion Check exhibits the
nonzero class of `Tu − 1` before saturation. The point Check asserts unique lifting at
`T = ϖ` and nonexistence at `T = ϖ²`; the unit-threshold Check identifies the open image
by invertibility of the section in the formal stalk. `sectionDomainModel_test_scholze`
identifies a model of a lift with `hasseDomainModel`, uniquely over the original model
(Scholze15 Definition III.2.12 and Lemma III.2.13, p. 38).

**Hasse domains `X(ε) = {|Ha| ≥ |p|^ε}` and their formal models.** (*hasse-domain*) Let `p` be a
prime, `K` a complete extension of `ℚ_p` (`|p| = p⁻¹`), `𝔛` an admissible formal `O_K`-scheme, `ω`
an invertible `O_𝔛`-module, and `Ha ∈ Γ(𝔛 ⊗_{O_K} O_K/p, ω^{⊗(p−1)})` a section — the Hasse
invariant; for modular curves and Shimura varieties it is supplied by the moduli roadmaps. For `ε ∈
ℚ` with `0 ≤ ε < 1` the Hasse domain is `X(ε) := 𝔛_η(|Ha| ≥ |p|^ε) ⊆ d(𝔛)`, the section domain
(*section-valuation-domain*) of any local lift `H̃a` of `Ha` to `ω^{⊗(p−1)}`, with the fractional
convention of *fractional-valuation-bound*; it is well defined because two lifts differ by
`p·(section)` and `|p| < |p|^ε` for `ε < 1` (for `ε = 1` the domain depends on the lift). If `O_K`
contains an element `p^ε` of `p`-adic valuation `ε` (an explicitly chosen element; for instance the
completion of `ℚ_p(μ_{p^∞})` contains such elements for every `ε ∈ (1/(p−1))·ℤ[1/p]`), the formal
model `𝔛(ε) := 𝔛(|H̃a| ≥ |p^ε|)` (*section-domain-formal-model*) is independent of the local lift up
to canonical isomorphism — equivalently it represents, on `p`-adically complete flat `O_K`-algebras
`S`, pairs `(g : Spf S → 𝔛, u ∈ Γ(Spf S, g*ω^{⊗(1−p)}))` with `u·Ha(ḡ) = p^ε` in `S/p`, modulo `u ~ u(1 + p^{1−ε}h)` — and `d(𝔛(ε)) = X(ε)`; without such an element one uses the fractional-bound
domain on the generic fibre or passes to an explicit extension. `X(0) = {|Ha| = 1}` is the tube of
the ordinary locus `𝔛_s ∖ V(Ha)`. Formation of `X(ε)` commutes with pull-back along morphisms `𝔜 → 𝔛`
(with the pulled-back `ω` and `Ha`) and with base change along complete extensions of `K`.
The formal functor has the same compatibility on flat, complete test algebras: its pullback
is taken among admissible models, removing `p`-power torsion when necessary; an ordinary
formal fibre product need not be flat. In `FormalScheme`, define `hasseDomain` (`X(ε) ⊆ d(𝔛)` for `0 ≤ ε < 1`) and
`hasseDomainModel` (`𝔛(ε)` when `p^ε ∈ O_K`); prove `hasseDomain_eq_sectionDomainGE` (`X(ε) =
sectionDomainGE H̃a ε` for every local lift `H̃a`), `hasseDomain_indep_lift` (`X(ε)` does not depend
on the lifts, `ε < 1`), `hasseDomainModel.homEquiv` (maps `Spf S → 𝔛(ε)` over `𝔛`, `S` flat
`p`-adically complete, correspond to `u ∈ Γ(g*ω^{⊗(1−p)})` with `u·Ha(ḡ) = p^ε` in `S/p`, modulo `u ~ u(1 + p^{1−ε}h)`), `hasseDomainModel_genericFibre` (`d(𝔛(ε)) = X(ε)`),
`hasseDomainModel_isoOfLift` (different local lifts give canonically isomorphic models),
`hasseDomain_zero` (`X(0)` is the tube of the ordinary locus), `hasseDomain_mono` (`ε ≤ ε'` implies
`X(ε) ⊆ X(ε')`), `hasseDomain_preimage` (for `g : 𝔜 → 𝔛` with `ω_𝔜 = g*ω` and `Ha_𝔜 = g*Ha`:
`d(g)⁻¹(X(ε)) = Y(ε)`, the Hasse domain of `(𝔜, g*ω, g*Ha)` in `d(𝔜)`) and `hasseDomainModel_flat`
(if `Ha` is a non-zero-divisor on `𝔛 ⊗ 𝔽_p`, e.g.
`𝔛 ⊗ 𝔽_p` normal and `Ha` nonzero on every component, the local rings `O⟨u⟩/(uH̃a − p^ε)` are
`p`-torsion-free, Scholze Lemma III.2.10) (Scholze15 §III.2, Def. III.2.12, p. 38, the functorial
definition of the formal model; after Lem. III.2.13, p. 38, the generic fibre of the model; before
Def. III.2.12, p. 37, the Hasse invariant as a section of `ω^{⊗(p−1)}` on the special fibre; BHW
§2.1, p. 7 of the author version, the definition through local lifts). For the modular curve (`Γ(N)`, `N ≥ 3`) with `ω`
the Hodge bundle, `X(ε)` is BHW's `ε`-nearly ordinary locus `X*(ε)`, and `𝔛(ε)` is the canonical
formal model of BHW Definition 4.1 when `0 ≤ ε ≤ 1/p^{m+1}` for a canonical-subgroup level
`m ≥ 1`, the range of that definition. *Needs:* *section-valuation-domain*;
*section-domain-formal-model*; *fractional-valuation-bound*; *admissible-formal-scheme*; *tube*;
*generic-fibre-fibre-products*.

**Section and model signatures.** `hassePower ω p` is the `(p−1)`-fold tensor
product, formed with the supplied sheaf tensor product. The section `Ha` is a morphism
`O_𝔛 → cokernel (p • id)` on this sheaf; this is a section modulo `p`, not a choice of
global lift. `hasseDomain` takes the union of the local lift inequalities in affine
integral frames. Its parameter is `ε : ℚ≥0` together with `hε : ε < 1`.
`sectionDomainGE 𝔛 ℒ s a q` evaluates the numerator and denominator powers in the
analytic stalk valuations, with `a ∈ Γ(𝔛,O_𝔛)`; for Hasse domains `a = p`.
`hasseDomain_eq_sectionDomainGE` assumes a global lift with reduction `Ha` and gives
this equality; on restrictions it gives the identical statement for each local lift.
`hasseDomain_indep_lift` explicitly assumes `s' = s + p • t`.
The geometric theorems carry an admissible structural map to a complete rank-one
valuation base with pseudouniformizer `p`, and local triviality of `ω`. This includes
complete extensions of `ℚ_p`, without requiring a discrete value group.
`hasseDomain_isOpen` states openness; `hasseDomain_mono` requires both radii below one;
`hasseDomain_zero` identifies the inverse image of the ordinary open via unit
coefficients in formal stalks. `hasseDomain_preimage` uses integral isomorphisms identifying the pulled-back unit
and Hasse line, and the induced map of cokernels; unit changes of frame do not
affect the resulting domain.
These are the local valuation consequences of Scholze15, pp. 37–38, especially
Definition III.2.12 and the paragraph following Lemma III.2.13.

`hasseDomainModel` takes `c ≠ 0` and an integral unit `w` with
`c^{ε.den} = p^{ε.num} w`; this is the exact meaning of the chosen threshold.
It glues the `SectionDomainModel` charts of local lifts.
`hasseDomainModel_admissible` states admissibility and adicity of its projection.
`hasseDomainModel_localIso` makes each local lift chart a cartesian square over a
formal open, including when `Ha` has no global lift.
`hasseDomainModel_isoOfLift` identifies every such model with the selected model
and identifies the models for two lifts, uniquely over `𝔛`.
`hasseDomainModel_genericFibre` states open immersion and equality of its image with
`hasseDomain`. For a global lift, `hasseDomainModel.homEquiv` identifies maps from
a `p`-torsion-free formal test model with `SectionInverse`; these identifications
apply locally and glue. On any `p`-adically complete, `p`-torsion-free `O_K`-algebra,
without a finite-presentation assumption, `hasseDomainModel.homEquiv_mod` identifies the
quotient of `{u : uf − c ∈ pS}` by `u' = u(1 + rh)`, where `cr = p` and
`r ∈ m_K`, with `{u : uf = c}`. This supplies the residue-class formulation above.
`hasseDomainModel_flat` assumes an admissible `p`-adic algebra and regularity of
`f mod p`, and asserts that the unsaturated chart `A⟨u⟩/(fu−c)` has no `p`-torsion,
including the unit-threshold case. The model statements use Scholze15,
Definition III.2.12 and Lemma III.2.13, p. 38; the flatness statement is the
flatness portion of Lemma III.2.10, p. 36 (normality is needed there for the
additional extension theorem, not for this assertion).

**Checks for the tensor power and section domain.**

- `hassePower_two` — at `p = 2` the Hasse line is `ω`.
- `hassePower_three` — at `p = 3` it is `ω ⊗ ω`.
- `hassePower_unit` — every tensor power of the structure line is the structure line.
- `sectionDomainGE_unit` — the unit section has the entire generic fibre at every
  nonnegative radius with integral scalar `p`.
- `sectionDomainGE_zeroSection` — the zero section has empty domain at radius zero.
- `sectionDomainGE_half` — with zero section and zero scalar, radius `1/2` gives
  the whole generic fibre, whereas radius zero gives the empty set (`0⁰ = 1`).

**Checks.**

- `hasseDomain_test_toy` (inclusion) — the ordinary domain lies in the half-radius
  section domain of every lift. For `Ha = T mod p` on `Spf ℤ_p⟨T⟩`, the local
  equation is `|T²| ≥ |p|`; the point computation is the direction-of-`GE` Check of
  *fractional-valuation-bound*.
  Over `ℤ_p[√p]` the chart has equation `Tu = √p`.
- `hasseDomain_test_liftAtOne` (non-example) — for `ε = 1` the locus depends on the lift: with `H̃a
  = T` and `H̃a' = T + p` on `Spf ℤ_p⟨T⟩`, the classical point `T = −p` lies in `{|T| ≥ |p|}` but
  not in `{|T + p| ≥ |p|}`; hence the restriction `ε < 1`.
- `hasseDomain_test_ordinary` (degenerate) — `hasseDomain 0 = {|Ha| = 1}`, the tube of the ordinary
  locus `𝔛_s ∖ V(Ha)`; for `Ha` invertible (`𝔛_s` ordinary) every `X(ε)` is `d(𝔛)`.
- `hasseDomain_test_scholze` (compatibility) — for Scholze's `X*` over `ℤ_p^cycl` with `p^ε ∈
  ℤ_p^cycl`, `hasseDomainModel ε ≅ X*(ε)` of Definition III.2.12 and its generic fibre is `{|Ha| ≥
  |p|^ε}`.
- `hasseDomain_test_noRoot` (non-example) — for `K = ℚ_p` and `ε = 1/2` there is no element of `ℚ_p`
  of absolute value `|p|^{1/2}`: `hasseDomain (1/2)` is still defined by `|H̃a²| ≥ |p|`, while the
  model with linear equation requires an extension containing a square root of `p`;
  over `ℤ_p` one can instead use the open chart of the blow-up of `(H̃a², p)` in
  `ω^{⊗2(p−1)}`.

- `hasseDomain_zeroSection` — a zero section modulo `p` has empty domain for every
  `ε < 1`; a lift divisible by `p` cannot meet the threshold.
- `hasseDomainModel_unit` — a globally generating lift gives the original model.
- `hasseDomainModel_zeroSection` — the zero Hasse section gives the empty model.
- `hasseDomainModel_associated` — associated choices of the threshold give a unique
  isomorphism over the original formal scheme.

**Transition maps between Hasse domains as the radius changes.** (*hasse-domain-transition-maps*) In

**Formal Hasse-section interface.** For an admissible formal `O`-scheme `𝔛`
of type (S), with `O` a complete rank-one valuation ring for the `p`-adic topology,
`p` prime, an invertible integral module `ω`, and a section `Ha` of
`ω^{⊗(p−1)}/p`, `FormalScheme.hasseLocusGE` bundles `hasseDomain` as an
`Opens (genericFibre 𝔛).obj`. Its argument `ε : ℚ≥0`, `ε < 1`, is the
exponent: the absolute threshold is `h = |p|^ε`. `FormalScheme.hasseLocusGT`
is the union of the non-strict opens with exponents `δ < ε`, `δ < 1`.
At `ε = 1` this is the strict locus above the floor, and at `ε = 0` it is empty.
On classical points these have the inequalities for `max(|a|, 1/p)` above;
on the adic space the non-strict inequality uses the full stalk valuation,
and the strict open uses the admissible exhaustion.
`FormalScheme.hasseInvariantValue` takes a point and a real valuation of its
analytic stalk. With a rank-one representative of the point's valuation,
normalized by `v(p) = 1/p`, `FormalScheme.hasseInvariantValue_local` computes
it as `max(v(a), 1/p)` for every integral frame and every lift of `Ha` modulo `p`
(Conrad-MR Definition B.3.3 and its preceding calculation, pp. 49–50).
`FormalScheme.hasseLocusGE_mem_iff` and `FormalScheme.hasseLocusGT_mem_iff`
identify membership with the respective real inequalities under precisely
these normalization and rank-one hypotheses (Conrad-MR Theorem 4.1.1,
proof on p. 27).

`FormalScheme.isOpen_hasseLocusGE` states openness of both loci.
`FormalScheme.hasseLocusGE_quasiCompact` states compactness of the intersection
with every compact open of the ambient generic fibre, hence quasi-compactness
of the inclusion without assuming that the ambient space is compact.
`FormalScheme.iUnion_hasseLocusGE` states the union identity and a finite
subcover on each compact open contained in the strict locus, for `ε ≤ 1`.
`FormalScheme.hasseLocusGE_local` identifies the locus with `sectionDomainGE`
for any global lift; restricting to formal affine opens gives the local formula.
`FormalScheme.hasseLocusGE_eq_hasseDomain` identifies the two subsets exactly.
`FormalScheme.hasseLocus_baseChange` assumes an adic map of admissible formal
`O`-schemes, integral isomorphisms of the pulled-back unit and Hasse line,
and a compatible isomorphism of their cokernels modulo `p`; it identifies the
inverse images of both opens with the opens of the pulled-back section
(Conrad-MR Theorem 4.1.1(1)–(2), pp. 26–27; Scholze15 Definition III.2.12,
Lemma III.2.13 and the following generic-fibre description, pp. 37–38).
`FormalScheme.hasseLocus_extendScalars` states the same comparison for a
cartesian square of admissible formal models over a map of complete rank-one
valuation-ring bases, with the integral line and cokernel isomorphisms as above;
both bases have the `p`-adic topology (same source locators). The strict comparison
includes `ε = 1`, while the non-strict comparison requires `ε < 1`.
The generalized-curve interface in R3.7a also requires construction of the
Hodge line and its Hasse section from the curve, including semistable descent;
the formal Hasse-section interface takes that integral section as input. The
classifying covers and the descent of the opens come from
*rigid-generalised-elliptic-level-classification* and
*rigid-etale-descent-admissible-opens*, not from this interface.

**Checks for the formal opens.**

- `hasseInvariantValue_ordinary` — a generating section modulo `p` has value `1`.
- `hasseInvariantValue_zeroSection` — a zero section modulo `p` has value `1/p`.
- `hasseInvariantValue_bounds` — every value lies between `1/p` and `1`,
  excluding both negative values and values above the ordinary endpoint.
- `hasseLocusGE_ordinary` — a generating section modulo `p` gives the whole
  generic fibre at `ε = 0`.
- `hasseLocusGE_zeroSection` — the zero section gives the empty open for `ε < 1`.
- `hasseLocusGE_half` — at `ε = 1/2` any lift gives the bound `|a²| ≥ |p|`,
  without a square root of `p` in the base field.
- `hasseLocusGT_top` — at absolute threshold `1`, the strict open is empty.
- `hasseLocusGT_ordinary` — a generating section has the whole generic fibre
  strictly above the floor `1/p`.
- `hasseLocusGT_floor` — the zero section has empty strict locus above the floor,
  even though its fibrewise non-strict locus at the floor is the whole space.

**Flatness from flatness modulo powers of an ideal.** (*adic-local-flatness-criterion*) Let `A` be a
commutative ring, `I ⊆ A` an ideal and `M` an `A`-module, with no noetherian or completeness
hypothesis on `A`. Assume that for every finitely generated ideal `a ⊆ A` (1) the `I`-adic topology
of `A` induces the `I`-adic topology of `a`: for every `n` there is `m` with `a ∩ I^m ⊆ I^n a`, and
(2) `a ⊗_A M` is `I`-adically separated: `⋂_n I^n (a ⊗_A M) = 0`; the two conditions replace
Artin–Rees and Krull intersection. Prove that if `M/I^n M` is flat over `A/I^n` for every `n ≥ 1`,
then `M` is flat over `A`; and that in the same situation, if moreover `I ⊆ Jac(A)` and `M/IM` is
faithfully flat over `A/I`, then `M` is faithfully flat over `A` (BL I §1, proof of Lem. 1.6, p.
295: Bosch–Lütkebohmert reduce Lemma 1.6 to the proof of Bourbaki AC III §5 no. 2 Theorem 1 under
exactly the conditions (1) and (2), condition (2) reading '`a ⊗ M` is separated with respect to the
`𝔍`-adic topology'; p. 296, the faithful-flatness addendum via Nakayama). For `A` noetherian, `I ⊆
Jac(A)` and `M` finite over a noetherian `A`-algebra `B` with `IB ⊆ Jac(B)`, (1) is Artin–Rees and
(2) Krull's intersection theorem, giving the noetherian local flatness criterion used in the
noetherian case of Bosch–Lütkebohmert I 1.6. *Needs:* Mathlib `Module.Flat`,
`Module.Flat.iff_rTensor_injective`.

**Conrad's Berthelot-type generic fibre preserves finiteness, smoothness, flatness, properness and
fibre dimension.** (*berthelot-rig-functor-preserves-properties*) Let `C` be an adic noetherian ring
with a continuous map `C → R` to the valuation ring of a complete nonarchimedean field `k` (no
discreteness assumption), and let `f : X → Y` be a morphism in `FS_C` that is locally topologically
of finite type. Prove: (a) if `f` is finite so is `f^rig`; (b) if `f` is formally smooth of pure
relative dimension `d` then `f^rig` is smooth of pure relative dimension `d` (formally étale implies
étale), in Part II's sense, on generic fibres that are locally noetherian and hence locally
Huber-standard; (c) if `f` is finite flat of constant rank `d` so is `f^rig`; (d) if `f` is proper so is
`f^rig`; (e) if `f` is flat (resp. faithfully flat) so is `f^rig`; (f) if all fibres of `f` have
dimension `≤ d` so do those of `f^rig`; (g) if `f` is flat with geometrically reduced fibres of pure
dimension `d`, so is `f^rig` (Conrad-MR §3.1, Thm 3.1.6, p. 17, statements (a)–(g); proof of Thm
3.1.6, p. 18, the reduction by base change along `Spf R → Spf C` and by the rescalings `Y_c` to
Raynaud's generic fibre of formal `R`-models). After that reduction the inputs for (d), (f) and
(g) are targets of this roadmap. In (d), `f^rig` is proper in the adic sense of
*universally-closed-and-proper-morphism* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R0). This is the forward direction
of *formal-rigid-properness-comparison* (ii), applied to the `R`-flat quotients of the base-changed
models; `d` kills `ϖ`-torsion, so their generic fibres do not change. Conrad's rigid statement
asserts Kiehl-properness. For non-discrete `|k^×|` that needs Temkin's comparison through Berkovich
spaces [Te, Cor. 4.4 and 4.5, p. 18 of the
[author version](https://math.huji.ac.il/~temkin/papers/Local_Properties_I.pdf)], which is not
asserted here. Clauses (f) and (g) are *formal-model-fibre-comparison* (v) for the base-changed
models, the statement Conrad uses on p. 18 as Thm A.2.1. For `C = ℤ` and the Tate curve over
`ℤ[[q^{1/n}]]`, (d) and (e) give a proper flat adic curve over the open unit disc (Conrad-MR §3.1,
after Thm 3.1.6). *Needs:* *berthelot-type-rig-functor-nonnoetherian-base*; *raynaud-generic-fibre*;
*raynaud-theorem*; *formal-rigid-properness-comparison*; *formal-model-fibre-comparison*;
*smooth-formal-scheme*; *formal-etale-site-invariance*; *rigid-analytic-space* (AdicSpacesPartII
layer R1); *universally-closed-and-proper-morphism* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R0).

`FormalScheme.rigOfFSC_preservesProperties` has seven conjuncts in the order
(a)–(g) above. Its field presentation identifies the chart ring with the complete
nontrivially valued field `K`, continuously in both directions, and its plus ring
with `K`'s power-bounded subring. The coefficient map is continuous and lands in
that plus ring. The common hypothesis `Hom.LocallyOfFiniteType f` includes
adicness. Write `rₙ` for `Hom.adicReduction f hft.choose n`, formed using powers
of the target ideal of definition extended to the source. In (b), formal
smoothness of dimension `d` is expressed by `SmoothOfRelativeDimension d rₙ`
for every `n`; the conclusion uses Part II's `Smooth.relativeDimension` and
includes `Etale` when `d = 0`. In (c), formal stalk flatness, finiteness of `r₀`
and `r₀.finrank y = d` yield analytic finiteness, flatness and local bases indexed
by `Fin d` for the sections over inverse images of affinoid target neighbourhoods.
Clause (e) also preserves surjectivity under its flatness hypothesis.

In (f), the scheme fibres of `r₀` have topological Krull dimension at most `d`.
In (g), `r₀` is geometrically reduced with pure-dimensional fibres, and `f` is
flat on formal stalks. Both analytic conclusions quantify over maps from every
complete rank-one field spectrum and supply an actual cartesian fibre. Clause
(f) bounds the ring Krull dimension on each affinoid chart of that fibre;
(g) requires those chart rings to be reduced and their prime spectra to have
pure dimension `d`. Quantifying over field extensions is essential for geometric
reducedness. These formulations retain empty fibres. Sources: Conrad-MR,
[Theorem 3.1.6 and Remark 3.1.7, pp. 17–18](https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/genpaper.pdf);
Fujiwara–Kato I.4.8.2, p. 329, and I.5.3.18, pp. 346–347, for reduction criteria.

**Checks.**

- `rigOfFSC_preservesProperties_emptyRank` — the zero algebra over a field has
  rank zero and Krull dimension `⊥`; its empty spectrum is pure of every dimension,
  in particular dimension one.
- `rigOfFSC_preservesProperties_identityRank` — a field over itself has rank one
  and its spectrum is pure of dimension zero.
- `rigOfFSC_preservesProperties_doublePoint` — `F[T]/(T²)` has rank two over `F`
  and pure dimension zero, but is not reduced, in every characteristic. Finite
  flat rank counts length, and the reducedness hypothesis in (g) is independent
  of the dimension bound in (f).

**Coherent modules and coherent rings.** (*coherent-modules*) Let `A` be a commutative ring, with no
noetherian hypothesis: the point of the notion is the non-noetherian rings `O_K⟨ξ⟩/a`. A finitely
generated `A`-module `M` is coherent if every finitely generated submodule of `M` is finitely
presented (coherent means finitely generated with all finitely generated submodules finitely
presented, not merely finitely presented); `A` is a coherent ring if it is coherent as an
`A`-module, i.e. every finitely generated ideal is finitely presented. This is the ring case of EGA
0 §5.3 as recalled in Bosch–Lütkebohmert I §1. Neither predicate is in Mathlib or Tau Ceti (Tau
Ceti's `FinitelyPresentedSheaf` is finite presentation only), and SchemeAndStackFoundations'
pseudo-coherence (Layer 0, §0.5) is a different notion — a module with a resolution by finite free
modules up to a given degree. Its finite syzygy conditions are distinct from requiring every
finite submodule to be finitely presented. Define `Module.IsCoherent` (`M` is finitely generated
and every finitely generated submodule of `M` is finitely presented) and `IsCoherentRing` (`A` is
`Module.IsCoherent` over itself); prove `Module.IsCoherent.of_exact_left`,
`Module.IsCoherent.of_exact_right` and `Module.IsCoherent.of_exact_middle` (in a short exact
sequence `0 → M' → M → M'' → 0` any two coherent members make the third coherent),
`Module.IsCoherent.ker`, `Module.IsCoherent.coker`, `Module.IsCoherent.range`,
`Module.IsCoherent.sup` and `Module.IsCoherent.inf` (kernels, cokernels and images of linear maps
between coherent modules, and sums and intersections of coherent submodules of a coherent module,
are coherent; hence finite direct sums are), `IsCoherentRing.isCoherent_iff_finitePresentation`
(over a coherent ring, `Module.IsCoherent A M ↔ Module.FinitePresentation A M`),
`Module.IsCoherent.tensorProduct` and `Module.IsCoherent.linearMap` (over a coherent ring, `M ⊗_A N`
and `Hom_A(M, N)` are coherent for coherent `M`, `N`), `IsCoherentRing.quotient` (if `A` is coherent
and `a ⊆ A` is a finitely generated ideal then `A/a` is a coherent ring, and an `A/a`-module is
coherent over `A/a` iff it is coherent over `A`) and the instance `IsNoetherianRing.isCoherentRing`
(noetherian rings are coherent) (BL I §1, before Prop. 1.3, p. 294: the definition, and the
two-out-of-three and closure properties quoted from EGA I_new 0 5.3.2;
[Stacks, Definition 10.90.1 and Lemmas 10.90.3–10.90.5](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05CU),
for the general predicates, exact sequences and finite-presentation comparison). *Needs:* Mathlib
`Module.FinitePresentation`.

**Checks.**

- `coherent_test_noetherian` (compatibility) — a noetherian ring is `IsCoherentRing`, and over it
  `Module.IsCoherent` coincides with `Module.Finite`.
- `coherent_test_nonCoherentRing` (non-example) — for a field `k`, `A = k[x, y_1, y_2, …]/(x y_1, x
  y_2, …)` is not a coherent ring: the principal ideal `(x)` is finitely generated but not finitely
  presented, since its annihilator `(y_1, y_2, …)` is not finitely generated.
- `coherent_test_notJustFinitelyPresented` (non-example) — in the ring `A` of
  `coherent_test_nonCoherentRing`, the module `A` itself is finitely presented (free of rank one)
  but not coherent, since its finitely generated submodule `(x)` is not finitely presented; so over
  non-noetherian rings 'coherent' cannot be replaced by 'finitely presented' (or by 'finitely
  generated').
- `coherent_test_infinitePolynomial` (computation) — the polynomial ring `ℤ[x_1, x_2, …]` in
  countably many variables is a coherent ring that is not noetherian.
- `coherent_test_zero` (degenerate) — the zero module is coherent over every ring, and the zero ring
  is a coherent ring.

The finite-syzygy predicate `Module.IsPseudoCoherentTo R M n` uses a projective
resolution whose terms in degrees `0` through `n` are finite free. The augmentation is
part of Mathlib's `ProjectiveResolution`, so the finite terms resolve the specified module.
This is the module form of finite pseudo-coherence (Stacks, Tag 064N).

**Checks.** `IsPseudoCoherentTo_zeroModule` holds in every degree for the zero module;
`IsPseudoCoherentTo_finite` identifies degree zero with finite generation;
`IsPseudoCoherentTo_presentation` identifies degree one with finite presentation.

### R2.11 notions this roadmap states for its own use

The moduli scheme below and its formal completion supply the algebraic family and formal
group used for Hasse invariants. Étale descent of admissible opens is also developed here.
The analytic local-algebraicity, classification and level-cover package
(*rigid-generalised-elliptic-level-classification*) and its application
*hasse-loci-admissible-opens* are R3.7a targets, after R3.6's proper coherent theory
and R3.7's GAGA. Formal Hasse-section domains and their models remain in R2.10.

**The compactified moduli of generalised elliptic curves with level structure, and the formal group
along the identity section.** (*compactified-moduli-generalised-elliptic-curves*) Let `Γ` be
`Γ(N)` with `N ≥ 3`, or `Γ₁(N)` with `N` divisible by an integer `d ≥ 5`.
`GeneralisedEllipticCurve.Level` records `N`, an auxiliary factor `d ∣ N` and `full`
(`true` for full level, `false` for cyclic level); full level takes `d = N`. The base
of `L` is `ℤ[1/d]`. In cyclic level only the primes dividing `d` are inverted, so `N`
may be divisible by a prime `p` with `p ∤ d`. Over this base, the compactified fine
moduli scheme `moduli L` carries
`universalCurve L` and `universalLevel L`. Full level includes all values of the
Weil pairing; fixing a primitive root selects the corresponding component over
`ℤ[ζ_N,1/N]`. Smaller levels require stacks; level one has the affine coarse
j-line on the smooth locus and its projective completion on the compactification.

`EllipticModuli.GroupCurve S` has a proper flat locally finitely presented
structure map, its entire smooth open as a commutative group object, and an
action of that group on the whole curve extending multiplication. Properness
supplies the quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness required for finite
presentation. `GroupCurve.Iso` preserves the inclusion, group and action;
`GroupCurve.baseChange` uses scheme pullbacks. `ofElliptic` uses the imported
Modular Curves carrier. `nGon S n` uses positive `n` and cyclically identifies
infinity on component `i` with zero on component `i+1`; `nGon_normalization`
states this gluing's universal property over a field, including the self-gluing
for `n = 1`. `nGon_smoothLocus` identifies the smooth scheme over any ring
with the disjoint union of `n` multiplicative groups. `nGon_smoothPoints`
identifies its group of points over any ring `A` with units times locally constant
component labels on `Spec A`, including disconnected and nonreduced rings. The points `[a:b]` in this statement are `projectivePoint K a b h`
in Mathlib's `Proj K[X₀,X₁]`. `GeneralisedEllipticCurve S` requires every
geometric fibre, with its smooth group and whole-curve action, to be isomorphic
to a smooth elliptic curve or a standard polygon. This imposes the rotation
condition on singular fibres. Explicitly, a generalised elliptic curve over `S` is a proper flat
finitely presented curve `E → S` whose geometric fibres are elliptic curves or standard `n`-gons,
with a morphism `+ : E^sm ×_S E → E` that is an action of the smooth locus `E^sm` on `E`,
restricts on `E^sm ×_S E^sm` to a commutative group law on `E^sm`, and on every singular geometric
fibre acts by rotations on the cyclic polygon of irreducible components; the identification of
such a fibre with a standard `n`-gon carries this group and action structure, not only the curve.
The definition and classification are those of
[Conrad-GEC](https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/kmpaper.pdf), Definition 2.1.4
and the paragraph following it, p. 5; the polygon construction is on pp. 4–5.

In full level, over a `ℤ[1/N]`-scheme `S`, `LevelStructure L E` is an isomorphism
of commutative `S`-group schemes `α : ((ℤ/N)²)_S ≅ E^sm[N]` whose labelled
sections meet every irreducible component of every geometric fibre of `E`.
The label of `(i,j)` is `α(i,j) = iP + jQ`, where `P = α(1,0)` and `Q = α(0,1)`;
these sections are killed by `N` and give a basis of the `N`-torsion in every geometric fibre.
This extends ModularCurves §3N's naive full-level group-scheme definition to generalised
elliptic curves; for smooth `E` it agrees with `GammaFullStructure` via
ModularCurves §3D's naive–Drinfeld comparison. The generalised-curve extension and its
component condition belong to this target. Prove `LevelStructure_map_zero`, giving
`α(0,0) = 0`, and `LevelStructure_map_add`, giving `α(u + v) = α(u) + α(v)` for
full level over every `S`-scheme after base change. In cyclic level the
section `P` is an ample Drinfeld `ℤ/N`-structure: the relative effective Cartier
divisor `∑_{j ∈ ℤ/N} [jP]` in `E^sm` is a subgroup scheme and meets every
irreducible component of every geometric fibre. In residue characteristic `p ∣ N`
this divisor need not be étale; allowing such structures is what gives an integral
moduli problem over a `p`-adic base containing curves whose polygon fibres have a
multiple of `p` sides (Conrad-MR §3.2, p. 19). Where `N` is invertible the
divisor is étale, and the condition says that `P` has exact order `N` on every
geometric fibre and that its multiples meet every component. The component
condition is the curve-specific ampleness criterion, not an extra assumption on an
arbitrary moduli scheme (Conrad-GEC, Definitions 2.4.1–2.4.2, p. 14, and 2.4.7,
p. 16). `moduli_classifies` states existence and uniqueness of the classifying
map for every such family over a `ℤ[1/d]`-scheme, with an isomorphism preserving
the smooth-group law, the whole-curve action and the level structure.
`moduli_isProper` and `moduli_finitePresentation` apply
to this particular representing scheme over `ℤ[1/d]`. For the latter, the conclusion
is local finite presentation together with quasi-compactness and
quasi-separatedness. Sources: Conrad-GEC, Theorems 3.1.4, p. 19, 3.2.7 and
3.3.1, p. 26, and 4.2.1(2), pp. 35–36 (the stack is a scheme over `ℤ[1/d]` for
every factor `d ∣ N` with `d ≥ 5` in cyclic level); Deligne–Rapoport IV §3 gives the
historical construction.

For a prime `p ∤ d` and a complete field `k` over `ℚ_p` with valuation ring `R`,
the base change of `moduli L` to `R` is a proper flat finitely presented
`R`-scheme with generic fibre the moduli scheme over `k`; it is the integral model
whose formal completion *hasse-loci-admissible-opens* uses, with `formalGroup`
applied to the base change of `universalCurve L`
(Conrad-MR §4.1, proof of Thm 4.1.1, p. 26, the level `Γ₁(N)` with an
auxiliary factor `d ≥ 5` invertible in `R`). A level prime to `p` does not
reach curves with a `p`-gon fibre: the component group of a `p`-gon is `ℤ/p`, on
which multiplication by an `N` prime to `p` is invertible, so every `N`-torsion
point lies on the identity component and no level structure meets the other components,
over any extension of the base field (`LevelStructure_pGonPrimeToP`). With `p ∤ d` and
`N = dp` the mixed range applies (`LevelStructure_pGonMixed`).

`identitySection E` is the identity of the smooth group. `formalGroup E` is
its completion along the kernel ideal of that section, using
`FormalScheme.idealCompletion`; `formalGroup.structure` is the induced base
map. The instances `formalGroup.grp` and `formalGroup.comm` supply the
completed commutative group law. `formalGroup_points` identifies its points on
discrete test schemes with smooth-group points supported on the identity,
commutes with the map into the smooth group, and preserves multiplication. Completion uses the identity ideal, so it
retains nilpotents in the base. For a smooth augmented algebra `ε : B →ₐ[A] A`,
write `I = ker ε`. If `t ∈ I` is a basis of `I/I²`, then
`formalGroup.coordinate ε t` identifies `B̂_I` with `A[[X]]`;
`formalGroup_coordinate` sends the image of `t` to `X`.
`formalGroup_affineCoordinate` gives the formal-scheme isomorphism for an
actual affine neighbourhood of `identitySection E`, with compatibility of its
structure map and augmentation, and the `X`-adic topology on `A[[X]]`.
`formalGroup_localParameter` supplies these affine neighbourhoods and a
parameter locally around every base point, with a scalar-preserving completed-ring
equivalence. The basis condition is stated explicitly by generation and linear independence
modulo `I²`. Source: [Stacks, 10.139.4](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05D5);
the local choice of neighbourhoods is [29.35.20](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05D9).
Completion of multiplication uses EGA I, 10.9.1–3, pp. 198–199.
After completion of the base these give the same one-parameter formal group
over the affine formal opens where the invariant differential line is trivial.

`jMap L b` has the complex fibre of `moduli L` as source and `Proj ℂ[X₀,X₁]`
as target. `jMap_values` uses points over `ℂ` and identifies its value on a smooth Weierstrass fibre
with `[j(W):1]` and characterizes the inverse image of `[1:0]` by polygon
fibres (Conrad-GEC, proof of Theorem 4.2.1, p. 36).
`tateCurve n` is the algebraic `n`-gon Tate family over `ℤ[[Q]]`, with
`Q = q^(1/n)`; it specializes to `nGon` and becomes smooth after inverting `Q`.
Its identity completion is isomorphic as a formal group to the identity
completion of the standard 1-gon over the same base, hence to `𝔾̂_m`
(Conrad-GEC, §2.5, construction and (2.5.3), p. 17).
*Needs:* the imported Modular Curves elliptic scheme and group law;
*formal-completion*; `FormalScheme.idealCompletion`; Mathlib `Scheme`,
`IsProper`, `LocallyOfFinitePresentation` and `GrpObj`.

**Checks.**

- `generalisedEllipticModuli_test_jLine` (computation) — the `j`-invariant of the universal curve
  is a finite surjective morphism `j : M_Γ ⊗ ℂ → P¹_ℂ` onto the compactified `j`-line (the coarse moduli space
  of the compactified level-`1` problem, which is not itself one of the `M_Γ`: the level-`1` problem is not representable,
  every curve having the automorphism `−1`); the cusps are `j⁻¹(∞)`.
- `generalisedEllipticModuli_test_tateCurve` (computation) — the Tate curve over `ℤ[[q]]` (with level after adjoining the
  required roots of unity and a root of `q` over `ℤ[1/d]`) has formal
  group `𝔾̂_m` along its identity section: `[p](X) = (1 + X)^p − 1`, with coefficient `1` at `X^p`,
  so its Hasse invariant is `1` and its fibres lie in `S^{≥1}` of *hasse-loci-admissible-opens*.
  The Check uses the formal-group isomorphism of `tateCurve n` with the
  standard 1-gon's identity completion. The power-series coefficient calculation
  applies in the multiplicative coordinate supplied by that isomorphism.
- `generalisedEllipticModuli_test_nGon` (characterisation) — the smooth locus of the standard
  `n`-gon (the fibre of `E` over a cusp, `n ∣ N`) is `𝔾_m × ℤ/n`, with identity component `𝔾_m`;
  for `n = 1` the fibre is the nodal cubic with smooth locus `𝔾_m`.

**Checks for the curve and moduli definitions.** Names without a prefix in this
table are in `GeneralisedEllipticCurve`, except `GroupCurve`, `ofElliptic`,
`nGon` and `projectivePoint`, which are in `EllipticModuli`.

| Definition | Checks |
|---|---|
| `GroupCurve` | `GroupCurve_actionIdentity`: identity acts trivially; `GroupCurve_actionInverse`: a translation followed by its inverse cancels; `GroupCurve_smoothTranslation`: restriction agrees with multiplication. |
| `GroupCurve.Iso` | `GroupCurve.Iso_refl`: reflexivity; `GroupCurve.Iso_symm`: inversion; `GroupCurve.Iso_polygonSize`: different polygon sizes are not isomorphic over a field. |
| `GroupCurve.baseChange` | `GroupCurve.baseChange_id`: identity pullback; `GroupCurve.baseChange_comp`: iterated pullback; `GroupCurve.baseChange_polygon`: standard polygons commute with base change. |
| `ofElliptic` | `ofElliptic_smooth`: the smooth inclusion is an isomorphism; `ofElliptic_identity`: the imported zero section is the identity; `ofElliptic_notPolygon`: no elliptic curve is a polygon. |
| `nGon` | `nGon_one`: the nodal cubic's smooth points are `Kˣ`; `nGon_components`: smooth points are `Kˣ × ℤ/n`; `nGon_twoSingular`: the 2-gon has exactly two singular points, also in characteristic two. |
| `projectivePoint` | `projectivePoint_scaling`: unit scaling fixes a point; `projectivePoint_zeroInfinity`: zero and infinity differ; `projectivePoint_affine`: `[a:1] = [b:1]` exactly when `a = b`. |
| `GeneralisedEllipticCurve` | `GeneralisedEllipticCurve_smooth`: imported elliptic curves qualify; `GeneralisedEllipticCurve_polygon`: every positive polygon qualifies; `GeneralisedEllipticCurve_noEmptyFibre`: every base point has a point above it. |
| `Level` | `Level_fullThree`: full level three is allowed; `Level_cyclicFive`: cyclic level five is allowed; `Level_smallExcluded`: full levels below three, and cyclic levels without a factor at least five, are excluded; `Level_mixed`: for a prime `p ≠ 5`, cyclic level `5p` with factor `5` is allowed and its base `ℤ[1/5]` does not invert `p`. |
| `LevelStructure` | `LevelStructure_fullBasis`: a full `N`-torsion basis on a smooth elliptic curve over `ℂ` gives a structure; `LevelStructure_nonadditiveExcluded`: for `N = 3` and a basis `P,Q`, swapping only the labels `(1,0)` and `(0,1)` fixes zero and bijects onto the torsion but fails `α(2,0) = 2α(1,0)`, since `2P ≠ 2Q`, so is excluded; `LevelStructure_torsion`: labelled sections are killed by `N`; `LevelStructure_trivialExcluded`: a constant identity labelling fails over a geometric point; `LevelStructure_polygonDivides`: the polygon size divides `N`; `LevelStructure_pGonPrimeToP`: over every field of characteristic zero, the standard `p`-gon has no cyclic level structure of level prime to `p`; `LevelStructure_pGonMixed`: for `d ≥ 5` prime to `p`, the point `(ζ_d, 1)` of `G_m × ℤ/p` is a cyclic level structure of level `dp` on the standard `p`-gon over `ℚ_p(ζ_d)`. |
| `moduli` | `moduli_fullThree`: full level three is proper; `moduli_cyclicFive`: cyclic level five is locally finitely presented; `moduli_nonemptyComplex`: every allowed moduli scheme has complex points; `moduli_mixedCharP`: for a prime `p ≠ 5`, the moduli scheme of cyclic level `5p` with factor `5` has a nonempty fibre over `𝔽_p`. |
| `universalCurve` | `universalCurve_flat`: the curve is flat; `universalCurve_proper`: it is proper; `universalCurve_cusp`: it has a complex polygon fibre. |
| `universalLevel` | `universalLevel_zero`: the zero label gives the identity; `universalLevel_torsion`: `N` kills every label; `universalLevel_classifiesIdentity`: identity pullback preserves all labels. |
| `identitySection` | `identitySection_section`: composition with the structure map is the identity; `identitySection_closed`: it is a closed immersion; `identitySection_smooth`: its image lies in the smooth locus. |
| `formalGroup` | `formalGroup_support`: its topological space is the base; `formalGroup_smoothAffine`: over a field `K` the identity completion is `Spf K[[X]]` with its `X`-adic topology; `formalGroup_emptyBase`: an empty base gives an empty completion. |
| `formalGroup.structure`, `formalGroup.grp`, `formalGroup.comm` | `formalGroup.structure_identity`: the identity lies over the base; `formalGroup.structure_inverse`: inverse cancels; `formalGroup.structure_commutes`: the law is commutative. The same examples are labelled `formalGroup.grp_identity`, `formalGroup.grp_inverse`, `formalGroup.grp_commutes`, and `formalGroup.comm_identity`, `formalGroup.comm_inverse`, `formalGroup.comm_commutes`. |
| `formalGroup.coordinate` | `formalGroup.coordinate_linear`: the parameter `T` gives `A[[X]]`; `formalGroup.coordinate_unitMultiple`: so does `uT` for a unit `u`; `formalGroup.coordinate_squareExcluded`: `T²` does not generate the conormal line over a field. |
| `jMap` | `jMap_finite`: finite and surjective; `jMap_zero`: `j = 0` occurs; `jMap_infinity`: a cusp occurs. The first is also `generalisedEllipticModuli_test_jLine`; `jMap_values` identifies precisely which fibres are cusps. |
| `tateCurve` | `tateCurve_specialFibre`: `Q = 0` gives the standard `n`-gon; `tateCurve_genericSmooth`: inverting `Q` gives a smooth curve; `tateCurve_formalMultiplicative`: the completed group is the completed multiplicative group. The last is also `generalisedEllipticModuli_test_tateCurve`; its coefficient calculation uses this isomorphism. |

**Admissible opens, admissible coverings and quasi-compactness descend along étale coverings with
local quasi-sections.** (*rigid-etale-descent-admissible-opens*) Let `k` be a complete
nonarchimedean field with nontrivial absolute value. A morphism `q : S' → S` of rigid spaces over
`k` is an étale covering, `RigidSpace.IsEtaleCovering q`, if it is étale (`RigidSpace.IsEtale`,
*rigid-adic-etale-comparison*, AdicSpacesPartII layer R1), surjective on points, and admits local
étale quasi-sections: there are an admissible covering `{S_i}` of `S` and, for each `i`, a
quasi-compact étale surjection `U_i → S_i` with an `S_i`-morphism `U_i → q⁻¹(S_i)` (Conrad-RA
Def 4.2.1, p. 30). Prove:

(a) `RigidSpace.IsEtaleCovering.baseChange`, `RigidSpace.IsEtaleCovering.ofAdmissibleCover` and
`RigidSpace.IsEtaleCovering.analytification`: étale coverings are stable under base change; the
coproduct of the members of an admissible affinoid covering maps to the base by an étale
covering; and the analytification of an étale surjection of `k`-schemes locally of finite type is
an étale covering (Conrad-RA, p. 31, after Def 4.2.1, and Thm 4.2.2, p. 31).

(b) `RigidSpace.descendOpen`: if `q` is an étale covering and `U' ⊆ S'` an admissible open whose
inverse images under the two projections `S' ×_S S' ⇉ S'` coincide, then `q(U')` is an admissible
open `U` of `S` with `q⁻¹(U) = U'` (`descendOpen_preimage`), and `U` is the only admissible open of
`S` with this inverse image (`descendOpen_unique`) (Conrad-RA Lemma 4.2.4, pp. 32–33).

(c) `RigidSpace.descendOpen_isAdmissibleCover`: if `{U'_j}` is an admissible covering of `S'` by
admissible opens satisfying the hypothesis of (b), the descended opens form an admissible covering
of `S` (Conrad-RA Cor 4.2.6, p. 34).

(d) `RigidSpace.IsEtaleCovering.isQuasiCompact_iff`: a morphism `f : X → S` is quasi-compact if and
only if its base change `X ×_S S' → S'` is (Conrad-RA Thm 4.2.7, pp. 34–36, for this property).

Conrad states (b)–(d) for faithfully flat maps with local fpqc quasi-sections, of which étale
coverings are a special case (Conrad-RA Def 4.2.1); the étale class is enough here because the
level covers of *rigid-generalised-elliptic-level-classification* are étale. On quasi-separated
rigid spaces these statements are read on adic spaces through `r_K`
(*rigid-adic-quasi-separated-equivalence*, AdicSpacesPartII layer R1). Part II's admissible-cover
comparison transports a given covering and its finite-locally-free coequaliser descends morphisms
into a fixed target; neither constructs the descended open of (b).
*Needs:* *rigid-analytic-space*, *rigid-analytification*, *rigid-adic-etale-comparison*,
*analytification-etale-smooth*, *analytification-surjective* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R1);
quasi-compact morphisms of rigid spaces (RigidAnalyticGeometry §6.3, transported through
Part II's *rigid-analytic-space* and *proper-separated-comparisons*).

**Checks.**

- `descendOpen_identity` (degenerate) — for `q = id_S` every admissible open satisfies the
  hypothesis of (b) and descends to itself.
- `descendOpen_fold` (non-example) — the fold map `Sp k ⊔ Sp k → Sp k` is an étale covering; the
  first summand has different inverse images under the two projections and is not `q⁻¹(U)` for
  any admissible open `U`.
- `descendOpen_needsQuasiSections` (boundary) — the map `{|t| = 1} ⊔ {|t| < 1} → Sp k⟨t⟩` is étale
  and surjective, and each summand satisfies the hypothesis of (b), but the images do not form an
  admissible covering of the closed disc; by (c) this map admits no local étale quasi-sections, and
  that hypothesis cannot be removed from (c).
- `isQuasiCompact_iff_openDisc` (characterisation) — the inclusion of `{|t| < 1}` into `Sp k⟨t⟩` is
  not quasi-compact, and neither is its base change along the étale covering
  `Sp k⟨t⟩ ⊔ Sp k⟨t⟩ → Sp k⟨t⟩`.

### Examples

The worked examples of this layer are the checks above and the instances recorded at the lemmas. On
the algebra side: `O_K⟨T⟩` is admissible with generic fibre `K⟨T⟩`, `O_K⟨T⟩/(ϖT)` is topologically
finitely presented but not admissible, the `m_K`-adic completion of `O_K[T]` over `ℂ_p` is `k[T]`
(so the `m_K`-adic topology is the wrong one), and `Spf O_K[[T]]` with the `(ϖ, T)`-adic topology is
neither locally of tf presentation nor, for non-discrete `K`, of type (S). On generic fibres and
specialisation: `t(Spf ℤ_p) = Spa(ℤ_p, ℤ_p)` has two points, `d(Spf O_K⟨T⟩) = Spa(K⟨T⟩, O_K⟨T⟩)` is
the closed unit disc; for discretely valued `K`, the full analytic locus
`d(Spf O_K[[T]])` is quasi-compact and also has points with `|ϖ| = 0`, whereas its fibre
over `Spa(K, O_K)` is the non-quasi-compact open unit disc; `ϖ`-torsion is invisible (`d(Spf O_K/ϖ) = ∅`), the Gauss point specialises to the generic
point of `A¹_k`, the tube of the origin is the open unit disc while `λ⁻¹(0)` also contains `η_{1⁻}`,
the rig-points of `Spf O_K⟨T⟩` correspond to closed points of `Spec K⟨T⟩`
(including points with finite residue-field extension; its `K`-rational points are `T ↦ c` for
`c ∈ O_K`), and the admissible blow-up of `(T, ϖ)`
has special fibre `P¹_k ∪ A¹_k` and an isomorphic generic fibre, whereas blowing up the non-open
`(S, T)` changes the generic fibre. The annulus model `X = Spf O_K⟨ζ, ξ⟩/(ζξ − ϖ) → T = Spf O_K⟨ζ⟩`
runs through the whole flattening argument: its étale-local structure is `Z' = D¹_T` without
localisation, the quotient map `O_{D¹_T} → O_X` is a complete one-step dévissage in dimension `1`
with `𝒫 = 0` and non-injective `α`, its flat locus is `X_0 ∖ V(ζ)` so `O_X` is `T`-flat in dimension
`≥ 2` but not `≥ 1`, it is rig-flat at every rig-point, `F_0 = (ζξ − ϖ)` has ideal of coefficients
`(ζ, ϖ)`, and the admissible blow-up of `(ζ, ϖ)` makes the strict transform `O_K⟨u, ξ⟩/(uξ − 1)`
flat with the pull-back modulo `ϖ`-torsion equal to the strict transform. Contents are computed on
`O_K⟨ξ⟩` (`c(ϖ² + ϖξ + ϖ³ξ²) = (ϖ)`, Gauss's lemma `c(fg) = c(f)c(g)`), ideals of coefficients on
`Spf O_K⟨a, ζ⟩ → Spf O_K⟨a⟩` (`(a²ζ, ϖ)` has `(a², ϖ)`, not `(a, ϖ)`), Fitting ideals on diagonal
presentations (`F_0((O_X/ϖ)²) = (ϖ²) ≠ Ann = (ϖ)`), and the partition blow-up on `O_K⟨ζ⟩/(ζ(ζ − ϖ))`
gives `Spf O_K ⊔ Spf O_K`. For completions of schemes: `A¹_{O_K}` gives the closed unit disc inside
`A^{1,ad}_K`, `G_{m,O_K}` gives `{|T| = 1}`, `P¹_{O_K}` gives `d(P̂¹) ≅ P^{1,ad}_K`, `Spec O_K ⊔ A¹_{O_K/ϖ}` shows that flatness is needed in the properness converse, and `P¹_{O_K} ⊔ Spec K` is a
flat non-proper quasi-projective model whose `φ` misses a point. For Conrad's functor and
smoothness: `Spf(ℤ[[q]])^rig` is the open unit disc over any `k`, `Spf O_{ℂ_p}⟨T⟩` is not in any
`FS_C`, `Spf O_K⟨T_1, …, T_d⟩` and the formal torus are smooth with `Ω¹` free on the `dT_i`, `Spf O_K⟨S, T⟩/(ST − ϖ)` is flat with smooth generic fibre but not smooth, `Spf W(𝔽_{p²}) → Spf ℤ_p`
corresponds to `Spec 𝔽_{p²} → Spec 𝔽_p` with generic fibre `Spa(ℚ_{p²}) → Spa(ℚ_p)`, the Frobenius
lift on the torus is `Σ a_ν T^ν ↦ Σ σ(a_ν) T^{pν}`, and the residue discs of `P̂¹_{O_K}` at `0` and
`∞` are the open unit discs in coordinates `T` and `1/T` (the increasing rational unions
of *residue-disc*). For odd `p` with `2` nonsquare modulo `p`, the closed point `T² = 2` of
`P¹_{𝔽_p}` has a residue disc with no `ℚ_p`-point. For valuative loci: `{|T| ≤ |p|^{1/2}}` in the closed disc over `ℚ_p` is `{|T²|
≤ |p|}` and contains `T = p` but not `T = 1`, the section domain of `T_0 ∈ O(1)` on `P̂¹` is the
complement of the closed valuation subset `{|T_0/T_1| < |ϖ|}`, the formal model of `{|T| ≥ |ϖ|}` on `Spf O_K⟨T⟩` is
`Spf O_K⟨T, u⟩/(Tu − ϖ)` while `s = ϖT` produces `ϖ`-torsion that must be killed, the toy Hasse
domain of `Ha = T mod p` on `Spf ℤ_p⟨T⟩` is `{|T²| ≥ |p|}` with model `Spf ℤ_p[√p]⟨T, u⟩/(Tu − √p)`,
`ε = 1` depends on the lift, Scholze's `X*(ε)` and BHW's `X*(ε)` are instances, and Conrad's
`S^{≥|p|^ε}` for the universal elliptic curve is the Hasse domain of the Hodge bundle, with the
`j`-invariant onto the `j`-line, the Tate curve's formal group `𝔾̂_m` and the `n`-gon's smooth
locus `𝔾_m × ℤ/n` as the checks on the moduli input; the `p`-gon over `ℚ_p` carries no level prime
to `p` and acquires level `dp` over `ℚ_p(ζ_d)`.

## Layer R3: coherent sheaves and finite traces

This layer builds on AdicSpacesPartII R0–R1 and F0 of this roadmap. It constructs the sheaf `M̃ = M ⊗ 𝒪_X` of a finite module on a
noetherian affinoid and proves its acyclicity in both of Huber's noetherian cases (Huber's Theorem
2.5); R3.1a identifies sections of analytified modules on strongly noetherian affinoid charts
with scalar extension, using Part II R1.3–R1.4's general module pullback;
it proves Čech acyclicity of the structure sheaf on every sheafy Tate affinoid (Kedlaya–Liu)
through the reduction of rational coverings to simple Laurent coverings — Tau Ceti has this
reduction for the structure presheaf in degree 0 only, and the results here are for an arbitrary
presheaf in all degrees; it introduces glueing squares and proves Kiehl's theorem; it builds the
abelian tensor category of coherent sheaves, the correspondence between coherent ideals and closed
adic subspaces and between coherent algebras and finite morphisms; it applies Kiehl's Theorems A
and B on quasi-Stein spaces to the open polydisc; it identifies vector bundles on sheafy Tate
affinoids with finite projective modules and treats uniform rings (Tau Ceti's `Huber.IsUniform` is
uniformity as boundedness of `A°`; here its Banach-ring form through the square bound is proved
equivalent); it constructs the coherent sheaf of continuous differentials; it develops strict
complete continuity, relative compactness, Kiehl-properness and étale base change of proper
coherent cohomology around Kiehl's proper mapping theorem, and the GAGA comparison maps; and it
constructs traces of finite projective modules, of finite locally free algebras, of finite locally
free morphisms of schemes and of adic spaces, and the pull–identify–trace operators along
correspondences that the Hecke-operator consumers use. The last subsection states the Gel'fand
spectrum of a Banach ring and Berkovich's spectral-seminorm formula, which the uniform-ring results
of this layer need.

### R3.1 the associated sheaf and acyclicity for finite modules

**The sheaf `M̃ = M ⊗ 𝒪_X` associated with a finite module on a noetherian affinoid.**
(*associated-module-sheaf*) Let `(A, A⁺)` be a Huber pair with `A` complete and Hausdorff and
`A⁺ ⊆ A` a ring of integral elements (AdicSpaces layer 0.2), where `A` is of one of Huber's two
noetherian types: (I) `A` has a noetherian ring of definition, or (II) `A` is a strongly noetherian
Tate ring (Tau Ceti `Huber.IsStronglyNoetherian`: every `A⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩` is noetherian). Let
`X = Spa(A, A⁺)` and let `M` be a finitely generated `A`-module. The associated presheaf `M̃`
(Huber's `M ⊗ 𝒪_A`) is the presheaf of topological `𝒪_X`-modules on `X` defined on the rational
basis by `M̃(U) = M ⊗_A 𝒪_X(U)` for `U = R(T/s)`, where `𝒪_X(U) = A⟨T/s⟩` is the complete rational
localisation of AdicSpaces layer 3.1 and the ordinary (uncompleted) tensor product carries its
natural `𝒪_X(U)`-module topology (the quotient topology along any surjection
`𝒪_X(U)ⁿ ↠ M ⊗_A 𝒪_X(U)`); the restriction for rational `V ⊆ U` is `id_M ⊗ ρ_{V,U}`. On an
arbitrary open `W ⊆ X`, `M̃(W) = lim M̃(V)` over the rational `V ⊆ W`, with the inverse-limit
topology. An `A`-linear map `φ : M → N` induces `φ̃ : M̃ → Ñ`, functorially. The tensor product is
not completed: for finite `M` over these rings `M ⊗_A 𝒪_X(U)` is already complete and equals the
completed tensor product (Huber94 §2, Lem. 2.3(iii) and Lem. 2.4(ii)), and these topological assertions require finitely generated `M`. In `AdicSpace`,
define `tilde` by sheafifying the tensor presheaf for arbitrary modules; for finite
modules over noetherian-type affinoids equip rational sections with their natural
module topology and prove `tilde_obj_rational`
(for `U = R(T/s)`, `M̃(U) = M ⊗_A A⟨T/s⟩` as topological `A⟨T/s⟩`-modules), `tilde_map` (an
`A`-linear `φ : M → N` induces `φ̃ : M̃ → Ñ`, with `tilde_map_id` and `tilde_map_comp`),
`Coh.test_point_baseChange` (for a rational `U` with coordinate pair `(B, B⁺)`, so that `Spa(B, B⁺) ≅ U` by
`spaLocalizationHomeomorph`, `M̃|_U ≅ (M ⊗_A B)~` as presheaves on `Spa(B, B⁺)`; Huber94 §1,
(1.4)), `tilde_test_zero_and_self` and `tilde_free` (`Ã ≅ 𝒪_X` as presheaves of topological `𝒪_X`-modules, and more generally
`(Aⁿ)~ ≅ 𝒪_Xⁿ`), `moduleTensor_associated` (the tensor comparison for associated sheaves; for finite
`M`, `N` on a noetherian-type affinoid its rational-section form is
`(M ⊗_A N)~(U) ≅ M̃(U) ⊗_{𝒪_X(U)} Ñ(U)`), and `Coh.test_point_tensor`
(the specialization to finite modules on the imported analytic point `fieldAffinoid K`), `tilde_exact` (in type II,
strongly noetherian Tate, for every rational `U` the functor `M ↦ M̃(U)` is exact, because
`A → 𝒪_X(U)` is flat, Tau Ceti `Huber.PairOfDefinition.flat_toCompletionLoc`),
`completeSpace_tilde_obj` (for rational `U`, `M̃(U)` is complete and Hausdorff, and every
`A`-linear map of finite modules induces a strict map `M̃(U) → Ñ(U)`) and `tilde_obj_top`
(`M̃(X) = M ⊗_A A = M`, since `X` is the rational subset `R({1}/1)` and `𝒪_X(X) = A`, AdicSpaces
layer 3.5) (Huber94 §2, definition preceding Thm 2.5, p. 525, where Huber defines `M ⊗ 𝒪_A` on an
open `U` as the projective limit of `M ⊗ 𝒪_A(V)` over rational `V ⊆ U`; Huber94 §2, Thm 2.5,
p. 525 for the generality, the two noetherian types and finitely generated modules; Kiehl-AB §1,
Def. 1.1, p. 259 for the rigid form, where a sheaf of modules is associated with the finite
`A`-module `M` when on affinoid subdomains `Sp(B)` it is `B ↦ M ⊗_A B`). *Needs:*
*locally-noetherian-adic-space*, *noetherian-rod-sheafy*, *noetherian-rod-module-complete* (all
AdicSpacesPartII layer R0); Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.spa`, `ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset`,
`Huber.PairOfDefinition.completionLocObj`, `Huber.IsStronglyNoetherian`,
`Huber.PairOfDefinition.isStronglyNoetherian_completion`, `Huber.IsTateRing.isModuleTopology`,
`TauCeti.Huber.isClosed_of_isNoetherian`, `ValuationSpectrum.spaLocalizationHomeomorph`,
`Huber.PairOfDefinition.flat_toCompletionLoc`.

The underlying sheaf of modules is `AdicSpace.tilde`, the sheafification of
`AdicSpace.tensorPresheaf`, whose value is `𝒪(U) ⊗_{𝒪(X)} M` and whose restriction maps act on
the first factor. `tilde_eq` is its characterising equation; `tilde_obj_rational` identifies its
rational sections for finite modules. The coefficient ring is identified with `𝒪(X)` by the
canonical global-section isomorphism. The auxiliary `ringCatSheaf` forgets only the topology on
sections, `Modules` is Mathlib's category of modules over that sheaf, and `sectionsAlgebra` is
restriction from the whole space. Topological completeness is stated separately for finite
modules.

`tilde_map_sections` fixes the induced map on the image of each pure tensor
under the sheafification unit: `a ⊗ m` maps to `a ⊗ φ(m)`. This, together with
`tilde_map_id` and `tilde_map_comp`, specifies association on morphisms.
`tilde_free` includes rank zero. `tilde_obj_top` requires a finite coefficient
module and a noetherian-type chart. `tilde_exact` concerns short exact sequences
of finite modules on rational opens of strongly noetherian Tate affinoids.
`completeSpace_tilde_obj` uses the topology of the original structure-ring
sections and compatible additive uniformities with `IsModuleTopology`; it
asserts completeness, Hausdorffness and strictness on the actual associated
sheaf sections. `tilde_obj_rational_topology` makes the linear equivalence of
`tilde_obj_rational` a homeomorphism for the natural module topologies. Sources: Huber94 §2, Lemmas 2.3–2.4 and Theorem 2.5,
pp. 523–525; KL15 Theorem 2.5.20, pp. 51–52, and Remark 2.5.23, pp. 52–53.

**Checks for induced maps.** `tilde_map_zero` sends a zero map to zero;
`tilde_map_identity` fixes identities; `tilde_map_double` sends twice the
identity to twice the identity, including in characteristic two.

**Checks for the underlying constructions.**

- `ringCatSheaf_sections`, `ringCatSheaf_empty`, `ringCatSheaf_gluing`: sections are the original
  structure-ring sections; sections on the empty open are zero; two sections on `U ∪ V` agree
  when their restrictions to both opens agree.
- `sectionsAlgebra_top`, `sectionsAlgebra_empty`, `sectionsAlgebra_comp`: restriction to the
  whole space is the identity, restriction to the empty open is zero, and restriction through
  an intermediate open is unchanged.
- `tensorPresheaf_zero`, `tensorPresheaf_self`, `tensorPresheaf_empty`: the zero coefficient
  module gives zero sections, the regular module gives `𝒪(U)`, and the empty open gives zero
  for every coefficient module.
- `tilde_zero`, `tilde_self`, `tilde_empty`: association takes zero to zero and the regular
  module to `𝒪_X`; on the empty space every associated module sheaf is zero.

**Checks.**

- `AdicSpace.tilde_test_quotient` (computation) — let `K` be a complete nontrivially
  normed nonarchimedean field, with the compatible ultrametric and Huber-ring instances,
  and choose `ϖ ≠ 0` with `‖ϖ‖ < 1`. Take `A = RigidSpace.Affinoid.polydisc K 1`
  and its image `D` under `rigidToAdic`. The map `A → 𝒪(D)` is the coefficient map
  pulled back along `rigidToAdic_Sp`; it fixes the sections `t = T` and `s = ϖ`.
  For `M = 𝒪(D)/(t)`, construct the opens `U = {|t| ≥ 1}` and `V = {|t| ≤ |s|}`
  using stalk valuations. Prove that `t|_U` is a unit and `M̃(U) = 0`, whereas
  `M̃(V) ≅ K` as additive groups. On `V`, construct a surjective evaluation map
  `ev : 𝒪(V) → K` with kernel `(t|_V)` and the induced ring isomorphism
  `𝒪(V)/(t|_V) ≃ K`. Its value on every restricted polynomial `p(T)` is `p(0)`;
  in particular, constants are fixed and `T` maps to zero. The computation uses
  `𝒪(U) = K⟨T,S⟩/(TS − 1)` and `𝒪(V) = K⟨T,S⟩/(T − ϖS)`:
  quotienting the latter by `T` kills `S` because `ϖ` is invertible in `K`.
  Sources: Bosch, §3.3, Proposition 11 and its constructions, pp. 50–53;
  KL15, Theorem 2.5.20, pp. 51–52.
- `AdicSpace.tilde_test_zero_and_self` (degenerate) — `0̃ = 0`, and for `M = A` the presheaf `Ã`
  is isomorphic, as a presheaf of topological `𝒪_X`-modules, to `𝒪_X`.
- `AdicSpace.tilde_test_not_algebraic_localisation` (non-example) — for `A = ℚ_p⟨T⟩`, `M = A` and
  `U = {|T| ≥ 1}`, the algebraic localisation `M ⊗_A A[1/T] = ℚ_p⟨T⟩[1/T]` is not
  `M̃(U) = ℚ_p⟨T, T⁻¹⟩`, since `Σ_{n≥0} pⁿT⁻ⁿ` lies in the latter and not in the former; the
  definition must use the completed rational localisation.
- `AdicSpace.tilde_test_completed_tensor` (compatibility) — for finite `M` the canonical map
  `M ⊗_A 𝒪_X(U) → M ⊗̂_A 𝒪_X(U)` is a topological isomorphism; for the non-finite module
  `M = ⊕_{n∈ℕ} A` it is not surjective (`Σ ϖⁿ e_n ⊗ 1` is a limit not in the algebraic tensor
  product), which is why the completed-tensor comparison requires finite `M`.
  `tilde_completed_tensor_infinite` constructs the dense linear map
  `K ⊗_K (ℕ →₀ K) → c₀(ℕ,K)`, characterized by `(a ⊗ v)(n) = a·v(n)`.
  For `0 < |ϖ| < 1`, the sequence `ϖⁿ` lies outside its image. With the uniformity
  induced by this map, the canonical map from the tensor product to its separated
  completion is not surjective. This specifies the topology in the infinite-module control.

**Tate acyclicity for finite modules over a strongly noetherian Tate affinoid.**
(*tate-acyclicity-finite-modules*) Let `(A, A⁺)` be a Huber pair with `A` a complete Hausdorff
strongly noetherian Tate ring and `A⁺` a ring of integral elements, `X = Spa(A, A⁺)` and `M` a
finitely generated `A`-module. Prove that (i) for every rational subset `U ⊆ X` and every finite
covering `𝔘` of `U` by rational subsets, the augmented alternating Čech complex
`0 → M̃(U) → ∏ M̃(U_i) → ∏ M̃(U_i ∩ U_j) → ⋯` is exact and all its differentials are strict;
(ii) `M̃` is a sheaf of complete Hausdorff topological `𝒪_X`-modules; (iii) `Hⁱ(U, M̃) = 0` for
`i > 0` and `H⁰(U, M̃) = M ⊗_A 𝒪_X(U)` for every rational `U`, where `Hⁱ` is sheaf cohomology of
the underlying abelian sheaf on the topological space `U`. In particular `M̃(X) = M`, so
`M ↦ M̃` is fully faithful, `Hom(M̃, Ñ) = Hom_A(M, N)`. Degenerate instances: for `M = 0` every
term of (i)–(iii) vanishes; the empty set is the rational subset `∅ = R({1}/0)` (no point has
`v(0) ≠ 0`), with `𝒪_X(∅) = A⟨1/0⟩ = 0` and `M̃(∅) = 0`, so its empty covering has the exact
complex `0 → 0 → 0`, while a covering of a nonempty `U` is nonempty (Huber94 §2, Thm 2.5, p. 525,
Case II;
Huber94 §2, proof of Thm 2.5, Case II, (II.3), p. 531, which refines to standard rational
coverings and uses the Laurent case; Huber94 §2, proof of Thm 2.5, p. 531, where the topological
half of the sheaf statement is proved separately through the open mapping theorem, Lem. 2.4(i);
KL15 §2.5, Rem. 2.5.23, pp. 52–53, recording that Čech acyclicity of `M̃` extends beyond affinoid
algebras over a field by Huber's Theorem 2.5; Stacks Tag 01EW, Lem. 20.11.9, Cartan's criterion
passing from Čech acyclicity on a basis to sheaf-cohomology vanishing). The case `M = A` in
degree 0 is Tau Ceti's sheaf condition `isSheaf_presentationLimitPresheaf_of_isStronglyNoetherian`,
and in all degrees it is AdicSpaces layer 4.1, whose base-change step `M ⊗_A A⟨X⟩ ≅ M⟨X⟩` is
`restrictedMvPowerSeriesBaseChange`; the statement for a finite module `M` is new. *Needs:*
*associated-module-sheaf*; DerivedModuleAlgebra §S.1 `DoubleComplex.totalCohomology_of_exact_rows` and its transpose, applied to a sheaf resolution on the rational basis; Tau Ceti
`isSheaf_presentationLimitPresheaf_of_isStronglyNoetherian`, `restrictedMvPowerSeriesBaseChange`,
`Huber.PairOfDefinition.flat_toCompletionLoc`, `TauCeti.Huber.isNoetherianRing_of_isStronglyNoetherian`,
`Huber.PairOfDefinition.isStronglyNoetherian_completion`, `Huber.IsTateRing.isModuleTopology`,
`Huber.IsTateRing.isStrictMap_of_isClosed_range`,
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.isSheaf_iff_isSheafFor_rationalCover`,
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.exists_span_eq_top_forall_rationalSubset_subset_of_isTateRing`; Mathlib
`Module.Flat.lTensor_exact`, `CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.ShortExact.homology_exact₂`. Lean: the
simple Laurent case of (i) for finite modules, `Huber.laurent_exact_of_finite` (stated for complete
rings of noetherian type, which include the strongly noetherian Tate rings, with the rational
completions given by `Huber.IsRationalCompletion`); the sheaf and cohomology statements are
specified in this README only.

**Acyclicity of `M̃` when `A` has a noetherian ring of definition (Huber's Theorem 2.5, Case I).**
(*noetherian-rod-acyclicity-finite-modules*) Let `(A, A⁺)` be a complete affinoid ring such that
`A` has a noetherian ring of definition, `X = Spa(A, A⁺)` and `M` a finitely generated
`A`-module. Prove that `M̃` is a sheaf of complete topological groups on `X`, and that
`Hⁱ(U, M̃) = 0` for every `i > 0` and every rational subset `U ⊆ X`. The Čech input — exact strict
Čech complexes of `M ⊗ 𝒪` on standard rational coverings of rational subsets, which refine every
open covering, and the case `M = A` (sheafiness of `𝒪_X`) — is *noetherian-rod-sheafy* (Huber94
(1.5)); this theorem adds the sheaf `M̃` and sheaf-cohomology vanishing. The statement includes
non-analytic points: for `A = ℤ_p` with its `p`-adic ring of definition `ℤ_p`, `X = Spa(ℤ_p, ℤ_p)`
has a closed non-analytic point and the theorem still applies (Huber94 §2, proof of Thm 2.5,
Case I, pp. 525–529, by Raynaud-type blow-up arguments; Huber94 §2, (1.5), p. 529, the existence
of a refinement with exact strict Čech complex; Huber94 §2, Lem. 2.6, p. 531, the refinement lemma
by standard rational coverings). *Needs:* *associated-module-sheaf*; *noetherian-rod-sheafy*,
*noetherian-rod-module-complete* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R0); DerivedModuleAlgebra §S.1 `DoubleComplex.totalCohomology_of_exact_rows` and its transpose, applied to a sheaf resolution on the rational basis; Tau Ceti
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.isSheaf_iff_isSheafFor_rationalCover`. Lean: the exactness of
`0 → M → B₁ ⊗ M × B₂ ⊗ M → B₁₂ ⊗ M → 0` on a simple Laurent cover, `Huber.laurent_exact_of_finite`,
whose hypothesis `Huber.IsNoetherianType` (AdicSpacesPartII) covers this case; the sheaf and
cohomology statements are specified in this README only.

The passage from simple Laurent coverings to all rational coverings, in every degree and for an
arbitrary presheaf, is proved in five steps. Prove the reduction of local transitive properties of
rational coverings to simple Laurent coverings (*rational-covering-reduction*): let `(A, A⁺)` be a
Tate Huber pair (`A` contains a topologically nilpotent unit, used to rescale in KL15
Lem. 2.4.19(b); completeness is not needed, since the statement concerns only subsets of
`Spa(A, A⁺) = Spa(Â, Â⁺)`, and the binary-cover variant
`AdicSpace.rationalCovering_induction_of_binary` assumes `IsTateRing A` without completeness)
and let `P` be a property of finite rational coverings of rational subsets of
`Spa(A, A⁺)` such that (a) `P` is local — if `P` holds for a refinement of a covering then it holds
for the covering; (b) `P` is transitive — if `P` holds for `{U → V_i}` and for coverings
`{V_i → W_ij}` of each `V_i` then it holds for the composite covering `{U → W_ij}`; (c) `P` holds
for every simple Laurent covering `{v(f) ≤ 1}`, `{v(f) ≥ 1}` of every rational subset; then `P`
holds for every finite nonempty rational covering of every rational subset. The empty covering of
the empty rational subset `∅ = R({1}/0)` must be excluded (a covering of a nonempty `U` is
nonempty, so this is the only case): (a)–(c) never reach `P(∅, ∅)`, since the property
`P(U, 𝔘) := "𝔘 ≠ ∅"` satisfies (a) (a refinement of `𝔘` is nonempty only if `𝔘` is), (b) and (c)
(the Laurent covering has two members) and fails for `(∅, ∅)`; the statement
`AdicSpace.rationalCovering_induction_of_simpleLaurent` carries the hypothesis `𝔘.Nonempty` (KL15 §2.4, Prop. 2.4.20,
pp. 44–45; KL15 §2.4, Lem. 2.4.19, p. 44, the refinement step; Kiehl-AB §1, after Hilfssatz 1.3,
p. 260, where Kiehl uses Tate's refinement lemma to reduce his glueing theorem to Laurent and
formal coverings, whereas the Kedlaya–Liu version reduces to simple Laurent coverings only). For
`P(U, (V_i))` = "for every rational `U' ⊆ U`, the augmented Čech complex of
`F` for the given covering `(V_i ∩ U')` of `U'` is exact", this gives the
positive-degree step of KL15 Prop. 2.4.21 after establishing separatedness and the
sheaf condition as below. The quantifier ranges over rational pullbacks of the
specified covering. For `P` = "every finite
glueing datum of finite modules on the covering is effective" it reduces Kiehl's theorem to simple
Laurent coverings (used by *tate-kiehl-affinoid*). Tau Ceti runs this reduction for one property
only, the sheaf condition (degree 0) of the structure presheaf of a strongly noetherian Tate pair:
`isSheafFor_ofArrows_spaRationalOpens_of_iSup_eq`,
`isSheafFor_ofArrows_inf_spaBasicOpen_of_span_eq_top`, `isSheafFor_laurentSieve`,
`isSheafFor_ofArrows_iff_locOpensComap` and `Opens.isSheafFor_trans`; the statement here is for an
arbitrary local transitive property, hence for an arbitrary presheaf in every degree. *Needs:* Tau
Ceti `TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.exists_span_eq_top_forall_rationalSubset_subset_of_isTateRing`,
`isSheafFor_ofArrows_spaRationalOpens_of_iSup_eq`, `isSheafFor_laurentSieve`,
`Opens.isSheafFor_trans`, `Huber.IsTateRing`.

The binary-cover variant (stronger hypothesis) `AdicSpace.rationalCovering_induction_of_binary` assumes
`P U {V,W}` for every pair of rational subdomains with `V ∪ W = U`, together with the same
locality and transitivity hypotheses, and concludes `P` for every finite nonempty rational
cover. Its base case includes all simple Laurent coverings. The simple-Laurent criterion
`AdicSpace.rationalCovering_induction_of_simpleLaurent` is stated over a complete Hausdorff Tate ring
and uses functions in each rational localisation `O(U)`;
functions in the original ring `A` alone are not its hypothesis.

`AdicSpace.RationalChart S U B Q` records a rational presentation of `U`, the
completion algebra `B`, and a morphism `S → Q` whose ring map is `A → B` and whose
map on spectra embeds `Spa(Q)` with image exactly `U`. Its algebra identification is
`Huber.IsRationalCompletion` (Lean): a ring equivalence from Tau Ceti's completion for
`locUniformSpace`, continuous in both directions, intertwining `toCompletionLoc`
with `algebraMap A B`. Thus the function in the Laurent hypothesis has type `B`.
The spectral identification is supplied by `spaCompletedLocalizationHomeomorph`
(Wedhorn, Proposition 8.2(2)); its construction is already in Tau Ceti.

**Checks for rational completion models.**

- (zero denominator) — `A⟨1/0⟩` is the zero ring.
- (identity) — `A⟨1/1⟩` is the original complete
  Hausdorff ring as a topological `A`-algebra.
- (diagonal) — for nonzero complete Hausdorff `A`,
  the diagonal algebra `A × A` cannot be a model of `A⟨1/1⟩`, even when abstract
  ring isomorphisms fail to distinguish the two rings.

**Checks for rational charts.**

- `AdicSpace.RationalChart.test_whole`: the whole spectrum has an identity chart,
  with the identity morphism of Huber pairs.
- `AdicSpace.RationalChart.test_empty`: a chart over the empty rational domain has
  no points in its source spectrum.
- `AdicSpace.RationalChart.test_zero_function`: in every rational chart the Laurent
  cover for the localized function `0` pulls back to `(U, ∅)`.

Prove that Čech acyclicity is inherited from a refinement whose restrictions are acyclic
(*cech-acyclicity-refinement*): let `X` be a topological space, `ℬ` a family of open subsets of `X`
closed under finite intersections, and `F` a presheaf of abelian groups on `ℬ` (restriction maps
along inclusions in `ℬ`, functorial). For `U ∈ ℬ` and a finite covering `𝔘 = (U_i)_{i∈I}` of `U` by
members of `ℬ`, call `𝔘` `F`-acyclic if the augmented alternating Čech complex
`0 → F(U) → ∏_{i₀} F(U_{i₀}) → ∏_{i₀<i₁} F(U_{i₀i₁}) → ⋯` (for a chosen total order of `I`) is
exact. Let `𝔙 = (V_i)_{i∈I}` and `𝔚 = (W_j)_{j∈J}` be finite coverings of `U ∈ ℬ` by members of
`ℬ` such that `𝔚` refines `𝔙` (every `W_j` is contained in some `V_i`), and suppose that for every
`p ≥ 0` and every `i₀ < ⋯ < i_p` in `I` the covering `𝔚 ∩ V_{i₀…i_p} = (W_j ∩ V_{i₀…i_p})_{j∈J}`
of `V_{i₀…i_p}` is `F`-acyclic. Then `Ȟⁿ(U, F; 𝔙) ≅ Ȟⁿ(U, F; 𝔚)` for every `n ≥ 0`, compatibly
with the maps from `F(U)` in degree 0; in particular `𝔙` is `F`-acyclic if and only if `𝔚` is.
Consequently (the locality used by Kedlaya–Liu) if `𝔚` refines `𝔙` and the restriction of `𝔚` to
every member of `ℬ` contained in `U` is `F`-acyclic (`𝔚` is universally `F`-acyclic), then so is
every restriction of `𝔙` (KL15 §2.4, proof of Prop. 2.4.21, p. 46, where the locality is referred
to BGR 8.1.4/3 and is supplied here through the Čech double complex; Stacks Tag 0G6S,
Lem. 20.9.3, a covering having the whole set as a member has contractible augmented Čech
complex, which gives exactness of the rows; Stacks Tag 01FM, Lem. 20.23.6, alternating and full
Čech complexes have the same cohomology). If `𝔙 = (U)` is the trivial covering the lemma is a
tautology, and if `𝔚 = 𝔙` the hypothesis is that `𝔙` is universally acyclic on its own
intersections. Use the double complex whose `(p,q)` term is the product of
`F(V_{i₀…i_p} ∩ W_{j₀…j_q})` over increasing tuples. Its column augmentations
are exact by the hypothesis. For each W-intersection, refinement makes the restricted
V-cover contain that whole intersection as a member, giving exact row augmentations.
Identify both augmented edges with the supplier's kernel complexes and use its canonical
comparisons; naturality gives the refinement map and compatibility with `F(U)`.
*Needs:* DerivedModuleAlgebra §S.1 `DoubleComplex.totalCohomology_of_exact_rows`
and `DoubleComplex.spectralSequence_map`, with transposition and the sign transport
specified in the supplier contract.

Prove Kedlaya–Liu's Proposition 2.4.21 (*cech-acyclicity-simple-laurent-reduction*): for a complete Hausdorff Tate Huber
pair `(A, A⁺)`, `X = Spa(A, A⁺)`, and a presheaf `F` of abelian groups on the rational subsets of
`X`, with `F(∅) = 0`, such that for every rational `U ⊆ X` and every `f ∈ 𝒪_X(U)`, with `V₁ = {|f| ≤ 1}` and
`V₂ = {|f| ≥ 1}` in `U`, the sequence `0 → F(U) → F(V₁) ⊕ F(V₂) → F(V₁ ∩ V₂) → 0` is exact, the
augmented alternating Čech complex of `F` is exact on every finite rational covering of every
rational subset, including its empty cover. The assumption `F(∅) = 0` is necessary for
that last case: the constant presheaf `ℤ` has exact two-member Laurent complexes but its
empty-cover augmentation is `ℤ → 0` (KL15 §2.4, Prop. 2.4.21 and its proof, pp. 45–46). For `F = 𝒪_X` of a complete
strongly noetherian Tate pair the hypothesis is AdicSpaces layer 4.1's two-piece Laurent exactness
(Wedhorn Lem. 8.33) and the conclusion is its all-degree Čech exactness; for `F = M ⊗_A 𝒪_X` with
`M` finite projective over a sheafy Tate `A` the hypothesis follows from the case `F = 𝒪_X` by
taking direct summands (stated as *finite-projective-module-acyclicity* below). *Needs:*
*rational-covering-reduction*; *cech-acyclicity-refinement*;
DerivedModuleAlgebra §S.1 `DoubleComplex.totalCohomology_of_exact_rows` and
`DoubleComplex.spectralSequence_map`; Tau Ceti `Huber.IsTateRing`.

`AdicSpace.isCechAcyclic_of_simpleLaurent` takes precisely the injectivity, middle
exactness and surjectivity of this three-term sequence in each `RationalChart`,
plus `Subsingleton (F.obj (op ⊥))`. It concludes `IsCechAcyclic` for every finite
rational cover, with no nonemptiness restriction on the indexing type. A presheaf
on the rational basis is used through its right Kan extension to all opens.

Apply *rational-covering-reduction* first to injectivity of
`F(U) → Ȟ⁰(U, F; (V_i))`. Locality and transitivity follow from restriction maps;
the Laurent hypothesis supplies the base case. Next apply it to bijectivity of
this map. For locality, a matching family descends along the refinement by its
sheaf condition, and separatedness on the original members identifies its
restrictions with the original family. Transitivity is gluing in two stages.
Together with `F(∅) = 0`, these steps give the sheaf condition on the rational basis.
For positive degrees use exactly
`P(U, (V_i)) := ∀ rational U' ⊆ U, the augmented Čech complex for (V_i ∩ U') is exact`.
Locality follows from *cech-acyclicity-refinement* on each `U'`, and transitivity
from the Čech double-complex comparison for composite coverings, using the
universal acyclicity hypotheses on rational intersections. These comparisons use
DerivedModuleAlgebra §S.1 with the same total differential and natural edge maps.
A rational pullback of a simple Laurent covering is the simple Laurent covering
for the restricted function, so the localized three-term hypothesis supplies this
base case. The empty cover is handled separately by `F(∅) = 0`.

**Checks for `IsCechAcyclic`.**

- `IsCechAcyclic.test_singleton`: the one-member cover `V₀ = U` is acyclic for every
  presheaf; its augmentation is the identity and its higher cohomology is zero.
- `IsCechAcyclic.test_empty`: the empty family is acyclic exactly when `F(U) = 0`.
  In particular, the constant presheaf `ℤ` fails this test, even at `U = ∅`.
- `IsCechAcyclic.test_empty_cover_obstruction`: the constant presheaf `ℤ` on a point
  has an exact two-member Čech complex over the empty open, but its empty-cover
  augmentation is not injective. Binary-cover exactness alone cannot force `F(∅) = 0`.
- `IsCechAcyclic.test_zero`: the zero presheaf is acyclic for every family and every `U`.
- For `f = 1`, the Laurent covering is `(U, U)` and every rational pullback is
  `(U', U')`. Its augmented complex is the split exact sequence
  `0 → F(U') → F(U') ⊕ F(U') → F(U') → 0`, with diagonal and difference maps.
  Every finite rational cover refines `(U, U)`; exactness for those other covers
  is a conclusion of the reduction, while this base case only concerns the
  duplicated cover; the diagonal–difference sequence is split exact for any abelian group.
- For `f = 0`, the covering and its pullbacks are `(U, ∅)` and `(U', ∅)`.
  With `F(∅) = 0` the augmentation is the identity of `F(U')`.
- For a localized function `f ∈ 𝒪_X(U)` and rational `U' ⊆ U`, the pullback
  pieces are `{|f|_{U'} ≤ 1}` and `{|f|_{U'} ≥ 1}`; the base case uses the
  Laurent sequence on `U'` itself, including when `U'` is empty.

Prove that for a simple Laurent covering the difference map `B₁ ⊕ B₂ → B₁₂` is surjective,
Kedlaya–Liu's Lemma 2.4.22 (*simple-laurent-difference-surjective*): let `(A, A⁺)` be a complete
Hausdorff Huber pair and `f ∈ A` arbitrary; let `A → B₁`, `A → B₂`, `A → B₁₂` be the rational
localisations (AdicSpaces layer 3.1, Tau Ceti `Huber.PairOfDefinition.completionLocObj`) of the
rational subsets `S₋ = R({f, 1}/1) = {v(f) ≤ 1}`, `S₊ = R({1, f}/f) = {v(f) ≥ 1}` and
`S₋ ∩ S₊ = R({1, f, f²}/f) = {v(f) = 1}` of `Spa(A, A⁺)`, and `ρ₁ : B₁ → B₁₂`, `ρ₂ : B₂ → B₁₂` the
restriction maps. Then the map `B₁ ⊕ B₂ → B₁₂`, `(b₁, b₂) ↦ ρ₁(b₁) − ρ₂(b₂)`, is surjective. No
sheafiness, noetherian or Tate hypothesis is made (KL15 §2.4, Lem. 2.4.22, p. 46; KL15 §2.4, proof
of Lem. 2.4.22, p. 46, the presentations `A⟨T⟩ → B₁`, `A⟨U⟩ → B₂`, `A⟨T, U⟩ → B₁₂` and the
splitting of a lift by the sign of `i − j`; KL15 §2.4, before Lem. 2.4.22, p. 46, for the absence
of a sheafiness hypothesis). For `A = ℚ_p⟨X⟩` and `f = X` one has `B₁ = ℚ_p⟨X⟩`,
`B₂ = ℚ_p⟨X, X⁻¹⟩ = B₁₂` and `ρ₂` the identity, so the map is onto for trivial reasons; for
`f = X/p` the lemma is the splitting of a Laurent series on the annulus `|X| = |p|` into its parts
of nonnegative and negative degree; for a non-sheafy pair (KL15 Ex. 2.8.7) the two-term Čech
sequence can fail to be exact only at `A` or at `B₁ ⊕ B₂`. Tau Ceti has the surjectivity on
presentations, for every complete nonarchimedean ring, as `TauCeti.Huber.laurentCoverDiff_surjective`, and
on the rational localisations `completionLocObj` of a strongly noetherian Tate ring as
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.laurentCover_surjective`; the statement here is on `completionLocObj` for an
arbitrary complete Huber pair, where the passage from presentations needs
`rationalQuotientRingEquiv`, whose closed-ideal hypothesis is known only in the strongly
noetherian Tate case. *Needs:* Tau Ceti `TauCeti.Huber.laurentCoverDiff_surjective`,
`TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.laurentCover_surjective`, `Huber.PairOfDefinition.rationalQuotientRingEquiv`,
