`A' = A⟨T'/s'⟩`, does not change `Ωᶜ_{B/A} = Ωᶜ_{B/A'}`. Prove the following properties:
(a) universal property: for every coherent `O_X`-module `F`, `Hom_{O_X}(Ω¹_{X/Y}, F)` is the set of
`f⁻¹O_Y`-linear derivations `D : O_X → F` that are continuous on sections over affinoid opens, via
`u ↦ u ∘ d`; (b) exact sequences: for `X → Y → Z` (both locally of finite type) the sequence
`f*Ω¹_{Y/Z} → Ω¹_{X/Z} → Ω¹_{X/Y} → 0` is exact, and for a closed embedding `i : X → P` over `Y`
with coherent ideal `𝓘` (by *coherent-ideal-closed-subspace*),
`𝓘/𝓘² → i*Ω¹_{P/Y} → Ω¹_{X/Y} → 0` is exact; (c) `f` is unramified iff `Ω¹_{X/Y} = 0`; if `f` is
smooth of relative dimension `n` at `x`, `Ω¹_{X/Y}` is a vector bundle of rank `n` near `x`
(*locally-free-sheaf*), and for `X → Y → Z` with `f` smooth the sequence of (b) is left exact and
locally split; if `f` is étale, `f*Ω¹_{Y/Z} ≅ Ω¹_{X/Z}`, in particular `u*Ω¹_{X/Y} ≅ Ω¹_{U/Y}` for
every étale `u : U → X`, which makes `U ↦ Ω¹_{U/Y}(U)` a sheaf on the small étale site of `X`;
(d) base change: for a cartesian square `X' = X ×_Y Y'` (*fibre-products-existence*, AdicSpacesPartII layer R0,
case (a)) with projection `p : X' → X`, `p*Ω¹_{X/Y} ≅ Ω¹_{X'/Y'}` compatibly with `d`;
(e) analytification: for a morphism `h` of schemes locally of finite type over a complete
nonarchimedean field `K`, `Ω¹_{X^ad/Y^ad} ≅ (Ω¹_{X/Y})^ad` compatibly with `d`
(*analytic-kahler-differentials*, AdicSpacesPartII layer R1); (f) exterior powers: `Ωⁱ_{X/Y} := ⋀ⁱ_{O_X} Ω¹_{X/Y}`,
the sheaf associated with `U ↦ ⋀ⁱ_{O(U)} Ω¹_{X/Y}(U)`, is coherent, with sections
`(⋀ⁱ_B Ωᶜ_{B/A})~` over `U` as above; for `f` smooth of relative dimension `n` it is a vector
bundle of rank `C(n, i)`; `d` extends uniquely to `f⁻¹O_Y`-linear maps `d : Ωⁱ_{X/Y} → Ωⁱ⁺¹_{X/Y}`
with `d ∘ d = 0` and `d(ω ∧ η) = dω ∧ η + (−1)ⁱ ω ∧ dη`, the relative de Rham complex `Ω•_{X/Y}`.
For (b) the second morphism is locally of finite type; for (c) `f` is unramified, smooth or étale
in the sense of AdicSpacesPartII layer R0 (R0.16–R0.17; the spaces, analytic and locally
noetherian, are locally Huber-standard, which is where Part II states these classes). This is the coherent sheaf of the continuous differentials of AdicSpacesPartII layer R0
(Huber96 (1.6.2)); Mathlib's algebraic `KaehlerDifferential` of the rings `O_X(U)` does not impose
continuity and need not be finite; the continuous quotient is the object used here.
Huber96 §1.6, Proposition 1.6.3(i)–(iv), p. 77, supplies the two exact sequences,
base change and rational localization. The paragraph preceding Lemma 1.6.4, p. 78,
defines the sheaf via the diagonal ideal and identifies its affinoid restrictions. The Kähler differentials of rigid and dagger spaces
(Grosse-Klönne) and the log differentials of Diao–Lan–Liu–Zhu with trivial log structures are the
same sheaf. The sheaf on the étale site in (c) and the pro-étale sheaves built from it belong to
AdicEtaleGeometry layer A2 and to the `p`-adic Hodge theory roadmaps. In `AdicSpace`, define
`relativeDifferentials`
as `Ω¹_{X/Y}`, a sheaf of `O_X`-modules (Mathlib `SheafOfModules`) for `f` locally of finite type
between locally noetherian analytic adic spaces, `relativeDifferentials.d` as the
`f⁻¹O_Y`-linear derivation `d : O_X → Ω¹_{X/Y}`, `relativeDifferentials.exteriorPower` as
`Ωⁱ_{X/Y} = ⋀ⁱ Ω¹_{X/Y}` (coherent; a vector bundle of rank `C(n, i)` for `f` smooth of relative
dimension `n`). The definition is exactly
`(SheafOfModules.exteriorPower (commRingSheaf X) i).obj (relativeDifferentials f hf hX hY)`.
For every such `f`, with the strongly noetherian Tate charts on `X` and `Y` specified
by `hX` and `hY`, `relativeDifferentials.exteriorPower_zero` and
`relativeDifferentials.exteriorPower_one` give isomorphisms with `O_X` and `Ω¹_{X/Y}`,
respectively. They are the components of Tau Ceti's `SheafOfModules.exteriorPowerZeroIso`
and `SheafOfModules.exteriorPowerOneIso` in the supplier file above; no smoothness
assumption is needed. The differential sheaf is the one of Huber96 §1.6, p. 78.
Define `relativeDifferentials.deRhamComplex` as the relative de Rham complex
`(Ω•_{X/Y}, d)` with `f⁻¹O_Y`-linear `d : Ωⁱ → Ωⁱ⁺¹`, `d ∘ d = 0` and the graded Leibniz rule;
prove the instance `relativeDifferentials.isCoherent` (`Ω¹_{X/Y}` is coherent),
`relativeDifferentials.affinoidIso` (for affinoid `U = Spa B`, `V = Spa A` with `f(U) ⊆ V` and
`A → B` topologically of finite type, `Ω¹_{X/Y}|_U ≅ (Ωᶜ[B⁄A])~` compatibly with `d`),
`relativeDifferentials.homEquiv` (for coherent `F`,
`Hom_{O_X}(Ω¹_{X/Y}, F) ≃` continuous `f⁻¹O_Y`-linear derivations `O_X → F`, `u ↦ u ∘ d`),
`relativeDifferentials.map` (a commutative square `g : X' → X` over `h : Y' → Y` induces
`g*Ω¹_{X/Y} → Ω¹_{X'/Y'}`, with `map_id` and `map_comp`),
`relativeDifferentials.exact_firstFundamental` (for `X → Y → Z`,
`f*Ω¹_{Y/Z} → Ω¹_{X/Z} → Ω¹_{X/Y} → 0` is exact; *first-fundamental-sequence*, AdicSpacesPartII layer R0),
`relativeDifferentials.exact_conormal` (for a closed embedding `i : X → P` over `Y` with ideal
`𝓘`, `𝓘/𝓘² → i*Ω¹_{P/Y} → Ω¹_{X/Y} → 0` is exact; *conormal-sequence*, AdicSpacesPartII layer R0),
`relativeDifferentials.eq_zero_iff_unramified` (`Ω¹_{X/Y} = 0 ↔ f` is unramified;
*infinitesimal-criteria*, AdicSpacesPartII layer R0), `relativeDifferentials.isVectorBundle_of_smooth` (if `f` is
smooth of relative dimension `n`, `Ω¹_{X/Y}` is a vector bundle of rank `n` and the first
fundamental sequence is left exact and locally split), `relativeDifferentials.pullbackEtaleIso`
(for `u : U → X` étale, `u*Ω¹_{X/Y} ≅ Ω¹_{U/Y}`, compatibly with composition of étale maps),
`relativeDifferentials.baseChangeIso` (for `X' = X ×_Y Y'` with projection `p`,
with all four spaces locally noetherian analytic and both vertical maps locally of finite type,
there is a unique isomorphism `e : p*Ω¹_{X/Y} ≅ Ω¹_{X'/Y'}` such that, for every open
`U ⊆ X` and section `r ∈ O_X(U)`, `e(p*(d r)) = d(p# r)` on `p⁻¹U`.
Here `p*(d r)` is given by `moduleUnit`, and `p# r` by the imported
`ringCatSheafMap`; Huber96 Proposition 1.6.3(iii), p. 77, and the sheaf construction,
p. 78) and `relativeDifferentials.analytificationIso`
(`(Ω¹_{X/Y})^ad ≅ Ω¹_{X^ad/Y^ad}` for schemes locally of finite type over `K`;
*analytic-kahler-differentials*, AdicSpacesPartII layer R1) (DLLZ-A §3.3, Construction 3.3.2, p. 34, the affinoid module of log differentials,
whose trivial-log case is Huber's `Ω_{B/A}`; Construction 3.3.4, p. 35, the associated
sheaf on affinoid charts;
DLLZ-A §3.3, Lem. 3.3.5, p. 35, the universal property (a) and independence of the charts for all

base change (d); DLLZ-A §3.3, Thm 3.3.17(2), p. 39, the smooth case of (c), left exactness of the
first fundamental sequence and local freeness; Scholze13 §6, Def. 6.8(i), p. 37, the sheaf of
differentials of a smooth adic space and its exterior powers pulled back to the pro-étale site,
as the `p`-adic Hodge theory roadmaps consume it; GK02 §1, 1.1, p. 4, the relative sheaf
`Ω¹_{X/Y} = J/J²` with
`d(a) = 1 ⊗ a − a ⊗ 1` for rigid and dagger spaces, the local form used here; GK00 §4, 4.1, p. 19,
the de Rham complex of coherent locally free `Ωⁱ` and its comparison with the rigid space `X'`;

sheaf is coherent). *Needs:* *coherent-sheaf*; *associated-module-sheaf*;

AdicSpacesPartII layer R0); *analytic-kahler-differentials*, *analytification-of-modules* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R1);
R3.1a `analytification.modules_chartSections` for the associated-sheaf comparison; Mathlib
`SheafOfModules`, `SheafOfModules.pullback`, `Derivation`, `ExteriorAlgebra.exteriorPower`.

**Checks.**

- `relativeDifferentials_disc` (computation) — with `K` a complete nonarchimedean
  field with nontrivial rank-one valuation, `K°` its valuation ring and
  `D = Spa(K⟨T⟩, K°⟨T⟩)`: `Ω¹_{D/Spa K} ≅ O_D`, generated by `dT`, with
  `d(Σ aₙTⁿ) = (Σ n aₙTⁿ⁻¹) dT`, and `Ω²_{D/Spa K} = 0`.
- `relativeDifferentials_openImmersion` (degenerate) — for an open embedding
  `j : U → X`, `Ω¹_{U/X} = 0` and `j*Ω¹_{X/Y} ≅ Ω¹_{U/Y}`; `Ω¹_{Y/Y} = 0` for every `Y`.
- `relativeDifferentials_notAlgebraic` (non-example) — the presheaf
  `U ↦ Ω[O_D(U)⁄K]` of Mathlib's algebraic Kähler differentials on the disc `D`,
  for `K = ℚ_p`, is not a coherent
  `O_D`-module (its value on `D` is not a finitely generated `K⟨T⟩`-module), whereas
  `Ω¹_{D/K}(D) = K⟨T⟩ dT`: algebraic differentials do not give the required construction
  in this case. The characteristic-zero restriction matters: for perfect `K` of
  characteristic `p`, decomposition of a series by exponents modulo `p` gives
  `Ω[K⟨T⟩⁄K] = K⟨T⟩ dT`.
- `relativeDifferentials_analytification` (compatibility) — for `X = A¹_K`,
  `(Ω¹_{A¹/K})^ad ≅ Ω¹_{A^{1,ad}/K} = O dT`; for `P¹_K`, `Ω¹_{P^{1,ad}/K} ≅ O(−2)^ad`
  (*analytic-kahler-differentials*, AdicSpacesPartII layer R1).
- `relativeDifferentials_derivations` (characterisation) — on `D`,
  `Hom_{O_D}(Ω¹_{D/K}, O_D)` is the `O_D(D)`-module of continuous `K`-derivations of `K⟨T⟩`, free
  on `d/dT`; `relativeDifferentials_node` uses the node `T₁T₂ = 0` has a nonzero torsion section `T₁ dT₂` of `Ω¹` whose support is
  the origin (Huber96, (1.6.2)(i), p. 76: the presentation by the relation
  `T₂ dT₁ + T₁ dT₂ = 0`).

- `AdicSpace.relativeDifferentials.test_perfect_characteristic`: for perfect `K`
  of characteristic `p > 0`, the algebraic differentials of the one-variable Tate
  algebra are free of rank one. Each series is a sum of `Tⁱ gᵢ(T)^p`, `0 ≤ i < p`,
  so every algebraic derivation is determined by its value on `T`.

**Checks for `relativeDifferentials.d`, exterior powers and the de Rham complex.**

The exterior powers and de Rham complex also have the following direct Checks.
`relativeDifferentials.polydiscBasis` fixes the coordinates on actual rigid
polydiscs carried to adic spaces, and `relativeDifferentials.deRhamComplex_degreeZero`
identifies the degree-zero differential with the universal derivation.

- `relativeDifferentials_disc`, `relativeDifferentials.exteriorPower_disc`: the closed disc has a free rank-one differential sheaf, a nonzero derivative, and zero second exterior power.
- `relativeDifferentials.exteriorPower_zero`: degree zero is the structure sheaf.
- `relativeDifferentials.exteriorPower_one`: degree one is the differential sheaf.
- `relativeDifferentials.exteriorPower_supplier`: in every degree, the object is definitionally the supplied sheaf exterior power applied to `Ω¹_{X/Y}`.
- `relativeDifferentials.exteriorPower_etale`, `relativeDifferentials.deRhamComplex_etale`: positive degrees vanish for an étale morphism.
- `relativeDifferentials.exteriorPower_bidisc`: degree two on the bidisc is a line bundle and degree three vanishes.
- `relativeDifferentials_notAlgebraic`: algebraic differentials of the Tate disc over `ℚ_p` are not finite, whereas continuous differentials are free of rank one.
- `relativeDifferentials.deRhamComplex_point`: over the identity, degree zero is the structure sheaf and every positive degree vanishes.
- `relativeDifferentials.deRhamComplex_disc`: under the degree-zero and degree-one identifications, `d(Tⁿ) = nTⁿ⁻¹ dT`.
- `relativeDifferentials.deRhamComplex_sign`: `d(a db) = da ∧ db` and `d(b da) = −da ∧ db` on an affinoid chart.
- `relativeDifferentials.deRhamComplex_empty`: all degrees vanish on the empty space.
- `relativeDifferentials.deRhamComplex_twoTerm`: consecutive differentials compose to zero on sections.

- `relativeDifferentials.d_coordinate`: on the disc, `d(T²) = 2T dT`;
  in characteristic two this is zero while `dT` is nonzero.
- `relativeDifferentials.d_identity`: on `Spa(K,K°)` over itself,
  every differential vanishes.
- `relativeDifferentials.d_product`: on the bidisc,
  `d(T₁T₂) = T₁ dT₂ + T₂ dT₁`.
- `relativeDifferentials.exteriorPower_zero`: degree zero is `𝒪`
  even on a point, where `Ω¹ = 0`.
- `relativeDifferentials.exteriorPower_disc`: on the disc, degrees
  one and two are `𝒪 dT` and zero.
- `relativeDifferentials.exteriorPower_bidisc`: on the bidisc,
  `Ω² = 𝒪(dT₁ ∧ dT₂)` and `dT₂ ∧ dT₁ = −dT₁ ∧ dT₂`.
- `relativeDifferentials.deRhamComplex_point`: a point over itself
  has complex `K → 0 → 0`.
- `relativeDifferentials.deRhamComplex_disc`: the disc has two
  terms `𝒪 → 𝒪 dT`, with `Tⁿ ↦ nTⁿ⁻¹ dT`.
- `relativeDifferentials.deRhamComplex_sign`: on the bidisc,
  `d(T₁ dT₂) = dT₁ ∧ dT₂` and `d(T₂ dT₁) = −dT₁ ∧ dT₂`, fixing the
  degree-one sign in the Leibniz rule.

**Kiehl's proper mapping theorem.** (*kiehl-proper-mapping-theorem*)
Let `K` be complete with nontrivial nonarchimedean valuation. For a proper morphism
`f : X → Y` locally of finitetype over `Spa(K,K°)`, Kiehl-proper over every affinoid open
of `Y`, and `F` coherent, prove `kiehlProperMapping`: `Rⁱf_*F` is coherent for all `i ≥ 0`.
On an affinoid `V ⊆ Y` it is the sheaf of the finite module `Hⁱ(f⁻¹(V),F)`
(Kiehl-E §2, Satz 2.6, pp. 204–205; Bosch 2014 §6.3, Theorem 1, pp. 129–130).
*Needs:* *proper-affinoid-cohomology-finite*; *proper-cohomology-affinoid-subdomain*;
module-sheaf derived direct image; Part II *rigid-adic-quasi-separated-equivalence*.

Checks:

- For the identity, degree zero is `F` and higher direct images vanish.
- For zero coefficients all direct images vanish.
- For `P¹_K → Spa K`, `R¹f_*O(−2)` is the rank-one module `K`.

Throughout the rest of this subsection `K` is a complete nonarchimedean field with nontrivial
absolute value, adic spaces are locally of finite type over `Spa(K, K°)`, and `A` denotes an
affinoid `K`-algebra (a quotient of some `K⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩`, strongly noetherian Tate) with `A⁺ = A°`.
In the cohomology and base-change statements below, proper morphisms are also assumed
Kiehl-proper over each affinoid in the base. This is the hypothesis of Kiehl's theorems
and Conrad-RA Appendix A.1, pp. 38–39. Removing this additional assumption over a general
nondiscretely valued field requires the comparison in *proper-relatively-compact-covers*;
that comparison remains a separate target.
A proper morphism `f : X → Spa(A, A°)` is *Kiehl-proper* if there are finite affinoid open
coverings `{U_i}`, `{V_i}` of `X` with `V_i ⋐_A U_i` (*proper-relatively-compact-covers*); every
proper `f` is Kiehl-proper when `K` is discretely valued. Each target below that assumes `f`
proper assumes in addition that `f` is Kiehl-proper, a hypothesis that is empty for discretely
valued `K`.

**Completely continuous maps of Banach modules over an affinoid algebra.**
(*completely-continuous-map*) For the nonzero affinoid `K`-algebra `A` above,
`Huber.IsCompletelyContinuous` is the affinoid specialization of CompactOperators §0.1's
`IsCompletelyContinuous` on compatible complete ultrametric Banach models. Since `A` is
noetherian, a map whose range is contained in a finite `A`-submodule has finitely generated
range. Use that supplier's `isFiniteRank_iff_range_fg` to identify the approximation
conditions, and transport its finite-rank, sum, composition-ideal and operator-norm
closedness laws.
For an open bounded `A₀`-lattice `M₀`, with `A₀` an open bounded `K°`-subalgebra of `A`,
use CompactOperators §0.1's scalar lattice norm
`α_M(m) = inf{|c| : c ∈ K×, m ∈ cM₀}`. For a scalar `π ∈ K×` with `q = |π| < 1`,
use parameter `a = q⁻¹` in PadicFunctionalAnalysis §0.4's ring gauge and the
module gauge `g_M(m) = inf{q^n : n ∈ ℤ, π^(−n)m ∈ M₀}` of CompactOperators §0.1.
The supplied bounds are `α_M ≤ g_M ≤ q⁻¹ α_M`, and likewise for `A₀`.
This identifies the chosen lattice model with Part II's Banach-module carrier and
transports the supplied complete-continuity predicate. Arbitrary gauge parameters give
power comparisons and do not assert bounded equivalence to the original `K`-norm.
For `A = 0` every unital `A`-module is zero; the specialization is the unique-map case.
Define `IsStrictlyCompletelyContinuous` using a single nonzero `a ∈ K°` and approximants
`f_n → f`: for each `n`, `a f_n(M₀)` lies in a finitely generated `A₀`-submodule of `N₀`.
The finite submodule may depend on `n`; the scalar may not. Prove that strict complete
continuity implies complete continuity (Kiehl-E §1, Definition 1.1, p. 198;
Bosch 2014 §6.4, Definition 1, p. 134).

Part III supplies the comparison with its lattice formulation. For complete compatible
ultrametric `K`-algebra and module norms inducing the specified topologies, compare their closed
unit balls with the chosen open bounded lattices, including the coefficient lattice `A₀`.
Each pair of lattices contains a nonzero `K°`-scalar multiple of the other. Prove that the
uniform-scalar approximation condition is unchanged by these replacements: multiply the
uniform scalar by fixed scalars for the source, target and coefficient comparisons, and
rescale the finitely many target generators into the new target lattice. Operator-norm
convergence is unchanged under equivalent norms. The scalar depends on the comparisons but
not on the approximant; the finite generating set may depend on the approximant. Thus the
lattice condition is an equivalent characterization of this predicate. *Needs:*
CompactOperators §0.1, finite-image approximation and the normalized scalar lattice comparison;
PadicFunctionalAnalysis §0.4 (*tate-ring-norm*); Part II *completed-tensor-banach-module*; Tau Ceti `Huber.IsTateRing`;
Mathlib continuous linear maps and their operator norm.

Prove `isStrictlyCompletelyContinuous_tsum` as an extension of that same predicate: over a
nontrivially normed nonarchimedean field `K`, a noetherian normed `K`-algebra `A`, compatible
normed `K`-modules with contractive `A`-actions and an ultrametric target `N`, let
`vᵢ : M →L[A] A` be uniformly bounded and
`nᵢ → 0` in `N`. Then `f(x) = Σᵢ vᵢ(x) • nᵢ` is strictly completely continuous. The source
and target need not be complete if the displayed sums exist and define a continuous map;
the finite truncations converge in operator norm. The finitely many generators in each
truncation can be scaled into the target unit ball by one scalar independent of the
truncation, since the sequence is bounded (Bosch 2014, §6.4, proof of Proposition 2, p. 135).
Decay cannot be replaced by boundedness: the coefficient functionals and `nᵢ = Tⁱ` on
`K⟨T⟩` reconstruct the identity pointwise, which is not completely continuous.

**Checks.**

- (negative control, non-decaying basis) — construct evaluation
  functionals `vᵢ(x) = x(i)` and vectors `eᵢ(j) = δᵢⱼ` in `c₀(ℕ,K)` over a complete
  nontrivially valued nonarchimedean field. They satisfy `‖vᵢ(x)‖ ≤ ‖x‖`, `‖eᵢ‖ = 1`
  and `Σ vᵢ(x)eᵢ = x`, while `eᵢ` does not tend to zero and the resulting identity
  is not completely continuous. The example asserts existence of these data.
- (computation, restriction to a smaller disc) — over `A = K`, the map
  `K⟨T⟩ → K⟨T/ϖ⟩`, `Σ aₙTⁿ ↦ Σ (aₙϖⁿ)(T/ϖ)ⁿ`, is the limit of its truncations below degree `N`, at
  operator-norm distance `≤ |ϖ|^N`, and each truncation maps `K°⟨T⟩` into the finitely generated
  `K°`-module `⊕_{n<N} K°(T/ϖ)ⁿ ⊆ K°⟨T/ϖ⟩` (a module that grows with `N`); hence it is strictly
  completely continuous with `a = 1`. Under the misreading "one finitely generated submodule for
  all `i`" it would not be, since its image is not contained in a finitely generated `K`-subspace.

**Checks for the strict predicate and its lattice comparison.**

- (zero map): the zero map is strict for every `A₀`;
  take all approximants zero and each finite generating set empty.
- (zero algebra): every module over `A = 0` is zero, and its unique map is strict
  without choosing a norm-one coefficient model.
- (one-dimensional identity): over `A = K` with `A₀ = K°`, the identity
  on `K` is strict; take `a = 1` and the one generator `1`.
- (infinite-dimensional identity): the identity on an infinite-dimensional
  Banach `K`-space is not strict, since it is not completely continuous.
- (rescaled lattices): replacing `M₀` and `N₀` by `ϖʳM₀` and `ϖˢN₀` for integers `r`, `s`
  preserves strictness and complete continuity; the uniform scalar and operator-norm error
  bounds change by fixed factors independent of the approximant.
- (gauge normalization): on `ℚ_p` with lattice `ℤ_p`, pseudouniformiser `p²` and
  parameter `p`, the discrete gauge of `p^(2m)` is `p^(−m)` while the scalar norm is
  `p^(−2m)`, so there is no comparison by fixed multiplicative constants. Parameter `p²`
  gives the supplied bounded comparison, including the value `1` at `p`.

The Schwartz finiteness theorem over affinoid algebras
(*completely-continuous-finite-cokernel*): if `f : M → N` is a continuous surjective `A`-linear
map of Banach `A`-modules and `g : M → N` is completely continuous, then `(f + g)(M)` is closed in
`N` and `N/(f + g)(M)` is a finitely generated `A`-module (Kiehl-E §1, Satz 1.2, p. 198). For
`M = N = K⟨T⟩`, `f = id` and `g = −h` with `h(T) = ϖT` (strictly completely continuous),
`(id − h)(Σ aₙTⁿ) = Σ aₙ(1 − ϖⁿ)Tⁿ` has closed image `T·K⟨T⟩` and cokernel `K`. Prove this from finite-rank
approximation and *surjection-small-perturbation*, with compatible complete ultrametric norms.
Equivalent lattice norms preserve the image and cokernel. *Needs:* *completely-continuous-map*;
*surjection-small-perturbation*; finite modules over noetherian affinoid algebras.

**Checks.** The rescaling example above has cokernel `K`; with `g = 0` the cokernel is zero;
with `f = id` and `g = −id` on `K⟨T⟩`, the cokernel is infinite-dimensional, and `g` fails
complete continuity.

Strict complete continuity descends to a closed submodule for topologically free
sources (*strictly-completely-continuous-closed-target*): let `f : M → N` be `A`-linear, `N ⊆ G` a
closed submodule of a Banach `A`-module, with compatible ultrametric norms,
`A₀ = {a : |a| ≤ 1}`, and an `IntegralAffinoidPresentation K A K° A₀`
as in *almost-noetherian-integral-affinoid-modules*, and suppose `j ∘ f : M → G` is strictly completely
continuous; if `M` is topologically free (the completed direct sum of copies of `A` with respect
to `A₀`), then `f : M → N` is strictly completely continuous. Use the model-space surjection
of PadicFunctionalAnalysis §§2.1–2.2 for the chosen Banach `A`-module model: its
`c₀(I,A)` has a discrete index set `I`, with no countability assumption
(Kiehl-E §1, Satz 1.4, p. 199; Kiehl-E
§1, remark before Satz 1.4, p. 199, where over discretely valued or spherically complete fields
closed subspaces are complemented, a hypothesis Satz 1.4 avoids). For `G = K⟨T⟩`, `N = T·K⟨T⟩` and
`M` topologically free, a strictly completely continuous map into `G` landing in `N` is strictly
completely continuous into `N`. The adapter `exists_c0_surjective` identifies that supplied
surjection with Part II's lattice model. Prove `IsStrictlyCompletelyContinuous.of_subtype_comp`
using finite approximations in the integral presentation. Identify the source with `c₀(I,A)`
by its basis and supremum norm. Require the coefficient unit ball to equal the image of
the Gauss unit ball of the chosen presentation, and preserve this equality in the lattice
comparison. *Needs:* *completely-continuous-map*; *almost-noetherian-integral-affinoid-modules*;
PadicFunctionalAnalysis §§2.1–2.2, model-space quotients;
Part II *completed-tensor-banach-module*, including `c₀(I,A)`.

**Checks.** For `N = G` the subtype is the identity; for `N = 0` the map and all approximants
are zero; for `N = T·K⟨T⟩ ⊆ G = K⟨T⟩` the conclusion holds without choosing a complement.

**Relatively compact affinoid subdomains over an affinoid base (Kiehl).**
(*relatively-compact-affinoid*) Let `V = Spa(B, B°)` be an affinoid adic space over `Spa(A, A°)`
with `B` topologically of finite type over `A`, and `U ⊆ V` an affinoid open subspace. `U` is
relatively compact in `V` over `A`, written `U ⋐_A V`, if there are a closed immersion
`V ↪ Dⁿ_A = Spa(A⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩)` over `A` and `ε ∈ √|K^×|` with `ε < 1` such that
`U ⊆ {|X_i| ≤ ε for all i}`. In `AdicSpace`, define
`RelativelyCompact K A f j` for the structure map `f : V → r(Sp A)` and
inclusion `j : U → V`. Its definition uses affinoid rigid realizations and the relative-compactness criterion
of RigidAnalyticGeometry §6.3, transported through Part II's
*proper-separated-comparisons*, with equations identifying both maps
under `rigidToAdic`.
`RelativelyCompact.iff_presentation` identifies it with the stated closed-immersion
criterion: for some `m > 0` and `a ≠ 0` with `|a| < 1`, all presentation coordinates
satisfy `|g_i(x)|^m ≤ |a|` on the inner affinoid. Thus `ε = |a|^(1/m)` lies in the
divisible value group. The open quotient presentation includes its equation on
coefficients from `A`; classical-point bounds are uniform and hence give the same
closed rational domain on the adic space (Bosch 2014, §6.3, Definition 6, p. 131;
Huber96, Remark 1.3.19, pp. 59–60).

Prove `RelativelyCompact.mono`
(`U' ⊆ U ⋐_A V`, with `U'` affinoid, `V'` affinoid over `A`, a closed immersion
`V → V'` over `A`, and the composite `U' → V'` an **open immersion**, gives
`U' ⋐_A V'`). The openness assumption is essential: a closed point of the unit
disc is not an affinoid open subdomain. This is the closed-immersion specialization
of the generator criterion (Bosch 2014, §6.3, Definition 6, p. 131). Prove
`RelativelyCompact.inter` (if `V`, `V'` are affinoid opens of an `A`-separated `X`, `U ⋐_A V` and
`U' ⋐_A V'` then `U ∩ U' ⋐_A V ∩ V'`; Kiehl-E §2, property (2) after Def. 2.2, p. 202), `RelativelyCompact.prod` (products over `A` of
relatively compact inclusions are relatively compact; the product and intersection
maps are specified by pullback squares and their projection equations),
`relativelyCompact_self_of_finite` (if `B`
is finite over `A` then `Spa(B) ⋐_A Spa(B)`), `RelativelyCompact.baseChange` (base change along an
affinoid `A → A'` preserves `⋐`; a finite extension `L/K` is included by taking
`A' = A ⊗̂_K L`, viewed as a strict `K`-affinoid algebra),
`RelativelyCompact.of_isRational` (if `U = {|g_i| ≤ ε}` for generators `g_i` of `B` over `A`,
after rescaling, then `U ⋐_A V`) and `RelativelyCompact.strictlyCompletelyContinuous` (the
restriction `𝒪(V) → 𝒪(U)` composed with a continuous surjection from a topologically free Banach
`A`-module is strictly completely continuous over `A`; stated as
*restriction-strictly-completely-continuous* below) (Kiehl-E §2, Def. 2.1, p. 202; Kiehl-E §2,
examples after Def. 2.3, p. 202, finite maps are proper via `V ⋐_A V` for `B` finite over `A`;
Huber96 §1.3, Rem. 1.3.19, pp. 59–60, Huber's comparison of Kiehl's relative-compactness notion of
(partial) properness with adic properness). *Needs:* *rigid-adic-comparison-functor* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R1); Tau
Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.closedPolydisc`, `Huber.Pair.Hom.isClosedEmbedding_spaComap_quotientHom`.
For `inter`, `prod`, and `baseChange`, see also Bosch 2014, §6.3, statement 7(iii),
7(ii), and 7(i), p. 131, respectively. The finite and rational-domain statements
follow from Definition 6 and the finite-map example following Definition 8,
pp. 131–132. The finite case includes the identity and the zero algebra.

**Checks.**

- `RelativelyCompact_disc` (computation) — for `V = Spa(K⟨X⟩)` and
  `U = {|X| ≤ |ϖ|}`, `U ⋐_K V` via the identity embedding and `ε = |ϖ|`.
- `RelativelyCompact_finite` (degenerate) — if `B` is a finite `A`-algebra (in
  particular `V = Spa(A)`) then `V ⋐_A V`: for integral generators `x₁,…,xₙ` of `B` over `A`
  choose `a ∈ K° ∖ {0}` with `|a xᵢ| < 1` on `V`; then `Xᵢ ↦ a xᵢ` gives `A⟨X⟩ ↠ B` with
  `V ⊆ {|Xᵢ| ≤ ε}` for some `ε < 1` (Kiehl-E §2, examples after Def. 2.3, pp. 202–203).
- `RelativelyCompact_unit_disc_not_self` (non-example) — the closed unit disc is
  not `⋐_K` itself: otherwise its structure morphism to `Spa(K, K°)` would be proper in
  Kiehl's sense (relatively compact affinoid coverings, *proper-relatively-compact-covers*) and
  `K⟨X⟩ = H⁰` would be finite over `K` by *kiehl-proper-mapping-theorem* (R3.6).
- `RelativelyCompact_rigid` (compatibility) — for rigid `V = Sp(B)` over `Sp(A)`,
  Kiehl's `U ⋐_A V` holds iff `r(U) ⋐_A r(V)`, with the same structure map
  `Sp(B) → Sp(A)`. The theorem relates the adic predicate to imported
  AdicSpacesPartII *proper-separated-comparisons* on the imported affinoid carriers.
- `RelativelyCompact_closed_point` (non-example) — a closed point in the unit disc
  is not an open subdomain, even when its coordinate has norm less than one.

The examples `RelativelyCompact_disc`, `RelativelyCompact_finite`,
`RelativelyCompact_unit_disc_not_self`, `RelativelyCompact_rigid`, and
`RelativelyCompact_closed_point` mirror these Checks. The disc case requires
`a ≠ 0`: radius zero is a point, not an affinoid open disc.

Prove `IsKiehlProper.relativelyCompact_covers` over every complete nontrivially
valued `K`: a Kiehl-proper morphism to `r(Sp A)` admits two finite affinoid open
covers, with each inner member relatively compact in the corresponding outer
member over `A`. `isKiehlProper_of_relativelyCompact_covers` gives the converse
for a separated morphism. The inclusions commute with the structure maps, and
their images cover every adic point. Bosch 2014, §6.3, Definition 8, p. 131, and §6.4, p. 133,
transported by Huber96, Remark 1.3.19(i), pp. 59–60, define properness by such pairs of finite
covers over the members of an admissible affinoid covering of the target; that the two covers
can be taken over all of `Sp A` is the characterisation of properness through formal models
(Lütkebohmert [L1] for discretely valued `K`, Temkin [Te] in general), which Bosch cites after
Definition 8, p. 131.

Prove `proper_relativelyCompact_covers` for adic proper morphisms obtained from
rigid morphisms over a discretely valued `K`
(*proper-relatively-compact-covers*): let `f : X → Spa(A, A°)` be a proper morphism of adic spaces
(*universally-closed-and-proper-morphism*, AdicSpacesPartII layer R0: +weakly finite type, separated, universally
closed); then `X` is quasi-compact and separated over `A`. Under the discrete-valuation
hypothesis, Part II's `rigidToAdic.proper_iff` supplies `IsKiehlProper`. For general
`K`, the finite-cover statement takes `IsKiehlProper K f` explicitly, as in
`IsKiehlProper.relativelyCompact_covers`. There are then finite affinoid open coverings `{U_i}_{i=1..r}`, `{V_i}_{i=1..r}` of `X` with
`V_i ⋐_A U_i` for every `i`; that is, `r⁻¹(f)` is proper in Kiehl's sense. Conversely a
Kiehl-proper morphism is proper, for every `K` (Kiehl-E §2, Def. 2.3, p. 202, Kiehl-properness via
relatively compact affinoid coverings; Conrad-RA Appendix A.1, p. 38, the cohomological theory is
proved for Kiehl-proper maps, hence the need for the comparison, and the comparison adic-proper
⇔ Kiehl-proper for general `K` rests on Temkin's comparison [Te], which this roadmap grants rather
than proves: for general `K`, Kiehl-properness is an explicit hypothesis). For `X = P^{1,an}_K` take
`U_i = {|x_j| ≤ |ϖ|⁻¹|x_i|}` and `V_i = {|x_j| ≤ |x_i|}` (`i ≠ j ∈ {0, 1}`): both families cover
`X` and `V_i ⋐_K U_i` (the unit disc inside the disc of radius `|ϖ|⁻¹` in the chart `x_j/x_i`).
*Needs:* *universally-closed-and-proper-morphism*, *separated-proper-partially-proper* (AdicSpacesPartII layer
R0); *proper-separated-comparisons* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R1); *relatively-compact-affinoid*.

Prove strict complete continuity of relatively compact restriction
(*restriction-strictly-completely-continuous*): let `V = Spa(B)` and `U = Spa(C)` be affinoid over
`Spa(A)` with `U ⋐_A V`, and `F` a coherent sheaf on `V` with `M = F(V)`, `N = F(U) = M ⊗_B C`
(finite modules with their Banach topologies); then `RelativelyCompact.strictlyCompletelyContinuous` says that for a continuous
surjection `q : c₀(I,A) → M` the composite with restriction is strictly completely
continuous over `A`. Such surjections exist by the topologically free surjection of
*strictly-completely-continuous-closed-target*. The statement takes complete
ultrametric norms compatible with the finite-module actions, an integral
presentation of the chosen ring of definition `A₀`, and the scalar-tower
compatibilities for `A → B → C`. The restriction is fixed by a `C`-linear
isomorphism `C ⊗_B M ≃ N` and the equation `res(m) = 1 ⊗ m` under that
isomorphism. It therefore applies to the actual coherent restriction, including
`M = B` and `N = C`. Prove `RelativelyCompact.strictlyCompletelyContinuous` using the finite-module section
comparison, finite-rank truncations of the rescaled presentation coordinates and
*strictly-completely-continuous-closed-target*. The lattice/norm comparison identifies
these truncations with the actual restriction map. Require the coefficient unit ball
to equal the image of the Gauss unit ball of the chosen presentation.
See Bosch 2014, §6.4, Proposition 2, p. 135, statement 6,
pp. 138–139, and the proof of Proposition 7, pp. 140–141. The same holds for finite intersections of such pairs inside an
`A`-separated space (Kiehl-E §2, before Satz 2.5, p. 204, the rescaling map `h_a` is strictly
completely continuous, and finite modules over affinoid algebras carry a unique complete
topology). For `V` the unit disc, `U = {|X| ≤ |ϖ|}` and `F = 𝒪`, the restriction `K⟨X⟩ → K⟨X/ϖ⟩`
itself is strictly completely continuous. In the rescaled target coordinate `S = X/ϖ`,
the rescaling statement characterizes this map by
`coeffₙ(f(g)) = ϖⁿ coeffₙ(g)` on the pinned restricted-series Tate algebra.

**Checks.** (small disc) for `0 < |ϖ| < 1` that
coefficient map is strictly completely continuous and sends the constant series `1` to `1`;
thus strict complete continuity does not require every coefficient, including degree zero,
to be contracted; (truncations) the degree-`N` truncation has error at most `|ϖ|^N` and its
finite `K°`-span grows with `N`, with uniform scalar `1`; (negative control) the identity
restriction on the unit disc is not completely continuous over `K`, and the disc is not
relatively compact in itself. *Needs:* *relatively-compact-affinoid*, `RelativelyCompact_rigid`;
*completely-continuous-map* (lattice/norm comparison);
*strictly-completely-continuous-closed-target*;
*tate-kiehl-affinoid*.

Finiteness of coherent cohomology over an affinoid base, Kiehl's Satz 2.6
(*proper-affinoid-cohomology-finite*): provides, for a Kiehl-proper `f : X → Spa(A, A°)` and a
coherent `𝒪_X`-module `F`, that every `Hⁱ(X, F)` is a finite `A`-module and that the differentials
of the Čech complex of every finite affinoid covering of `X` have closed image. Prove both assertions by the
relatively compact Čech comparison and Schwartz finiteness (Kiehl-E §2, Satz 2.6,
pp. 204–205; Bosch 2014 §6.4, Proposition 7, pp. 140–141).
*Needs:* *restriction-strictly-completely-continuous*; *completely-continuous-finite-cokernel*;
*proper-relatively-compact-covers*; the Čech-to-derived comparison.

Checks: for the identity of an affinoid `H⁰ = F(X)` is finite and positive cohomology
vanishes; zero coefficients give the zero complex; for `P¹_K` with `O(−2)`,
`H¹ = K` and the two-chart Čech difference has closed image.

The adic comparison for proper formal functions (*proper-cohomology-adic-completion*):
for a Kiehl-proper `f : X → Spa(A, A°)`, coherent `F` and an ideal `𝔞 ⊆ A`,
transport RigidAnalyticGeometry §7.5's completion theorem and stable principal filtration
through Part II's rigid–adic equivalence. Identify the quotient sheaves `F/𝔞ᵏF`, their
epimorphisms and transitions with the corresponding rigid quotients; on cohomology these
identifications intertwine the maps from `Hⁱ(X,F)` at every `k`. Consequently the transported
isomorphism is the canonical map
`Hⁱ(X,F)^∧_𝔞 ≃ lim_k Hⁱ(X,F/𝔞ᵏF)`.
For `𝔞 = (a)`, the comparison identifies
`R_k = ker(Hⁱ(X,F) → Hⁱ(X,F/aᵏF))` and the kernel and cokernel systems with the
supplier's systems, preserving their transitions and uniform shifts. This is ideal-adic
completion of the finite `A`-module, distinct from Banach completion
(Kiehl-E §3, Theorems 3.4 and 3.7, pp. 207–209).
*Needs:* RigidAnalyticGeometry §7.5, principal filtrations and formal functions;
Part II *rigid-adic-quasi-separated-equivalence*; *coherent-sheaf-operations*;
*proper-affinoid-cohomology-finite*.

Checks: with `𝔞 = 0` the comparison is the identity; with `𝔞 = A` both sides are zero;
for `X = Spa A`, `F = O`, it is `Â ≅ lim A/𝔞ᵏ`.

Kiehl's Satz 3.5 (*proper-cohomology-affinoid-subdomain*): provides, for a Kiehl-proper
`f : X → Spa(A, A°)`, coherent `F` and an affinoid subdomain `U = Spa(B, B°)` of `Spa(A, A°)`, the
`B`-linear isomorphism `B ⊗_A Hⁱ(X, F) ≅ Hⁱ(f⁻¹(U), F)` sending `b ⊗ m` to `b` times the
restriction of `m`. Prove this for the actual
restriction `cohomologyPullback` along `f⁻¹(U) → X` (Kiehl-E §3, Satz 3.5,
pp. 207–208). *Needs:* *proper-affinoid-cohomology-finite*; Part II *affinoid-subdomain-flat*;
finite-module base change and the strict Čech complex.

Checks: for `U = Spa A` the map is `b ⊗ m ↦ bm`; zero coefficients give a zero
isomorphism; restricting `P¹_A` with `O(−2)` to `Spa B` sends its rank-one `H¹ = A` to `B`.

Countable-type splittings on the Banach-module tensor carrier
(*countable-type-closed-subspace-section*): for a strict exact sequence
`0 → F → E → E/F → 0` of Banach `K`-spaces with `E` of countable type and `F` closed,
use PadicFunctionalAnalysis §2.4's `exists_continuousLinearEquiv_prod_of_countableType`.
Identify its completed projective tensor with Part II's Banach-module completed tensor
by their continuous balanced universal properties. For every complete isometric extension
`K'/K`, prove that this identification intertwines the tensored inclusion, quotient,
section and projection on pure tensors. It therefore transports the supplied continuous
splitting and strict exactness to `K' ⊗̂_K (−)` on Part II's carrier
(BGR §2.7, countable-type Banach spaces; KL15, Lemma 2.2.9, pp. 30–31).
*Needs:* PadicFunctionalAnalysis §2.4, countable type and strict splitting;
Part II *completed-tensor-banach-module*, *banach-completed-tensor-field-exactness*.

Checks: `F = 0` gives complement `E`; `F = E` gives the zero complement; in
`c₀(ℕ,K)`, the subspace of sequences with first coordinate zero has complement `K e₀`
and projection `x ↦ x(0)e₀`.

Completed extension of the base field for affinoid algebras (*affinoid-completed-field-extension*):
provides, for an affinoid `K`-algebra `A`, an extension `K'/K` of complete nonarchimedean fields
and `A' = K' ⊗̂_K A`, that `A → A'` is faithfully flat and that `A' ⊗_A M → K' ⊗̂_K M` is a
topological isomorphism for every finite `A`-module `M`. Use
`A' = Huber.CompletedTensor K A K'` with structure map `a ↦ a ⊗ 1` and prove both
assertions for this map (BGR §6.1.1, completed scalar extension; Conrad-RA Appendix A.1,
Theorem A.1.2 and its proof, p. 39, the finite-module comparison).
*Needs:* Part II *completed-tensor-product*, *completed-tensor-banach-module*,
*banach-completed-tensor-field-exactness*; noetherian affinoid module topologies.

Checks: for `K' = K` the map is the identity; for `A = K` it is the faithfully flat
field extension `K → K'`; for `M = 0` both tensor modules vanish.

`AdicSpace.moduleUnit` is the adjunction unit on abelian sheaves and
`AdicSpace.cohomologyPullback` is its induced pullback on cohomology.
**Checks:** `moduleUnit_identity` / `cohomologyPullback_identity` are isomorphisms;
`moduleUnit_zero` / `cohomologyPullback_zero` vanish on the zero module;
`moduleUnit_sections` / `cohomologyPullback_sections` agree with the section map in degree zero.

Proper coherent cohomology commutes with completed extension of the base field
(*proper-coherent-cohomology-field-extension*): provides, for a Kiehl-proper
`f : X → Spa(A, A°)`, coherent `F` on `X` and an extension `K'/K` of complete nonarchimedean
fields, that the natural map `A' ⊗_A Hⁱ(X, F) → Hⁱ(X', F')` is an isomorphism of finite
`A'`-modules for every `i`, where `A' = K' ⊗̂_K A` and `F'` is the pullback of `F` to
`X' = X ⊗̂_K K'`. Prove invertibility of this
natural map using the strict finite Čech complex (Conrad-RA Appendix A.1, Theorem A.1.2,
p. 39). *Needs:* *proper-affinoid-cohomology-finite*; *affinoid-completed-field-extension*;
Part II *banach-completed-tensor-field-exactness*.

Checks: the identity extension gives the identity; zero coefficients give zero on both
sides; `P¹_K` with `O(−2)` has `H¹ = K`, and the comparison carries its Čech generator
to that of `H¹(P¹_{K'},O(−2)) = K'`.

Proper coherent cohomology commutes with finite flat base change of affinoids
(*proper-cohomology-finite-flat-base-change*): provides, for a Kiehl-proper `f : X → S` with
`S = Spa(A, A°)`, coherent `F` on `X` and a finite flat `g : T = Spa(B, B°) → S`, that the map
`B ⊗_A Hⁱ(X, F) → Hⁱ(X ×_S T, F_T)` induced by pullback is an isomorphism for every `i`. Prove this using the finite
flat scalar extension of the affinoid Čech complex (Scholze13 §9, proof of Proposition 9.2,
p. 54). *Needs:* *proper-affinoid-cohomology-finite*; Part II *finite-algebra-tensor-complete*;
Mathlib flat tensor exactness.

Checks: identity base change gives the identity; `B = A × A` gives the pair of pullback
classes on the disjoint union; zero coefficients give zero on both sides.

**Base change of proper coherent cohomology along étale maps of affinoids (Scholze's Proposition
9.2(ii)).** (*proper-coherent-base-change*) Let `g : T → S` be an étale morphism
(*differentials-unramified-smooth-etale*, AdicSpacesPartII layer R0) of affinoid adic spaces locally of finite type
over `Spa(K, K°)` (locally noetherian, hence locally Huber-standard), `f : X → S` proper, `F_X` coherent on `X`, `Y = X ×_S T` and `F_Y` the
pullback. Prove `AdicSpace.proper_directImage_etale_baseChange`: for all `i` the natural map
`Hⁱ(X, F_X) ⊗_{𝒪_S(S)} 𝒪_T(T) → Hⁱ(Y, F_Y)` is an isomorphism; equivalently, the canonical
sheaf base-change map `g*(Rⁱf_*F_X) → Rⁱf_{T*}F_Y` is an isomorphism
(Scholze13 §9, Prop. 9.2(ii), p. 54;
Scholze13 §9, proof of Prop. 9.2, p. 54, the reduction used in the proof).
Use `IsKiehlProper K f`, charts `c` and `d` presenting `S` and `T`, a pullback square
`hs : IsPullback p q f g` fixing `Y` and its projections, and a coefficient homomorphism
`φ : A → B` agreeing with `g` on coefficients. The conclusion includes a
`B`-linear equivalence satisfying `E(a ⊗ m) = a • cohomologyPullback p F_X i m`,
with module actions induced by `f` and `q`, as well as the natural isomorphism of
higher-direct-image functors on coherent modules. For `T ⊆ S` rational
the statement is Kiehl's Satz 3.5; for `T = S ⊔ S` it is `Hⁱ(X ⊔ X) = Hⁱ(X)²`. *Needs:*
*kiehl-proper-mapping-theorem*, *proper-cohomology-affinoid-subdomain*,
*proper-cohomology-finite-flat-base-change* (R3.6); *etale-flat-unramified*,
*differentials-unramified-smooth-etale*, *base-change-stability*,
*etale-affinoid-finite-etale-embedding* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R0).

**Checks:** `proper_cohomology_baseChange_identity` computes `a ⊗ m ↦ a • m`
for identity scalar extension using `TensorProduct.lid`;
`proper_cohomology_baseChange_zero` sends `a ⊗ 0` to zero;
`proper_cohomology_baseChange_zeroMap` exhibits isomorphic rank-one finite
`ℚ`-modules whose zero comparison map is not bijective. Thus the pure-tensor
equation specifies which map must be invertible.

Almost noetherianity of modules over integral affinoid rings, Kiehl's Anhang Satz 5.1
(*almost-noetherian-integral-affinoid-modules*): let `K` be a complete nonarchimedean field with
nontrivial absolute value of rank one and valuation ring `K°`, `A` an affinoid `K`-algebra and
`A₀ ⊆ A` a `K°`-subalgebra which is a ring of definition of `A` and a quotient of `K°⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩`
(Kiehl's case; for instance the image of `K°⟨X⟩` under a presentation `K⟨X⟩ ↠ A`); let `M` be a
finitely generated `A₀`-module and `N ⊆ M` an `A₀`-submodule; then for every real `ε` with
`0 < ε < 1` there is a finitely generated `A₀`-submodule `N′ ⊆ N` such that `a·N ⊆ N′` for every
`a ∈ K°` with `|a| ≤ ε`. If `K` is discretely valued, `N` itself is finitely generated (`A₀` is
noetherian) (Kiehl-E §5 (Anhang), Satz 5.1, p. 212, proved by Kiehl for `B₀` a quotient of
`V⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩`, the general case reducing to this; Kiehl-E §1, proof of Satz 1.4, p. 200, where the
lemma is used). For `K = ℂ_p`, `A₀ = 𝒪_{ℂ_p}` and `N = 𝔪` (not finitely generated), for every
`ε < 1` one may take `N′ = x·𝒪_{ℂ_p}` with `ε < |x| < 1`, since `a·𝔪 ⊆ x𝒪` when `|a| ≤ ε`; for
`K` discretely valued the lemma is the noetherianity of `K°⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩`. Prove these estimates for the integral presentation below. *Needs:*
Tau Ceti `Huber.restrictedMvPowerSeriesCompletion`; Mathlib `IsNoetherianRing`;
finite-submodule approximation in the restricted-series presentation.

The integral carrier `Huber.IntegralAffinoidPresentation K A V A₀` consists of
`V = {a ∈ K : |a| ≤ 1}`, a coefficient homomorphism `V → A₀` whose composite into `A`
is the given scalar map, and a continuous surjection
`Huber.restrictedMvPowerSeriesCompletion n V → A₀` agreeing with this coefficient map.
The subring `A₀` is open and bounded in `A`. These are presentation data; almost
noetherianity is a theorem, not a field of the structure. Part III compares the restricted-series
carrier with the Gauss unit ball, preserving coefficients. Inverting `ϖ` extends
the integral surjection to `K⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩ → A`: every restricted series over `K` becomes integral
after multiplication by a power of `ϖ`, and every element of `A` enters the open ring `A₀`
after such multiplication. Prove surjectivity and identify the image of the Gauss unit ball
with the given subring `A₀`, with its specified presentation. The declarations
`IntegralAffinoidPresentation.almost_noetherian` and `.fg_of_discrete` prove the two estimates
through this identification, with the latter assuming `IsDiscreteValuationRing V`.
The identification fixes the actual subring and scalar action, not merely an abstract ring
isomorphism (Kiehl-E §5, Satz 5.1, p. 212; Bosch 2014, §6.4, proof of Lemma 5, pp. 137–138).

**Checks for the integral estimates.** For `ℂ_p` the maximal-ideal example above gives the
finite approximation while the ideal itself is not finitely generated; for `ℚ_p` one obtains
noetherianity of `ℤ_p⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩`; for `N = 0` take `N′ = 0`.

**Checks for the integral carrier.**

- `Huber.IntegralAffinoidPresentation.test_field`: for `A = K`, `A₀ = V = K°`,
  there is a presentation with zero variables and coefficient map the identity.
- `Huber.IntegralAffinoidPresentation.test_zero`: the zero `K`-algebra has a
  zero-variable presentation, with image the zero subring.
- `Huber.IntegralAffinoidPresentation.test_unbounded`: `A₀ = K` cannot be an integral
  model of `A = K` when its valuation is nontrivial; the whole field is unbounded.

The higher direct-image functor `AdicSpace.higherDirectImage f i` is the right derived
functor of module-sheaf direct image. `higherDirectImage_resolution` computes it by applying
direct image to an injective resolution and taking degree-`i` homology. The affinoid
coefficient ring acts on cohomology through the scalar action induced by multiplication on the
coefficient sheaf; this is the module structure in which *proper-affinoid-cohomology-finite* is
read. `moduleScalar_app` specifies multiplication on sections, and `cohomologyAction` sends a
global function to the cohomology map of that scalar endomorphism.

**Checks for derived direct image and scalar actions.**

- `higherDirectImage_degreeZero` — degree zero is ordinary direct image.
- `higherDirectImage_identity` — positive-degree direct images of the identity vanish.
- `higherDirectImage_injective` — injective coefficient sheaves have no positive-degree direct images.
- `moduleScalar_zero` — multiplication by zero is the zero sheaf morphism.
- `moduleScalar_one` — multiplication by one is the identity.
- `moduleScalar_product` — multiplication of functions corresponds to composition of scalar morphisms.
- `cohomologyAction_zero` — on the analytic projective line with `𝒪(−2)`, choose the
  linear identification of `H¹` with `K`. The class corresponding to `1` is nonzero,
  and multiplication by the pulled-back scalar zero sends it to zero.
- `cohomologyAction_one` — on the same nonzero class, the pulled-back scalar one
  acts as one; more generally the scalar `a` sends that class to the class corresponding
  to `a`. These checks use the structural coefficient map into global analytic sections.
- `cohomologyAction_degreeZero` — the action on zeroth cohomology agrees with multiplication of sections.

### R3.7 proper GAGA

The relative carrier Part II’s `AdicSpace.SchemePullback f c.affinoid.spa c.affinoid.toSpec` represents pairs of compatible
maps to the scheme and the affinoid base. Its field `homEquiv_apply` specifies composition
with the projection. Part II’s `schemePullback` chooses this representing object, whose
existence is Huber96 (1.2.7), p. 50. `analytificationMap_projection` fixes the induced
morphism on every scheme map over the base. The construction is compatible with identity,
composition, isomorphisms and finite morphisms.

`schemeModulePullback` is pullback on module sheaves along the actual morphism of locally
ringed spaces. `schemeModuleUnit` is its adjunction unit and `schemeSectionsPullback` is
that unit on global sections. `cohomologyComparison` applies inverse image to extensions
of the constant integer sheaf and composes with this unit. `cohomologyComparison_zero`
identifies degree zero with the section map; `cohomologyComparison_naturality` states
naturality in the coefficient module. The rigid-site map is defined independently by the
composite inverse-image functor, and `cohomologyComparison_test_rigid` equates the two maps.
`cohomologyComparison_test_skyscraper` uses the actual quotient by the coordinate on
`Spec A[T]`. `cohomologyComparison_affineLine_not_surjective` states failure of surjectivity
for the canonical map on the affine line.

**Checks for relative analytification and module pullback.**

- `relativeAnalytification_identity` — analytifying the identity of the affine base gives that base.
- `relativeAnalytification_empty` — the empty scheme has empty analytification.
- `relativeAnalytification_affineLine` — maps to the analytic affine line over the base correspond to global functions.
- `analytificationMap_identity` — the identity induces the identity.
- `analytificationMap_composite` — induced maps preserve composition.
- `analytificationMap_isomorphism` — an algebraic isomorphism induces an analytic isomorphism.
- `schemeModulePullback_zero` — the zero module pulls back to zero.
- `schemeModulePullback_self` — the structure sheaf pulls back to the structure sheaf.
- `schemeModulePullback_free` — a finite free module retains its rank.
- `cohomologyComparison_zeroSheaf` — the comparison for zero coefficients is zero.
- `cohomologyComparison_empty` — the comparison into an empty analytic space is zero.
- `cohomologyComparison_functions` — the section comparison for the structure sheaf is the structural ring map.


Throughout this subsection `K` is a complete nonarchimedean field with nontrivial absolute value
and `A` an affinoid `K`-algebra (`A = K` allowed); `X` is a scheme locally of finite type over
`Spec A`, `X^an = X ×_{Spec A} Spa(A, A°)` its relative analytification
(*scheme-fibre-product-analytification*, AdicSpacesPartII layer R1; for `A = K`, *analytification-functor*, AdicSpacesPartII layer
R1) with the morphism of locally ringed spaces `ι_X : X^an → X`, and `F ↦ F^an = ι_X*F` is the
analytification of `𝒪_X`-modules (*analytification-of-modules*, AdicSpacesPartII layer R1).

Analytification carries coherent sheaves to coherent sheaves (*analytification-coherent*): provides
that `F ↦ F^an` is an exact functor from `𝒪_X`-modules to `𝒪_{X^an}`-modules carrying coherent
sheaves to coherent sheaves. Prove exactness by stalk flatness and coherence by local finite presentations
(Conrad-AWS §2.3, pp. 16–17; Conrad-RA Appendix A.1, Remark A.1.1, pp. 38–39).
*Needs:* Part II R1.3–R1.4 *analytification-map-flat*, *analytification-of-modules*;
R3.1a `analytification.modules_chartSections`; *tate-kiehl-affinoid*.

Checks: zero modules pull back to zero; the structure sheaf pulls back to the analytic
structure sheaf; `O/(T²)` on `A¹_K` pulls back to its coherent nonreduced quotient,
including the class of `T` with square zero.

**The GAGA comparison maps on cohomology and higher direct images.** (*gaga-comparison-map*) Let
`F` be an `𝒪_X`-module with analytification `F^an`. The comparison map
`c_F : Hⁱ(X, F) → Hⁱ(X^an, F^an)` is the composite of `Hⁱ(X, F) → Hⁱ(X, ι_*ι*F)` (the unit
`F → ι_*ι*F`) with the edge map `Hⁱ(X, ι_*F^an) → Hⁱ(X^an, F^an)`; it is `A`-linear and
δ-functorial in `F`. For `f : X → Y` over `Spec A`, the relative comparison map
`(Rⁱf_*F)^an → Rⁱf^an_*(F^an)` is the adjoint of the sheafified map
`V ↦ [Hⁱ(f⁻¹V, F) → Hⁱ((f^an)⁻¹V^an, F^an)]`, δ-functorial in `F` and compatible with
composition in `f`. For coherent `F`, `c_F` is an isomorphism when `X` is proper over `Spec A`
(*proper-gaga* (a)), and the relative map is an
isomorphism when `f` is proper (*proper-gaga* (b)).
Properness of `f` alone does not make `c_F` an isomorphism (`proper_gaga_test_identityAffineLine`).
In `AdicSpace`, define `cohomologyComparison` as
`c_F : Hⁱ(X, F) →ₗ[A] Hⁱ(X^an, F^an)` and `directImageComparison` as
`(Rⁱf_*F)^an → Rⁱf^an_*(F^an)`, δ-functorial; prove `cohomologyComparison_naturality`
(naturality in `F`: `c_G ∘ Hⁱ(φ) = Hⁱ(φ^an) ∘ c_F`), `cohomologyComparison_delta` (compatibility with
the connecting morphisms of short exact sequences), `cohomologyComparison_zero` (in degree 0,
`c_F` is `F(X) → F^an(X^an)`, `s ↦ ι*s`), `directImageComparison_comp` (compatibility with
composition `f ∘ g`, via the Leray spectral sequences), `directImageComparison_global` (for
proper `f`, coherent `F` and `Y = Spec A`, the relative comparison map on global
sections is the absolute one under the acyclic edge identifications) and
`cohomologyComparison_baseChange` (compatibility with base change along an affinoid `A → A'` and
with pullback along morphisms of schemes) (Conrad-RA Appendix A.1, pp. 38–39, Conrad's δ-functorial
GAGA isomorphisms (A.1.1) `Rⁱf_*(F)^an ≃ Rⁱf^an_*(F^an)`, which are instances of these comparison
maps; Conrad-RA Ex. 3.2.6, p. 24, the relative comparison map defined by δ-functoriality).
*Needs:* *analytification-of-modules*, *analytification-fibre-products* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R1);
DerivedModuleAlgebra §S.1 `DoubleComplex.totalCohomology_of_exact_rows` and its transpose, applied to a sheaf resolution on the rational basis; Mathlib `SheafOfModules.pullback`; Tau Ceti
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.Cohomology`.

**Checks.**

- `AdicSpace.cohomologyComparison_test_affineLine` (non-example) — for `X = A¹_K` and `F = 𝒪`
  the degree-0 comparison `K[T] → 𝒪(A^{1,ad}_K)` is not surjective (the series `Σ ϖ^{n²}Tⁿ` is
  entire), so `c_F` is not an isomorphism when `X` is not proper over `Spec A`.
- `AdicSpace.cohomologyComparison_test_point` (degenerate) — for `X = Spec K` the comparison maps
  are the identity of `H⁰ = F(X)` and `0` in positive degrees.
- `AdicSpace.cohomologyComparison_test_skyscraper` (computation) — for `X = A¹_K` and
  `F = 𝒪_X/(T)`, the degree-0 comparison `K → K` is an isomorphism.
- `AdicSpace.cohomologyComparison_test_rigid` (compatibility) — under the rigid–adic comparison
  (*rigid-adic-comparison-functor*, AdicSpacesPartII layer R1) `c_F` agrees with Köpf's and Conrad's rigid-analytic
  comparison maps.

`AdicSpace.directImageZeroComparison` is the natural transformation from analytified
ordinary direct image to ordinary analytic direct image. Its equation
`directImageZeroComparison_sections` sends the pullback of a section over `f⁻¹(V)`
to the same section pulled back on the analytic source; linearity and sheafification
then determine the map. `directImageComparison_resolution` fixes the higher map:
for an algebraic injective resolution and an analytic injective resolution, every
chain map lifting the coefficient unit gives the same map on homology after the
canonical comparison between exact pullback and homology. The natural transformation
`directImageComparison` is an isomorphism for proper morphisms and coherent
coefficients by *proper-gaga* (b); the target `Y` need not be proper over `Spec A`.

**Checks for the relative comparison constructions.**

- `directImageZeroComparison_identity` — the degree-zero comparison for the identity is invertible.
- `directImageZeroComparison_zero` — zero coefficients give the zero morphism.
- `directImageZeroComparison_finite` — finite morphisms and coherent coefficients give an isomorphism.
- `directImageComparison_identity` — the identity comparison is invertible in every degree.
- `directImageComparison_zero` — the map for zero coefficients is zero in every degree.
- `directImageComparison_finite` — finite morphisms give comparison isomorphisms and zero higher direct images in positive degrees.

**Checks for `directImageComparison`.**

- `directImageComparison_identity`: for `f = id`, degree zero is
  the identity on `F^an`; both higher direct images vanish.
- `directImageComparison_quadraticBasis`: for
  `Spec(A[Z]/(Z²-t)) → Spec A` and `F = 𝒪`, degree zero identifies the two
  free rank-two modules with basis `1,Z`, and higher degrees vanish, including at `t=0`.
- `directImageComparison_projectiveLine`: for `P¹_A → Spec A`
  and `F = 𝒪(-2)`, degree one identifies `A` with `A`, and degree zero identifies
  the two zero modules. `cohomologyComparison_projectiveLine` computes these
  modules; `directImageComparison_projectiveLine` checks the direct-image map.

`AdicSpace.projectiveSpaceBundle A n` equips Part II's `projectiveSpace A n`
with F0's `ProjectiveBundleData` for the free module `A^(n+1)`. Its universal
quotient sends the standard basis to the homogeneous coordinates. Define
`AdicSpace.projectiveSpaceTwist A n m` using the `m`th tensor power of this
quotient line when `m ≥ 0`, and the `−m`th tensor power of its dual when `m < 0`.
These definitions apply over every commutative ring, including the zero ring.
They use the imported `tensorPower` interface of F0 and the existing sheaf dual.

Prove `AdicSpace.cohomologyComparison_projectiveSpace`, the coherent cohomology
of `𝒪(m)` on analytic projective space (*analytic-projective-space-cohomology*).
Let `(A,A⁺)` be a complete affinoid whose ring is Tate, strongly noetherian and
noetherian. For `n ≥ 0` and `m ∈ ℤ`, the comparison map
`Hⁱ(Pⁿ_A, 𝒪(m)) → Hⁱ((Pⁿ_A)^an, 𝒪(m)^an)` (by *gaga-comparison-map*) is an isomorphism of finite
`A`-modules for every `i`, with the equivalence explicitly equal to
`cohomologyComparison` on every class. Its other three clauses state vanishing
for `i > 0`, `i ≠ n` (in particular `0 < i < n`); the degree-zero calculation
`H⁰ = A[x₀,…,xₙ]_m` for `n ≥ 1`; and `Hⁿ` dual to `H⁰` of `𝒪(−m−n−1)`.
The polynomial piece is `MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule` for `m ≥ 0` and
the zero submodule for `m < 0`. The degree-zero clause also states that for `n = 0`,
`P⁰_A = Spec A`, every `𝒪(m)` is `𝒪`, and `H⁰ = A` for all `m ∈ ℤ`, which differs from
`A[x₀]_m = 0` for `m < 0`. The algebraic computation is EGA III₁,
2.1.12–2.1.14, pp. 98–99, with the duality pairing in 2.1.16, p. 99.
Conrad-RA Appendix A.1, pp. 38–39 explains Köpf's projective GAGA route;
§3.1, Remark 3.1.3, pp. 18–19 identifies the projective-space twist computation
as its input. Over a general strongly noetherian Tate affinoid the target uses
the standard rational affinoid cover and Tate acyclicity, without assuming a
proper-GAGA theorem. For `n = 1`,
`m = −2`: `H¹((P¹_K)^an, 𝒪(−2)) = K`, spanned by the class of `x₀⁻¹x₁⁻¹` on `W₀ ∩ W₁ = {|x₀| =
|x₁|}`, `W_i = {|x_j| ≤ |x_i|}` the
standard affinoid charts; for `n = 1`,
`m ≥ 0`: `H⁰ = K[x₀, x₁]_m` of dimension `m + 1` and `H¹ = 0`. The algebraic side, the
cohomology of `𝒪(m)` on `Pⁿ_A`, is SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 2 (§2.6, `projectiveSpace_cohomology`)
and *projective-bundles-ample-serre* (layer F0); the analytic computation is new. *Needs:*
*gaga-comparison-map*; *analytification-coherent* (R3.7, for `K`-affinoid `A`; over the other strongly noetherian
Tate affinoids it is applied only to the twists `𝒪(m)^an`, which are coherent as line bundles);
*tate-acyclicity-finite-modules*;
*analytic-projective-space-proper* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R1); *projective-bundles-ample-serre* (layer F0);
SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 2 (§2.6, `projectiveSpace_cohomology`); DerivedModuleAlgebra §S.1 `DoubleComplex.totalCohomology_of_exact_rows` and its transpose, applied to a sheaf resolution on the rational basis; Tau Ceti `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.Cohomology`.

**Checks for projective bundles and twists.** Each Check carries the indicated name.

- `projectiveSpaceBundle_point`: in dimension zero the universal quotient is an isomorphism.
- `projectiveSpaceBundle_line`: over a field the universal line on `P¹` is not the structure sheaf.
- `projectiveSpaceBundle_empty`: over the zero ring the universal line is a zero object.
- `projectiveSpaceTwist_zero`: the zeroth twist is the structure sheaf.
- `projectiveSpaceTwist_one`: the first twist is the universal quotient line.
- `projectiveSpaceTwist_negOne`: the negative first twist is its dual.
- `analyticProjectiveSpaceCohomology_test_point`: the theorem of this name gives
  `H⁰((P⁰_A)^an, 𝒪(m)^an) ≃ₗ[A] A` for every `m < 0` over a complete
  affinoid with Tate, strongly noetherian, noetherian ring. The scalar action
  comes from the projection to `Spa(A,A⁺)`. This is the dimension-zero clause of
  `cohomologyComparison_projectiveSpace`, alongside the vanishing polynomial
  piece; its example specializes to `m = −1`. Thus for nonzero `A` the sections
  are nonzero even though the negative polynomial piece is zero. EGA III₁,
  Proposition 2.1.12, pp. 98–99 assumes positive projective dimension;
  here `P⁰_A = Spec A` and all twists are trivial.

`cohomologyComparison_smul` gives semilinearity for the actual map on global
functions. `cohomologyComparison_delta` gives compatibility with connecting maps
when the pulled-back short sequence remains exact; analytification supplies this
through flatness. The connecting maps use the same Ext sign convention.

`directImageComparison_comp` uses Mathlib
`CategoryTheory.E₂CohomologicalSpectralSequenceNat`
(`Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/SpectralSequence/Basic.lean`): its second page is the
composite of the two relative comparisons, and its finite abutment filtrations
carry the comparison for the composite morphism. The quotient equations fix
the associated graded maps without choosing splittings.

`moduleCohomologyResolutionIso` compares Ext cohomology of the underlying
abelian sheaf with global sections of a module injective resolution. It differs
from Mathlib `CategoryTheory.InjectiveResolution.isoRightDerivedObj` by relating
the module resolution to the abelian-sheaf Ext definition. Its degree-zero,
naturality and horseshoe connecting-map equations fix its normalization.
`directImageComparison_global` then uses these isomorphisms and Mathlib's
homology comparisons for global sections; properness and coherence supply the
acyclicity over the affinoid base (Conrad-RA (A.1.1), p. 39).

**Checks for the resolution comparison.**

- `moduleCohomologyResolutionIso_zeroCoefficients`: zero coefficients give the zero map.
- `moduleCohomologyResolutionIso_injective`: a module injective has zero positive cohomology, using its degree-zero resolution.
- `moduleCohomologyResolutionIso_degreeZero`: a section has zero class exactly when it is zero.

**Checks for the comparison helpers.**

| Definition | Three direct Checks |
|---|---|
| Part II `toLocallyRingedSpace` | `locallyRingedSpace_emptyCarrier`: an empty adic space stays empty; `locallyRingedSpace_localStalk`: its stalk is local; `locallyRingedSpace_affinoidSections`: affinoid global sections recover the coefficient ring. |
| `commRingSheaf` | `commRingSheaf_emptyOpen`: sections on the empty open form the zero ring; `commRingSheaf_affinoidSections`: the coefficient map is bijective; `commRingSheaf_gluing`: two sections agreeing on a two-open cover are equal. |
| Part II `forgetToLocallyRingedSpace.map` | `locallyRingedSpaceMap_identity`, `locallyRingedSpaceMap_composition`, `locallyRingedSpaceMap_isomorphism`: identities, composition and invertibility are preserved. |
| Part II `Affinoid.toSpec`, applied to `c.affinoid` | `Chart.toSpec_empty`: the zero ring gives empty image; `Chart.toSpec_coefficients`: constants pull back by the coefficient map; `Chart.toSpec_support`: the image prime is the support of the valuation. |
| `constantPullbackIso` | `constantPullbackIso_zero`: the zero group gives the zero morphism; `constantPullbackIso_naturality`: coefficient homomorphisms commute with the comparison; `constantPullbackIso_constantSections`: every constant section retains its value. |
| `sheafCohomologyPullback` | `sheafCohomologyPullback_zeroMap`: a zero coefficient map gives zero; `sheafCohomologyPullback_identity`: identity data gives the identity; `sheafCohomologyPullback_sections`: degree zero is the given map of sections. |
| `rigidRingCatSheaf` | `rigidRingCatSheaf_point`: a point has sections `K`; `rigidRingCatSheaf_empty`: the empty space has zero sections; `rigidRingCatSheaf_affinoid`: an affinoid recovers its algebra. |
| `rigidAbelianRestriction` | `rigidAbelianRestriction_zero`: zero stays zero; `rigidAbelianRestriction_biprod`: finite direct sums are preserved; `rigidAbelianRestriction_point`: constant sheaves on a point retain their coefficient group. |
| `rigidConstantIso` | `rigidConstantIso_zero`: zero coefficients give zero; `rigidConstantIso_naturality`: coefficient maps commute with the specified comparison; `rigidConstantIso_point`: evaluation on the rigid point is bijective. |
| `rigidModuleSheafIso` | `rigidModuleSheafIso_zero`: zero modules give zero; `rigidModuleSheafIso_unit`: the unit section returns to one under the section comparison; `rigidModuleSheafIso_naturality`: module morphisms commute with the comparison. |
| `rigidCohomologyRestriction` | `rigidCohomologyRestriction_zero`: zero coefficients give zero; `rigidCohomologyRestriction_sections`: degree zero is the section comparison; `rigidCohomologyRestriction_affinoid`: positive-degree coherent classes on an affinoid vanish. |
| `rigidSchemeCohomologyComparison` | `rigidSchemeCohomologyComparison_zero`: zero coefficients give zero; `rigidSchemeCohomologyComparison_sections`: degree zero pulls back and then restricts sections; `rigidSchemeCohomologyComparison_affineHigher`: positive-degree classes from an affine scheme vanish. |

**Checks for the comparison maps on proper schemes.** On a strongly noetherian Tate affinoid with
noetherian coefficient ring, `cohomologyComparison_projectiveLine` uses the representing
projective bundle of a free module of rank two and the tensor square
of its universal line's dual: both algebraic and analytic first cohomology are the
coefficient ring, all other algebraic degrees vanish, and the canonical analytic
comparison is bijective. The analytic group is nontrivial whenever the coefficient
ring is nontrivial; `Cohomology_projectiveLine` specializes this to `K` and exhibits
its nonzero class.
`directImageComparison_quadraticBasis` uses `Spec(A[t]/(t²-d)) → Spec A` and sends
each actual section `a+bt` to its analytic pullback. The formula includes
characteristic two and nonreduced quadratic covers.

**Proper GAGA: comparison of coherent cohomology (Köpf).** (*proper-gaga*) Provides two
comparisons for a coherent `𝒪_X`-module `F`, under different properness hypotheses.
(a) Absolute: if `X` is proper over `Spec A`, the maps `Hⁱ(X, F) → Hⁱ(X^an, F^an)` of
*gaga-comparison-map* are `A`-linear isomorphisms of finite `A`-modules for every `i`.
(b) Relative: if `f : X → Y` is a proper morphism of schemes locally of finite type over
`Spec A`, then `f^an` is Kiehl-proper and `(Rⁱf_*F)^an → Rⁱf^an_*(F^an)` is an isomorphism for
every `i`; `Y` need not be proper over `Spec A`. Clause (a) is clause (b) for `Y = Spec A` under
`directImageComparison_global`; for a target `Y` that is not proper over `Spec A`, (b) does not
yield (a) for `X`. Prove the comparison on projective space, extend to projective schemes by coherent
resolutions, and pass to proper schemes by Chow's lemma and dévissage. Use the relative
argument on affine opens of `Y` to obtain (b) and its Kiehl-properness
(Conrad-RA Appendix A.1, Remark A.1.1 and (A.1.1), pp. 38–39; Example 3.2.6, p. 24,
relative GAGA over affinoids). The isomorphisms are the actual `cohomologyComparison`
and `directImageComparison`, fixed by their coefficient-unit equations.
*Needs:* *analytic-projective-space-cohomology*; *proper-cohomology-adic-completion*;
*analytification-coherent*; F0 *chow-lemma-devissage*; scheme proper coherent direct images;
Part II *analytification-separated-proper*, *rigid-analytification-comparison*.

**Checks.**

- `proper_gaga_test_identityAffineLine` (boundary) — for `X = Y = A¹_K`, `f = id_X` and `F = 𝒪`,
  `f` is proper and (b) applies: the relative maps are isomorphisms in every degree
  (`directImageComparison_identity`). `X` is not proper over `Spec K`, (a) does not apply, and the
  degree-zero absolute map `K[T] → 𝒪(A^{1,ad}_K)` is not surjective
  (`cohomologyComparison_test_affineLine`).
- `proper_gaga_test_relativeProjectiveLine` (relative over a nonproper base) — for the projection
  `f : P¹_{A¹_K} → A¹_K` and `F = 𝒪(−2)`, (b) identifies `(R¹f_*F)^an` and `R¹f^an_*(F^an)`, both
  free of rank one; the absolute `H¹` comparison is `K[T] → 𝒪(A^{1,ad}_K)` under these
  identifications, again not surjective, so (b) does not upgrade to (a) over `A¹_K`.
- `proper_gaga_test_projectiveLine` (absolute) — for `X = P¹_K` and `F = 𝒪(−2)`, (a) gives
  `H¹(X, F) ≅ H¹(X^an, F^an) ≅ K`, the computation of `cohomologyComparison_projectiveLine`.

**Proper GAGA: analytification is an equivalence on coherent sheaves.**
(*proper-gaga-coherent-equivalence*) Provides, for `X` proper over `Spec A`, that `F ↦ F^an` is an
exact equivalence of abelian tensor categories `Coh(X) → Coh(X^an)`, identified with coherent
pullback. Prove full faithfulness and essential surjectivity for this pullback functor
(Conrad-RA §3.2, Example 3.2.6, p. 24).
*Needs:* *proper-gaga*; *analytification-coherent*; projective resolutions and F0's
proper-support existence and Chow dévissage.

Checks: for `X = Spec A`, the equivalence is the finite-module affinoid equivalence;
the zero sheaf algebraizes to zero; on `P¹_K`, the analytic line bundle `O(1)`
algebraizes to its scheme counterpart and its endomorphisms are `K`.

Prove that finite analytic covers of proper varieties are algebraic (*gaga-finite-covers*): let
`K` be a complete nonarchimedean field, `X` a proper `K`-scheme and `g : Y → X^an` a finite
morphism of adic spaces; then there is a finite morphism of schemes `g₀ : Y₀ → X`, unique up to
unique isomorphism compatible with the chosen `X^an`-isomorphism `Y ≅ Y₀^an`;
`g₀ ↦ g₀^an` is an equivalence between
finite `X`-schemes and finite adic spaces over `X^an`, and if `X` is projective then so is `Y₀`
(Conrad-RA proof of Thm 3.1.5, p. 21, exactly this argument; Conrad-RA Thm 2.2.5(3), p. 10,
relative Spec commutes with analytification, the isomorphism (2.2.2)).
`AdicSpace.analytification_finiteCover_algebraization` gives essential surjectivity,
`AdicSpace.analytification_finiteCover_hom` gives full faithfulness on maps over
`X`, and `AdicSpace.analytification_finiteCover_unique` gives uniqueness with the
analytic identification fixed. This qualification is necessary for covers with
automorphisms, including a split double cover. **Check**
`analytification_finiteCover_unique_split`: the factor swap of `ℚ × ℚ` is a
nonidentity algebra automorphism fixing every diagonal scalar. The projectivity conclusion is
`AdicSpace.analytification_finiteCover_projective`: from a closed embedding of
`X` into a finite-dimensional projective space it produces such an embedding for
any finite `X`-scheme, commuting with the structural map. It uses Part II's
`projectiveSpace` and `projectiveSpace.toSpec` directly.
The analytification of the degree-2 map `E → P¹` from an elliptic curve is recovered from the finite analytic cover; for
`X = P¹_K`, every finite étale cover of `(P¹_K)^an` of degree `d` is the analytification of a
finite étale cover of `P¹_K`, hence trivial when `K` is algebraically closed (in every
characteristic, `P¹` over an algebraically closed field being simply connected).
*Needs:* *finite-morphism-coherent-algebra-equivalence*; *proper-gaga-coherent-equivalence*
(R3.7); *analytification-finite*,
*analytification-reflects-finite-closed-immersion* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R1);
*finite-morphism* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R0).

### R3.7a analytic algebraisation and Hasse loci for generalised elliptic curves

Let `k` be a complete
nonarchimedean field of characteristic zero with nontrivial absolute value and valuation ring
`R`. `RigidSpace.GeneralisedEllipticCurve S`, for a rigid space `S` over `k`, is a proper flat
morphism `E → S` whose fibre at each point `s` is a smooth geometrically connected curve of genus
one or becomes a standard polygon over a finite extension of `k(s)`, together with a section `e` of
the smooth locus `E^sm` and a morphism `+ : E^sm ×_S E → E` that restricts to a commutative group
law on `E^sm` with identity `e` and is an action of `E^sm` on `E` rotating the cycle of components
of every singular geometric fibre (Conrad-MR Def 2.1.1, pp. 3–4, and Def 2.1.8, p. 6).
`RigidSpace.GeneralisedEllipticCurve.analytification` sends a generalised elliptic curve over a
`k`-scheme `𝒮` locally of finite type to one over `𝒮^an` (Conrad-MR Example 2.1.10, p. 6), and
`RigidSpace.GeneralisedEllipticCurve.baseChange` pulls back along a morphism `T → S`. For cyclic
`L`, `RigidSpace.GeneralisedEllipticCurve.LevelStructure L E` is a section `P` of `E^sm` killed by
`N` whose divisor `∑_{j ∈ ℤ/N} [jP]` is a subgroup with `S`-ample inverse ideal sheaf, the analytic
form of the cyclic `LevelStructure` above; analytification carries algebraic level structures to
analytic ones (Conrad-MR §3.2, p. 19).

The following four inputs are targets of Part III. They use R3.6 and R3.7 through
Part II's rigid–adic comparison; none uses the classification or the Hasse-locus
application. RigidAnalyticGeometry on main supplies the classical carriers and
local rings (§§6.2, 8.1, 8.3), and assigns proper GAGA back to R3.7.

**Projective embeddings of analytic genus-one curves.**
(*rigid-genus-one-projective-embedding*) For a proper flat DR semistable genus-one
curve `f : C → S` over a rigid space over `k`, let `D` be a relative effective
Cartier divisor in `C^sm`, finite flat of locally constant degree `d ≥ 1` over
`S`, meeting every component of every geometric fibre. Prove
`RigidSpace.genusOne_projectiveEmbedding`: for `r ≥ 1`, `O(rD)` is relatively
ample, `R¹f_*O(rD) = 0`, and `f_*O(rD)` is locally free of rank `rd`, with its
natural base-change map an isomorphism for every rigid base change. For `r ≥ 3`
the evaluation map is surjective and gives a closed immersion
`C → P(f_*O(rD))`, compatible with base change. In particular `O(3D)` supplies
a projective embedding on any open where its direct image is free
(Conrad-MR Appendix B.1, Theorem B.1.2, p. 46, and Corollary 2.2.5, p. 14).
Also supply the preliminary projectivity statement without a chosen `D`:
a proper flat rigid curve has an admissible covering of its base on each member
of which it becomes projective after a quasi-compact étale surjection
(Conrad-MR Theorem 2.1.4, pp. 4–5). Use flat formal models with fibre dimension
at most one, lift a special-fibre polarization through the thickenings using
vanishing of `H²`, and take the generic fibre of the resulting formal projective
embedding. The polarization lifting and embedding statement includes reductions over
the possibly nonnoetherian valuation ring: descend the finitely presented scheme
data to noetherian bases before applying the algebraic cohomology and base-change
theorems. This statement precedes the torsion-divisor construction below.
*Needs:* R3.6 proper coherent direct images and affinoid cohomology;
R2 *formal-model-fibre-comparison*, *formal-rigid-properness-comparison*,
*raynaud-theorem* and *rigid-etale-descent-admissible-opens*;
F0 *formal-serre-vanishing* and *projective-bundles-ample-serre*;
StableReduction Layer 2's relative ampleness and curve cohomology.

**Checks.**

- `genusOneEmbedding_smooth` — for a smooth elliptic curve and `D = [e]`, `f_*O(3D)` has rank three and
  embeds the curve as a plane cubic.
- `genusOneEmbedding_polygon` — on the standard `n`-gon, one smooth point on each component gives degree
  `d = n` and an embedding into `P^{3n-1}`.
- `genusOneEmbedding_missingComponent` — on a 2-gon a divisor supported only on one component fails the hypothesis;
  its line bundle has degree zero on the other component and is not ample.

**Analytic Hilbert and Hom comparisons for projective families.**
(*rigid-projective-hilbert-hom*) Let `B` be a `k`-scheme locally of finite type,
`X → B` projective and flat, and `Y → B` projective and flat.
`RigidSpace.projectiveHilbertComparison` and `RigidSpace.projectiveHomComparison`
provide the following representing-object comparisons. The analytification
of the algebraic Hilbert scheme of `X/B`, with its universal family, represents
flat closed analytic subspaces of `X^an ×_{B^an} T` proper over a rigid test
space `T`; fix the Hilbert polynomial on each open-and-closed component.
Likewise the analytification of the algebraic Hom scheme represents
`T`-morphisms `X^an_T → Y^an_T`. Require the universal evaluation equations,
compatibility with rigid base change, and analytic field extension for
quasi-separated or pseudo-separated test spaces. For a flat projectively
embedded analytic family its fibre Hilbert polynomial is locally constant;
these comparisons therefore give local maps into algebraic Hilbert charts.
They also parameterise finite diagrams of projective flat families, including
finite flat divisors and their group operations and actions, by imposing the
diagram equations on products of Hom schemes
(Conrad-RA Theorem 4.1.3, Example 4.1.4, Corollaries 4.1.5–4.1.6, pp. 29–30;
Conrad-MR proof of Theorem 2.2.1, pp. 9–10).
Use the projective relative GAGA of R3.7 for the universal-quotient comparison;
the algebraic representing schemes are SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.14's.
*Needs:* SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.14, `hilbert_quot_schemes`;
*proper-gaga*, *proper-gaga-coherent-equivalence*, *analytification-coherent*;
*finite-morphism-coherent-algebra-equivalence*; R3.6 proper coherent cohomology; Part II R1's analytification and fibre products.

**Checks.**

- `projectiveHilbertComparison_point` — the analytification of `Hilb¹(P¹_k) = P¹_k` represents single points over
  arbitrary rigid test bases, rather than only over fields.
- `projectiveHilbertComparison_nilpotents` — over `k[ε]/(ε²)`, the divisor `t = ε` on `P¹` differs from `t = 0` and is
  retained by the Hilbert comparison although their reduced fibres agree.
- `projectiveHomComparison_identity` — the graph of the identity of a projective family corresponds to the identity
  section of its Hom space; its pullback remains that graph.

**Artinian GAGA and infinitesimal rigidity for genus-one curves.**
(*rigid-artinian-genus-one-gaga*) Let `A` be a finite local `k`-algebra, allowing
nilpotents. `RigidSpace.artinianGenusOneGAGA` provides the following algebraisation
and full-faithfulness statements. A proper flat analytic DR semistable genus-one curve over `Sp A`
is the analytification of a projective curve over `Spec A`; maps between such
proper curves and finite closed subspaces are algebraic, with their analytic
identifications fixed. This includes relative effective Cartier divisors,
sections, finite flat group structures on such divisors, and their actions on
the proper curve. For a generalised elliptic curve, algebraisation also
preserves the smooth-group law and its action on the whole curve, and any
cyclic level structure. Construct a polarization by smooth multisections
