meeting every component and apply the projective embedding above and coherent
GAGA to its closed ideal. Algebraize finite-divisor actions by proper GAGA;
recover the full smooth-group action by the translation uniqueness argument
of Conrad-MR Theorem 2.2.1 and Appendix B.2, Theorems B.2.5–B.2.6. The smooth
locus is not proper, so the last assertion uses this rigidity argument.
Include detection of equality of rigid morphisms by their values on all local
Artinian test spaces over the base (Conrad-MR Lemma 2.1.12, p. 7, proof by
Krull intersection). Thus uniqueness for structured families may be tested
on infinitesimal fibres, including their nilpotents
(Conrad-MR proofs of Theorems 2.1.11, pp. 7–8, 2.2.1, pp. 9–10, and 3.2.3, p. 20).
*Needs:* *rigid-genus-one-projective-embedding*; *proper-gaga*;
*proper-gaga-coherent-equivalence*; *gaga-finite-covers*;
RigidAnalyticGeometry §§3–4 and §8.1's local-ring comparisons;
R2.11's algebraic generalised elliptic curves and finite level data.

**Checks.**

- `artinianGenusOneGAGA_smooth` — a smooth elliptic curve over `k[ε]/(ε²)` retains its infinitesimal deformation
  and identity section under algebraisation.
- `artinianGenusOneGAGA_polygon` — the standard `n`-gon over this Artinian base retains both the smooth group
  `G_m × ℤ/n` and its rotation action on the whole polygon.
- `artinianGenusOneGAGA_nilpotents` — two maps `Sp(k[ε]/(ε²)) → A¹_k` with coordinates `0` and `ε` agree on the
  reduced point but differ as maps; testing only residue-field points cannot
  replace the Artinian tests.

**Local algebraicity with group, action and level data.**
(*rigid-generalised-elliptic-local-algebraicity*) For a generalised elliptic
curve `E → S` over `k`, `RigidSpace.GeneralisedEllipticCurve.localAlgebraicity`
produces an admissible open covering `{S_i}`, locally
finite type `k`-schemes `B_i`, algebraic generalised elliptic curves
`𝓔_i → B_i`, maps `a_i : S_i → B_i^an` and isomorphisms
`E|_{S_i} ≅ a_i^*(𝓔_i^an)` preserving the identity, smooth-group law and
whole-curve action. If `E` has a cyclic level structure `P`, require algebraic
level structures `𝓟_i` and the same isomorphisms to carry `P` to `a_i^*𝓟_i^an`
(Conrad-MR Corollary 2.2.5, pp. 14–15, and Lemma 3.2.2, pp. 19–20).
As inputs within this target, prove that the polygon size on the nonsmooth
locus is Zariski-locally constant. On an admissible open where every singular
geometric fibre has `n ≥ 1` sides, prove that the kernel
`D = E^sm[n] = E^sm ×_{[n], E^sm, e} S` is a finite locally free commutative
`S`-group of rank `n²`, and that `D ↪ E` is an `S`-ample relative effective
Cartier divisor. Formation of the kernel, its group law, its inclusion and
`O(D)` commute with every rigid base change `T → S`
(Conrad-MR Theorems 2.2.3–2.2.4 and Corollary 2.2.5, pp. 11–15).
On a constant `n`-gon, `[n](z,i) = (z^n,0)` on `G_m × ℤ/n`:
its rank as a finite flat map to the whole smooth locus is `n²` on the
identity target component and `0` on every other target component.
Use the preliminary étale-local projectivity, Hilbert/Hom comparisons and
Artinian rigidity to establish the assertions about `D → S`, then embed using
`f_*O(3D)`, which is locally free of rank `3n²` and commutes with base change.
The Hilbert/Hom charts algebraize the divisor, its finite group and action. Prove the
fibrewise extension criterion of Conrad-MR Theorem 2.2.1 and Appendix B.2,
Theorem B.2.6 for these data, yielding the algebraic generalised elliptic
structure with the original action. For level data, use the finite-type
scheme of level structures on the algebraic family and its analytic Hom
comparison. Compatibility with base change is through these isomorphisms;
the algebraic bases and families themselves are not claimed unique.
*Needs:* *rigid-genus-one-projective-embedding*; *rigid-projective-hilbert-hom*;
*rigid-artinian-genus-one-gaga*; *compactified-moduli-generalised-elliptic-curves*;
Part II R1's analytification and étale morphisms.

**Checks.**

- `localAlgebraicity_smooth` — a constant smooth elliptic curve is pulled back from its algebraic curve
  over `Spec k`, with its identity and addition preserved.
- `localAlgebraicity_polygon` — a constant `n`-gon is pulled back with its component rotations, rather than
  only its underlying nodal curve.
- On the standard `2`-gon over `ℚ₃`, `D = μ₂ × ℤ/2` has rank `4` over
  `Sp ℚ₃`, with points `(1,0)`, `(−1,0)`, `(1,1)`, `(−1,1)`. It has degree `2`
  on each polygon component, so `O(D)` is ample and `f_*O(3D)` has rank `12`.
- On that same `2`-gon, `[2] : G_m × ℤ/2 → G_m × ℤ/2` has fibre length `4`
  over `(1,0)` and empty fibre over `(1,1)`; its rank function on the target
  components is `(4,0)`. Extending `ℚ₃` to `ℚ₃(√3)` preserves both this rank
  function and the rank-`4` kernel over the base.
- `localAlgebraicity_mixedLevel` — for the standard `p`-gon over `ℚ_p(ζ_d)`, `d ≥ 5` prime to `p`, the cyclic
  level `(ζ_d, 1)` of level `dp` is preserved; no level prime to `p` meets all
  components. The mixed-level boundary persists under local algebraisation.

**Rigid-analytic generalised elliptic curves acquire level étale-locally and are classified by the
analytified moduli.** (*rigid-generalised-elliptic-level-classification*) For the curve and cyclic
level data above, prove:

(a) `RigidSpace.GeneralisedEllipticCurve.classify`: for cyclic `L`, with `M_k` the base change of
`moduli L` to `k`, every generalised elliptic curve `E → S` with level structure `P` has a unique
classifying morphism `c : S → M_k^an` and a unique isomorphism of generalised elliptic curves from
`E` to the pullback along `c` of the analytified universal curve, carrying `+`, `e` and `P` to the
pulled-back universal structures (`classify_iso`, `classify_unique`). For `g : T → S` the
composite `c ∘ g` classifies the pullback of `(E, P)` (`classify_baseChange`); for an analytic
extension `k'/k` and quasi-separated or pseudo-separated `S`, the extended pair is classified by
the extension of `c` (`classify_extendScalars`) (Conrad-MR Thm 3.2.3, p. 20, uniqueness through
artinian points and existence locally; Lemma 3.2.2, pp. 19–20, local algebraisation of curves with
level and the comparison of algebraic and analytic Hom functors).

(b) `RigidSpace.GeneralisedEllipticCurve.exists_levelCover`: for `E → S` and an integer `d ≥ 5`
there are an admissible affinoid covering `{S_i}` of `S`, integers `n_i ≥ 1`, étale coverings
`q_i : S'_i → S_i` (`RigidSpace.IsEtaleCovering`, *rigid-etale-descent-admissible-opens*) and
cyclic level structures of level `d·n_i` with factor `d` on `E ×_S S'_i`. Each `q_i` is the base
change, along a morphism `S_i → 𝒮_i^an`, of the analytification of an étale surjection of
`k`-schemes locally of finite type; consequently, for an analytic extension `k'/k` and
quasi-separated or pseudo-separated `S`, the extension of `q_i` is again surjective. Here `n_i` is
divisible by the number of sides of every polygon fibre over `S_i`; in characteristic zero the
scheme of such level structures on the algebraic family is étale over `𝒮_i` and surjective over
the open locus where every polygon size divides `n_i`, which contains the image of `S_i`
(Conrad-MR, proof of Thm 4.1.1, p. 26, through Cor 2.2.5, p. 14, local algebraicity with the group
law, Thms 2.2.3–2.2.4, pp. 11–12, local constancy of the polygon size, and the scheme of level
structures in the proof of Lemma 3.2.2, pp. 19–20; Conrad-RA Thm 4.2.2, p. 31, for the local
étale quasi-sections).

When `k` is analytic over `ℚ_p` and `p ∤ d`, `M_k` is the generic fibre of the proper flat finitely
presented `R`-model of *compactified-moduli-generalised-elliptic-curves*; the factor `n_i` carries
the polygon sizes, including multiples of `p`, so a level prime to `p` is never required.
*Needs:* *rigid-generalised-elliptic-local-algebraicity*; *rigid-artinian-genus-one-gaga*;
*compactified-moduli-generalised-elliptic-curves*; *rigid-etale-descent-admissible-opens*;

- `classify_universal` (degenerate) — the analytified universal pair over `M_k^an` is classified

- `exists_levelCover_pGon` (negative control) — for `S = Sp ℚ_p` and `E` the standard `p`-gon, no

**Conrad's Hasse-invariant loci `S^{>h}`, `S^{≥h}` of a generalized elliptic curve are admissible
opens.** (*hasse-loci-admissible-opens*) For a generalized elliptic curve `E → S` over a rigid space
`S` over `k` (`RigidSpace.GeneralisedEllipticCurve S` of *rigid-generalised-elliptic-level-classification*; `k` complete nonarchimedean of residue characteristic `p`, analytic over `ℚ_p`, `|p| =
p⁻¹`), the Hasse invariant of a fibre `E_s` is `h(E_s) = max(|a|, 1/p) ∈ [1/p, 1]` (Conrad-MR Definition B.3.3: `a` lifts the coefficient of `X^p` in `[p]*(X) mod p` on the formal group of a
semistable model, after finite extension). Prove that the loci `S^{>h}` (`h ∈ [1/p, 1) ∩ √|k^×|`)
and `S^{≥h}` (`h ∈ (1/p, 1] ∩ √|k^×|`) of points with `h(E_s) > h` (resp. `≥ h`) are admissible
opens; that their formation commutes with base change on `S` and, for quasi-separated or
pseudo-separated `S` (Conrad-MR 4.1.1(2)), with analytic extension of `k`; that `S^{≥h} → S` is
quasi-compact; and that `{S^{≥h}}_{h ∈ (h_0,1)}` is an admissible cover of `S^{>h_0}`.

The reduction to the universal case uses the classification above and the étale descent of
R2.11. Fix an integer `d ≥ 5` prime to `p`. By *rigid-generalised-elliptic-level-classification* (b) there are an admissible affinoid
covering `{S_i}` of `S` and étale coverings `q_i : S'_i → S_i` over which `E` acquires a cyclic
level structure of level `N_i = d·n_i` with factor `d`; by (a) of that target,
`E ×_S S'_i` is the pullback of the analytified universal curve along some
`c_i : S'_i → M_{i,k}^an`, with group, action and level preserved. Here `M_i` is the base change to
the valuation ring `R` of `k` of the moduli scheme of
*compactified-moduli-generalised-elliptic-curves* for this level, proper flat and finitely
presented over `R` because `p ∤ d`. The Hasse value of a fibre does not change under extension of
its residue field (Conrad-MR Appendix B.3, p. 49, the formal group commutes with analytic
extension), so `q_i⁻¹(S_i^{>h}) = c_i⁻¹((M_{i,k}^an)^{>h})`, and likewise for `≥ h`. These
are admissible opens by the universal case below and, being inverse images of subsets of `S_i`,
satisfy the hypothesis of *rigid-etale-descent-admissible-opens* (b). Hence `S_i^{>h}` and
`S_i^{≥h}` are admissible opens by (b), `S_i^{≥h} → S_i` is quasi-compact by (d), and the
`S_i^{≥h}` with `h ∈ (h_0, 1)` form an admissible covering of `S_i^{>h_0}` by (c), applied to the
restriction of `q_i` over `S_i^{>h_0}`, an étale covering by (a). Admissibility, quasi-compactness
over the base and admissible coverings are local on `S` for its admissible topology, which gives
the statements on `S`. For an analytic extension `k'/k` and quasi-separated or pseudo-separated
`S`, the two opens compared by `hasseLocus_extendScalars` have the same inverse image in the
extension of `S'_i`, by `classify_extendScalars` and the universal case, and that extension of
`q_i` is surjective. `M̂^rig ≅ M^an_k` and `Ê^rig ≅ E^an_k` use properness
(*good-reduction-locus*). Local description: on a formal affine `Spf A` of the formal
completion `M̂` of the proper moduli scheme `M` over which `e*Ω̂¹` is trivial, with `Γ_A ≅ Spf A[[X]]` the formal group and `a_{Γ_A}` the coefficient of `X^p` in `[p]*(X)`, `S^{>h} ∩ (Spf A)^rig = {|a_{Γ_A}| > h}` and `S^{≥h} ∩ (Spf A)^rig = {|a_{Γ_A}| ≥ h}`, independent of the coordinate `X`.
Thresholds `h ∈ √|k^×|` are read with the convention of *fractional-valuation-bound*. Through the
comparison `r` of AdicSpacesPartII layer R1 these are opens of the adic space, and for `h = |p|^ε` with `0 ≤ ε < 1`
(so `h ∈ (1/p, 1]`) `S^{≥h}` is the Hasse domain `X(ε)` of *hasse-domain* for `ω` the Hodge bundle
and `Ha` the Hasse invariant. Here `ω = e*Ω̂¹` and its cotangent frame `dX` is the pullback
along `e` of the differential of `X`. The coordinate functional `τ_X = (dX)∨ : ω → O`
satisfies `τ_X(dX) = 1`.
Modulo `p`, the comparison is `Ha = ā_{Γ_A}(dX)^{⊗(p−1)}` and
`τ_X^{⊗(p−1)}(Ha) = ā_{Γ_A}`, where `ā_{Γ_A}` is the reduction of `a_{Γ_A}`;
the integral coefficient is a local lift of this scalar coordinate. In
`AdicSpace`, define `hasseInvariantValue` (`h(E_s) = max(|a|, 1/p)` for a fibre `E_s`, via a
semistable model after finite extension), `hasseLocusGT` (`S^{>h}` for `h ∈ [1/p, 1) ∩ √|k^×|`) and
`hasseLocusGE` (`S^{≥h}` for `h ∈ (1/p, 1] ∩ √|k^×|`); prove `isOpen_hasseLocusGE` (`S^{>h}` and
`S^{≥h}` are admissible opens), `hasseLocusGE_quasiCompact` (`S^{≥h} → S` is quasi-compact),
`hasseLocus_baseChange` (formation commutes with base change `S' → S`), `hasseLocus_extendScalars`
(formation commutes with analytic extension of `k` for quasi-separated or pseudo-separated `S`),
`iUnion_hasseLocusGE` (`S^{>h_0} = ⋃_{h ∈ (h_0,1)} S^{≥h}`, an admissible cover),
`hasseLocusGE_local` (on `(Spf A)^rig` with formal group `Spf A[[X]]`: `S^{≥h} = {|a_{Γ_A}| ≥ h}`,
independent of `X`) and `hasseLocusGE_eq_hasseDomain` (for the universal curve and `h = |p|^ε`,
`S^{≥h}` is the Hasse domain `X(ε)`) (Conrad-MR §4.1, proof of Thm 4.1.1, p. 27, the local
description by a formal-group coefficient; Appendix B.3, Def. B.3.3, p. 50, the Hasse invariant
used; §4.1, Thm 4.1.1(1), p. 26, the cover statement). `{h(E) = 1}` is the locus of potentially
ordinary or potentially toric reduction, and `h(E) < 1` iff potentially supersingular reduction
(Conrad-MR after Remark B.3.4); `S^{≥h} → S` is quasi-compact for non-strict inequalities. *Needs:*
*berthelot-type-rig-functor-nonnoetherian-base*; *good-reduction-locus*; *rig-point*;
*fractional-valuation-bound*; *section-valuation-domain*; *hasse-domain*;
*hasse-domain-transition-maps*; *generic-fibre-fibre-products*; *rigid-analytic-space* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R1);
*rigid-adic-comparison-functor* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R1); *analytification-functor* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R1);
*compactified-moduli-generalised-elliptic-curves*; *rigid-generalised-elliptic-level-classification*;
*rigid-etale-descent-admissible-opens*.

**Checks.**

- `hasseLocus_test_ordinary` (computation) — for an elliptic curve `E` over `k` with good ordinary
  reduction, `h(E) = 1`, so the point lies in `S^{≥1}`; for good supersingular reduction `h(E) < 1`.
- `hasseLocus_test_floor` (degenerate) — `h(E_s) ≥ 1/p` always, so the locus `{h(E_s) ≥ 1/p}` is all
  of `S`; this is why `S^{≥h}` is only defined for `h > 1/p`.
- `hasseLocus_test_top` (degenerate) — `h(E_s) ≤ 1` always: `S^{≥1} = {h(E_s) = 1}` is the locus
  of potentially ordinary or potentially toric reduction, equal to the Hasse domain `X(0) = {|Ha|
  = 1}` for the universal curve, and `{h(E_s) > h}` is empty for every `h ≥ 1`, which is why
  `S^{>h}` is only defined for `h < 1`; the thresholds `h` are absolute values in `[1/p, 1]`, not
  exponents, and `h = |p|^ε` decreases as `ε` grows, so `S^{≥h} = X(ε)` shrinks as `h` grows.
  The object-level Check is `hasseLocusGT O p b hX ω hω Ha 0 = ⊥`, also labelled
  `hasseLocusGT_top`; the real maximum inequality is its numerical bound.
- `hasseLocus_test_withoutMax` (non-example) — for `h < 1/p` the locus `{|a_{Γ_A}| ≥ h}` can be
  strictly smaller than `S` (`a` can be divisible by `p`), whereas `{h(E_s) ≥ h} = S`: dropping the
  `max(·, 1/p)` in Definition B.3.3 gives a different, coordinate-dependent set.
- `hasseLocus_test_hasseDomain` (compatibility) — for `S = M^an` with the universal curve and `h = |p|^ε`, `0 ≤ ε < 1`: `S^{≥h} = X(ε)`, the Hasse domain of `M̂` with `ω` the Hodge bundle and `Ha`
  the Hasse invariant.
- Under an integral coordinate change `X′ = uX + O(X²)`, `u ∈ A^×`, the reductions satisfy
  `ā′ = ū^{1−p}ā`, while `dX′ = u dX` along the identity and `τ_{X′} = u⁻¹τ_X`.
  Thus `ā′(dX′)^{⊗(p−1)} = ā(dX)^{⊗(p−1)}` modulo `p`, and the scalar lifts give the same
  Hasse domains for `0 ≤ ε < 1`: their reductions differ by an integral unit and their lift
  errors by multiples of `p`, below the threshold `|p|^ε`.
- `hasseLocus_test_fractionalThreshold` (characterisation) — for `h = |c|^{1/n} ∈ √|k^×|` (`c ∈ k^×`), `S^{≥h} ∩ (Spf A)^rig = {|a_{Γ_A}^n| ≥ |c|}`, independent of the choice of `(c, n)`
  representing `h`.
- `hasseLocus_test_pGon` (negative control for the reduction) — for `S = Sp ℚ_p` and `E` the
  standard `p`-gon, the formal group is `𝔾̂_m`, `h(E) = 1` and `S^{≥1} = S`. The reduction reaches
  `E` only through a cyclic level `dp` with `d ≥ 5` prime to `p` (`exists_levelCover_pGon`); no
  level prime to `p` meets its `p` components.

### R3.8 finite locally free traces and pull–identify–trace

**Trace of endomorphisms of finite projective modules.** (*projective-module-trace*)
For a commutative ring `R`, specialize PivotalSpherical Layers 0–2 and 10’s
symmetric categorical trace to `(TauCeti.finiteProjectiveModules R).FullSubcategory`:
coevaluation, the endomorphism,
the symmetry and evaluation give an endomorphism of the unit `R`. Left and right
traces agree by the symmetric duality, and evaluation at `1` gives the scalar trace
(Stacks Tag 02DU, Exercise 111.22.6; Mathlib's evaluation and coevaluation for exact pairings).
*Needs:* PivotalSpherical Layers 0–2 and 10 (generic trace, coherence, cyclicity and
symmetric pivotal/spherical structures); the pinned symmetric category and finite-projective duals in
`TauCeti/Algebra/Category/ModuleCat/FiniteProjective/Monoidal.lean` and `Dualizable.lean`;
`CategoryTheory.ExactPairing.evaluation`, `CategoryTheory.ExactPairing.coevaluation`
(`Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Rigid/Basic.lean`). The scalar comparison is *projective-trace-realization*.

Checks: the unit's identity has trace `1`; the zero module has trace `0`;
on `R²`, the matrix with diagonal `a,d` has trace `a+d`.

**Cross-object cyclicity for finite projective modules.** (*projective-trace-cyclicity*)
For a commutative semiring `R`, finite projective `R`-semimodules `M`, `N` (additive
commutative monoids) and linear maps `f : M → N`, `g : N → M`,
prove `LinearMap.projectiveTrace_cyclic`: `tr_M(g ∘ f) = tr_N(f ∘ g)`.
The contraction formula proves this by finite sums of pure tensors; over rings it also
transports PivotalSpherical Layer 2’s categorical cyclicity through the scalar realization
(Stacks Tag 02DU, Exercise 111.22.6; Mathlib #44636's `_root_.LinearMap.trace_comp_comm'`;
the pinned `_root_.LinearMap.trace_comp_comm'` is its free-module specialization).
*Needs:* PivotalSpherical Layer 2; *projective-trace-realization*; finite-projective duality.
Lean: `LinearMap.projectiveTrace_cyclic`.

Checks: with `M = N = R`, this is `ab = ba`; with `M = 0`, both traces vanish;
with `M = R`, `N = R²`, `f(x) = (ax,bx)` and `g(y,z) = cy+dz`, both traces are `ca+db`.

**Finite-projective trace realization and scalar extension.** (*projective-trace-realization*)
Let `R` be a commutative semiring and `M` a finitely generated projective `R`-semimodule
(an additive commutative monoid). For the categorical comparison assume that `R` is a
commutative ring and `M` an additive commutative group; use
`(TauCeti.finiteProjectiveModules R).FullSubcategory` and its supplied
`TauCeti.finiteProjectiveModulesSymmetricCategory` structure, with
`ModuleCat.hasLeftDualOfFiniteProjective` and `ModuleCat.hasRightDualOfFiniteProjective`.
The dual is `M^∨ = Hom_R(M,R)`. Identify its canonical double dual with
PivotalSpherical’s symmetric pivotal structure and use its equality of left and right
traces; identify `End_R(R)` with `R` by evaluation at `1`.
Prove that the scalar categorical trace is the contraction below. The trace
`tr_M : End_R(M) → R` is the `R`-linear map `tr_M = contractLeft ∘ (dualTensorHomEquiv R M M)⁻¹`,
where `dualTensorHomEquiv : M^∨ ⊗_R M ≅ End_R(M)` (Mathlib, for `M` finite projective) and
`contractLeft(φ ⊗ m) = φ(m)`. This is the trace used throughout this layer; Mathlib's
`LinearMap.trace R M` agrees with it when `M` is free but is defined to be `0` when `M` has no
finite basis, so it is not the trace of a finite projective non-free module. The same
construction `contractLeft ∘ dualTensorHomEquiv⁻¹` in the almost category is PerfectoidSpaces
layer P0 (P0.12), the almost-ring version of this target. In `LinearMap`,
retain `projectiveTrace` as compatibility with the pin for the standard `LinearMap.trace`
of Mathlib [#44636](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/44636), using the same
contraction definition over commutative semirings. Prove that
`projectiveTrace (dualTensorHom φ m) = φ m`, equivalently `projectiveTrace ∘ dualTensorHom =
contractLeft`; `projectiveTrace_eq_trace` (for `M` free finite,
`projectiveTrace R M = LinearMap.trace R M`; in particular it equals `Matrix.trace` of the matrix
in any basis); `projectiveTrace_baseChange` (for `R → R'`,
`tr_{R' ⊗ M}(f.baseChange R') = algebraMap R R' (tr_M f)` for a commutative `R`-semialgebra `R'`); that
`tr_{M × N}(f.prodMap g) = tr_M f + tr_N g`; that `tr_N(e ∘ f ∘ e⁻¹) = tr_M f` for a linear
equivalence `e : M ≃ N`. Over commutative rings prove that the image of `tr_M(id)` in `R_𝔭`
is `Module.rankAtStalk M 𝔭` for every prime `𝔭`; and that `tr_M f` is nilpotent when `f` is
nilpotent (Stacks Tag 02DU, Exercise 111.22.6, the trace of an endomorphism of a finite locally
free, equivalently finite projective, module; Stacks Tag 0BVH, §49.3, the sheaf version for

`LinearMap.projectiveTrace_baseChange`, `LinearMap.projectiveTrace_eq_categoricalTrace` and

and Checks are specified in this README only.

**Checks.**

- `LinearMap.projectiveTrace_nonfree` (non-example) — for `R = ℚ × ℚ` and `M = ℚ × 0`,
  `projectiveTrace R M id = (1, 0)`, while Mathlib's `LinearMap.trace R M id = 0` because `M` has
  no finite basis; the Mathlib trace is not the trace of a finite projective module.
- (computation) — for `M = R²` and `f` with matrix
  `[[a, b], [c, d]]`, `projectiveTrace R M f = a + d`.
- (degenerate) — for `M = 0` the trace is `0`; for
  `M = R`, `projectiveTrace R R f = f 1`.
- (compatibility) — if `M` is free and finite,
  `projectiveTrace R M = LinearMap.trace R M`.

**The trace of a finite locally free algebra.** (*finite-locally-free-algebra-trace*) Let `R` be a
commutative ring and `B` a commutative `R`-algebra which is finitely generated and projective as
an `R`-module (a finite locally free `R`-algebra). The trace `Tr_{B/R} : B → R` is `b ↦ tr_B(m_b)`,
the scalar realization (*projective-trace-realization*) of the symmetric categorical trace of
multiplication by `b`. It is
`R`-linear, `Tr_{B/R}(1)` is the locally constant degree function (its image in `R_𝔭` is
`rank_𝔭 B`), and the trace form `(x, y) ↦ Tr_{B/R}(xy)` is symmetric; it carries no normalising
factor: for `B = R × R` it is the dot product, `Tr((x₁, x₂)(y₁, y₂)) = x₁y₁ + x₂y₂`, and for
`B = 0` (rank `0`) the trace and the form are `0`. It is not defined as a sum
over geometric points: for `B = k[x]/(x²)`, `Tr(1) = 2` although `Spec B` has one geometric point.
In `Algebra`, define `projectiveTrace` as `Tr_{B/R} : B →ₗ[R] R` and `projectiveTraceForm` as the
bilinear form `(x, y) ↦ Tr(xy)`, the compatibility spellings for Mathlib #44636's
`Algebra.trace` and `Algebra.traceForm` on finite projective algebras. Use that standard API
for the Tau Ceti construction. Prove that this form is symmetric; prove that
`projectiveTrace R B b = LinearMap.projectiveTrace R B (lmul R B b)` (the definition); that for
`B` free and finite `projectiveTrace R B = Algebra.trace R B`; that `Tr(algebraMap r) = r · Tr(1)`
and the image of `Tr(1)` in `R_𝔭` is `rank_𝔭 B`; base change along `R → R'` (stated as
*algebra-trace-base-change* below); `projectiveTrace_trans` (`Tr_{C/R} = Tr_{B/R} ∘ Tr_{C/B}` in
towers; stated as *algebra-trace-transitivity* below); that
`Tr_{B × C/R}(b, c) = Tr_{B/R} b + Tr_{C/R} c`; that for `B = Rⁿ`, `Tr(b) = Σ bᵢ`; and that for a
multiplicative set `S ⊆ R`, `Tr_{S⁻¹B/S⁻¹R}` of the image of `b` is the image of `Tr_{B/R}(b)`
(Stacks Tag 02DV, Exercise
111.22.7, the trace of a finite locally free algebra; KL15 §1.2, p. 13, where Kedlaya–Liu use
`Trace_{S/R}` for finite projective algebras; Stacks Tag 0BVH, §49.3, `Tr(1)` is the locally
constant degree). The free clauses are Mathlib's: `Algebra.trace`, `_root_.Algebra.trace_prod` (which needs
`Module.Free` of both factors, so it gives the product formula only for free `B`, `C`) and
`_root_.Algebra.trace_localization`; the projective case is new. The almost version of this trace and its
trace form is PerfectoidSpaces layer P0 (P0.12), the almost-ring version of this target.
*Needs:* *projective-trace-realization*;
Mathlib `Algebra.trace`, `Algebra.traceForm`,
`Module.Projective`, `_root_.Algebra.trace_prod`, `_root_.Algebra.trace_localization`. Lean:
`Algebra.projectiveTrace` and `Algebra.projectiveTraceForm`; the other clauses and Checks are
specified in this README only.

**Checks.**

- (non-example, ramified) — for `B = k[x]/(x²)` over a field `k`,
  `projectiveTrace k B 1 = 2` while `Spec B` has a single geometric point; a definition as a sum
  over geometric points gives `1`.
- (non-example, nonconstant rank) — for `R = ℚ × ℚ` and
  `B = ℚ × (ℚ × ℚ)` with `R → B`, `(a, b) ↦ (a, (b, b))`, `B` is projective of rank `(1, 2)` and
  `projectiveTrace R B 1 = (1, 2)`, whereas Mathlib's `Algebra.trace R B 1 = 0`.
- (computation, quadratic) — for `B = R[x]/(x² − d)` (free on `1`,
  `x`), `Tr(a + bx) = 2a` and `Tr(x²) = 2d`.
- (degenerate) — `projectiveTrace R R = id` and
  `projectiveTrace R 0 = 0`.
- (compatibility) — for `B` free and finite over `R`,
  `projectiveTrace R B = Algebra.trace R B`.

**Checks for `Algebra.projectiveTraceForm`.**

- (self) — on `R` over itself the form is multiplication,
  `projectiveTraceForm R R = LinearMap.mul R R`.
- (product) — on `R × R`, the form is
  `x₁y₁ + x₂y₂`, with no division by `2`.
- (zero algebra) — on the zero algebra the form is zero and perfect;
  the zero algebra is étale of rank zero.
- (characteristic two) — over a field of characteristic `2`, the form on
  `k[x]/(x² − 1)` is not perfect (it vanishes) and the algebra is not étale.

Prove the base change of the finite projective trace (*algebra-trace-base-change*): let `R → R'`
be a homomorphism of commutative rings, `M` a finite projective `R`-module, `f ∈ End_R(M)`, and
`B` a finite projective `R`-algebra; then `tr_{R' ⊗ M}(id ⊗ f)` is the image of `tr_M(f)` in
`R'`, and `Tr_{R' ⊗_R B / R'}(1 ⊗ b)` is the image of `Tr_{B/R}(b)` for all `b ∈ B` (Stacks Tag
02DV, Exercise 111.22.7, base change for finite locally free algebras; Stacks Tag 0BJF, proof of
Lem. 49.3.1, base change of the trace used to reduce to fibres). For `R = ℤ → R' = 𝔽_p` and
`B = ℤ[i]`, `Tr_{𝔽_p[i]/𝔽_p}(1) = 2 mod p`; for `R → R_𝔭` the lemma gives the localisation API
of the algebra trace. For `M` free and finite the module statement is Mathlib's
`_root_.LinearMap.trace_baseChange`; the projective case is new. *Needs:* *projective-trace-realization*;
*finite-locally-free-algebra-trace*; Mathlib `dualTensorHomEquiv`, `contractLeft`,
`_root_.LinearMap.trace_baseChange`. Lean: the module statement is
`LinearMap.projectiveTrace_baseChange`; the algebra statement is `Algebra.projectiveTrace_baseChange`.

Prove the transitivity of the finite projective trace in towers (*algebra-trace-transitivity*):
let `R → B → C` be homomorphisms of commutative rings with `B` finite projective over `R` and `C`
finite projective over `B`; then `C` is finite projective over `R` and
`Tr_{C/R} = Tr_{B/R} ∘ Tr_{C/B}`. More generally, for a finite projective `B`-module `M` and
`φ ∈ End_B(M)`, `M` is finite projective over `R` and `tr_{M/R}(φ) = Tr_{B/R}(tr_{M/B}(φ))`
(*projective-trace-cyclicity* supplies the scalar cyclicity law used in the tower argument).
For `ℚ ⊆ ℚ(i) ⊆ ℚ(i, √2)`: `Tr_{ℚ(i,√2)/ℚ}(1) = 4 = Tr_{ℚ(i)/ℚ}(2)`; for `R = k`,
`B = k × k`, `C = k × k[x]/(x²)`: `Tr_{C/k}(1) = 3 = Tr_{B/k}((1, 2))`. For `B` and `C` free the
statement is Mathlib's `_root_.Algebra.trace_trace` and `_root_.Algebra.trace_comp_trace`; the projective case
is new. *Needs:* *projective-trace-realization*; *projective-trace-cyclicity*; *finite-locally-free-algebra-trace*; Mathlib
`_root_.Algebra.trace_trace`, `_root_.Algebra.trace_comp_trace`, `Module.Projective`. Lean:
`Algebra.projectiveTrace_trans` (the algebra tower); the module form is specified in this README
only.

Prove that a finite locally free algebra is étale iff its trace pairing is perfect
(*etale-iff-trace-pairing-perfect*): let `R` be a commutative ring and `S` a finite projective
`R`-algebra; then `S` is étale over `R` (Mathlib `Algebra.Etale`) if and only if the `R`-linear
map `S → Hom_R(S, R)`, `x ↦ (y ↦ Tr_{S/R}(xy))`, is an isomorphism (KL15 §1.2, p. 13, the
criterion; Stacks Tag 0BJF, Lem. 49.3.1, the scheme form; Stacks Tag 0BIL, Lem. 9.20.7, the field
case). For `ℚ(√2)/ℚ` the trace form has Gram matrix `diag(2, 4)` in the basis `1, √2`, perfect;
for `k[x]/(x²)`, `x` is in the kernel of the pairing and the algebra is not étale; for `S = R`
the pairing is `(x, y) ↦ xy`, perfect, and for `S = 0` (étale, `Spec 0 = ∅`) it is the bijection
`0 → 0`. The field case is Mathlib's `_root_.Algebra.traceForm_nondegenerate` and
`traceForm_nondegenerate_tfae`; the statement over an arbitrary commutative ring is new, and its
almost version is PerfectoidSpaces layer P0 (P0.15).
*Needs:*
*finite-locally-free-algebra-trace*; *algebra-trace-base-change*; Mathlib `Algebra.Etale`,
`Algebra.Etale.iff_exists_algEquiv_prod`, `traceForm_nondegenerate`,
`traceForm_nondegenerate_tfae`. Lean: `Algebra.etale_iff_projectiveTraceForm_bijective` (`S` is
étale iff `projectiveTraceForm`, read as the map `S → Hom_R(S, R)`, is bijective); the
characteristic-two Check of `Algebra.projectiveTraceForm` is specified in this README only.

Prove that the trace of a finite étale algebra over a field is the sum over geometric points
(*trace-geometric-point-formula*): let `k` be a field, `Ω` an algebraically closed field
containing `k` and `B` a finite étale `k`-algebra; then `Hom_k(B, Ω)` has exactly `dim_k B`
elements and `Tr_{B/k}(b) = Σ_{σ ∈ Hom_k(B, Ω)} σ(b)` in `Ω` for every `b ∈ B`. The formula fails
without étaleness: for `B = k[x]/(x²)`, `Hom_k(B, Ω)` has one element while `Tr(1) = 2`, and
for `k = 𝔽_p(t)`, `B = k[x]/(xᵖ − t)` (inseparable), `Hom_k(B, Ω)` has one element while
`Tr(1) = p = 0 ≠ 1` (Stacks
Tag 03SH, §59.66, étale-locally the trace of a finite étale map is the sum over the sheets; Stacks
Tag 0BIL, Lem. 9.20.7, separability is exactly what makes the trace nondegenerate and the
embedding count equal the degree). For `B = ℚ × ℚ(i)` and `Ω = ℚ̄`:
`Tr(1, i) = 1 + (i + (−i)) = 1`. *Needs:* *finite-locally-free-algebra-trace*; Mathlib
`Algebra.Etale.iff_exists_algEquiv_prod`, `_root_.Algebra.trace_prod`, `trace_eq_sum_embeddings`.
Lean: `Algebra.projectiveTrace_eq_sum_geometricPoints`.

**The trace of a finite locally free morphism of schemes.** (*scheme-trace-finite-locally-free*)
Let `π : X → Y` be a finite locally free morphism of schemes (Mathlib
`AlgebraicGeometry.IsFinite`, `Flat` and `LocallyOfFinitePresentation`). The trace
`Tr_π : π_*𝒪_X → 𝒪_Y` is the `𝒪_Y`-linear map which on every affine open `V = Spec A ⊆ Y` with
`π⁻¹(V) = Spec B` is `Tr_{B/A}` (*finite-locally-free-algebra-trace*); these glue because the
affine formula is compatible with localisation (by *algebra-trace-base-change*). `Tr_π ∘ π^♯` is
multiplication by the locally constant degree of `π`, the locally constant rank of `π_*𝒪_X`. The
degree is Mathlib's
`Scheme.Hom.finrank` (`AlgebraicGeometry/Morphisms/FlatRank`; Tau Ceti adds only
`finrank_eq_of_nonempty_iso_over`). Its comparison with the proper duality counit of
SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 2 (§2.19, §2.21, `trace`) is the composite
`π_*𝒪_X → π_*π^!𝒪_Y → 𝒪_Y`. The first map is the trace pairing and the second the
counit. Affinely, they are `b ↦ (c ↦ Tr_{B/A}(bc))` and `λ ↦ λ(1)` on `Hom_A(B,A)`.
Construct this pairing adapter and prove that it is invertible exactly when `π` is étale
(*etale-iff-trace-pairing-perfect*);
it is stated separately because its affine description through `Algebra.projectiveTrace` is what
the analytic trace *analytic-trace-finite-locally-free* is compared with. In
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom`, define `finiteTrace` as
`Tr_π : π_*𝒪_X ⟶ 𝒪_Y` for finite locally free `π` and `traceForm` as the pairing
`π_*𝒪_X ⊗ π_*𝒪_X → 𝒪_Y`, `(f, g) ↦ Tr(fg)`; prove `finiteTrace_app_affine` (on affine `V` with
`π⁻¹V = Spec B`, `Tr = Algebra.projectiveTrace A B`), `finiteTrace_comp_unit`
(`Tr_π ∘ π^♯ = deg π · id`), `finiteTrace_baseChange` (for a pullback square, the base-change
isomorphism carries `g*Tr_π` to `Tr_{π'}`), `finiteTrace_comp` (`Tr_{π ∘ π'} = Tr_π ∘ π_*(Tr_{π'})`),
`finiteTrace_coprod` (for `X = ⊔_{i=1}^d Y`, `Tr` is the sum map) and
`etale_iff_traceForm_perfect` (`π` is étale iff the trace pairing is perfect, the discriminant
locus being empty; by *etale-iff-trace-pairing-perfect*) (Stacks Tag 0BVH, §49.3, the
scheme-theoretic trace of a finite locally free morphism and its local description). *Needs:*
*finite-locally-free-algebra-trace*; *algebra-trace-base-change*; *algebra-trace-transitivity*;
SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 2 (§2.19, §2.21, `trace`); Mathlib `AlgebraicGeometry.IsFinite`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Flat`, `AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFinitePresentation`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules`, `Scheme.Hom.finrank`.

AutomorphicBundles B5.1 is a consumer of this scheme trace and its unit, composition and
arbitrary-base-change laws. Its scheme-level `finiteLocallyFreeTrace` denotes this
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.finiteTrace`, by import or transparent alias; its coefficient
projection-formula and stack-descent adapters belong to AutomorphicBundles.

The declaration `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.finiteTrace_baseChange` gives the
commuting square on affine opens `W ⊆ g⁻¹(V)` in a cartesian square: the trace of
the pullback of a section is the pullback of its trace. The finite affine
base-change identification sends `b ⊗ c` to `g′*(b)·c`; linearity therefore gives
the entire trace square. No flatness of `g` is required.

**Checks.**

- (duality comparison) — Over `𝔽₂`, let `B = 𝔽₂[ε]/(ε²)`.
The algebra trace and the trace-pairing map are zero. The counit
`Hom(B,𝔽₂) → 𝔽₂` is nonzero: the coefficient functional with `λ(1) = 1`,
`λ(ε) = 0` maps to `1`. Their composite is the zero algebra trace.

- `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.finiteTrace_test_double_cover` (computation) — for
  `π : Spec k[t][x]/(x² − t) → Spec k[t]`, `Γ(Tr_π)(a + bx) = 2a`.
- `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.finiteTrace_test_ramified` (non-example) — for the same `π` and
  `char k ≠ 2`, the fibre over `t = 0` has one geometric point but `Tr_π(1)(0) = 2`: the trace is
  not the sum over geometric points of fibres.
- `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.finiteTrace_test_id` (degenerate) — `Tr_{id_Y} = id` and `Tr` for
  the empty scheme over `Y` is `0`.
- `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.finiteTrace_test_affine_free` (compatibility) — for `Y = Spec A`
  and `X = Spec B` with `B` free over `A`, `Γ(Y, Tr_π) = Algebra.trace A B`.

**Checks for the scheme trace pairing.**

- `Scheme.Hom.traceForm.test_id`: for the identity morphism, the pairing on `V` is `xy`.
- `Scheme.Hom.traceForm.test_empty`: for the empty finite cover, the pairing is zero.
- `Scheme.Hom.traceForm.test_affine`: on an affine open, it is the projective algebra trace
  pairing. This identifies both scalar actions and fixes the normalisation.

**Finite locally free morphisms of adic spaces.** (*finite-locally-free-morphism*) A morphism of
adic spaces `f : Y → X` is finite locally free if it is finite (*finite-morphism*, AdicSpacesPartII layer R0) and
`f_*𝒪_Y` is a vector bundle on `X` (*locally-free-sheaf*). Its degree is the rank of `f_*𝒪_Y`, a
locally constant function on `X`. Over an open affinoid `Spa(A, A⁺) ⊆ X` with `A` a complete Tate
ring such that `f⁻¹(Spa A)` is affinoid — such affinoids cover `X` by the definition of
finiteness, and every open affinoid with `A` strongly noetherian qualifies (*finite-morphism*;
Zavyalov-Q Appendix B.2, Thm B.2.18, p. 47) — `f⁻¹(Spa A) = Spa(B, B⁺)` with `B` a finite
projective `A`-algebra
(*sheafy-tate-acyclicity-and-kiehl-gluing*) and `B⁺` the integral closure of `A⁺`, and for every
rational `V ⊆ Spa(A, A⁺)`, `f⁻¹(V) = Spa(B ⊗_A 𝒪_X(V))` with the uncompleted tensor product
(*finite-algebra-tensor-complete* (iii), AdicSpacesPartII layer R0). It is not asserted that `f⁻¹` of every sheafy
Tate affinoid is affinoid (Zavyalov-Q Appendix B.2, Rem. B.2.19; KL15 Rem. 8.2.18). In `AdicSpace`,
define
`IsFiniteLocallyFree` as the predicate (finite with `f_*𝒪_Y` a vector bundle) and
`finiteDegree` as the locally constant degree `X → ℕ`; prove
`IsFiniteLocallyFree.comp` (composites of finite locally free morphisms are finite locally free,
if the second map has constant degree `e` above the first map's fibre, the composite has
degree `e` times the first degree; in general the geometric fibre ranks are summed, weighted
by the lengths of the first fibre. The identity has degree `1`), `IsFiniteLocallyFree.baseChange` (stable
under base change along `X′ → X` whenever the fibre product exists, that is, `X′` is covered by
open affinoids with complete stably sheafy rings, for instance `X′` locally noetherian, as
*fibre-products-existence* (a) requires, `f` being finite and hence locally of finite type; fibre
products of adic spaces do not exist in general; the degree is preserved),
`finiteEtale_isFiniteLocallyFree` (over a target covered by strongly noetherian
Tate charts, finite étale morphisms are finite locally free, since finite étale
algebras are finite projective; such a target and its finite source are locally noetherian,
hence locally Huber-standard, where Part II states étaleness), `isFiniteLocallyFree_affinoid_iff` (over an open
affinoid `Spa(A, A⁺) ⊆ X` with `A` a complete Tate ring and `f⁻¹(Spa A)` affinoid — every such
affinoid when `A` is strongly noetherian — `f` is finite locally free over `Spa(A, A⁺)` iff
`𝒪(f⁻¹ Spa A)` is a finite projective `A`-algebra), `IsFiniteLocallyFree.analytification` (`π`
finite locally free implies `π^an` finite locally free of the same degree) and
Part II's `IsFinite.isProper` (apply it to the finiteness component when the target
is analytic and has stably sheafy charts)
(BHW §10.1, Def. 10.2, p. 1789, where the consumers use finite locally free maps of adic spaces
and their traces; KL15 §2.4, Rem. 2.4.2, p. 38, finite étale algebras over affinoids as the main
examples, finite projective by KL15 §1.2). *Needs:* *finite-morphism*,
*differentials-unramified-smooth-etale*, *fibre-products-existence*,
*finite-algebra-tensor-complete* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R0); *locally-free-sheaf*;
*sheafy-tate-acyclicity-and-kiehl-gluing*; *analytification-finite* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R1).

`AdicSpace.finiteDegree f hf y` is the rank of the stalk at `y` of `f_* O_X`.
`finiteDegree_basis` computes it from a finite basis and `finiteDegree_locallyConstant`
states local constancy. `isFiniteLocallyFree_affinoid_iff` identifies finite local
freeness with finite projectivity of the coordinate algebra on strongly noetherian
Tate affinoids.

**Checks.** `finiteDegree_identity` gives one, `finiteDegree_empty` gives zero,
and `finiteDegree_double` gives two for a direct image isomorphic to `O²`.


**Checks.**

- (algebraic negative control, composite rank) — in the tower
  `ℚ → ℚ × ℚ → ℚ × (ℚ × ℚ)`, the second degree is `(1,2)` and the composite degree is
  `3 = 1 + 2`. The example supplies finite projectivity for the second scalar action,
  computes `Tr_{C/B}(1) = (1,2)` and `Tr_{B/ℚ}(Tr_{C/B}(1)) = Tr_{C/ℚ}(1) = 3`.
  There is no constant degree of the second map to multiply by `2`.
- (algebraic negative control, the power map for `n = 0`) — the polynomial-ring map
  `k[w] → k[z]`, `w ↦ 1`, over any field `k` is not finite. State this as
  `¬ (Polynomial.eval₂RingHom (algebraMap k (Polynomial k)) (1 : Polynomial k)).Finite`:
  `RingHom.Finite` uses the scalar action induced by this homomorphism
  (`Mathlib/RingTheory/Finiteness/Defs.lean`). That action factors through `k`, while
  `1,z,z²,…` are linearly independent over `k`.
- `IsFiniteLocallyFree_power_map` (computation) — `f : Spa(K⟨z⟩) → Spa(K⟨w⟩)`,
  for `n ≥ 1`, `w ↦ zⁿ` is finite locally free of degree `n` (basis `1, z, …, z^{n−1}`); it is étale exactly
  away from `w = 0` when `n ≥ 2` and `char K ∤ n` (always when `char K = 0`, whatever the residue
  characteristic `p`), the discriminant being `± nⁿ w^{n−1}`, and nowhere étale when
  `char K ∣ n`. For `n = 1` it is the identity and is étale everywhere. For `n = 0`
  the map `w ↦ 1` is not finite: its fibre at `w = 1` is the whole disc.
- `IsFiniteLocallyFree_closed_point` (non-example) — the closed immersion
  `Spa(K) → Spa(K⟨w⟩)` of the origin is finite but `f_*𝒪 = (K⟨w⟩/(w))~` is not locally free.
  Evaluation at zero defines the morphism in the example
  (Conrad-RA, Corollary 2.2.8, p. 12; KL15, Theorem 2.7.7, p. 58).
- `IsFiniteLocallyFree_id_empty` (degenerate) — `id_X` is finite locally free of
  degree `1`; `∅ → X` is finite locally free of degree `0`.
- `IsFiniteLocallyFree_analytification` (compatibility) — for a finite locally
  free morphism `π` of `K`-schemes locally of finite type, `π^an` is finite locally free of the
  same degree.

Prove the projection formula for finite morphisms (*finite-locally-free-projection-formula*): let
`f : Y → X` be a finite locally free morphism of adic spaces and `E` a vector bundle on `X` (or
`X` locally noetherian analytic, `f` finite and `E` coherent); then the natural map
`f_*𝒪_Y ⊗_{𝒪_X} E → f_*(f*E)` is an isomorphism; in particular `f_*f*E` is a vector bundle (resp.
coherent). `AdicSpace.finite_projection_formula` gives the vector-bundle
comparison, and `AdicSpace.finite_projection_formula_vectorBundle` states finite
local freeness of its target when `f` is finite locally free.
`AdicSpace.finite_projection_formula_coherent` supplies the coherent comparison
and coherence of the target on spaces covered by strongly noetherian Tate charts.
The coherent case follows from the affinoid module equivalence and the finite
algebra description (Huber96 §1.4, (1.4.2)–(1.4.4), p. 61);
the trace application is BHW §10.1, Def. 10.2, p. 1789, where the `T_a`-operator applies `Tr_{π₁}` to sections
of `π₁*ω`, which requires `π₁_*π₁^*ω = π₁_*𝒪 ⊗ ω`. For `f : z ↦ z²` on the disc and `E = 𝒪`,
`f_*f*𝒪 = f_*𝒪 = 𝒪 ⊕ 𝒪·z`. *Needs:* *finite-locally-free-morphism*;
*coherent-sheaf-operations*; *finite-projective-module-acyclicity*; *locally-free-sheaf*.

**The trace of a finite locally free morphism of adic spaces.**
(*analytic-trace-finite-locally-free*) Let `f : Y → X` be a finite locally free morphism of adic
spaces (*finite-locally-free-morphism*). The trace `Tr_f : f_*𝒪_Y → 𝒪_X` is the composite of the
multiplication map `f_*𝒪_Y → ℋom_{𝒪_X}(f_*𝒪_Y, f_*𝒪_Y)` with the trace `ℋom(E, E) → 𝒪_X` of the
vector bundle `E = f_*𝒪_Y`, defined on every open `U` over which `E` is free as the matrix trace
(independent of the basis) and glued. On a sheafy Tate affinoid `U = Spa(A, A⁺)` it is `Tr_{B/A}`
for `B = 𝒪_Y(f⁻¹U)` (*finite-locally-free-algebra-trace*). `Tr_f` is `𝒪_X`-linear, `Tr_f ∘ f^♯`
is multiplication by the degree, the locally constant rank of `f_*𝒪_Y`, and `Tr_f` is not a sum
over geometric points of fibres unless
`f` is étale. In `AdicSpace`, define `finiteTrace` as `Tr_f : f_*𝒪_Y ⟶ 𝒪_X`,
`VectorBundle.trace` as the trace `ℋom(E, E) ⟶ 𝒪_X` of a vector bundle `E`, and
`finiteTraceForm` as the pairing `f_*𝒪_Y ⊗ f_*𝒪_Y → 𝒪_X`, `(s, t) ↦ Tr_f(st)`; prove
`finiteTrace_app_affinoid` (on a sheafy Tate affinoid `U`,
`(Tr_f)(U) = Algebra.projectiveTrace 𝒪(U) 𝒪(f⁻¹U)`), `finiteTrace_comp_unit`
(`Tr_f ∘ f^♯ = degree · id`), `finiteTrace_linear` (`Tr_f(f^♯(a) · s) = a · Tr_f(s)`, a simp
lemma), `finiteTrace_baseChange` (base change; stated as *trace-base-change-composition* below),
`finiteTrace_comp` (`Tr_{g∘f} = Tr_g ∘ g_*(Tr_f)`; stated as *trace-base-change-composition* below)
and `finiteTrace_test_split` and `finiteTrace_affine_split` (for `Y = ⊔_{i=1}^d X`
the trace is the sum map on every affinoid chart) (BHW §10.1, Def. 10.2, p.
1789, the analytic trace of a finite locally free map as used for Hecke operators; Stacks Tag 0BVH,
§49.3, the trace is the algebra trace over affine, here affinoid, opens; Stacks Tag 03SH, §59.66,
for finite étale maps the trace is étale-locally the sum over sheets). *Needs:*
*finite-locally-free-morphism*; *finite-locally-free-algebra-trace*; *algebra-trace-base-change*;
*projective-trace-realization*;
*locally-free-sheaf*; Mathlib `LinearMap.trace`.

`VectorBundle.trace_matrix` fixes `VectorBundle.trace` on a trivializing open
by the matrix trace of its section endomorphism. `finiteTraceForm_sections`
fixes the pairing on the images of pure section tensors. `finiteTrace_linear`
uses the actual structure-ring map of `f`; `finiteTrace_comp_unit` assumes
constant degree `n` on the specified open and gives multiplication by `n`.
No inverse of `n` is used. `IsFiniteLocallyFree.analytification` works for
relative analytification over a locally noetherian stably sheafy affinoid,
with the algebraic morphism finite, flat and locally of finite presentation;
its degree equality is pointwise along the analytification map. The local
calculations are finite projective trace and scalar extension; see BHW
§10.1, Definition 10.2 (arXiv v2, p. 45), and Conrad-RA Example 2.2.11, p. 13.

**Checks for bundle trace.** `VectorBundle.trace_zero` gives the zero morphism
for the zero bundle; `VectorBundle.trace_one` reads the sole diagonal entry;
`VectorBundle.trace_two` adds both diagonal entries in a local basis.

**Checks for the trace form.** `finiteTraceForm_empty` gives the zero morphism
for an empty source; `finiteTraceForm_identity` is multiplication `s t`;
`finiteTraceForm_symmetric` interchanges the two input sections.

**Checks.**

- `AdicSpace.finiteTrace_test_power_map` (computation) — for `n ≥ 1` and `f : z ↦ zⁿ = w` on the closed disc,
  for every `k ≥ 0`, `Tr_f(zᵏ) = n·w^{k/n}` if `n` divides `k` and `0` otherwise.
  The statement evaluates `finiteTrace f hf` on an affinoid open, using an
  `A`-algebra equivalence of its inverse-image sections with `A[z]/(zⁿ-w)`.
  `finiteTrace_power_map_identity` checks `n = 1` and `finiteTrace_power_map_characteristic`
  checks that this sheaf trace is zero for `n = char A = p`.
- `finiteTrace_ramified` (non-example) — for `f : z ↦ z²` at the point `w = 0`,
  the fibre has one geometric point but `Tr_f(1)(0) = 2`; defining `Tr_f(s)(x) = Σ_{y ↦ x} s(y)`
  is wrong at ramified points.
- `finiteTrace_id` (degenerate) — `Tr_{id_X} = id` and for `∅ → X` the trace is
  `0`.
- `AdicSpace.finiteTrace_test_split` (characterisation) — for `Y = ⊔_{i=1}^d X → X`,
  `Tr_f(s₁, …, s_d) = Σ s_i`. The section algebra is identified with `Fin d → A`
  by an `A`-algebra equivalence, using the scalar action induced by `f`.
  `finiteTrace_split_empty` evaluates the actual trace of the empty analytic cover.
- `AdicSpace.finiteTrace_test_algebraic` (compatibility) — for `π` finite locally free between
  `K`-schemes locally of finite type, `Tr_{π^an} = (Tr_π)^an`
  (stated as *analytic-algebraic-trace-compatibility* below).

Prove the base change and composition laws for the analytic trace
(*trace-base-change-composition*): (a) let `f : Y → X` be finite locally free, `g : X' → X` a
morphism of adic spaces for which the fibre product exists — `X′` covered by open affinoids with
complete stably sheafy rings, for instance `X′` locally noetherian, as *fibre-products-existence*
(a) (AdicSpacesPartII layer R0) requires, `f` being finite and hence locally of finite type; fibre products of adic
spaces do not exist in general — and `f' : Y' = Y ×_X X' → X'`; under the base-change isomorphism
`g*f_*𝒪_Y ≅ f'_*𝒪_{Y'}`, `g*(Tr_f) = Tr_{f'}`. (b) If `f : Z → Y` and `h : Y → X` are finite
locally free then so is `h ∘ f`, and `Tr_{h∘f} = Tr_h ∘ h_*(Tr_f)` (Stacks Tag 0BJF, proof of
Lem. 49.3.1, base change of the trace; Stacks Tag 02DV, Exercise 111.22.7, base change at the
level of algebras, where Stacks sets up `B′ = B ⊗_A A′` for the norm, the trace being the same
argument stated in 0BVH). For `z ↦ z² ↦ z⁴` on discs, `Tr(1) = 4 = Tr_h(Tr_f(1)) = Tr_h(2)`.
*Needs:* *analytic-trace-finite-locally-free*; *algebra-trace-base-change*;
*algebra-trace-transitivity*; *fibre-products-existence*, *affinoid-fibre-product* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R0).

The analytic section formula is `AdicSpace.finiteTrace_baseChange`: for a cartesian
square and opens `W ⊆ g⁻¹(U)`, it equates the trace of the restricted pullback of a section
with the restricted pullback of its trace. `AdicSpace.finiteTrace_comp` fixes the order
of traces for a composite. `AdicSpace.finiteTrace_power_cover` gives the power-map
formula on an affinoid with basis `1,z,…,z^(n−1)` and relation `z^n = w`:
`Tr(z^k) = n w^(k/n)` if `n ∣ k`, and zero otherwise, including characteristic dividing `n`.

Prove the perfect trace pairing and point-count formula for finite étale morphisms
(*finite-etale-trace-pairing*): let `f : Y → X` be a finite étale morphism between locally
Huber-standard adic spaces (étale in the sense of *differentials-unramified-smooth-etale*,
AdicSpacesPartII layer R0, and finite: `AdicSpace.IsFinite`, `AdicSpace.Etale`,
`AdicSpace.IsLocallyHuberStandard`); then `f` is finite
locally free and the trace pairing `f_*𝒪_Y → ℋom_{𝒪_X}(f_*𝒪_Y, 𝒪_X)`, `s ↦ (t ↦ Tr_f(st))`, is an
isomorphism; for `x ∈ X` with residue field `κ(x)` and an algebraically closed field `Ω ⊇ κ(x)`,
`Tr_f(s)(x) = Σ_σ σ(s)` over the `κ(x)`-algebra maps `σ : 𝒪_Y(f⁻¹U) ⊗ κ(x) → Ω` (`U` an affinoid
neighbourhood). Conversely a finite locally free `f` with perfect trace pairing is étale. Without
étaleness both statements fail (`z ↦ z²` at `0`) (KL15 §1.2, p. 13, finite étale algebras are
finite projective; Stacks Tag 0BJF, Lem. 49.3.1, perfect pairing iff étale). For the Kummer cover
`z ↦ z²` over the annulus `{|w| = 1}` (`char K ≠ 2`), the pairing has Gram matrix
`[[2, 0], [0, 2w]]` in the basis `1, z` and discriminant `4w`, a unit of `K⟨w, w⁻¹⟩` (for
`K = ℚ_2` as well, `4 ∈ ℚ_2^×`; over `ℤ_2⟨w, w⁻¹⟩` it is not a unit), and `Tr(1) = 2` is the
number of geometric points in each fibre; over the full disc the discriminant `4w` vanishes at
`0`, the pairing is not perfect and `f` is not étale. *Needs:*
*analytic-trace-finite-locally-free*; *etale-iff-trace-pairing-perfect*;
*trace-geometric-point-formula*; *algebra-trace-base-change*; *finite-locally-free-morphism*;
*differentials-unramified-smooth-etale*, *locally-huber-standard* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R0).

On a Tate affinoid, `AdicSpace.finiteTrace_perfect_iff_etale` expresses perfection
without choosing a basis: every linear functional is uniquely `t ↦ Tr(b t)`.
`AdicSpace.finiteTrace_geometric` computes the same analytic trace after any map of the
base ring to an algebraically closed field, as the sum over algebra maps of the finite
étale algebra. These use the trace morphism on the structure sheaf (Stacks Tag 0BJF).

Prove that the analytic trace of an analytified finite locally free morphism is the analytified
algebraic trace (*analytic-algebraic-trace-compatibility*): let `A` be an affinoid `K`-algebra
(`A = K` allowed) and `π : X' → X` a finite locally free morphism of schemes locally of finite type
over `Spec A`; then `π^an : X'^an → X^an` is finite locally free of the same degree, the canonical
map `(π_*𝒪_{X'})^an → π^an_*𝒪_{X'^an}` is an isomorphism, and under it `(Tr_π)^an = Tr_{π^an}`
(Stacks Tag 0BVH, §49.3, both traces are affine(-oid)-locally the algebra trace; Conrad-RA
Thm 2.2.5(3), p. 10, relative Spec of a finite algebra commutes with analytification, the
isomorphism (2.2.2)). For `π : A¹ → A¹`, `z ↦ z²`, `Tr_{π^an}` on the analytic line is the
analytification of `Tr_π(a(w) + b(w)z) = 2a(w)`. *Needs:* *scheme-trace-finite-locally-free*;
*analytic-trace-finite-locally-free*; *algebra-trace-base-change*; *analytification-of-modules*,
*analytification-finite* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R1); *analytification-coherent* (R3.7); *finite-locally-free-morphism*.

`finiteTrace_pairing` states the global pairing morphism, fixed on pure local
tensors by `s ⊗ t ↦ Tr(st)`, and identifies invertibility of its adjoint with
étaleness. `finiteEtale_isFiniteLocallyFree` supplies the finite locally free
hypothesis from finiteness and étaleness on strongly noetherian Tate charts.

**Pull–identify–trace operators along correspondences.** (*pull-identify-trace*) A
correspondence from `Y` to `X` is an adic space `C` with morphisms `q : C → Y` and `p : C → X`,
`p` finite locally free and `q` arbitrary. Given vector bundles (or, on locally noetherian
analytic spaces, coherent sheaves) `E_Y` on `Y` and `E_X` on `X` and an `𝒪_C`-linear
identification `φ : q*E_Y → p*E_X`, the pull–identify–trace operator
`T = T(C, φ) : Hⁱ(Y, E_Y) → Hⁱ(X, E_X)` is the composite
```text
Hⁱ(Y, E_Y) →(q*) Hⁱ(C, q*E_Y) →(φ) Hⁱ(C, p*E_X) = Hⁱ(X, p_*p*E_X)
           = Hⁱ(X, p_*𝒪_C ⊗ E_X) →(Tr_p ⊗ id) Hⁱ(X, E_X),
```
using that `p` is finite (`p_*` exact on coherent sheaves and vector bundles) and the projection
formula. No normalising factor is included; consumers multiply by their own constants (for
instance `1/q_a` in BHW). In `AdicSpace`, define `Correspondence` as the structure `(C, q, p)`
with `p` finite locally free and `Correspondence.pullIdentifyTrace` as the operator
`Hⁱ(Y, E_Y) → Hⁱ(X, E_X)` attached to any `𝒪_C`-linear `φ : q*E_Y → p*E_X`. It is unnormalised: no
factor depending on `p` or on a source convention is built in. For `E_X = 𝒪_X`, `E_Y = 𝒪_Y`, on
`H⁰`, `T(C, φ)(1) = Tr_p(φ(1))` with `φ(1) ∈ Γ(C, 𝒪_C)`; in particular `T(C, φ)(1) = deg p`, the
locally constant rank of `p_*𝒪_C` on `X` (one integer only when that rank is constant), when
`φ(1) = 1`, i.e. for the canonical identification `q*𝒪_Y = 𝒪_C = p*𝒪_X` (Stacks Tag 0BVH). Prove
`Correspondence.pullIdentifyTrace_id` (the identity correspondence with `φ = id` gives the
identity), `Correspondence.pullIdentifyTrace_comp` (for `C₁` from `Y` to `X` and `C₂` from `Z` to
`Y`, when the fibre product `C₂ ×_Y C₁` of `p₂ : C₂ → Y` and `q₁ : C₁ → Y` exists —
*fibre-products-existence* (a), AdicSpacesPartII layer R0: `p₂` is finite hence locally of finite type, and `C₁`
must be covered by stably sheafy affinoids, for instance locally noetherian — the composite
correspondence with the composite identification gives the composite operator; by
*trace-base-change-composition*), `Correspondence.pullIdentifyTrace_add` (additivity in `φ`, and
disjoint unions of correspondences give sums), `Correspondence.pullIdentifyTrace_one` (with
trivial coefficients, `T(C, φ)(1) = Tr_p(φ(1))` on `H⁰`; for the canonical `φ`, `φ(1) = 1` and
`T(1) = Tr_p(1) = deg p`, the locally constant rank of `p_*𝒪_C`),
`Correspondence.pullIdentifyTrace_analytification` (compatibility with the algebraic operator
under analytification) and `Correspondence.pullIdentifyTrace_restrict` (compatibility with
restriction to open subspaces `U ⊆ X`, `V ⊆ Y` with `p⁻¹U ⊆ q⁻¹V`, for changes of domain or
radius) (BHW §10.1, Def. 10.2, p. 1789, the `T_a`-operator: pull back along `π₂`, identify
`π₂*ω ≅ π₁*ω`, trace along `π₁`, normalised by `1/q_a`; Stacks Tag 03SH, §59.66, in the finite
étale case the trace step is the sum over sheets). BHW Def. 10.2 is `T_a = q_a⁻¹ · T(C, φ)` with
`C = X_{c,Γ₀(pⁿ)∩Γ₀(a)}`, `p = π₁`, `q = π₂` and `φ` the isomorphism `π₂*ω ≅ π₁*ω`
(*pull-identify-trace-hecke-normalisation*). *Needs:*
*analytic-trace-finite-locally-free*; *finite-locally-free-projection-formula*;
*coherent-sheaf-operations*; *trace-base-change-composition*; *tate-acyclicity-finite-modules*;
*finite-projective-module-acyclicity*; Mathlib `SheafOfModules.pullback`. The operator and its
coefficient Checks are specified in this README only.

`finiteTraceWithCoefficients` is fixed on local generators by
`finiteTraceWithCoefficients_sections`: `s ⊗ e ↦ Tr(s)e`.
`Correspondence.pullIdentifyTrace_factorization` specifies the operator in every
degree using pullback, the coefficient map, the inverse of the finite-pushforward
cohomology comparison, and this trace. The comparison itself is fixed by the
identity on local sections. `Correspondence.pullIdentifyTrace_sections` gives
the resulting formula in degree zero.
`Correspondence.pullIdentifyTrace_disjointUnion` identifies a two-summand
operator with the sum, with each coefficient map transported through the
actual coprojections. `Correspondence.pullIdentifyTrace_analytification`
specifies the algebraic operator as its pullback, coefficient-map, finite
pushforward comparison and trace composite; all comparison maps are normalized
on local sections.

`modulePullbackCompIso` is the associator used in composition and restriction;
`modulePullbackCompIso_sections` fixes it by sending a composite pullback unit
to the two successive units. This is the associativity of extension of scalars
in Mathlib `SheafOfModules.pullback`.

**Checks for pullback associativity.**

- `modulePullbackCompIso_zero`: the comparison on zero coefficients is zero.
- `modulePullbackCompIso_identity`: two identity pullbacks preserve every unit generator.
- `modulePullbackCompIso_unit`: the structure-sheaf generator one becomes the iterated unit of one.

**Checks for coefficient traces and correspondence operators.**

- `finiteTraceWithCoefficients_identity`: the identity trace fixes every pulled-back section.
- `finiteTraceWithCoefficients_zero`: zero coefficients give the zero map.
- `finiteTraceWithCoefficients_rankTwo`: trace after the unit is multiplication by two for constant rank two, also in characteristic two.
- `Correspondence_identity`, `Correspondence.pullIdentifyTrace_identity`: the identity correspondence acts identically in every degree.
- `Correspondence_empty`, `Correspondence.pullIdentifyTrace_empty`: empty correspondences act by zero.
- `Correspondence_rankTwo`, `Correspondence.pullIdentifyTrace_rankTwo`: for equal legs of constant rank two and identity coefficient map, the operator is multiplication by two, including ramified covers.
- `Correspondence.pullIdentifyTrace_split`: on the two-summand correspondence with second leg an endomorphism `σ`, a function `s` maps to `s + σ*s`.

**Checks.**

- `Correspondence.pullIdentifyTrace_split` (computation) — for `C = X ⊔ X`, `p = id ⊔ id`,
  `q = id ⊔ σ` and `E = 𝒪` with `φ` canonical, `T(s) = s + σ*s` on `H⁰`.
- `Correspondence_identity` (degenerate) — for `C = X = Y`, `p = q = id` and
  `φ = id`, `T` is the identity on every `Hⁱ`; for `C = ∅` (`p` finite locally free of degree
  `0`, `p_*𝒪_C = 0`) `T = 0`.
- `Correspondence_ramified_count` (non-example) — for `X = Y = disc`, `C = disc`,
  `p : z ↦ z²`, `q : z ↦ z²` and trivial coefficients, `T(1) = Tr_p(1) = 2` everywhere, including
  at `0` where the `p`-fibre has one geometric point; "sum over geometric points of the fibre"
  gives `1` at `0`.
- `Correspondence_algebraic` (compatibility) — for an algebraic correspondence of
  `K`-schemes locally of finite type with `p` finite locally free, `T(C^an, φ^an)` on
  `Hⁱ(Y^an, E_Y^an)` is the analytification of the algebraic operator
  (*analytic-algebraic-trace-compatibility* and the GAGA comparison maps).
- (coefficient map, negative control) — on the identity correspondence of `Spa(K, K°)` (both maps
  the identity), the coefficient maps `φ = 1, 0, 2` give `T(1) = 1, 0, 2`: the value is
  `Tr_p(φ(1))`, not the degree `1`.
- (coefficient map, canonical) — for the canonical `φ` on the degree-two cover `X ⊔ X → X`,
  `T(1) = Tr_p(1) = 2`.

**Hecke normalisation.** (*pull-identify-trace-hecke-normalisation*) Normalised operators are
formed explicitly from `T(C, φ)`: for an integer `N` invertible on the coefficients, `N⁻¹T(C, φ)`;
`T(C, φ)` itself is never divided by a degree. BHW's tame Hecke operator `T_a` (Def. 10.2,
p. 1789), for an ideal `a ⊆ O_F` prime to the tame level and to the residue characteristic `p`, is
`q_a⁻¹ T(C, φ)` on global sections of the weight-`κ` sheaf, where `q_a = |O_F/a|`, `C` is the
Hilbert modular variety with added `Γ₀(a)`-structure `D`, the forgetful map `π₁` is the finite
locally free leg, the quotient map `π₂ : A ↦ A/D` is the other leg, and `φ : π₂*ω ≅ π₁*ω` is the
canonical isomorphism of BHW Lem. 10.1. As `a` is prime to `p`, `q_a` is a unit of `ℤ_p`, so the
normalisation is defined on the integral sheaf `ω^{κ,+}` on which BHW work. *Needs:*
*pull-identify-trace*; *finite-locally-free-morphism*.

**Check.** (trivial ideal) — for `a = O_F`, `D = 0`, both legs are the identity, `q_a = 1` and
`T_a = T(C, id) = id`.

### R3.9 the Gel'fand spectrum of a Banach ring

This target is stated here because this roadmap needs it: the uniform-ring result
*uniform-spectral-seminorm* of this layer is phrased through the Gel'fand spectrum and Berkovich's
formula for the spectral seminorm (the glueing squares of R3.2 avoid it through condition (c) of
*glueing-square*). This
layer owns the statement; PerfectoidSpaces layer P1 (P1.12, the units and the maximum formula)
and DiamondsAndVStacks layer D5 (D5.13, the Berkovich spectrum of a complete Tate ring) cite it.

**The Gel'fand spectrum of a Banach ring and Berkovich's formula for the spectral seminorm.**
(*gelfand-spectrum-banach-ring*) For a complete normed commutative ring `A` (a Banach ring, not
assumed an algebra over a field), the Gel'fand spectrum `M(A)` is the set of bounded
multiplicative seminorms on `A`, with the topology of pointwise convergence. Prove that `M(A)` is
nonempty when `A ≠ 0`, compact Hausdorff, and functorial in bounded ring homomorphisms, and that
the spectral seminorm of `x ∈ A` is `lim ‖xⁿ‖^{1/n} = max_{α ∈ M(A)} α(x)`, where for `A = 0`
the maximum over the empty `M(0)` is read as `0` (a multiplicative seminorm has `α(1) = 1`, and
`1 = 0` in `A = 0`, so `M(0) = ∅`, which is compact; `lim ‖0ⁿ‖^{1/n} = 0`). Define
`Huber.GelfandSpectrum` as `M(A)` with its topology, and the continuous map `M(B) → M(A)`
induced by a bounded ring homomorphism `A → B`; prove that `M(A)` is compact Hausdorff and that
`M(A) ≠ ∅` when `A ≠ 0` (together `GelfandSpectrum.compactSpace_nonempty`), and that
`lim ‖xⁿ‖^{1/n} = sup_{α ∈ M(A)} α(x)` for every `x ∈ A`, the supremum being attained for `A ≠ 0`
(together `GelfandSpectrum.smoothingFun_eq_sSup`, with Mathlib's `smoothingFun` of the norm as the
spectral seminorm) (Berkovich
Thm 1.2.1, the nonempty compact spectrum; Berkovich Thm 1.3.1, the spectral-seminorm formula;
KL15 §2.3, Def. 2.3.2 and Thm 2.3.4, p. 34;
Thm 2.3.10, p. 35; Rem. 2.3.11(b), p. 36). *Needs:* *tate-ring-norm* (PadicFunctionalAnalysis §0.4);
*spectral-seminorm* (AdicSpacesPartII layer R0). Lean: `Huber.GelfandSpectrum` with its topology,
`GelfandSpectrum.compactSpace_nonempty`, `GelfandSpectrum.smoothingFun_eq_sSup`,
`GelfandSpectrum.test_padic`, `GelfandSpectrum.test_zero_ring` and `GelfandSpectrum.test_dualNumbers`.
The nilpotent-value Check is a proved Lean example; functoriality and the other Checks are
specified in this README only.

**Checks.**

- `Huber.GelfandSpectrum.test_padic` (computation, `ℚ_p`) — `M(ℚ_p)` is a single point, the `p`-adic absolute
  value.
- (characterisation, Gauss point) — for a complete nonarchimedean field
  `K` with nontrivial valuation, the Gauss norm on
  `MvPowerSeries.IsRestricted.subring (fun _ : Fin n ↦ 1)` is a point of `M(K⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩)` at which the maximum `max_{α ∈ M(K⟨X⟩)} α(f)` is
  attained for every `f`. Use the pinned Gauss norm, multiplicativity and completeness in
  `TauCeti/RingTheory/MvPowerSeries/TateAlgebra/Basic.lean` for this Check.
- `Huber.GelfandSpectrum.test_dualNumbers` (non-example, nilpotent) — the spectral seminorm of a nilpotent element
  is `0` while its norm need not be, so the norm of `A` is not in general a point of `M(A)` and
  the spectral seminorm is not the norm: for `A = K[ε]/(ε²)` with the supplied
  `TrivSqZeroExt` norm `‖a + bε‖ = |a| + |b|` (equivalent to the maximum norm),
  `‖ε‖ = 1`, `‖εⁿ‖ = 0` for `n ≥ 2`, every `α ∈ M(A)` has `α(ε)² = α(ε²) = 0`, so
  `M(A) = M(K)` (one point for `K = ℚ_p`) and `max_α α(ε) = 0 = lim ‖εⁿ‖^{1/n}`: Berkovich's
  formula holds on the non-reduced `A`, and the norm is not a point of `M(A)`.
  The check computes `smoothingFun` and the supremum over `GelfandSpectrum`
  itself, and rules out a spectrum point equal to the ambient norm (KL15,
  Theorem 2.3.10 and Remark 2.3.11(b), pp. 35–36).
- (negative control, constant one) — on the zero ring the constant
  function `α = 1` is multiplicative and has `α(1) = 1`. On the dual numbers it also has
  `α(ε) = 1`. Both fail the seminorm axiom `α(0) = 0`, which is essential in the two checks.
- `Huber.GelfandSpectrum.test_zero_ring` (degenerate, zero ring) — `M(0) = ∅` (no seminorm has `α(1) = 1` when
  `1 = 0` and `α(0) = 0`), compact, and `lim ‖0ⁿ‖^{1/n} = 0 = max_∅`; for `A = ℚ_p` the spectral seminorm of a
  nonzero `x` is `|x|_p ≠ 0`, so nonemptiness needs `A ≠ 0` and nothing more.

The pointwise topology and the induced maps are defined for every normed commutative ring; compactness,
nonemptiness and the spectral formula assume completeness. `MulRingSeminorm` supplies the
seminorm axioms; the spectrum adds a bound `α(x) ≤ C‖x‖` for one `C > 0`.

**Further Checks.**

- (subsingleton) — for every subsingleton normed ring, the spectrum is empty.
- (nilpotent value) — if `x² = 0`, every spectrum point sends `x` to
  zero, since `α(x)² = α(0) = 0`.
- (pullback, identity) — pullback along the identity fixes every seminorm.
- (pullback, composition) — for `A → B → C`, pullback from `C` to `A` is first
  pullback to `B`, then to `A`; this fixes the contravariant direction.
- (pullback, values) — the pulled-back seminorm sends `0` to `0` and
  `1` to `1`, so the zero function cannot be a spectrum point.

### Examples

For `A = K⟨T⟩`, `M = A/(T)` and the two-piece cover `|T| ≤ |ϖ|`, `|T| ≥ |ϖ|`, the
augmented Čech complex of `M̃` is `0 → K → K ⊕ 0 → 0`. The restriction to the outer piece
vanishes because `T` becomes invertible there.

For `B = R[x]/(x² − d)`, multiplication by `a + bx` has matrix `[[a,bd],[b,a]]` in the basis
`1,x`, so its trace is `2a`. The trace-pairing matrix is `diag(2,2d)`; over `ℚ` at `d=2` its
determinant is `8`, whereas in characteristic `2` it vanishes. The trace is unnormalised,
including at ramified points.

For the restriction from the unit disc to `|T| ≤ |ϖ|`, the coefficient of `Tⁿ` is multiplied
by `ϖⁿ` in the rescaled coordinate. Truncation below degree `N` has error at most `|ϖ|^N`.
For the identity restriction those coefficients are all `1`, and no finite-rank truncation
has error less than `1`.

On the identity correspondence the pull–identify–trace operator with coefficient map `2` sends `1`
to `2`, not to the degree `1`; on the degree-two cover `X ⊔ X → X` with the canonical coefficient
map it sends `1` to `2`.

### Dependencies

Layers AdicSpacesPartII R0 (noetherian-type rings and their modules, Čech exactness for noetherian rings of
definition, completed tensor products, Tate-ring norms and spectral seminorms, locally noetherian
adic spaces, locally Huber-standard adic spaces (*locally-huber-standard*), fibre products and base
change, closed adic subspaces, proper and finite morphisms, continuous differentials and the
unramified, smooth and étale classes (*differentials-unramified-smooth-etale*), Banach modules over
complete Tate rings), AdicSpacesPartII R1 (analytification of schemes and general module pullback, the rigid–adic comparison,
properness and finiteness comparisons, analytic affine and projective spaces, analytic Kähler
differentials), R3.1a's affinoid section comparison for analytified modules,
DerivedModuleAlgebra §§1.T.1 and 1.1 (generic tower calculus and ML vanishing) and
§S.1 (canonical double-complex comparisons),
*mittag-leffler-criteria* here (quotients, extensions and Artinian terms),
and F0 (formal-module tower applications, the theorem on formal functions, Chow's lemma and
dévissage) of this roadmap, and the structure sheaf, rational localisations, sheafiness,
uniformity and the Buzzard–Verberkmoes theorem of the Foundations of adic spaces roadmap
(AdicSpaces), layers 0.2, 3.1, 3.4, 3.5, 4.1, 4.2, 5 and 5.2; DerivedModuleAlgebra §S.1 `DoubleComplex.totalCohomology_of_exact_rows` and its transpose, applied to a sheaf resolution on the rational basis; SchemeAndStackFoundations Layer 2 (§2.6, `ample_serre_vanishing`; §2.19, §2.21, `trace`);

## Downstream consumers

F0 applies Part II R0's noetherian completion and finite-module results to formal schemes.
AdicSpacesPartIV uses formal models, coherent sheaves and differentials for families and
dagger geometry. AdicEtaleGeometry A2 uses F0 and R2's formal schemes and generic fibres.
PerfectoidSpaces P1.12 uses R3's Gel'fand spectrum; P0.12 and P0.15 are the almost versions of its classical traces.
PerfectoidSpaces P3.17a–P3.17b uses the adic-space carriers for sousperfectoid spaces and
products with polydiscs, applying R3.5's *stably-uniform-sheafy* and
*split-injection-completed-base-change* to sousperfectoid frames.
DiamondsAndVStacks D5.13 uses the Gel'fand spectrum, and its formal interfaces use F0's
formal spectrum and R2's specialization and pre-adic interface.
The étale-cohomology, Shimura-variety, rigid-cohomology and `p`-adic Hodge theory roadmaps
use the coherent and differential sheaves of R3 and the formal models, Hasse domains and
residue discs of R2.
